records.title: Computer Programming — Study notes
records.text: Computer Programming Learn to design, trace, debug and justify small programs. C++17 is the default for valid C++ examples; Java-specific behavior is labeled. The official blueprint allocates six items. Trace a small state table before looking at output choices. Check types, precedence, side effects, control flow and bounds in that order. Write one function, one array traversal and one loop correctness argument from memory; test boundaries and invalid inputs. Use comparisons for revision, but derive answers from rules and check that the question states the necessary assumptions.

records.title: Computer Programming — Turn a problem into a program
records.text: Identify inputs, outputs, legal ranges and edge cases before coding. Solve one small case manually, choose an algorithm, express it as pseudocode or a flowchart, implement, test and maintain. For the largest of three numbers, initialize best to the first input, compare the second and third, then report best. Initializing best to zero fails when all inputs are negative. Programming includes writing, testing, debugging and maintaining instructions. A program can execute without solving its intended problem; compare its actual result with the required result. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Algorithm properties and paradigms
records.text: An algorithm gives precise, executable steps and terminates for every legal input. Definiteness means each step has an unambiguous meaning; effectiveness means a step can actually be performed. Inputs may be absent, but a useful algorithm specifies a result. Correctness means the result meets the specification. Efficiency is desirable and measurable, but an inefficient terminating algorithm is still an algorithm. Efficiency is also a desirable property of an algorithm. Procedural programming organizes operations in procedures; structured programming combines sequence, selection and iteration; object oriented programming organizes state and behavior in objects; functional programming emphasizes function evaluation. A conditional statement is a construct, not a separate programming paradigm. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Language levels, generations and portability
records.text: Machine instructions are conventionally first generation; symbolic assembly is second; general high-level languages such as C++ and Java are third. Database query and application generators such as SQL are conventionally fourth generation. Fifth generation is a loose historical category associated with declarative logic, constraints and AI/expert systems. Generations do not determine whether an implementation uses an interpreter. Machine and assembly code depend on an instruction set. High-level source is easier to read and often portable after recompilation, provided it avoids platform assumptions. People can write both assembly and high-level programs. Python, Perl and PHP are commonly called scripting languages; C++ is conventionally compiled. These labels describe common use, not an absolute technical prohibition. Computer Programming module University of Rhode Island: language levels and generations

records.title: Computer Programming — Compilation, linking, loading and Java translation
records.text: In the conventional C++ toolchain: source → preprocessing → compilation proper → assembly → object files → linking → executable → loading → execution. Preprocessing handles directives such as #include; compilation may emit assembly; the assembler emits machine instructions in an object file. The linker resolves external symbols and combines object files and libraries. The loader places an executable and required components in memory and starts it. GCC documents the first four stages explicitly. A compiler need not emit a complete executable or even native machine code. Java javac produces bytecode, which a JVM interprets or compiles at runtime. Interpreters execute a program representation; “one source line at a time” is a beginner approximation. Compilation uses multiple passes, so “whole program in one step” is not literally universal. Computer Programming module GCC manual: compilation stages

records.title: Computer Programming — Identifiers, keywords and comments
records.text: In the basic ASCII identifier rules, start with a letter or underscore; continue with letters, digits or underscores. Do not use a keyword. C++ is case sensitive: exitExam and ExitExam differ; delete and float are keywords, but FLOAT is a legal identifier. variable_1234 is valid; 4thInput, T-3 and names containing spaces are not single identifiers. Avoid reserved underscore patterns in application code. Comments use // to the line end or /* ... */ for a block. They explain intent and assumptions for maintenance; ordinary comments do not execute or automatically improve speed, reliability or portability. main is the conventional entry function name, not a C++ keyword. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Declarations, initialization, constants and types
records.text: Write type name; or type name = value; for ordinary variables: int age = 20;. Declaration introduces a name and type; initialization gives its initial value; later assignment replaces a value. a=b copies a scalar value, so later changes to b do not change a. A pointer or Java object reference instead copies an address/reference. Use int for whole numbers, float/double for fractional approximations, char for a character and bool for logical values in C++. Type sizes depend on the implementation; do not import Java widths into C++. short n, short int n and int short n denote the same signed short type. const int n=5 and int const n=5 are equivalent; an ordinary const int needs initialization. typedef creates an alias, not a distinct new type. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Literals, conversions and sizeof
records.text: Single quotes denote a character literal, such as 'A'; double quotes denote a string literal, such as "A". A string includes more storage than just its visible characters when a terminator is required. sizeof reports size in bytes, with sizeof(char)==1; the byte width and other sizes are implementation dependent. sizeof(array) gives total array storage before conversion to a pointer. With int x=5,y=2, x/y is 2. Assigning that quotient to double gives 2.0, not 2.5. static_cast<double>(x)/y performs floating division and yields 2.5. Converting an in-range fractional floating value to int truncates toward zero. Cast before the operation if a fractional result is needed. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Arithmetic and compound updates
records.text: Multiplication, division and remainder have higher precedence than addition and subtraction; equal-precedence arithmetic groups left to right. Integer division truncates toward zero. For integers, a == (a/b)*b + a%b when the division is valid. % requires integral operands in C++; (8.0*3)%5 is invalid. Division by zero and signed integer overflow cannot be given ordinary numeric outputs. x+=y, x-=y, x*=y, x/=y and x%=y update x using the operation and conversion to its type. For simple variables, trace them as x=x op y. Starting p=q=n=8, p+=n gives 16 and p/=q gives 2. Starting x=10, x+=5 then x/=2 gives 7. x=x+x doubles; it does not generally add one. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Prefix, postfix and evaluation safety
records.text: Prefix ++x changes x and yields the new value; postfix x++ yields the previous value and also increments x. Separate the value used in the expression from the stored value after it. Starting a=8,b=5, a++ + --b uses 8+4, gives 12, and leaves a=9,b=4. Starting x=1,y=10,z=-3, (x++*y--)+ ++z gives 8 and leaves x=2,y=9,z=-2. Precedence determines grouping, not a universal evaluation order. Avoid expressions that modify a variable multiple times without sequencing. In C++17 and later, chained operator-form stream insertions are sequenced left to right: with x=5, cout<<x++<<" "<<++x prints 5 7. Before C++17 this expression has undefined behavior. For the C++17 expression above, 5 6, 5 5, 6 5 and 6 6 are all incorrect outputs. Computer Programming module C++ draft: shift sequencing

records.title: Computer Programming — Boolean, relational, bitwise and short-circuit logic
records.text: Relational and equality operators test values; && and || combine truth values; ! negates. In C++, zero converts to false and a nonzero number to true. Streams display bool as 0 or 1 unless boolalpha is set. With a=3,b=5, cout<<(a==b) prints 0. && evaluates its right operand only if the left is true; || only if the left is false. Thus false && dangerousCall() skips the call. Bitwise & operates on bits and does not short circuit. With x=1,y=0,z=4, (x&y)||++z evaluates ++z, leaving z=5 and the Boolean result 1. The precedence ladder is grouping/postfix, unary, multiplicative, additive, shifts, relations, equality, bitwise &, ^, |, &&, ||, conditional, assignment, comma. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Conditional and comma expressions
records.text: condition ? yes : no evaluates the condition and exactly one alternative. The comma operator evaluates its left expression, then its right, and yields the right value. Do not confuse it with commas separating function arguments. For a=6,b=8,x=2,y=4, c=(x>y ? (a--,x) : (b--,y)) takes the false branch. b becomes 7, c receives 4 and a remains 6. Both alternatives are not executed. A semicolon in place of the internal comma is invalid syntax; a trace using a comma applies only after that syntax change. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Trace decisions and recognize flowcharts
records.text: A standalone if may execute independently of the following if. An else binds to its nearest unmatched if; an else-if ladder executes the first true branch only. In nested if(c1){if(c2) S1; else S2;}, S2 requires c1 true and c2 false. Braces determine grouping. With ph=15.3, an invalid-range if can print its warning, and a separate classification ladder can also print Alkaline. They are not mutually exclusive unless linked by else or an early return. A flowchart decision is a diamond, processing a rectangle, input/output a parallelogram and start/end a terminator. A pre-test loop checks before its body; a post-test loop checks after. Identify a flowchart’s loop from its arrows and the placement of its conditions. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Switch selection and fall-through
records.text: A traditional C++ switch selects using an integral or enumeration value. case labels are constant expressions. Execution starts at the matching label, then continues through subsequent statements until a break, return or the end. default handles an unmatched value but need not be the last physical label. If case 2 prints Bus. and case 3 prints Truck. before the first break, input 2 prints Bus.Truck. A break exits the nearest switch or loop; it does not by itself terminate the entire program. A case label is an entry point, not an automatically isolated if branch. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — While, do-while and for mechanics
records.text: while(condition) checks before each body execution and may run zero times. do {body;} while(condition); runs the body once before checking; it repeats while the condition remains true. Use it when a menu or input attempt must occur at least once. for(initialization; condition; update) executes initialization once, then condition → body → update → condition. A missing condition in for(;;) acts as true. A for loop is convenient for a known count but can also be condition controlled. To print indices 0 through n-1, use i=0; i<n; ++i. Starting i=0 with i<5 and i+=2 prints 0 2 4. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Break, continue, return and goto
records.text: break exits the nearest enclosing loop or switch. continue skips the rest of the current loop iteration: a for loop then runs its update; a while loop goes directly to its condition. return leaves the current function and may supply a result. In main it ends the program normally. A goto transfers to a label within its function; follow the label reached rather than reading lines in source order. In the sequence a: print Graduating; goto b; c: print Year; goto a; b: print fourth;, entry at a prints Graduating fourth and reaches the end. Year is not printed. Structured alternatives usually make such logic easier to reason about. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Count iterations and diagnose nontermination
records.text: Make a table with condition inputs, body output and updated values. For i=0,j=8; i<j; i++,j--, body entries are (0,8),(1,7),(2,6),(3,5). If odd i triggers continue, printing occurs twice. With outer i=1; i<5; i+=5, the outer loop runs once; an inner j=10; j>i; --j prints nine times. For n=1; n<=18; n+=2, print n unless n%7==0 then break: output is 1 3 5. A while(a>b) with fixed a=6,b=5 never changes its true condition. In data[10]={5,10,...,50}, i=0, advancing i only if data[i]%10==0 causes no progress because data[0]=5. It prints nothing and loops indefinitely; changing <=10 to <10 alone does not repair progress. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Functions, parameters and reusable modules
records.text: A function groups a named task. C++ definition: int add(int a,int b){return a+b;}. Call it with add(x,y);, without parameter type declarations at the call site. Parameters are names in the definition; arguments are supplied expressions or values. A void function produces no return value but can have side effects and return; to exit early. A method is a function associated with a class or object; methods can return values. Modules group related responsibilities behind interfaces. Reuse reduces duplication; independent functions are easier to understand and test. A library provides reusable components; a framework also supplies an organizing structure and often calls application callbacks. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Value, reference and pointer parameters
records.text: A C++ value parameter is a separate object initialized from the argument. In func(int a,int b){a*=5;b+=5;return a+b;}, calling func(9,3) returns 53 and leaves the caller values 9 and 3 unchanged. An int& parameter aliases the caller variable, so swap(int& a,int& b) changes both originals. An int* parameter copies an address; *p=value changes the pointed-to object, but p=anotherAddress only changes the local pointer. An array parameter int a[] is adjusted to int*: elements can change, and the length must be passed separately. Java always passes by value, including a copy of an object reference; it does not pass caller variables by reference. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Overloads, default arguments and inline
records.text: Overloads share a name but differ in parameter count or types/order. Return type alone cannot distinguish them. Choose a candidate using argument types, then required conversions; report ambiguity if there is no unique best match. int sum(int x,int y,int z=0) allows two or three arguments; defaults occupy trailing positions in ordinary declarations. inline does not compel the compiler to copy a function body at a call. Small frequently used functions may be good optimization candidates, but actual expansion is the optimizer’s decision. Inline also has language linkage/definition rules, so it is not simply a speed command. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Scope, lifetime and persistent static locals
records.text: Scope is where a name can be used; lifetime is when its object exists. A local name is restricted to its block; an outer name may be shadowed. A namespace/global variable is available where its declaration is visible, not magically in every file. C++ ::name selects a global name hidden by a local one. An automatic local is created anew on entry. A static local is initialized once and retains its value across calls even though its name remains local. If static x=0 changes by +1 when even and +2 otherwise, five calls return 1,3,5,7,9, whose sum is 25. Namespace/static storage integers are zero initialized; an ordinary uninitialized local int has no usable assumed zero value. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Recursion, base cases and call tracing
records.text: A recursive function calls itself directly or indirectly. It needs a base case and progress toward it for all supported inputs. factorial(0)=1 and factorial(n)=n*factorial(n-1) for positive n. factorial(3) expands to 3*2*1*1=6. Negative inputs require rejection or a separate definition; they do not reach zero under n-1. Evaluate conditions before expanding a recursive call. For if(n<m) return 0;, f(1,4) returns immediately; unreachable recursive branches add nothing. Record each call’s local parameters and pending operation, then unwind returned values. Recursion commonly uses smaller instances, but merely having a base-case branch does not prove it will be reached. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Arrays and bounds
records.text: A built-in C++ array has a fixed number of same-type elements in contiguous storage: int a[4]={10,20,30,40};. Valid indices are 0 through 3. a[4] is outside the array; accessing it has undefined behavior. Java checks bounds and throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Do not predict a C++ out-of-range value from nearby memory. A standard built-in array bound must be a compile-time constant; variable-length local arrays are compiler extensions. int a[5]={1,2,3}; fills the remaining elements with zeros. An uninitialized automatic array of int is different. a[i] equals *(a+i), so elements can be accessed using pointer notation without explicitly writing brackets. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Array algorithms and two-dimensional indexing
records.text: For a sum, start total=0 and add each element once. For a maximum/minimum, initialize from a[0] only after confirming the array is nonempty. For 50 inputs where nonpositive values are skipped, use a count-controlled loop and either if(x>0) total+=x; or continue for x<=0. These constructs solve different parts of the task. int a[R][C] has R rows, each with C elements. a[r][c] uses zero-based row then column. Its element offset is r*C+c in row-major storage. In the 4x4 matrix example, a[1][1]=6, a[2][3]=6 and a[3][3]=2. In Java, length belongs to each array; a traversal ending at arr.length-2 visits fewer elements than a full traversal. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — C strings and C++ string objects
records.text: A C string is a character array ending in '\0'. "Hello" needs six char positions; strlen counts five visible characters and excludes the terminator. sizeof a fixed char array reports its allocated bytes, which can exceed strlen+1. cout<<a prints a terminated char sequence, not its numeric address. <cstring> supplies strcpy(destination,source), strcat(destination,source), strlen and strcmp. Supply enough destination capacity; strcmp returns zero for equal content, otherwise a sign, not necessarily exactly -1 or 1. C++ std::string in <string> owns resizable text; + concatenates, == compares content, size()/length() counts stored characters and substr(start,count) extracts a segment. Standard std::string has no Java-style toUpperCase() or trim() member. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Pointers, dereferencing and assignment
records.text: int x=10; int* p=&x; stores x’s address in p. *p reads or writes x; &p is the address of the pointer variable itself. With p=&a,q=&b, p=q redirects p to b and leaves a and b unchanged. By contrast *p=*q copies the pointed-to value. Never dereference an uninitialized, null or dangling pointer. An array expression commonly converts to a pointer to its first element, but the array is not itself an assignable pointer variable. A pointer-to-pointer int** pp=&p allows **pp to reach x. A void* can hold an object address but requires conversion to a suitable object pointer before dereferencing in C++. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Scaled pointer arithmetic and dynamic allocation
records.text: If p points inside an array, p+k advances k elements, or k*sizeof(*p) bytes. Under the explicit assumption sizeof(float)==4 and first address 7000, p+3 has numeric address 7012. cout<<p++ displays the old address then advances p; cout<<*p++ displays the old element then advances p. ++*p changes the element. Pointer addition p+q is invalid; subtracting pointers within the same array gives an element distance. Arithmetic must stay within an array or its one-past position; one-past may not be dereferenced. C++ new T creates a dynamic object, delete releases it; new T[n] pairs with delete[]. Prefer resource-owning standard containers in real programs. Allocation does not automatically initialize every primitive value unless initialization is requested. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Structures and member access
records.text: A struct groups named members, possibly of different types. struct House{double price; int rooms;}; defines a type; House h{150000,3}; creates an object. h.rooms uses a dot. House* p=&h; p->rooms is equivalent to (*p).rooms. The pointer must refer to a live object before member access. A type definition alone does not create an ordinary instance. Aggregate initialization assigns members in declaration order. Modern C++ permits default member initializers such as int rooms=3;. C++11 list initialization rejects narrowing; a constant floating value exactly representable in the target floating type can be permitted, so 25.00 to float is not necessarily narrowing. Use 25.0f for clarity and check the language version. Structures can be copied, passed and returned; a structure cannot contain a full instance of itself, but may contain a pointer to its own type. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Console input, output and headers
records.text: Include <iostream> and qualify std::cin/std::cout or introduce the names explicitly. cout is the standard output stream; << inserts values. cin is standard input; >> extracts formatted values. std::endl inserts a newline and flushes. C++ names are case sensitive: Cout, Int and std: :cout are not equivalent valid spellings of cout, int and std::cout. Read a full line with getline(cin,text). After formatted numeric extraction, consume the pending newline before a line read when required. Input failure must be tested before trusting a value. Console output formatting matters: by default a double storing an exact 4 may print 4 rather than 4.0. Text, spaces and newlines are part of an output trace. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — File streams, modes and safe reading
records.text: Include <fstream>. ofstream writes, ifstream reads, and fstream can do both. The constructor’s default ofstream mode argument is ios::out; its ordinary effect is to create/truncate the file. Distinguish the default mode argument from effective out|trunc behavior. ios::app places each write at the end; ios::ate initially seeks to the end; ios::binary requests binary mode. Check if(!file) after opening. Read using while(file>>record) or while(getline(file,line)), because end-of-file is discovered by an attempted read. while(!file.eof()) can process an invalid extra record. Close or rely on stream destruction to release the resource. “ofstream” is a class, whereas <fstream> is the header. Computer Programming module C++ draft: ofstream constructors

records.title: Computer Programming — Mathematical functions and iterative powers
records.text: Use <cmath> for sqrt, pow, floor and ceil; integer abs is also provided by <cstdlib>. sqrt(16)=4; pow(3,4)=81; abs(-7)=7. ceil(x) is the least integer-valued result >=x; floor(x) the greatest <=x. Thus ceil(-2.7)=-2 and floor(-2.7)=-3; truncation toward zero differs from floor for negatives. C++ has no built-in exponentiation operator: ^ is bitwise XOR and ** is not a power operator. To compute b^e for a nonnegative integer e, start r=1 and repeat r*=b exactly e times; b=4,e=3 gives 64. Large powers and factorials can overflow fixed-width types; specify a valid input range. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Correctness by logic, invariants and induction
records.text: To prove an implication P⇒Q, a direct proof derives Q assuming P; a contrapositive proves not Q⇒not P; a contradiction assumes the claim false and derives an impossibility. A single counterexample disproves a universal claim. Induction proves a base case and proves P(k+1) assuming P(k). For sum=0,i=1; while(i<=n){sum+=i;++i;}, use invariant sum=(i-1)*i/2. It holds initially. Adding i gives i*(i+1)/2, then incrementing i restores the invariant. Exit gives i=n+1 and sum=n*(n+1)/2. Termination needs a separate decreasing nonnegative measure n-i+1 while the guard holds. Assume n>=0 and no arithmetic overflow. This connects mathematical proof to actual code. Western University: program verification Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Debugging, errors, exceptions and maintenance
records.text: A syntax error violates grammar; a type error can be syntactically well formed but rejected during semantic checking. A runtime error occurs during execution; a logic error gives the wrong behavior. A bug is a defect; debugging locates and corrects it. Read the first useful compiler diagnostic, inspect nearby tokens and declarations, repair and rebuild; a debugger is useful after a runnable program exists. Test ordinary, boundary and invalid inputs and trace the first point where actual state differs from expected state. Exceptions transfer control to a matching handler for exceptional conditions; they do not make arbitrary undefined behavior recoverable. Refactoring improves internal structure while preserving observable behavior. Version control records changes, supports comparison and rollback; documentation explains use, design and maintenance assumptions. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Static typing and Java-specific details
records.text: Static typing checks types before execution; type inference can still infer a static type, as with C++ auto. Dynamic typing checks operations using runtime values; it does not mean variables must have explicit static declarations. Static typing does not always require explicit type annotations. Java uses boolean, fixed-width numeric primitive types and references to objects. Java String is immutable, substring(begin,end) uses an exclusive end, equals compares content and == compares references. Java arrays have a length field. Scanner nextInt() can leave a newline for nextLine(). C++ std::string is mutable and uses substr(start,count); the two APIs must not be merged. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Check syntax and trace control flow
records.text: A program trace requires the complete code, and a diagram question requires its edges, conditions and labels. When entry reaches the body rectangle before the decision diamond and a decision branch returns to the body, the body executes before the condition is tested. This is a post-test do-while loop. Check that a program is valid before tracing it; state any syntax changes before analyzing the resulting program. Match pointer-member names exactly: Cout/Cin, C1 and car_mode do not match cout/cin, c1 and car_model. In the goto sequence above, Year is not printed because control does not reach its label. With valid C++ syntax for the stated assignments, the trace yields z=5 then a=1. Printing Z when only z is declared refers to a different, undeclared identifier. Use <0 for a less-than-zero comparison and the standard int main() declaration for a C++ entry point. Check int and cout case, quotation marks and comma-expression punctuation before tracing a C++ expression. Predict output only after the program and its execution conditions are clear. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Interpret programming questions precisely
records.text: Evaluate every choice against the language rules; more than one statement may be valid, or none may be valid. Distinguish linking from loading. Distinguish binary representation, machine code and executable files. Assess class membership and possible initialization separately; both statements can be correct. Check whether alternative short declarations are equivalent. Check the C++ version and narrowing rules before evaluating an initialization. Array subscripting and equivalent pointer access can refer to the same element. Use the definition of static typing rather than equating it with explicit annotations. An ordinary integer declaration can be written int x;. A void function definition can be complete without returning a value; int myFunction(){} can compile, but reaching its end is undefined behavior. A break statement exits the enclosing loop or switch. Check required initialization when evaluating const declarations, including alternative const spellings. Distinguish counting iterations from skipping inputs, and terminating a loop from ending only the current iteration. After inspecting and changing code, rebuild and retest to complete debugging. Computer Programming module

records.title: Computer Programming — Empty braces initialize aggregate members
records.text: For an aggregate with no default member initializers, empty braces initialize its members recursively. Numeric scalar members become zero, and the elements of a character-array member become zero characters. A zero character at the beginning of such an array makes it an empty, terminated C string. This differs from leaving an ordinary automatic scalar or array uninitialized. C++ working draft — Aggregate initialization

records.title: Computer Programming — High-level languages and scripting usage
records.text: Python is a high-level programming language with built-in high-level data types. Calling a language a scripting language describes a common way it is used; it does not make that language machine code or assembly. Language level and execution style are different classifications. Python tutorial — Whetting Your Appetite

records.title: Computer Programming — Keywords and names have different roles
records.text: A keyword is a reserved word with a predefined meaning in the language grammar. It cannot be repurposed as an ordinary variable or function name. An identifier is a name used to refer to a data object or function; its spelling must obey the identifier-character rules and avoid keywords. Computer Programming module · page 5

records.title: Computer Programming — Java print and println preserve output layout
records.text: Java System.out.print writes the supplied value without automatically ending the line. System.out.println writes its value and then a line separator. Successive println calls therefore place their values on separate lines, even when each printed expression also contains a trailing space. Java SE 17 — PrintStream print and println

records.title: Computer Programming — An assignment expression can accidentally become a condition
records.text: In C++, simple assignment changes its left-hand object, and the assignment expression refers to that updated object. When an ordinary numeric assignment is used as a condition, the newly assigned value is converted to truth: zero is false and nonzero is true. Equality testing with == instead produces a Boolean result without assigning either operand. Confusing the two can both change program state and choose an unintended branch. C++ working draft — Assignment and compound assignment operators

records.text: Problem-to-program workflow Inputs, outputs, legal ranges, edge cases Manual small-case solution Algorithm → pseudocode or flowchart Implement → test → maintain Largest-of-three: best=first input Compare second, then third Zero initialization fails all-negative inputs Programming responsibilities Writing, testing, debugging, maintaining Actual versus required result Execution alone insufficient

records.text: Algorithm properties Precise executable steps Termination for every legal input Definiteness: unambiguous meaning Effectiveness: performable steps Optional inputs, specified result Correctness against specification Efficiency: desirable, measurable Inefficient terminating algorithms still qualify Module's desirable-efficiency listing Programming paradigms Procedural: procedures organize operations Structured: sequence, selection, iteration Object oriented: state and behavior Functional: function evaluation Conditional: construct, not paradigm

records.text: Q00017 Question 1 CP03 In the conventional historical classification of programming-language generations, which generation is associated with declarative logic, constraints, AI and expert systems? Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details. A Fifth generation languages B Second generation languages C Fourth generation languages D Third generation languages A. Fifth generation languages The question uses the historical generation taxonomy, rather than asking which languages can implement AI. The note associates fifth-generation languages with logic, constraints and expert systems. Second generation refers to assembly, third to general high-level languages, and fourth to query languages and application generators. Those other languages can be used within AI applications, but that does not change their generation category. A correct Fifth generation is the historical logic/constraints and expert-system category. B incorrect Second generation denotes symbolic assembly. C incorrect Fourth generation denotes query languages and application generators. D incorrect Third generation includes general high-level languages such as C++ and Java.

records.title: Computer Programming — Question 5 · Q00051
records.text: Q00051 Question 5 CP04 In the conventional C++ build process, which program resolves external symbols and combines object files and libraries into an executable before it is loaded into memory? Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details. A Editor B Debugger C Linker D Loader C. Linker Combining object files and resolving their external references is the linker’s role in the conventional toolchain. This occurs after object-file generation and before the executable is loaded for execution. Loading has a separate responsibility: placing the executable and required components in memory and starting it. The question asks about the build operation, so an editor, debugger or loader does not satisfy it. A incorrect An editor changes source text. B incorrect A debugger investigates program execution and defects. C correct The linker combines objects/libraries and resolves external references. D incorrect The loader places an already linked executable into memory.

records.text: Q00071 Question 7 CP15 What words are printed, in order, when execution enters this C++ fragment at label a and ends after its final statement? Ignore padding spaces. a: cout<<"Graduating "; goto b; c: cout<<" Year "; goto a; b: cout<<"fourth "; Fix the input case and cost model, then count dominant work or simultaneously live storage. A GraduatingYear Fourth B Graduating fourth C YearFourth Graduating D GraduatingFourth Year B. Graduating fourth Execution starts at a and prints Graduating. The unconditional goto b then transfers directly to the final output statement. That jump skips label c and its Year output, as well as the jump back to a. records.text: Q00272 Question 24 CP05 Which of the following best describes the statement "C++ is a case sensitive programming language"? Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details. A All variables in C++ are identifiers B Every C++ statement should include the header file iostream.h C ExitExam and exitExam are distinct in C++ D Every statement in C++ ends with semicolon ExitExam and exitExam are distinct identifiers. Case sensitivity means changing uppercase to lowercase can change the identifier. ExitExam and exitExam therefore name different entities in C++. records.text: SM0009 Question 87 CP03 CP04 In the conventional native-execution model, which statement about programming-language generations is false? Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details. A Assembly language is machine independent B Machine language can be executed without translation C Assembly language should be translated to machine language before execution D Fifth-generation languages are historically associated with declarative logic, constraints and AI/expert systems. A. Assembly language is machine independent Assembly is symbolic source tied to an instruction set; it is not machine independent. Before native execution, an assembler translates it into machine instructions. Those machine instructions are already in the target machine’s instruction format. Fifth generation is instead a historical language category associated with declarative logic, constraints and expert systems, rather than a universal hardware-performance requirement. Only A contradicts the specified language and execution model. A correct Assembly depends on the target instruction set, so this claim is false. B incorrect Machine instructions do not require assembly-to-machine translation. C incorrect Symbolic assembly is translated before native execution. D incorrect This historical association is the fifth-generation description in the note.

A 81 B 256 C 12 D 64 D. 64 The accumulator r starts at one. With exponent e=3, the for loop executes for i=1, 2 and 3, multiplying by the base b=4 on each pass. Its successive values are 4, 16 and 64. The final insertion therefore prints 64 after the prompt. This is iterative exponentiation, rather than multiplying the base by the exponent or reversing their roles. A incorrect 81 is 3 raised to 4, reversing base and exponent. B incorrect 256 would require four multiplications by 4. C incorrect 12 multiplies base by exponent rather than computing the power. D correct Three multiplications by 4 starting at 1 give 64.

records.title: Computer Programming — Question 102 · SS167
records.text: SS167 Question 102 CP23 CP14 A program reads exactly 50 numbers and adds only positive values to a total. Which listed construct best expresses the known repetition count, while a separate if statement handles the positivity test? Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details. A for B break C jump D continue A. for The task has a counting responsibility and a filtering responsibility. A for loop naturally expresses the fixed total of 50 input attempts through its initialization, condition and update. The question assigns the positivity decision to a separate if, so it asks specifically about counting. continue can skip one contribution but cannot supply the repetition count; break would stop early, and jump is not a specific count-controlled construct. A correct for naturally expresses exactly 50 iterations. B incorrect break could stop processing before all 50 inputs. C incorrect Jump does not specify a count-controlled loop. D incorrect continue skips the rest of an iteration but does not establish 50 repetitions.

records.title: Computer Programming — Question 103 · SS173
records.text: SS173 Question 103 CP23 CP22 CP14 CP-S04 Which sequence of array values is printed by this Java code? Ignore each println call’s trailing space and line separator. class PrintResult { public static void main(String[] args){ int[] arr={3,4,5,6,7}; for(int i=0;i<arr.length-2;++i){ System.out.println(arr[i]+" "); } } } Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details. A 3 4 5 6 7 B 3 4 5 6 C 3 4 D 3 4 5 D. 3 4 5 The initializer contains five values, so arr.length-2 is 3. The loop starts at index zero and continues while i<3, visiting indices 0, 1 and 2. Those positions contain 3, 4 and 5. Each println also ends its line, but the question explicitly asks only for the value sequence. A incorrect The loop never reaches indices 3 and 4. B incorrect Four values would require the excluded index 3. C incorrect Index 2 also satisfies i<3, so a third value prints. D correct Indices 0,1,2 contain 3,4,5 in that order.

records.text: AM0247 Question 109 CP03 What is the main advantage of high-level programming languages? Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details. A They are easier to read and write than low-level languages. records.text: AM0250 Question 112 CP17 Which statement gives the defining relationship between a method and a function? records.title: Computer Programming — Question 121 · AM0259
records.text: AM0259 Question 121 CP32 What is the purpose of exception handling in programming? Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details. A To perform input/output operations B To optimize program performance C To handle and recover from runtime errors D To define variables and constants Handle exceptional runtime conditions and recover where appropriate. CP32 describes exceptions as transferring control to a matching handler for exceptional conditions. This supports handling and possible recovery from runtime errors. It does not promise that every runtime fault is recoverable: arbitrary undefined behavior is specifically excluded. Input/output, optimization and declarations are not exception handling’s defining purpose. A incorrect Input/output may raise exceptional conditions, but performing I/O is not the defining purpose of exception handling. B incorrect Exception handling routes exceptional control flow rather than being a mechanism for performance optimization. C correct Matching handlers support handling and possible recovery from runtime exceptions, subject to the note’s stated limits. D incorrect Variables and constants are introduced by declarations, not by exception-handling control flow.

records.title: Computer Programming — Question 122 · AM0260
records.text: AM0260 Question 122 CP33 Which statement accurately distinguishes static typing from dynamic typing? Consider type-checking time rather than mandatory annotations or programming paradigms. Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details. A Static typing is more efficient than dynamic typing. B Static typing checks types before execution, possibly using inferred types; dynamic typing checks operations using runtime values. C Static typing is used in object-oriented programming, while dynamic typing is used in procedural programming. D There is no difference; the terms are used interchangeably. B. Static typing checks types before execution, possibly using inferred types; dynamic typing checks operations using runtime values. Static typing checks types before execution, and the static type may be inferred rather than explicitly written. Dynamic typing checks operations using values at runtime. The difference is therefore about the typing/checking model, not a guarantee of execution speed or a choice between object-oriented and procedural programming. B states this distinction; static typing does not require explicitly written type declarations. A incorrect Typing discipline alone does not guarantee a universal efficiency ranking. B correct This correctly distinguishes before-execution checking from runtime checking and allows inference. C incorrect Object-oriented versus procedural organization does not determine typing discipline. D incorrect The two checking models have distinct meanings.

records.text: AM0281 Question 141 CP14 Which option describes the defining execution and test behavior of a C++ do-while loop? Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details. A To execute a block exactly once regardless of its condition. B To perform mathematical calculations. C To iterate over a collection of elements. D To execute the body before its first test and repeat while the continuation condition is true. D. To execute the body before its first test and repeat while the continuation condition is true. A do-while loop executes its body before the first condition test. It then repeats while its continuation condition is true and stops when that condition becomes false. Collection traversal and arithmetic can occur inside many constructs; neither describes this loop’s distinctive control rule. A incorrect A do-while loop can repeat, so it is not limited to exactly one execution. B incorrect Arithmetic is possible in the body but is not the defining control behavior. A 0 B 1 C 2 D 4 0 The remainder operation illustrated on p.8 gives 4%2=0 because 4=2*2+0. Module support: PDF p. 8. A correct Exact divisibility leaves zero remainder. records.title: Computer Programming — Question 164 · CS0086
records.text: CS0086 Question 164 CP08 What is the output of the following C++ fragment code? int x = 15, y = 2; int z = x / y; cout << z; Trace the initial state and each executed operation in order, preserving the requested output layout. A 7.5 B 7 C 3 D 12.5 7. x and y are int variables with values 15 and 2. Their division therefore produces integer 7 before assignment to z, as CP08 specifies truncation toward zero. z also has type int and cout prints 7. None of the fractional or unrelated numerical options follows from this expression. A incorrect 7.5 is the mathematical fractional quotient, but these int operands produce an integer quotient. B correct The integer quotient 15/2 truncates toward zero to 7, which z stores and cout prints. C incorrect Three is not the quotient obtained by dividing the stated values 15 and 2. D incorrect 12.5 is neither the integer quotient nor the fractional quotient of 15 divided by 2.

records.title: Computer Programming — Question 165 · CS0087
records.text: CS0087 Question 165 CP05 Writing comments in between our C++ program makes our program ________. Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details. A Portable B Maintainable C Reliable D Efficient Maintainable Page 5 says comments explain aspects of a program for human readers and are ignored by the compiler. records.title: Computer Programming — Question 166 · CS0088
records.text: CS0088 Question 166 CP16 CP22 What is the output of the following C++ fragment code? int data[10] = {5,10,15,20,25,30,35,40,45,50}; int i = 0; while (i <= 10) { if(data[i] % 10 == 0) { cout << data[i] << " "; i = i + 2; } } Trace the initial state and each executed operation in order, preserving the requested output layout. A 5 15 25 35 45 55 B 10 20 30 40 50 C 5 10 15 20 25 30 35 40 45 50 D No output No output Arrays are zero indexed (p.19), so initially data[0]=5. Its remainder on division by 10 is 5, not zero, so the if body is skipped. The only increment of i lies inside that skipped body. Therefore i stays zero, i<=10 remains true, and no cout is ever reached. The loop runs indefinitely with no output; it never reaches the potentially invalid index 10. Module support: PDF p. 19, PDF p. 11, PDF p. 8, PDF p. 9. A incorrect No print occurs at the first iteration or later, so this odd-value sequence cannot appear. B incorrect The loop never advances to data[1]=10. C incorrect No array traversal occurs because i never changes. D correct Correct: nothing is printed, and the loop does not terminate.

records.title: Computer Programming — Question 167 · CS0092
records.text: CS0092 Question 167 CP32 After a compiler reports a syntax error and before rebuilding, which action directly helps locate and repair its cause? Apply the naming, type and syntax rules before deciding whether an option can be used as stated. A Rewrite the entire program B Ignore the error and continue execution C Use a debugger tool D Check the code for typos or incorrect syntax D. Check the code for typos or incorrect syntax A syntax error violates the language grammar, so inspecting the relevant tokens and nearby declarations is the direct diagnostic step. The note recommends starting with the first useful compiler diagnostic, repairing the code and rebuilding afterward. Rewriting everything is unnecessary, ignoring the diagnostic leaves the defect in place, and a debugger is useful after a runnable program exists. The revised timing asks for inspection rather than the final verification step. A incorrect A complete rewrite is unnecessary for locating a local grammar mistake. B incorrect Ignoring a compiler error leaves the cause unresolved. C incorrect A debugger is useful after a runnable program exists. D correct Inspecting nearby tokens and declarations helps locate and correct grammar mistakes.

records.title: Computer Programming — Question 168 · NS0278
records.text: NS0278 Question 168 CP04 What is the difference between a compiler and an interpreter? Which is Java? Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details. Compilers translate representations; interpreters execute them. Java uses bytecode compilation and JVM interpretation/JIT. CP04 says javac produces bytecode, then a JVM interprets or compiles it at runtime. A compiler translates rather than necessarily producing a complete native executable, while an interpreter executes a program representation. Java therefore cannot be reduced to exclusively compiled or interpreted.

records.title: Computer Programming — Question 169 · NS0279
records.text: NS0279 Question 169 CP-S05 CP10 What is the difference between = (assignment) and == (comparison)? Why is this a common mistake? Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details. = assigns a value; == compares values for equality. CP06 describes assignment as replacing a variable’s value; CP10 describes equality as a value test. Confusing them can change state instead of testing it. In C++ a numeric assigned result can also convert to a condition, allowing an unintended assignment to alter control flow.

records.title: Computer Programming — Question 170 · NS0280
records.text: NS0280 Question 170 CP14 What is the difference between while and do-while loops? When would you use do-while? Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details. while tests first; do-while runs once before testing. Use do-while for a mandatory first menu/input attempt. CP14 allows a while body to execute zero times because its condition is checked first. A do-while body executes before its first check, making it suitable for a menu or input attempt that must happen at least once.

records.title: Computer Programming — Question 171 · NS0281
records.text: NS0281 Question 171 CP22 What happens if you try to access array index array[5] when the array has 5 elements (indices 0-4)? Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details. Index 5 is out of bounds: Java throws; C++ access has undefined behavior. Five elements occupy indices 0 through 4, so array[5] is outside the array. CP22 distinguishes Java’s bounds exception from C++ undefined behavior; an adjacent-memory value must not be guessed. The question does not specify a language, so both consequences are stated.

records.title: Computer Programming — Question 172 · NS0282
records.text: NS0282 Question 172 CP17 Why do we use functions? What are the benefits? Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details. Functions decompose named tasks, enable reuse, reduce duplication and simplify understanding/testing. CP17 defines a function as grouping a named task and explains that reuse reduces duplication while independent functions are easier to understand and test. Decomposition localizes responsibilities and supports maintenance through those clearer units.

records.title: Computer Programming — Question 173 · NS0283
records.text: NS0283 Question 173 CP18 What is the difference between pass-by-value and pass-by-reference? Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details. C++ value parameters copy; reference parameters alias caller variables. Java passes copied values, including references. CP18 makes a value parameter a separate initialized object, while int& aliases the caller variable and can change it directly. Passing a pointer copies an address and can change its target without rebinding the caller’s pointer. Java copies object references by value.

records.title: Computer Programming — Question 174 · NS0301
records.text: NS0301 Question 174 CP11 CP09 What does this C++ fragment print? Assume cout is available. int a=6,b=8; int x=2,y=4; int c(x>y ? (a--,x) : (b--,y)); cout<<"a="<<a; cout<<" b="<<b; cout<<" c="<<c; Trace the initial state and each executed operation in order, preserving the requested output layout. A a=6 b=5 c=4 B a=6 b=7 c=5 C a=8 b=6 c=5 D a=6 b=7 c=4 D. a=6 b=7 c=4 The condition x>y compares 2 with 4 and is false. Only the false branch is evaluated. Its comma expression first decrements b from 8 to 7 and then yields y, which is 4, for initializing c. The true branch does not execute, so a remains 6. With valid stream spelling, comma operators and ordinary string delimiters, the output is a=6 b=7 c=4. A incorrect b decreases once from 8 to 7, not to 5. B incorrect The comma expression yields y=4, not 5. C incorrect The false branch leaves a=6 and produces b=7,c=4. D correct Only b decrements; the branch yields y=4 and a remains 6.

records.title: Computer Programming — Question 175 · NS0325
records.text: NS0325 Question 175 CP03 Assume that you are computer science expert and you need to develop large programs within short period of time. Finally, you have planned to provide portable program to the concerned body. Which type of programming language is preferable for the above scenario? Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details. A Low level B Machine level C High level D Assembly A high-level language, with portability constraints checked. CP03 says high-level source is easier to read and often portable after recompilation if platform assumptions are avoided. That fits rapid development of a large program and a portable result better than instruction-set-dependent machine or assembly code. Portability remains conditional on the target environment; the answer is a preference, not an unconditional guarantee. A incorrect Low-level code retains instruction-set details and does not best match the stated readability/development and portability goals. B incorrect Machine-level code depends directly on the instruction set, opposing the requested portable-source preference. C correct High-level source offers the note’s readability and conditional portability advantages for the stated scenario. D incorrect Assembly depends on the instruction set and is not the preferred abstraction for these development goals.

records.title: Computer Programming — Question 177 · NS0358
records.text: NS0358 Question 177 CP19 Which of the following statement about function overloading is TRUE? Use the cited language rules to separate the purpose of each construct from its implementation details. A Overload function have same name but different parameters/type B Overload function is not supported C Overload function must have different return type D Overload function must have the same number of parameters Overloads share a name and differ in their parameter lists. CP19 requires a shared name with differences in parameter count or types/order. A states that relationship. Return type alone does not distinguish overloads, and neither different return types nor equal parameter counts are mandatory. Thus the other statements either deny supported overloading or impose restrictions contradicted here. A correct This states the shared-name and differing-parameter-list relationship required by CP19. B incorrect CP19 explicitly describes supported C++ function overloading, contradicting this blanket denial. C incorrect Different return types are not required and return type alone cannot distinguish overloads. D incorrect Parameter count may differ between overloads, so equal counts are not mandatory.
