For example, subtracting a sum excluding one person from a sum including that person can reveal their value even when their row is hidden. Ordinary access control grants or denies actions, integrity validates data and encryption protects encoded content. The specified indirect-disclosure threat identifies inference control specifically. A correct This directly prevents disclosure of individual facts inferred from allowed aggregates. B incorrect Authorization alone does not prevent inference from otherwise allowed answers. C incorrect Integrity constrains valid data rather than indirect disclosure. D incorrect Encryption does not stop an authorized user combining decrypted aggregate answers. E incorrect Inference control directly matches the threat.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 10 · Q00114
records.text: Q00114 Question 10 ADB18 ADB19 Which approach rewrites a query's internal representation using relational-algebra equivalences, without relying on integrity-constraint deductions or comparison of estimated plan costs? Consider which equivalent transformation changes intermediate work and what assumptions preserve meaning. A Systematic plan-cost estimation B Semantic query optimization C Cost Estimation D Heuristic rules E Both A and C Heuristic rules Heuristic rules rewrite algebraic representations using equivalences, such as applying suitable selections early or replacing a product followed by a join condition with a join. Semantic optimization additionally reasons from trusted constraints. Cost estimation predicts resources for candidate plans, and doing that systematically remains a costing activity. The stem isolates equivalence-based rewriting without those other bases, so D is correct and combining the two cost-estimation descriptions does not change the answer. A incorrect Incorrect: systematic cost estimation predicts plan costs rather than performing the specified equivalence-based rewriting. B incorrect Incorrect: semantic optimization additionally uses trusted constraints, which the stem excludes. C incorrect Incorrect: cost estimation compares resource predictions for candidate plans. D correct Correct: heuristic rules apply the stated relational-algebra equivalences. E incorrect Incorrect: A and C both describe costing, not the isolated algebraic-rewrite approach.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 11 · Q00115
records.text: Q00115 Question 11 ADB16 Which of the following is not true about locks? Consider conflicts, private work and validation costs, or lock-management overhead. A Locks with large granularity are easier for the DBMS to administer. B Locks with small granularity cause more conflicts. C Locks with large granularity produce fewer details for the DBMS to track. D Locks may have a table-level granularity. E Locks may have a database-level granularity. Locks with small granularity cause more conflicts. Fine granularity raises concurrency, whereas coarse granularity locks more data with fewer lock entries. Thus the claim that smaller units cause more conflicts reverses the tradeoff. A incorrect A single coarse lock can replace many fine locks and reduce management work. (PDF pp. 83, 95.) B correct Fine units allow more independent access, so this is the false claim. (PDF pp. 83, 95.) C incorrect Coarse locks reduce the number of entries tracked. (PDF pp. 83, 95.) D incorrect The file/relation granularity in the hierarchy permits table-level locking. (PDF pp. 83, 95.) E incorrect Entire-database locking is expressly listed. (PDF pp. 83, 95.)

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 12 · Q00116
records.text: Q00116 Question 12 ADB09 ADB10 For every transaction T participating in the schedule, if all the operations of T are executed consecutively in the schedule. The schedule is Distinguish transaction ordering, conflict conditions and full execution equivalence. A Cascaded schedule B Serial schedule C Cascadeless schedule D Recoverable schedule E None Serial schedule Consecutive execution of every transaction's operations is the definition of a serial schedule. Recoverability and cascadelessness instead constrain dependencies on commits. A incorrect Cascading concerns dependent rollbacks, not contiguous execution. (PDF pp. 72, 71.) B correct Serial exactly matches the consecutive-operations definition. (PDF pp. 72, 71.) C incorrect Cascadeless means reading only committed writes. (PDF pp. 72, 71.) D incorrect Recoverable constrains commit order after a read dependency. (PDF pp. 72, 71.) E incorrect A listed definition does match, so None is wrong. (PDF pp. 72, 71.)

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 13 · Q00117
records.text: Q00117 Question 13 ADB06 A transaction property state about changes applied to the database by a committed transaction must persist in the database? Track the transaction's guarantee or lifecycle boundary described by the scenario. A Isolation B Durability or permanency C Atomicity D Consistency preservation E None Durability or permanency Persisting committed modifications despite subsequent failure is durability or permanency. A incorrect Isolation regulates visibility between transactions. (PDF pp. 66.) B correct Durability protects committed changes against loss. (PDF pp. 66.) C incorrect Atomicity is all-or-nothing execution. (PDF pp. 66.) D incorrect Consistency preserves valid states rather than persistence. (PDF pp. 66.) E incorrect Durability is a listed matching property. (PDF pp. 66.)

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 14 · Q00118
records.text: Q00118 Question 14 ADB29 ADB27 Which update-timing policy keeps a transaction's uncommitted changes outside the persistent database until commit? Separate update timing from update location and follow the commit boundary. A Undo B In-place modification C Immediate-modification D Deferred-modification Deferred-modification Deferred modification keeps uncommitted updates outside the persistent database. If the transaction fails before commit, those database pages do not require undo for its changes; redo can still be needed after commit in a no-force system. Immediate modification permits precommit persistent changes. In-place modification describes overwriting the original location without specifying the commit timing, while undo is an action that reverses applied effects. D therefore names the requested timing policy. A incorrect Incorrect: undo reverses effects already applied rather than naming a policy postponing them. B incorrect Incorrect: in-place modification specifies overwriting location, not postponement until commit. C incorrect Incorrect: immediate modification permits persistent changes before commit. D correct Correct: deferred modification keeps uncommitted changes outside the persistent database.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 15 · Q00119
records.text: Q00119 Question 15 ADB01 ADB02 ADB03 Which one of the following is false? Distinguish an object instance from its class, attribute values and persistent identity. A In object-oriented database, data are stored as collections of rows and tables B In relational database, data are perceived by users as tables C Object oriented database allows object identification and communication D Object oriented database allows reusability of objects E None of the above The rows-and-tables claim is false for the object-oriented model. An OODBMS primarily models persistent objects with identity, state and behavior, rather than relational rows and tables. Objects communicate through methods and object references, and inheritance supports reuse. Relational presentation as tables is the contrasting model. Therefore A is the false statement. A correct This is false: an OODBMS primarily models persistent objects rather than relational rows and tables. B incorrect Presenting relations as tables describes the relational contrast correctly. C incorrect Object identity and method-based collaboration are supported object-model concepts. D incorrect Inheritance and reusable object behavior support reuse, so this is not the false statement. E incorrect A is false, so none of the above cannot answer this negative question.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 16 · Q00296
records.text: Q00296 Question 16 ADB33 ADB36 ADB37 27.----------is a collection of multiple logically related database distributed over a computer network. Separate coordinated network placement from engine compatibility and semantic integration. A Data Fragmentation B Distributed Database C Data Allocation D Data Replication Distributed Database A distributed database is a coordinated collection of logically related data across networked sites. Fragmentation divides a relation into row or column subsets; replication creates copies; allocation chooses the sites storing fragments or copies. These are design decisions within a distributed database rather than alternative names for the whole collection. Distribution does not require every fragment to be replicated, and the question's definition identifies the database as a whole. A incorrect Incorrect: fragmentation splits relations into subsets rather than naming the entire networked collection. B correct Correct: a distributed database is the coordinated logically related data collection across networked sites. C incorrect Incorrect: allocation assigns fragments or copies to sites; it is a placement decision. D incorrect Incorrect: replication creates copies and is a design choice rather than the definition of the collection.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 17 · Q00297
records.text: Q00297 Question 17 ADB06 ............... Means that a transaction must execute exactly once completely or not at all. Track the transaction's guarantee or lifecycle boundary described by the scenario. A Consistency B Durability C Isolation D Atomicity Atomicity Atomicity means a transaction is performed in its entirety or not performed at all. 'Exactly once' is interpreted here as all-or-nothing completion, rather than exactly-once delivery semantics. A incorrect Consistency concerns valid before/after states. (PDF pp. 66.) B incorrect Durability concerns survival after commit. (PDF pp. 66.) C incorrect Isolation concerns interaction with other transactions. (PDF pp. 66.) D correct Atomicity supplies the all-or-nothing rule. (PDF pp. 66.)

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 18 · Q00300
records.text: Q00300 Question 18 ADB30 Checkpoints are a part of Identify which history a recovery boundary can safely exclude and whether active work spans it. A Recovery measures B Concurrency measures C Authorization measures D Security measures Recovery measures A checkpoint synchronizes database and log so recovery need not search the entire history. Its purpose is recovery work reduction. A correct Checkpointing is described in database recovery. (PDF pp. 105, 107.) B incorrect Locking and scheduling are concurrency controls; this checkpoint has a recovery role. (PDF pp. 105, 107.) C incorrect Privileges authorize access rather than synchronize recovery state. (PDF pp. 105, 107.) D incorrect Checkpointing does not authenticate users or grant privileges. (PDF pp. 105, 107.)

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 19 · Q00304
records.text: Q00304 Question 19 ADB39 ADB29 ADB31 Which of the following is not a recovery technique? Distinguish coordinated transaction outcome from concurrent access and local storage. A ARIES Algorithm B Two-phase commit C Immediate update D Deferred update Two-phase commit Deferred update, immediate update, and ARIES are recovery approaches. Two-phase commit coordinates the distributed commit decision; it is the intended exception among the named recovery algorithms, though commit protocols also support distributed recovery. A incorrect ARIES is explicitly a recovery algorithm. (PDF pp. 107, 109, 123.) B correct Two-phase commit is a distributed commit approach, not the listed update-recovery algorithm. (PDF pp. 107, 109, 123.) C incorrect Immediate update appears under recovery techniques. (PDF pp. 107, 109, 123.) D incorrect Deferred update is a recovery scheme. (PDF pp. 107, 109, 123.)

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 20 · Q00305
records.text: Q00305 Question 20 ADB01 Which of the following is not true about OODBMS (object-oriented database management system). Distinguish an object instance from its class, attribute values and persistent identity. A The key concepts is objects B The object is persistent C The key concept is relation D Object Identity is unchangeable Relation is not the defining concept of an OODBMS. The defining unit of an object database is an object with identity, state and behavior. ADB01 explains both persistence beyond program execution and identifier stability throughout an object lifetime. Relation is instead the characteristic abstraction of the relational model. Thus C is the one statement that fails to describe an OODBMS. A incorrect Objects are the defining units of the object-oriented database model. B incorrect An OODBMS provides persistence so objects survive the program execution that created them. C correct This is false for OODBMS: relation is the central abstraction of the relational model. D incorrect The object identifier remains stable throughout the lifetime of its object.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 21 · Q00306
records.text: Q00306 Question 21 ADB18 ADB19 Which optimization approach uses algebraic rules, such as pushing suitable selections before joins, to choose an operation order without exhaustively enumerating plans or comparing estimated costs? Consider which equivalent transformation changes intermediate work and what assumptions preserve meaning. A Semantic query optimization based on trusted constraints B Heuristic- based C Cost estimation D Exhaustive search Heuristic- based Heuristic optimization orders or rewrites operations using algebraic rules intended to reduce intermediate work. Applying suitable selections early is a typical example. Semantic optimization additionally uses trusted constraints, cost estimation predicts resource usage for candidate strategies, and exhaustive search enumerates alternatives rather than selecting a small set through rules alone. Although practical optimizers can combine these methods, the stated stem asks specifically for rule-based algebraic ordering, making B unique. A incorrect Incorrect: this alternative bases deductions on trusted constraints rather than the isolated algebraic ordering rules. B correct Correct: heuristic optimization orders operations through algebraic rules such as early selection. C incorrect Incorrect: cost estimation predicts candidate-plan resources instead of the specified rule-only choice. D incorrect Incorrect: exhaustive search enumerates alternatives, which the stem explicitly excludes.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 22 · Q00533
records.text: Q00533 Question 22 ADB06 A transaction in which either all of the database actions occur or none of them does is called Track the transaction's guarantee or lifecycle boundary described by the scenario. A Atomicity B Consistency C Isolation D Durability Atomicity All database actions occurring or none occurring is atomicity, the first ACID property. A correct Atomicity is the entire-or-none requirement. (PDF pp. 66.) B incorrect Consistency is preservation of valid states. (PDF pp. 66.) C incorrect Isolation separates concurrent effects. (PDF pp. 66.) D incorrect Durability preserves completed commits. (PDF pp. 66.)

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 23 · Q00540
records.text: Q00540 Question 23 ADB29 ADB27 A transaction is still active when one of its changes is written into the persistent database. Which update-timing policy permits this? Separate update timing from update location and follow the commit boundary. A Deferred-Update B In-place update C Immediate-Update D Undo Immediate-Update Immediate update permits persistent database changes while the transaction is still active, before commit. An abort may therefore require undo. Deferred update keeps uncommitted changes outside the persistent database. In-place update describes overwriting a location rather than the commit-timing policy, and undo is the reversal of applied effects. The question concerns which timing policy permits the observed precommit write, not whether all immediate-update systems must flush every cache change immediately. A incorrect Incorrect: deferred update excludes uncommitted changes from the persistent database. B incorrect Incorrect: in-place update describes overwriting the existing location rather than the commit-timing policy. C correct Correct: immediate update permits persistent changes before commit. D incorrect Incorrect: undo reverses effects; it is not the update-timing policy.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 24 · Q00556
records.text: Q00556 Question 24 ADB13 ADB12 ADB30 Which of the following occurs when a transaction cannot proceed for an indefinite period while other transactions in the system continue normally? Distinguish a waiting cycle, a long wait and indefinite unfair postponement. A Starvation B Deadlock C checkpoint D lock point Starvation Starvation means indefinite postponement of a transaction while other transactions continue. It can result from repeated waiting or repeated victim selection without any waiting cycle. Deadlock instead involves a cycle of mutually blocked transactions. A checkpoint records recovery state, and the lock point in two-phase locking is the instant a transaction acquires its final lock. Neither is the name of indefinite unfair postponement, so A remains the unique answer. A correct Correct: indefinite postponement while others proceed is starvation. B incorrect Incorrect: deadlock requires a waiting cycle, which is not required for starvation. C incorrect Incorrect: a checkpoint records durable recovery state; it is not an indefinite waiting condition. D incorrect Incorrect: the lock point is the instant the transaction acquires its final lock in 2PL.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 25 · Q00565
records.text: Q00565 Question 25 ADB04 The atom constructor can represent the following basic atomic values except. Classify the shape of a value separately from an operation that creates an instance. A Integers B Real Numbers C Strings D Array Array is not an atom constructor. ADB04 lists integer, real, Boolean and string as examples of basic atomic values. An array instead supplies indexed positions and is a collection constructor, even when a programming variable holds it as one value. Consequently integers, reals and strings fit the atom category while an array is the requested exception. A incorrect An integer is explicitly listed as a basic atomic value. B incorrect A real number is explicitly included among atomic values. C incorrect A string is a basic atomic value under the object-model convention used here. D correct An array contains indexed positions and is a collection constructor rather than an atomic one.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 26 · Q00584
records.text: Q00584 Question 26 ADB31 ADB27 A system crashes again during ARIES recovery. Durable WAL, pageLSNs and compensation log records survive; storage is intact. No checkpoints were taken. Which statement correctly describes the second restart? Trace durable recovery metadata and what progress survives a second crash. A The same undo and redo list will be used while recovering again B The database will become inconsistent C Durable compensation records and pageLSNs preserve recovery progress, so already-installed actions can be skipped or safely redone as required. D The system cannot any further C. Durable compensation records and pageLSNs preserve recovery progress, so already-installed actions can be skipped or safely redone as required. ARIES records recovery progress in durable metadata. PageLSNs help determine whether a redo action is already installed, and compensation records preserve undo progress and its continuation. A second restart can therefore recover safely without assuming that the same undo and redo work lists recur. Lack of checkpoints may increase scanning work, but it does not erase this progress or make further recovery impossible. A incorrect Durable progress can change the required work, so identical lists are not guaranteed. B incorrect Restartable recovery does not make inconsistency inevitable. C correct PageLSNs and durable CLRs support safe continuation after repeated crashes. D incorrect ARIES can restart using surviving durable recovery metadata.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 27 · Q00590
records.text: Q00590 Question 27 ADB12 The rigorous two-phase locking protocol permits releasing all locks at the__________ Track the first lock release and the transaction-completion boundary. A Beginning of the transaction B During the execution of transaction C End of transaction D Never in the life-time of transaction At transaction end, on commit or abort. Rigorous 2PL retains both shared and exclusive locks until commit or abort, unlike basic 2PL, which permits release in its shrinking phase. FDB-style early release would allow interference before completion and would not meet rigorous locking. The locks are eventually released at the transaction boundary, so never is also false. A incorrect Releasing locks at the beginning would not protect the transaction's later accesses. B incorrect Rigorous 2PL does not permit early release during ongoing transaction execution. C correct Both shared and exclusive locks remain held until commit or abort ends the transaction. D incorrect Locks are released at completion; the protocol does not hold them forever.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 28 · Q00594
records.text: Q00594 Question 28 ADB06 In which of the following state of the transaction executes all its operations successfully and all the effects are now permanently saved on the database system? Track the transaction's guarantee or lifecycle boundary described by the scenario. A Active B Partial committed C Committed D Failed Committed The committed state guarantees persistent changes. Partially committed only signals the end of read/write operations and does not yet ensure permanence. A incorrect Active means execution is in progress. (PDF pp. 65.) B incorrect Partially committed explicitly does not guarantee permanent modification. (PDF pp. 65.) C correct Committed ensures persistent changes. (PDF pp. 65.) D incorrect Failed is an aborted or unsuccessful transaction. (PDF pp. 65.)

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 29 · Q00598
records.text: Q00598 Question 29 ADB11 Let transaction T1 has obtained a shared mode lock S on data item Y and transaction T2 has obtained an exclusive lock X on data item Z , according to the above statement which one is correct? Compare access permissions and same-item compatibility before granting a lock request. A T1 can read Y but cannot write Y B T2 can read Z but cannot write Z C T1 can read Z but cannot write Z D T2 can read and write item Y T1 can read Y but cannot write Y Shared locks permit reads but not updates. Exclusive locks permit both reading and updating while excluding other transactions' locks on that item. A correct T1's shared lock authorizes reading Y, not writing it. (PDF pp. 82, 83.) B incorrect T2's exclusive lock permits both read and update of Z. (PDF pp. 82, 83.) C incorrect T1 cannot read Z while another transaction holds its exclusive lock. (PDF pp. 82, 83.) D incorrect T2 cannot obtain an exclusive write lock on Y while T1 holds its shared lock. (PDF pp. 82, 83.)

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 30 · Q00615
records.text: Q00615 Question 30 ADB14 ADB13 Which claim about deadlock prevention and starvation is false? Identify requester and holder ages before applying the protocol's action. A In conservative 2PL, starvation may occur B Wound–wait guarantees starvation freedom regardless of restart priorities or scheduling fairness C Deadlock can be prevented by wait-die D Some deadlock-prevention methods may cause starvation Wound–wait guarantees starvation freedom regardless of restart priorities or scheduling fairness Deadlock freedom does not itself guarantee that each transaction eventually completes. Wound–wait uses transaction age to decide whether a requester waits or aborts a younger holder, but a starvation-freedom argument also needs appropriate restart priorities, fair scheduling and holders that eventually finish. Its unconditional guarantee in B is therefore false. Conservative 2PL can postpone a transaction indefinitely under unfair admission, and wait–die prevents waiting cycles. Some prevention policies can cause repeated waiting or victimization. A incorrect True: conservative 2PL prevents cycles but does not by itself guarantee fair admission. B correct Correct selection: the unconditional starvation-freedom claim omits necessary progress and priority assumptions. C incorrect True: wait–die is a timestamp-based deadlock-prevention policy. D incorrect True: preventing deadlock can still leave a transaction repeatedly postponed or aborted.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 31 · Q00616
records.text: Q00616 Question 31 ADB08 ADB09 ADB06 Concurrency control in DBMS is important for which of the following reasons? Trace which transaction wrote each value and whether an overwrite or mixed-version read occurs. A To ensure data integrity when updates occur to the database in a single user environment B To ensure data integrity when reads occur to the database in a single user environment C To ensure data integrity when updates occur to the database in a multi user environment D To ensure data integrity when reads occur to the database in a multi user environment To ensure data integrity when updates occur to the database in a multi user environment Concurrency control preserves consistency when multiple users' updates interleave and conflict. Read-only sharing alone does not cause lost updates; the intended scenario is a multiuser system with updates. A incorrect Single-user updates lack concurrent intertransaction conflicts. (PDF pp. 68, 70, 79.) B incorrect Single-user reads do not create the cited conflicts. (PDF pp. 68, 70, 79.) C correct Multiuser updates can create read/write and write/write conflicts requiring scheduling. (PDF pp. 68, 70, 79.) D incorrect Reads can be involved when others update, but reads alone do not capture the source's motivating condition. (PDF pp. 68, 70, 79.)

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 32 · Q00624
records.text: Q00624 Question 32 ADB13 A lock wait-for graph may contain several independent deadlock cycles. Which termination methods guarantee eliminating all deadlock cycles? Assume each aborted transaction is undone and releases its locks. Select all that apply. 'Half' and 'single' mean arbitrary selections without a repeated cycle check. Distinguish a waiting cycle, a long wait and indefinite unfair postponement. A Abort all deadlocked transaction B Abort half of the deadlocked transaction C Aborting single deadlocked transactio D Aborting one transaction at a time until the deadlock cycle is eliminated A. Abort all deadlocked transaction; D. Aborting one transaction at a time until the deadlock cycle is eliminated Aborting all deadlocked transactions removes every participating wait, although it wastes work. A more selective complete method aborts a suitable victim, releases its locks and repeats until no cycles remain. An arbitrary half of the participants can leave a cycle intact, and one arbitrary victim may resolve only one of several independent cycles. The guarantee therefore applies to A and D. A correct Removing all deadlocked participants eliminates all their cycles. B incorrect An arbitrary half may miss an entire remaining cycle. C incorrect One victim need not break other independent cycles. D correct Repeated victim selection and graph checking continues until every cycle is gone.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 33 · Q00643
records.text: Q00643 Question 33 ADB06 Among the components of the DBMS, which one is responsible for keeping the isolation of transactions? Track the transaction's guarantee or lifecycle boundary described by the scenario. A Recovery protocol B Application programmer C Concurrency -control protocol D Database administrator Concurrency -control protocol Concurrency control regulates interactions between simultaneous transactions and enforces isolation. Recovery supports atomicity and durability by undoing incomplete effects and preserving committed work. Application programmers must supply correct transaction logic, and the DBA administers the database rather than serving as the executing concurrency-control mechanism. The question asks for that mechanism's primary responsibility, so C is the precise answer even though administration, applications and recovery all contribute to a working database. A incorrect Incorrect: recovery primarily supports atomicity and durability, rather than scheduling concurrent interactions for isolation. B incorrect Incorrect: an application programmer supplies transaction logic but is not the executing isolation-control mechanism. C correct Correct: concurrency control regulates conflicting concurrent operations to enforce isolation. D incorrect Incorrect: the DBA is an administrative human role, not the DBMS mechanism scheduling transaction interactions.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 34 · Q00645
records.text: Q00645 Question 34 ADB08 _________Occurs when two transactions update the same data item, but both read the same original value before update Trace which transaction wrote each value and whether an overwrite or mixed-version read occurs. A Dirty read B Lost update C Incorrect summary D Unrepeatable read Lost update Both transactions reading the original value lets a later write overwrite the earlier transaction's update; that update is lost. A incorrect Dirty read concerns uncommitted values from another transaction. (PDF pp. 68, 70.) B correct Lost update matches the stale-original-value overwrite. (PDF pp. 68, 70.) C incorrect Incorrect summary combines differently timed values in an aggregate. (PDF pp. 68, 70.) D incorrect Unrepeatable read concerns a later reread seeing a changed value. (PDF pp. 68, 70.)

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 35 · Q00659
records.text: Q00659 Question 35 ADB06 ADB09 ADB07 Which of the DBMS component ensures that the concurrent execution of multiple operations on the database results into consistent database state? Track the transaction's guarantee or lifecycle boundary described by the scenario. A Log B Buffer manager C File manager D Transaction processing system Transaction processing system The transaction processing system contains the scheduler and recovery managers. Its scheduling ensures concurrent individual actions have a net effect equivalent to one-at-a-time execution. A incorrect The log records changes but does not itself schedule consistent execution. (PDF pp. 79, 99.) B incorrect Buffers hold blocks and arrange writes, not the entire consistency protocol. (PDF pp. 79, 99.) C incorrect File management is not the scheduler responsible for concurrent effects. (PDF pp. 79, 99.) D correct Transaction processing contains the concurrency-control component implementing this guarantee. (PDF pp. 79, 99.)

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 36 · Q00687
records.text: Q00687 Question 36 ADB25 How do you prevent system privileges deletion and updating authority on PRICE and YEAR column of the CATALOGUE table from user Mohammed Track whether a privilege is being added or withdrawn and whether it applies to rows or columns. A GRANT DELETE, UPDATE (price,year) ON catalogue From Mohammed B ALLOW DELETE, UPDATE (price,year) ON catalogue From Mohammed C REVOKE DELETE, UPDATE (price,year) ON catalogue From Mohammed D DENY DELETE, UPDATE (price,year) ON catalogue From Mohammed REVOKE DELETE, UPDATE (price,year) ON catalogue From Mohammed To withdraw Mohammed's DELETE and column-specific UPDATE privileges, use REVOKE DELETE, UPDATE(price,year) ON catalogue FROM Mohammed. This concerns object privileges, despite the stem's 'system privileges' wording. Other independent grants may remain. A incorrect GRANT adds privileges and also uses TO, not FROM. (PDF pp. 54, 55.) B incorrect ALLOW is not the module's SQL privilege command. (PDF pp. 54, 55.) C correct REVOKE with ON and FROM matches the module syntax. (PDF pp. 54, 55.) D incorrect DENY is not the revocation command presented in this module. (PDF pp. 54, 55.)

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 37 · Q00890
records.text: Q00890 Question 37 ADB34 ADB06 Inclient-server database architecture, what is the primary role of the server? Identify which tier submits, mediates or executes a request. A Provide the GUI for end users B Initiate all network connections and poll clients for updates C Store and manage shared data, enforce ACID properties, and process client requests D Cache all user sessions locally for offline access Store and manage shared data, enforce ACID properties, and process client requests The database server provides database functionality and manages local data, while clients submit requests and combine results. DBMS components enforce transaction properties. A incorrect The client-facing GUI is not the server's primary data-management role. (PDF pp. 125, 126, 66.) B incorrect Clients initiate requests; polling clients is not the described workflow. (PDF pp. 125, 126, 66.) C correct Managing data and processing client requests matches server responsibilities. (PDF pp. 125, 126, 66.) D incorrect Offline local session caching is not the described database server function. (PDF pp. 125, 126, 66.)

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 38 · Q00892
records.text: Q00892 Question 38 ADB12 ADB16 In two-phase locking (2PL), during which phase may a transaction acquire locks but not release any? Track the first lock release and the transaction-completion boundary. A Growing phase B Commit phase C . Validation phase D Shrinking phase Growing phase The growing phase acquires locks without releasing any. Shrinking starts with release and prohibits new acquisitions. A correct Growing has the acquisition-without-release rule. (PDF pp. 86.) B incorrect Commit is not the phase name in basic 2PL. (PDF pp. 86.) C incorrect Validation belongs to optimistic concurrency control. (PDF pp. 86.) D incorrect Shrinking permits release, not acquisition. (PDF pp. 86.)

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 39 · Q00915
records.text: Q00915 Question 39 ADB30 ADB29 ADB12 Assume durable logs and serializable concurrency control, but no checkpoints or other valid log-truncation boundary. In a high-transaction system using deferred update, which recovery cost can grow after long uptime? Identify which history a recovery boundary can safely exclude and whether active work spans it. A Recovery may require scanning a very long accumulated log B Increased disk I/O due to frequent page copying C Shared locks cannot be used D View serializability cannot be ensured Recovery may require scanning a very long accumulated log Checkpoints record recovery state so recovery need not inspect the entire accumulated history. Without a checkpoint or another valid truncation boundary, the log that must be searched can grow throughout a long-running workload. Deferred update does not remove that problem. It specifies when persistent changes occur, not a requirement to copy shadow pages or a prohibition on shared locks. Serializability is enforced by the assumed concurrency-control mechanism, rather than by the existence of checkpoints. A correct Correct: without a recovery boundary, a long-running system may need to inspect a very large accumulated log. B incorrect Incorrect: deferred update describes timing and does not require frequent shadow-page copying. C incorrect Incorrect: deferring persistent writes does not prohibit shared-lock concurrency control. D incorrect Incorrect: serializability is enforced by the assumed concurrency control; a checkpoint limits recovery work rather than determining schedule equivalence.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 40 · Q00933
records.text: Q00933 Question 40 ADB29 ADB31 Which listed techniques use transaction logs for recovery in the course model? Interpret deferred modification as the conventional logged, no-force deferred-update method. Select all that apply. Separate update timing from update location and follow the commit boundary. A Recovery in Multi-database Systems B ARIES Recovery Algorithm C Shadow Paging Technique D Deferred Database Modification B. ARIES Recovery Algorithm; D. Deferred Database Modification ARIES uses write-ahead logging and log-driven recovery metadata. Conventional logged deferred modification also uses recorded updates to redo committed effects that have not reached persistent pages. Both are log-based techniques under the stated model. Shadow paging instead preserves committed page mappings and installs a new map at commit. Recovery in multidatabase systems names an environment rather than one particular algorithm. A incorrect Multidatabase recovery names an environment rather than identifying a particular log-based technique. B correct ARIES explicitly relies on WAL and logged recovery metadata. C incorrect Shadow paging preserves page maps as an alternative to conventional log-based recovery. D correct Deferred modification can use a log to redo committed changes without undo.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 41 · Q00969
records.text: Q00969 Question 41 ADB36 ADB35 ADB37 Which type of fragmentation in a distributed database divides a relation into subrelations defined by subsets of its columns, normally repeating a key to support reconstruction? Identify whether rows or columns are split and reverse the split to reconstruct the original relation. A Replication B Location C Horizontal D Vertical Vertical Vertical fragmentation projects column subsets into separate fragments. Repeating an appropriate key or row identifier allows a join to reconstruct the original rows without spurious combinations. Horizontal fragmentation instead selects subsets of rows, reconstructed by union. Replication creates copies rather than dividing the relation by attributes. Location transparency hides where data resides; it does not name the column-splitting design operation. The corrected category therefore supports the existing vertical-fragmentation answer. A incorrect Replication creates copies of data rather than splitting a relation into column subsets. B incorrect Location transparency hides placement details; it is not a fragmentation method. C incorrect Horizontal fragmentation partitions rows, not columns. D correct Correct: vertical fragmentation splits columns and normally repeats a reconstruction key.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 42 · Q00993
records.text: Q00993 Question 42 ADB12 In two-phase locking, which phase permits releasing existing locks but forbids acquiring new locks? Track the first lock release and the transaction-completion boundary. A Expanding phase B Waiting phase C Shrinking phase D All of the above Shrinking phase Two-phase locking divides lock use into a growing phase and a shrinking phase. During growing, a transaction may acquire or upgrade locks; once it releases a lock, it enters shrinking and cannot acquire any new lock. Waiting describes delay on a conflicting request, not a separate 2PL phase defined by releasing locks. Because the growing phase allows acquisition instead of release, the all-of-the-above alternative also fails. A incorrect Incorrect: the growing/expanding phase acquires locks and does not release them. B incorrect Incorrect: waiting on a conflicting request is a delay condition, not the formal 2PL release phase. C correct Correct: shrinking permits release while forbidding new acquisitions. D incorrect Incorrect: the growing phase does not meet the release/no-new-lock rule.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 43 · Q01002
records.text: Q01002 Question 43 ADB25 Which one of the SQL keywords is used to provide access? Track whether a privilege is being added or withdrawn and whether it applies to rows or columns. A REVOKE B DISTINCT C GRANT D None of the above GRANT GRANT gives specified users privileges on an object. REVOKE removes privileges. A incorrect REVOKE withdraws access privileges. (PDF pp. 54, 55.) B incorrect DISTINCT is not the module's access-authorization command. (PDF pp. 54, 55.) C correct GRANT supplies the privileges on tables or views. (PDF pp. 54, 55.) D incorrect GRANT is listed, so None is false. (PDF pp. 54, 55.)

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 44 · Q01156
records.text: Q01156 Question 44 ADB17 ADB-S01 is a tree data structure that corresponds to a relational algebra expression. Separate query representation, strategy selection and execution. A a | Query graph x B i? Query tree WA C '@| Query optimizer x D | None of the above x i? Query tree WA A query tree corresponds to a relational algebra expression, with relations as leaves and operations as internal nodes. A incorrect Query graph corresponds to relational calculus. (PDF pp. 34.) B correct Query tree is the exact defined algebraic tree. (PDF pp. 34.) C incorrect The optimizer chooses an execution strategy; it is not this data structure. (PDF pp. 34.) D incorrect The matching tree is explicitly listed. (PDF pp. 34.)

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 45 · Q01184
records.text: Q01184 Question 45 ADB28 ADB31 ADB29 Which listed approaches use both undo and redo? Interpret Immediate Update as the conventional steal/no-force logged model and Deferred Update as no-steal/no-force; use the course's ARIES definition. Select all that apply. Determine whether uncommitted changes or unflushed committed changes may exist on persistent pages. A Immediate Update B Deferred Update C ARIES Algorithm D None A. Immediate Update; C. ARIES Algorithm Steal allows uncommitted changes to reach persistent pages, creating a possible need for undo. No-force allows committed changes to remain buffered, creating a possible need for redo. Immediate update under the specified combined policy therefore needs both. ARIES also performs redo and then undoes losers. The specified deferred no-steal/no-force model needs redo but no undo, so it does not qualify. A correct The stated steal/no-force policy requires undo and redo. B incorrect The specified deferred policy prevents persistent uncommitted effects and needs redo only. C correct ARIES repeats history with redo and reverses losers with undo. D incorrect Two listed approaches use both actions.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 46 · Q01209
records.text: Q01209 Question 46 ADB29 ADB26 Which recovery mechanism preserves the committed page map while writing modified pages elsewhere, then atomically installs a new map at commit as an alternative to conventional log-based recovery? Separate update timing from update location and follow the commit boundary. A Disk recovery B Shadow paging C Deferred update D Crash recovery Shadow paging Shadow paging preserves the committed page map and writes modified pages to separate locations. Once the required pages are durable, commit atomically installs the new map; before that point, recovery can use the old committed map. Deferred update instead describes postponing persistent database changes until commit and does not itself specify this page-map mechanism. Disk recovery and crash recovery name recovery domains or events, not the particular algorithm requested. A incorrect Incorrect: disk recovery describes a recovery domain, not the specified preserved-page-map mechanism. B correct Correct: shadow paging preserves the committed map and installs the new map atomically at commit. C incorrect Incorrect: deferred update specifies commit timing, not this copy-on-write page-map algorithm. D incorrect Incorrect: crash recovery describes recovery after an event rather than the particular page-map mechanism.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 47 · Q01225
records.text: Q01225 Question 47 ADB06 ADB27 Which specific DBMS component directly handles undo of incomplete persistent changes after failure to support transaction atomicity? Choose the specialized component rather than its broader parent subsystem. Track the transaction's guarantee or lifecycle boundary described by the scenario. A Transaction management component of DBMS B Application Programmer C Concurrency control component of DBMS D Recovery management component of DBMS D. Recovery management component of DBMS Atomicity requires all transaction effects or none. After failure, recovery can undo incomplete persistent changes to enforce that outcome. Transaction management is the broader subsystem containing these responsibilities, but the question asks for the specialized component. Concurrency control primarily addresses isolation, and application code alone cannot provide the DBMS's crash-recovery undo of partially persisted work. A incorrect This is the parent subsystem, not the specialized failure-undo component requested. B incorrect Application logic alone does not provide durable crash undo. C incorrect Concurrency control primarily enforces isolation. D correct Recovery directly supports atomicity by undoing incomplete effects.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 48 · Q01238
records.text: Q01238 Question 48 ADB39 ADB12 ADB30 If a database server is referenced in a distributed transaction, the value of its commit point strength determines which role it plays in the ________________. Distinguish coordinated transaction outcome from concurrent access and local storage. A Two-phase commit B Transaction locking C Two-phase locking D Checkpoints Two-phase commit. ADB39 explicitly links Oracle COMMIT_POINT_STRENGTH to choosing the commit point site in distributed transactions. This is a role in two-phase commit, which coordinates an atomic outcome among participants. It is not a setting for acquiring or releasing locks, nor for checkpoints that bound recovery work. Higher eligible strength is preferred for the commit point. A correct Commit-point strength selects an Oracle distributed-commit role within the two-phase commit mechanism. B incorrect Transaction locking controls concurrent access rather than choosing the distributed commit point site. C incorrect Two-phase locking governs lock acquisition and release, not the distributed commit decision. D incorrect Checkpoints record recovery state and do not choose an Oracle commit point site.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 49 · Q01240
records.text: Q01240 Question 49 ADB17 What is the distinctive purpose of query optimization within the broader query-processing pipeline? Select the most specific description. Separate query representation, strategy selection and execution. A Both are used to process SQL statements to return answers. B Both filter retrieved rows by a date/time condition. C Both improve the performance of the database by efficiently executing a query. D Both are important in executing queries to access information from the DB. C. Both improve the performance of the database by efficiently executing a query. Query optimization selects a suitable efficient execution strategy among equivalent ways of answering a query. C explicitly states that efficiency objective. Returning answers and accessing information are broader descriptions of processing and do not distinguish optimization's particular purpose. Filtering data by a date or time is a query condition rather than the general goal of choosing a plan. A incorrect Returning answers describes the broad pipeline but omits the distinctive efficiency objective. B incorrect Temporal filtering is query logic, not the general purpose of optimization. C correct Efficient execution is the specific objective of selecting a suitable plan. D incorrect Accessing information describes the broad pipeline rather than optimization's efficiency role.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 50 · Q01245
records.text: Q01245 Question 50 ADB09 What is the objective of a Serializable schedule? Distinguish transaction ordering, conflict conditions and full execution equivalence. A Find a Non-serial schedule that allows the interleaving of a transaction and produces the same result as a serial schedule. B Find a Serial schedule that allows the interleaving of a transaction and produces the same result as a serial schedule. C Find a Serial schedule that doesn't allow the interleaving of a transaction and produces the same result as a serial schedule. D Find a Non-serial schedule that doesn't allow the interleaving of a transaction and produces the same result as a serial schedule. Find a Non-serial schedule that allows the interleaving of a transaction and produces the same result as a serial schedule. Serial schedules run each transaction consecutively. Serializability permits nonserial interleaving while preserving the effect of a complete serial schedule (p.72). A expresses this concurrency objective. A correct Interleaving plus serial-equivalent effect meets the objective. B incorrect A serial schedule cannot interleave transactions as claimed. C incorrect This describes serial execution, not the benefit of serializable interleaving. D incorrect Nonserial execution is distinguished by departure from consecutive transaction execution; this denies the intended interleaving.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 51 · Q01249
records.text: Q01249 Question 51 ADB04 ADB01 Under the course data-model type-constructor convention, which statements are false? Select all that apply. Interpret type constructor as a data-model term, not an executable Java/C++ object constructor, and consider OID over one object's lifetime. Classify the shape of a value separately from an operation that creates an instance. A Object Identifier is immutable. B Type constructor is used to create a new object. C Tuple is a collection of records. D The atom constructor is a multi-value constructor. B. Type constructor is used to create a new object.; C. Tuple is a collection of records.; D. The atom constructor is a multi-value constructor. An OID remains stable over the object's lifetime, so A is true. A data-model type constructor specifies the shape of a value rather than executing creation of a new object. A tuple groups named components into one structured record, while an atom is one basic value. B, C and D therefore state incorrect properties under the specified convention. A incorrect OID stability over the object lifetime is true, so it does not answer the negative stem. B correct This is false under the note's convention: a type constructor specifies shape rather than executing object creation. C correct A tuple is one structured record of components, not a collection of records. D correct An atom represents one basic atomic value rather than a multivalued collection.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 52 · Q01264
records.text: Q01264 Question 52 ADB11 Assume transaction A holds a shared lock R. If transaction B also requests for a shared lock on R Compare access permissions and same-item compatibility before granting a lock request. A It will result in a deadlock situation B It will be granted as soon as it is released by A C It will immediately be granted D It will immediately be rejected It will immediately be granted The shared-mode rule permits more than one transaction to hold a read lock on X, while excluding write locks (p.82). With only A’s shared lock specified, B’s shared request is compatible. A incorrect Two compatible shared requests do not produce the stated deadlock. B incorrect Waiting for A is unnecessary for compatible reads. C correct The shared request is compatible and may be granted immediately under the stated conditions. D incorrect The shared rule supplies no rejection condition here.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 53 · Q01266
records.text: Q01266 Question 53 ADB08 In the dirty read problem, one transaction reads: Trace which transaction wrote each value and whether an overwrite or mixed-version read occurs. A an uncommitted value of another transaction B the committed value for another transaction C another transaction D one transaction commits another transaction an uncommitted value of another transaction The temporary-update/dirty-read definition involves another transaction accessing an updated item before the failed writer’s value is restored. The hazard is observing the other transaction’s uncommitted value. A correct This identifies the unsafe value from the other transaction. B incorrect A committed value lacks the defining uncommitted-update hazard. C incorrect Transactions read data items; this does not identify the dirty value. D incorrect One transaction committing another is not the read anomaly described.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 54 · Q01381
records.text: Q01381 Question 54 ADB17 Which sequence matches the course's logical query-processing pipeline for a SELECT, from checking the request to returning its result? Separate query representation, strategy selection and execution. A Parsing and semantic analysis → logical translation → query optimization → evaluation → output B DDL->DML->query optimizer-> Authentication->output C DML->query optimizer-> Authentication-> DDL-> output D All of the mentioned A. Parsing and semantic analysis → logical translation → query optimization → evaluation → output The request is first checked for grammar and meaning, then translated into a logical representation. Optimization selects equivalent operations and physical access methods; evaluation executes that plan and returns the output. Option A follows those roles in order. The other sequences treat DDL and DML language categories as processing stages and place unrelated checks after optimization, so they do not fit. A correct This sequence follows checking, representation, strategy selection and execution. B incorrect DDL/DML categories do not form these phases, and checking is misplaced. C incorrect DDL is not a mandatory post-optimization phase of SELECT processing. D incorrect Only option A follows the pipeline, so all sequences are not correct.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 55 · Q01501
records.text: Q01501 Question 55 ADB05 In object-oriented database, the keyword "inverse" is used in which of the following? Distinguish schema definitions, queries and opposite navigation directions. A Relationship B All choices are correct C Class D Attribute Relationship. An inverse declaration connects two navigation directions of the same association, such as Department.employees and Employee.department. ADB05 explains that it maintains their relationship consistency. It does not declare a class, establish inheritance or name an ordinary scalar attribute. Thus Relationship is the applicable category, and the inclusive option is false. A correct Inverse pairs the two directions of one relationship and expresses their consistency. B incorrect The other categories are not all valid uses of the inverse declaration. C incorrect Inverse is not the keyword that declares a class or establishes a class hierarchy. D incorrect The declaration links relationship directions rather than declaring an ordinary scalar attribute.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 56 · Q01621
records.text: Q01621 Question 56 ADB05 Which statements describe ODL? Select all that apply. In A, 'implement' specifically means choosing or carrying out physical storage implementation, rather than expressing a logical definition. Distinguish schema definitions, queries and opposite navigation directions. A A method to implement a logical schema B All choices are correct C Used to develop logical schemas D A data definition language for OODB C. Used to develop logical schemas; D. A data definition language for OODB ODL is the schema-definition language for object databases and describes classes or interfaces, attributes, operations and relationships. It is therefore both a data definition language and a language used to develop logical schemas. The question defines implementation in A as physical storage work, which is a different task. Because A is false in that sense, All choices are correct is also false. A incorrect Physical storage implementation is distinct from ODL logical definition. B incorrect A is false under the specified implementation meaning. C correct ODL develops logical object schemas. D correct ODL is a data definition language for object databases.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 57 · Q01622
records.text: Q01622 Question 57 ADB06 What are ACID properties of Transactions? Track the transaction's guarantee or lifecycle boundary described by the scenario. A Automatically, Concurrency, Isolation, Durability B Atomicity, Consistency, Inconsistent, Durability C Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Database D Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability Page 66 lists atomicity, consistency preservation, isolation, and durability/permanency. Only D preserves all four terms. A incorrect Automatically and concurrency replace atomicity and consistency. B incorrect Inconsistent replaces isolation. C incorrect Database replaces durability. D correct All four names match the listed properties.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 58 · Q01623
records.text: Q01623 Question 58 ADB06 ADB-S02 Which of the following commands is used to save any transaction permanently into the database? Distinguish completing a transaction from marking an intermediate recovery position. A Rollback B None of the choices are correct C Savepoint D Commit Commit COMMIT successfully completes the transaction and requests a durable committed outcome. ROLLBACK instead cancels uncommitted changes. SAVEPOINT marks an intermediate position to which later work can be rolled back, retaining earlier work within the same transaction; it neither completes that transaction nor makes the retained changes independently durable. Because COMMIT is offered, the none-of-the-choices alternative is false. D therefore identifies the permanent transaction-completion command. A incorrect Incorrect: ROLLBACK cancels uncommitted work rather than accepting it permanently. B incorrect Incorrect: COMMIT is offered and is the requested completion command. C incorrect Incorrect: SAVEPOINT marks an intermediate rollback position inside the still-open transaction; it does not commit. D correct Correct: COMMIT completes the transaction successfully and requests a durable outcome.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 59 · SM0003
records.text: SM0003 Question 59 ADB26 Which one of the following is NOT correct about transaction failure? Identify what failed, what durable resources survive and which restoration action is required. A Transactions fail if logical errors are detected B Catastrophes can be a cause of transaction failure C Concurrency control enforcement avoids transaction failure D Transactions fail if disk blocks lose their data Concurrency control enforcement avoids transaction failure The failure list includes logical programming errors, disk blocks losing data, and physical catastrophes. It also explicitly says concurrency enforcement may abort a transaction for serializability or deadlock (p.98). Thus claiming it avoids transaction failure is the incorrect statement. A incorrect Logical errors are explicitly a cause. B incorrect Physical problems and catastrophes are explicitly listed. C correct Concurrency enforcement itself may abort transactions, contradicting the absolute claim. D incorrect Loss of disk-block data is explicitly listed.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 60 · SM0004
records.text: SM0004 Question 60 ADB29 Which one of the data updates best describes: 'All modified data items in the cache is written either after transaction ends its execution or after a pre-determined number of transactions have concluded their execution'? Separate update timing from update location and follow the commit boundary. A Immediate update B In-place update C Shadow update D Deferred update Deferred update The deferred-update passage on p.110 almost exactly reproduces the stem: modified cache items are written after a transaction ends or a fixed number finish. A incorrect Immediate update writes as soon as an item changes in cache. B incorrect In-place describes overwriting the disk version, not the delay policy. C incorrect Shadow update writes a separate disk location. D correct Deferred update has precisely the stated timing.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 61 · SM0015
records.text: SM0015 Question 61 ADB08 T1 writes X but has not committed. T2 reads that value; T1 then fails and its write is rolled back. Which anomaly did T2 experience? Trace which transaction wrote each value and whether an overwrite or mixed-version read occurs. A Nonrepeatable-read problem B It is dirty read C It is an incorrect summary problem D It is a lost update problem B. It is dirty read T2 consumes a value written by another transaction before that transaction commits. The writer's later failure makes this a dirty-read dependency requiring reconsideration of dependent work. A nonrepeatable read involves repeated reads seeing a committed change, while an incorrect summary mixes inconsistent versions in an aggregate. Lost update involves a stale overwrite, which this trace does not describe. A incorrect No repeated read observing a committed change is described. B correct T2 reads another transaction's uncommitted write. C incorrect No aggregate combines inconsistent versions. D incorrect No stale value is written over another update.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 62 · SM0045
records.text: SM0045 Question 62 ADB08 When two transactions that access the same database items have their operations interleaved in a way that makes the value of some database item incorrect. Which option correctly identifies this? Trace which transaction wrote each value and whether an overwrite or mixed-version read occurs. A It is a temporary read problem B It is a dirty read problem C It is an incorrect summary problem D It is a lost update problem It is a lost update problem The lost-update definition on p.68 is the wording in the stem. The other anomalies concern reading a temporary failed update or mixing summary values. A incorrect Temporary-update/dirty-read requires access to an uncommitted failed update, not merely the interleaving described. B incorrect Dirty read is the temporary-update anomaly. C incorrect Incorrect summary concerns aggregate evaluation over mixed versions. D correct Lost update matches the stated definition.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 63 · SM0046
records.text: SM0046 Question 63 ADB13 ADB14 Which listed policy prevents lock-wait deadlock without comparing transaction-age timestamps? Here 'wait-wait' means allowing every conflicting request to wait with no ordering or cycle restriction. Distinguish a waiting cycle, a long wait and indefinite unfair postponement. A Wait-wait B No-wait C Wound-wait D Wait-die No-wait No-wait aborts immediately when a lock request conflicts, so transactions cannot form a lock-wait cycle and no age comparison is needed. Wait–die and wound–wait use relative transaction ages to decide who waits or aborts. Under the explicitly defined wait-wait alternative, every conflicting request may wait without a cycle-prevention restriction, so a transaction can hold one item while waiting for another in a cycle. That alternative therefore fails the deadlock-prevention requirement. A incorrect Incorrect: unrestricted waiting permits a hold-and-wait cycle, so this defined policy does not prevent deadlock. B correct Correct: immediate abort on a conflicting request prevents lock waits without comparing ages. C incorrect Incorrect: wound–wait compares requester and holder ages to choose waiting or aborting a younger holder. D incorrect Incorrect: wait–die compares ages to choose whether the requester waits or aborts.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 64 · SM0047
records.text: SM0047 Question 64 ADB11 ADB17 A database management system (DBMS) has ______ to control locks. Compare access permissions and same-item compatibility before granting a lock request. A Lock manager B Lock table C Query optimizer D Query processor Lock manager Page 83 distinguishes the manager that manages locks from the table it uses to store lock identities and modes. The controlling component is the lock manager. A correct This component manages locks. B incorrect The table stores lock information for the manager. C incorrect Optimization selects execution strategies, not lock ownership. D incorrect The named lock-control component is the manager, not query processing.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 65 · SM0205
records.text: SM0205 Question 65 ADB41 ADB-S01 In a columnar database, data is stored: Distinguish operational transactions, analytical workloads and physical storage layout. A Row-wise B In a hierarchical structure C Column-wise D In a network model Column-wise. ADB41 defines columnar storage as grouping values by column, which avoids reading irrelevant columns and can improve compression for scans. Row-oriented storage instead groups each record's fields. Hierarchical and network models are logical representation alternatives rather than the physical column-oriented layout requested by the stem. Columnar layout alone does not determine the logical data model. A incorrect Row-wise grouping is row-oriented storage, the contrasting physical layout. B incorrect A hierarchy describes parent-child organization, not the columnar physical storage arrangement. C correct Columnar storage groups the values of each column together. D incorrect A network model concerns linked records rather than this column-oriented physical layout.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 66 · SM0247
records.text: SM0247 Question 66 ADB37 ADB36 ADB33 ADB42 An online game wants extra read copies of player reference data near regional users while retaining the same logical data. Which concept specifically creates those additional copies, rather than dividing the only copy into fragments or choosing a model family? Separate copy placement, propagation timing and update-maintenance cost. A Replication B NoSQL databases C Distributed databases D Partitioning A. Replication Replication creates additional copies of selected data and can improve read locality by placing them near users. That directly satisfies the specified regional read-copy requirement. Distribution is the broader arrangement across sites, partitioning divides data into fragments, and NoSQL names a family of data models. Neither the broader architecture nor a model label specifically says that extra copies are created. A correct Replication creates the required regional read copies. B incorrect NoSQL selects a model family and does not itself create copies. C incorrect Distribution is broader than the requested copy-creation policy. D incorrect Partitioning divides data; by itself it creates no spare copy.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 67 · SM0298
records.text: SM0298 Question 67 ADB26 ADB07 ADB06 ADB17 In a generic DBMS component model applied to a MySQL deployment, which specialized role coordinates restoring valid data from stored backups and logs after data loss? Use generic functional roles, not claims about named MySQL engine internals. Identify what failed, what durable resources survive and which restoration action is required. A Buffer Manager B Transaction Manager C Query Engine D Recovery Manager D. Recovery Manager Recovery is the specialized responsibility for restoring valid database state after failure or loss. Backups supply a separate stored copy, and available logs can restore later recoverable changes. The recovery-manager role therefore matches the question's generic component model. Buffer management caches working pages; transaction management is the broader parent responsibility, while the query engine processes requests. This makes no claim about MySQL's internal module names. A incorrect Buffers cache working data and are not durable backup copies. B incorrect Transaction management is broader than the specialized restoration role requested. C incorrect A query engine processes queries rather than coordinating restoration. D correct The generic recovery role coordinates restoration using durable recovery resources.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 68 · SS102
records.text: SS102 Question 68 ADB43 Which listed sources can contain unstructured free text, images or audio? Select all that apply. Here Google search collections include free-text web pages; RDBMS systems may store text/BLOB attachments; the Apple Employee and Registrar student examples contain only fixed-field structured records. Classify the actual content or pattern being analyzed rather than the storage product. A Google search engine B RDBMS systems C Apple Employee database D Registrar student database A. Google search engine; B. RDBMS systems Unstructured classification depends on the actual content rather than the storage product. Search collections can contain free text and images, and an RDBMS can store text or binary attachments, so A and B qualify under the stated contents. The employee and registrar examples are explicitly restricted to fixed-field structured records, excluding the otherwise possible attachments that would change their classification. A correct The specified web collection includes unstructured free text. B correct The specified relational store may contain unstructured text/BLOB attachments. C incorrect This example is restricted to structured fixed-field records. D incorrect This example is restricted to structured fixed-field records.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 69 · SS123
records.text: SS123 Question 69 ADB43 Business people always remodel their business by closely studying their customers' purchasing habits over the course of their purchase history. Accordingly, a salesperson at Markato shop noticed that people who always buy shoes will also buy socks with probability of 0.75 and hence decided to put shoes and socks side by side for ease of accessibility. Which big data analytics technique could this salesperson could employ? Classify the actual content or pattern being analyzed rather than the storage product. A Association rule B Clustering algorithm C Predictive modeling D Regression modeling Association-rule mining: shoes ⇒ socks has confidence 0.75. The observation is a conditional co-purchase pattern: among shoe purchases, socks also appear with probability 0.75. ADB43 defines this as the confidence of an association rule and explicitly distinguishes co-occurrence mining from clustering, classification and numeric regression. The store-layout decision uses that rule; it does not change the underlying technique or prove causation. A correct The rule captures shoe/sock co-occurrence with conditional confidence 0.75. B incorrect Clustering groups similar cases without target labels rather than directly discovering this co-purchase rule. C incorrect The stated evidence is an association rule, not a separately specified predictive modeling task. D incorrect Regression predicts numeric outcomes rather than identifying this purchasing co-occurrence rule.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 70 · SS130
records.text: SS130 Question 70 ADB44 Using this convention, Model Testing means measuring a trained model on held-out test data; Model Evaluation means the subsequent release decision using those results and business success criteria. Which sequence applies before deploying this newly trained model? Identify the objective and the stated meanings of the workflow stages. A Model Training, Model Evaluation, Model Testing, Model Deployment B Model Training, Model Testing, Model Deployment, Model Evaluation C Model Training, Model Testing, Model Evaluation, Model Deployment D Model Evaluation, Model Training , Model Testing, Model Deployment C. Model Training, Model Testing, Model Evaluation, Model Deployment Under the stated convention, training first produces the model. Testing then measures it on held-out data, and evaluation uses those results to decide whether business criteria justify deployment. C follows that sequence. Evaluation during model selection can use a different ordering, but this question explicitly assigns evaluation to the subsequent release review, so the other sequences misplace that review. A incorrect It puts the specified post-test release review before testing. B incorrect It deploys before the required release review. C correct Training, held-out testing, release evaluation and deployment follow the defined roles. D incorrect It evaluates the newly trained model before that model has been trained.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 71 · SS188
records.text: SS188 Question 71 ADB44 Identify the one that comes first in data mining process Identify the objective and the stated meanings of the workflow stages. A Business understanding B Data integration C Data cleaning D Data selection Business understanding. ADB44 starts the data-mining workflow by defining the business decision and its success criteria. This establishes why data will be collected and modeled. Integration, cleaning and feature selection prepare data after the problem has been understood; they do not replace the initial business-understanding stage. Thus A precedes the other listed activities. A correct Business understanding first defines the decision to support and the criteria for success. B incorrect Data integration prepares sources after the business problem has been identified. C incorrect Cleaning improves data quality during preparation rather than defining the initial business objective. D incorrect Selecting relevant data depends on an already understood business problem and modeling objective.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 72 · AM0162
records.text: AM0162 Question 72 ADB06 ADB11 What is the defining purpose of a transaction in database management? Track the transaction's guarantee or lifecycle boundary described by the scenario. A To secure the database from unauthorized access B To optimize query performance C To group database operations into one logical unit of work D To define the structure and organization of a database C. To group database operations into one logical unit of work A transaction groups database operations into one logical unit of work. The DBMS supports its atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability requirements, including controlled interference with concurrent transactions. Grouping is the defining concept, rather than query tuning, access authorization or schema construction. Read-only work can also form a transaction, so the definition is not limited to operations that change stored data. A incorrect Authorization governs who may access data rather than defining transaction grouping. B incorrect Optimization chooses query execution strategies. C correct A transaction is one logical unit of database work. D incorrect Schema definition describes data structures rather than a unit of work.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 73 · AM0177
records.text: AM0177 Question 73 ADB06 A correctly implemented financial transaction must preserve a declared total-balance invariant when it completes. Which ACID property names preservation of such integrity rules? Focus on the invariant rather than partial execution, concurrent interference or survival after a crash. Track the transaction's guarantee or lifecycle boundary described by the scenario. A Atomicity B Consistency C Isolation D Durability B. Consistency Consistency means that correct transactional work preserves declared integrity rules. Maintaining the total-balance invariant is therefore the consistency requirement. Atomicity addresses whether the effects happen together, isolation controls interference among concurrent transactions and durability preserves committed effects after failure. These properties cooperate, but the revised question identifies invariant preservation as the particular guarantee to name. A incorrect Atomicity names all-or-none effects rather than invariant preservation itself. B correct Consistency names preservation of declared integrity rules by correct work. C incorrect Isolation controls concurrent interference. D incorrect Durability preserves committed effects after failure.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 74 · AM0185
records.text: AM0185 Question 74 ADB01 In the object-oriented model, an object is defined as: Distinguish an object instance from its class, attribute values and persistent identity. A An instance of a class B A collection of attributes C A primary key in a database D A relationship between tables An instance of a class. ADB01 explicitly distinguishes a class specification from each object instantiated from it. A class defines available attributes and operations, while an object is one individual instance with identity, state and behavior. A collection of attributes omits identity and behavior; a key or an intertable relationship belongs to a different relational description. A correct An object is an individual instance of a class with its own identity and state. B incorrect Attributes describe state but omit the identity and behavior that also characterize an object. C incorrect A database primary key is an identifier constraint, not the definition of an object instance. D incorrect A relationship between tables is a relational association rather than an object instance.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 75 · AM0186
records.text: AM0186 Question 75 ADB02 In the object-oriented model, encapsulation refers to: Separate the object boundary, the exposed contract and links between objects. A Combining multiple classes into a single entity B Hiding the internal details of an object C Establishing relationships between objects D Defining the inheritance hierarchy Hiding and controlling access to internal object details. ADB02 describes encapsulation as grouping state with operations and controlling access to implementation details. A withdrawal method can enforce rules while hiding storage. B states the relevant information-hiding aspect. Combining classes, associating objects and defining subtype hierarchies are distinct activities; none describes the encapsulation boundary around an object's state and operations. A incorrect Encapsulation groups an object's state and operations, not multiple classes into one entity. B correct Encapsulation controls access to the internal representation behind the object's operations. C incorrect Links between objects are associations rather than encapsulation itself. D incorrect Superclass/subclass structure concerns inheritance rather than information-hiding boundaries.
