B correct Relational algebra represents the logical operations used for rewriting and planning. C incorrect Python scripts are not the general internal representation specified here. D incorrect XML documents are not the defined general relational query representation.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 211 · NS0133
records.text: NS0133 Question 211 ADB19 What does query optimization aim to minimize? Identify the resource objective, counts and unit costs before comparing execution strategies. A The number of tables referenced B The overall cost (time and resources) of executing the query C The number of join operations D The character length of the SQL query Overall execution cost under the chosen resource model. ADB19 measures candidate plans using I/O, CPU, memory, temporary storage and network traffic. The aim is a suitable low-cost equivalent plan, not syntactic brevity or indiscriminate removal of joins and tables. Required tables and semantics must be preserved; even fewer operations do not necessarily imply lower runtime or resource cost. A incorrect Required tables cannot be discarded merely to reduce the table count. B correct Optimization compares equivalent plans using estimated time and resource costs. C incorrect Join count alone ignores access paths, cardinalities and the cost of each join. D incorrect Short SQL text does not necessarily produce a cheaper execution plan.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 212 · NS0134
records.text: NS0134 Question 212 ADB19 The dominant cost factor in query execution is typically: Identify the resource objective, counts and unit costs before comparing execution strategies. A CPU processing time B Network transmission time C Disk I/O time (seek + transfer) D Memory allocation time Disk I/O in the conventional local-disk query-cost model. ADB19 says disk I/O often dominates textbook local-disk examples, matching the question’s typical teaching model. C includes both seek and transfer work. This is a contextual tendency, not a universal claim: CPU can dominate in-memory work and communication can dominate distributed plans. The answer should retain that local-disk qualification rather than extend it to every system. A incorrect CPU can dominate in-memory work but is not the typical local-disk-model answer. B incorrect Network cost can dominate distributed plans rather than the conventional local-disk model. C correct Seek and transfer I/O often dominate the conventional disk-based cost model. D incorrect Memory allocation is not the dominant term specified for the textbook local-disk model.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 213 · NS0135
records.text: NS0135 Question 213 ADB19 If a query requires 5 seeks (tS=5ms each) and transfers 10 blocks (tT=1ms each), what is the disk I/O cost? Identify the resource objective, counts and unit costs before comparing execution strategies. A 50ms B 35ms C 15ms D 25ms 35 ms. ADB19 adds seeks times seek duration to blocks times per-block transfer duration. Five seeks cost 5×5=25 ms and ten block transfers cost 10×1=10 ms. Their sum is 35 ms. The terms must be added, not multiplied together or considered separately; this is the supplied simple disk model rather than a measured universal query runtime. A incorrect Fifty does not equal the sum of 25 ms seeking and 10 ms transfer. B correct Five times five plus ten times one gives 35 ms. C incorrect Fifteen omits the correct five-seek multiplication. D incorrect Twenty-five counts only seek time and omits ten milliseconds of transfer.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 214 · NS0136
records.text: NS0136 Question 214 ADB26 ADB27 Database recovery restores the database after failure to: Identify what failed, what durable resources survive and which restoration action is required. A Its state at database creation B A consistent and correct state, undoing incomplete transactions and reapplying committed ones C The state at the last user login D An empty state for fresh start A valid recovered state preserving durable commits and removing incomplete effects. ADB26 defines restart recovery by preserving durable commits and removing incomplete effects after failure. B matches the simple undo/redo teaching model. The detailed work depends on buffer policy and algorithm; not every committed update needs physical redo if already installed. Recovery does not reset the database to creation, last login or an empty replacement state. A incorrect Returning to creation would discard legitimate later durable commits. B correct Recovery preserves committed work and removes incomplete effects to restore valid state. C incorrect User login time is not the transaction recovery boundary. D incorrect Emptying the database would destroy committed data rather than recover it.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 215 · NS0137
records.text: NS0137 Question 215 ADB-S05 ADB26 Which type of failure occurs when DBMS software bugs cause unexpected behavior? Classify the stated cause rather than inferring it from the observed symptom. A Hardware Failure B Natural Disaster C Software Error D Network Failure Software error. The stem directly identifies DBMS software bugs as the cause. That is a software error rather than failed hardware, a natural event or broken communication. ADB26 separates transaction/system/media failure concerns so the recovery resource can be chosen appropriately; an observed crash alone would not identify its cause, but this question explicitly supplies it. A incorrect The stated cause is faulty software behavior rather than a malfunctioning hardware component. B incorrect No natural event is described; the prompt names a software bug. C correct Unexpected behavior caused by DBMS bugs is a software error. D incorrect No failed network connection is given as the cause of the behavior.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 216 · NS0138
records.text: NS0138 Question 216 ADB27 What does WAL require? In B, 'corresponding data changes' specifically means durable output of the changed data page; volatile buffer changes may occur earlier. Track durable-write ordering and distinguish reversing incomplete work from installing logged effects. A Data written to disk before the log record B Log records written to stable storage BEFORE corresponding data changes C Logs written only after transaction commits D Checkpoints before every write operation B. Log records written to stable storage BEFORE corresponding data changes The update log needed for recovery must be stable before the changed data page becomes persistent. B states that order under the question's explicit durable-write meaning. The buffer can be modified earlier. Data-before-log reverses the rule, waiting until after commit is not the required logging policy and checkpointing before every write is not a WAL requirement. A incorrect The durable log must precede the changed page, not follow it. B correct With the stated scope, stable logs precede corresponding durable page output. C incorrect Update logging is not deferred until after commit. D incorrect WAL does not require a checkpoint for every write.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 217 · NS0139
records.text: NS0139 Question 217 ADB27 ADB30 ADB11 The Redo operation during recovery: Track durable-write ordering and distinguish reversing incomplete work from installing logged effects. A Reverses incomplete transactions B Re-applies committed transactions whose changes were not yet persisted to disk C Creates new checkpoints D Locks data items during the recovery process Reapply missing logged committed effects in the simple undo/redo model. ADB27 uses redo to install logged after-images when necessary. B describes preserving committed work missing from disk pages in the simple teaching model. It does not mean re-running application side effects or blindly adding an amount twice. ARIES has a broader repeat-history phase before undo, but that does not make reversal, checkpoint creation or lock acquisition the definition of redo. A incorrect Reversing incomplete changes is undo rather than redo. B correct Redo installs required logged effects missing from data pages, preserving committed work in the simple model. C incorrect Checkpoint creation records recovery state rather than reapplying update after-images. D incorrect Locking may coordinate access but is not the operation of logged redo.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 218 · NS0140
records.text: NS0140 Question 218 ADB27 ADB29 The Undo operation during recovery: Track durable-write ordering and distinguish reversing incomplete work from installing logged effects. A Re-applies committed transactions B Reverses changes of incomplete/aborted transactions using before-images from the log C Writes the WAL to stable storage D Creates shadow page copies Restore before-images of incomplete or aborted work. ADB27 restores before-images when undoing incomplete effects, normally following that transaction’s updates backward. B states both the affected work and the supporting log information. Applying committed after-images is redo, forcing logs is a WAL durability action, and copying pages is part of a different update/recovery approach. None is the reversal operation itself. A incorrect Reapplying committed effects is the redo purpose in the simple model. B correct Undo restores logged old values to remove incomplete or aborted transaction effects. C incorrect Forcing the log supports durable ordering but does not itself reverse data changes. D incorrect Shadow-page copies preserve versions instead of defining logged before-image undo.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 219 · NS0141
records.text: NS0141 Question 219 ADB29 ADB15 ADB30 Shadow Paging recovery technique works by: Separate update timing from update location and follow the commit boundary. A Using timestamps to sequence recovery B Writing changes to shadow (copy) pages, keeping originals intact, then swapping on commit C Using transaction logs for all rollbacks D Taking checkpoints every transaction Copy changed pages and atomically install the new durable map on commit. ADB29 keeps the committed page map unchanged while modifications use new locations and a modified map. Commit durably installs the new root/map pointer after required pages are durable. B captures that preservation-and-switch mechanism. Timestamp ordering, mandatory per-transaction checkpoints and universal log-based rollback are not the defining shadow-paging steps. A incorrect Timestamp ordering controls concurrent operations rather than defining shadow page-map replacement. B correct Copy-on-write preserves originals and commit safely installs the new page map. C incorrect Shadow paging is an alternative to conventional log-based recovery, not mandatory logged rollback for all changes. D incorrect A checkpoint every transaction is not the mechanism that preserves the old page map.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 220 · NS0142
records.text: NS0142 Question 220 ADB30 ADB11 A checkpoint in database recovery helps because: Identify which history a recovery boundary can safely exclude and whether active work spans it. A It stops all transactions B Recovery can start from the checkpoint state rather than processing the entire log from the beginning C It creates a full database backup copy D It grants exclusive locks to all active transactions A checkpoint supplies recovery state that avoids scanning all historical logs from the beginning. ADB30 uses durable checkpoint state to avoid processing all old history. B describes that benefit if start means entering recovery analysis, not assuming every earlier update is irrelevant. Active transactions can span a checkpoint and fuzzy-checkpoint redo may require earlier log positions. A checkpoint is not a full backup, universal stop or lock grant. A incorrect Fuzzy checkpoints permit ongoing transactions, so stopping all work is not required. B correct Recorded recovery state provides a bounded starting point, while earlier necessary undo/redo must still be considered. C incorrect A checkpoint stores recovery metadata and is not a full separate database backup. D incorrect Checkpointing does not grant every active transaction exclusive locks.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 221 · NS0143
records.text: NS0143 Question 221 ADB29 ADB28 Under conventional deferred update with no-force, which recovery classifications describe the policy? Select all that apply. Interpret NO UNDO / REDO as 'no undo, redo required'. Separate update timing from update location and follow the commit boundary. A UNDO/REDO B UNDO only C REDO only D NO UNDO / REDO C. REDO only; D. NO UNDO / REDO Because uncommitted changes have not reached the persistent database, crash recovery does not need to undo them there. No-force permits committed changes to remain uninstalled, so redo may be required. REDO only and NO UNDO / REDO express the same classification under the stated notation. Undo-only and undo/redo both assert an undo requirement that this deferred model avoids. A incorrect Usual deferred update does not require undo of uncommitted persistent database changes. B incorrect Undo only gives the opposite recovery requirement from the usual deferred no-force model. C correct REDO only is the usual deferred-update recovery classification. D correct NO UNDO/REDO is another spelling of the same redo-only requirement.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 222 · NS0144
records.text: NS0144 Question 222 ADB29 Which data update strategy writes changes to a SEPARATE disk location preserving the original? Separate update timing from update location and follow the commit boundary. A Immediate Update B Deferred Update C Shadow Update D In-Place Update Shadow update, or copy-on-write. ADB29 distinguishes where an update is written from when it may become persistent. Shadow/copy-on-write uses a new location while retaining the committed version, matching C. Immediate and deferred classify commit timing, not necessarily a separate location. In-place update overwrites the original location, which directly contradicts the preservation condition in the stem. A incorrect Immediate update concerns allowing persistent changes before commit rather than requiring new locations. B incorrect Deferred update concerns withholding uncommitted persistent effects rather than necessarily copying pages. C correct Shadow/copy-on-write preserves the original and writes the changed value at a separate location. D incorrect In-place update overwrites the original location rather than preserving it intact.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 223 · NS0145
records.text: NS0145 Question 223 ADB07 ADB27 In the course's conceptual transaction-log model supporting undo of incomplete changes and redo of committed changes, what value information does a write-operation record store? Trace movement between program variables, buffers and disk, or the meaning of a recorded transaction event. A Only new (after-image) values B Only old (before-image) values C Both old (before-image) AND new (after-image) values D Only transaction IDs and timestamps C. Both old (before-image) AND new (after-image) values The given UPDATE record contains both the old and new values. The old value supplies a before-image for undo, while the new value supplies an after-image for redo. Therefore the record stores both kinds of image. Real systems can use other physical or logical formats, but that variation does not alter the explicit conceptual record being examined here. A incorrect The given format includes old as well as new, so after-images alone are incomplete. B incorrect The format includes new as well as old, so before-images alone are incomplete. C correct Both before-image and after-image fields are present. D incorrect Transaction identifiers alone omit the explicitly supplied value fields.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 224 · NS0146
records.text: NS0146 Question 224 ADB33 ADB37 A distributed database is best described as: Separate coordinated network placement from engine compatibility and semantic integration. A A single database on one powerful server B Multiple logically related databases across networked computers, managed transparently C A fully replicated database at every network location D A web-based file storage system Logically related data across networked sites under coordinated database management. ADB33 defines logically related data across networked sites managed as a coordinated system. B matches that architecture and its logical abstraction. Full replication is only one placement choice, not a defining requirement. A single powerful server is centralized, and generic web file storage does not establish coordinated database semantics across related distributed data. A incorrect A database confined to one server is centralized rather than distributed across networked sites. B correct Networked, logically related data with coordinated management fits the distributed database definition. C incorrect A distributed database need not replicate every row at every network location. D incorrect Generic web file storage does not by itself establish coordinated distributed database management.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 225 · NS0147
records.text: NS0147 Question 225 ADB33 ADB34 A homogeneous distributed database system requires: Separate coordinated network placement from engine compatibility and semantic integration. A Different DBMS at each site B Same DBMS software at all sites C No network between sites D Full independence of each site The same compatible DBMS technology at the sites. ADB33 defines homogeneity through compatible DBMS technology across sites. B is the listed form of that condition. It does not imply identical local schemas, replication or immediate synchronization. Different DBMSs describe heterogeneity, while removing the network or demanding full independence contradicts coordinated distributed management rather than defining homogeneity. A incorrect Different DBMS technologies characterize heterogeneous integration rather than homogeneity. B correct The same DBMS software supplies the compatible database technology described by homogeneous systems. C incorrect Distributed sites need network communication for coordinated management. D incorrect Full local independence is an autonomy choice rather than a homogeneity requirement.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 226 · NS0148
records.text: NS0148 Question 226 ADB33 ADB24 Heterogeneous distributed databases use which standards for inter-database communication? Separate coordinated network placement from engine compatibility and semantic integration. A Same DBMS software only B Direct SQL between databases C ODBC and JDBC generic connectivity D LAN protocols exclusively ODBC and JDBC connectivity interfaces. ADB33 explicitly names ODBC and JDBC as connectivity interfaces for differing systems. C therefore identifies the offered communication interfaces. They do not automatically reconcile schemas, units or transaction semantics and do not create a distributed transaction by themselves. Identical DBMS software is not heterogeneity, and generic LAN protocols do not replace database-level connectivity interfaces. A incorrect Requiring the same DBMS removes the differing-engine situation rather than identifying its connectivity interfaces. B incorrect Direct SQL alone does not identify the generic cross-system connectivity standards named in the note. C correct ODBC and JDBC provide generic database connectivity while semantic mappings remain necessary. D incorrect LAN protocols alone do not supply the database API/interface compatibility described.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 227 · NS0149
records.text: NS0149 Question 227 ADB36 Horizontal fragmentation divides a database table by: Identify whether rows or columns are split and reverse the split to reconstruct the original relation. A Columns (attributes) B Rows based on a condition or criterion C Both rows and columns simultaneously D Database schemas Rows selected by conditions. ADB36 defines horizontal fragmentation by selecting row subsets with predicates. B directly states that operation. Column division is vertical fragmentation, and combining both dimensions is hybrid fragmentation. Schema names and geographic placement can influence a design, but are not the definition of what is split by horizontal fragmentation. A incorrect Splitting attributes is vertical rather than horizontal fragmentation. B correct Horizontal fragmentation partitions rows according to stated predicates or criteria. C incorrect Splitting both dimensions combines horizontal and vertical operations in hybrid fragmentation. D incorrect Schemas are not the row units divided by the defined horizontal operation.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 228 · NS0150
records.text: NS0150 Question 228 ADB36 ADB-S01 To reconstruct a horizontally fragmented table, which operation is used? Identify whether rows or columns are split and reverse the split to reconstruct the original relation. A JOIN B UNION C INTERSECTION D DIFFERENCE UNION. Horizontal fragments contain selected subsets of the original relation’s rows. ADB36 reconstructs the relation by their union, assuming completeness and the intended overlap rules. Joining is used to align vertical column pieces by a key; intersection would keep only shared rows and difference would remove rows, so neither reconstructs all horizontal fragments. A incorrect Key joins reconstruct matching vertical column pieces, not ordinary horizontal row partitions. B correct Union collects the rows from every complete horizontal fragment. C incorrect Intersection keeps only common rows and would discard rows unique to individual fragments. D incorrect Difference removes rows instead of recombining all fragment members.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 229 · NS0151
records.text: NS0151 Question 229 ADB36 Vertical fragmentation divides a table by: Identify whether rows or columns are split and reverse the split to reconstruct the original relation. A Rows B Columns (attributes), with primary key repeated in each fragment C Number of concurrent transactions D Geographic location of data Column subsets with a repeated key or row identifier. ADB36 splits a relation by columns and repeats a key or row identifier so the pieces can be joined without spurious matches. B describes that usual primary-key form. Rows are split horizontally; transaction counts and geography concern workload or placement rather than the attribute-level split defining vertical fragmentation. The shared identifier can be an appropriate equivalent key. A incorrect Row subsets define horizontal rather than vertical fragmentation. B correct Vertical fragments contain column subsets plus a repeated identifier for reconstruction. C incorrect Concurrent transaction count is a workload property rather than the dimension being split. D incorrect Geographic placement does not define the column projection used for vertical fragments.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 230 · NS0152
records.text: NS0152 Question 230 ADB37 Full replication in distributed databases has which disadvantage? Separate copy placement, propagation timing and update-maintenance cost. A Low data availability B Every update must be applied to all copies, creating high overhead C Fast read performance D Simple concurrency control Propagating each update across all copies adds maintenance overhead. ADB37 says copies improve locality and can improve availability but require storage and update propagation. B names that maintenance burden for full replication. Propagation timing may be synchronous or asynchronous, so the answer does not imply every copy is updated simultaneously. Fast reads are a possible benefit, and concurrency control becomes more involved rather than inherently simple. A incorrect Usable replicas can improve availability rather than inherently making it low. B correct All copies must eventually reflect relevant updates, creating propagation and coordination overhead. C incorrect Fast reads are a potential benefit rather than the listed disadvantage. D incorrect Maintaining consistent copies does not inherently simplify concurrency control.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 231 · NS0153
records.text: NS0153 Question 231 ADB35 Fragmentation transparency in distributed databases means: Identify exactly which detail is hidden from the user. A Users can see all the fragmentation details B Users interact with the database as a single entity, unaware of fragmentation existence C Only DBAs know about fragments D Fragments are listed as separate tables in the schema Users query the logical relation without knowing its fragments. ADB35 defines fragmentation transparency as hiding the existence and reconstruction of fragments. B states that user-facing abstraction directly. It does not require literally only DBAs to know the implementation; developers and administrators may also need that knowledge. Exposing fragment tables or all fragmentation details to users would make fragmentation visible instead of transparent. A incorrect Showing all fragmentation details is the opposite of hiding them from ordinary queries. B correct Users operate on the whole logical relation without managing its fragment reconstruction. C incorrect Transparency describes the user abstraction, not exclusive knowledge restricted to DBAs alone. D incorrect Naming fragments separately exposes fragmentation rather than concealing it from the querying user.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 232 · NS0154
records.text: NS0154 Question 232 ADB34 The Middleware architecture in distributed DBMS uses: Identify which tier submits, mediates or executes a request. A Direct client-to-server connections B All servers collaborating on every query C A dedicated middleware server that mediates between clients and multiple independent database servers D A single centralized database server Middleware mediates between clients and independent database servers. ADB34 lets middleware translate requests, locate data, coordinate operations and combine results across independent servers. C describes that mediating tier. The logical responsibility does not require exactly one physical machine in every implementation. Direct connections omit this mediator, universal server collaboration is a different arrangement, and one centralized server is not the stated distributed middleware design. A incorrect Direct client-server links alone omit the middleware mediation that defines the requested architecture. B incorrect Every server need not participate in every query; relevant sources depend on the request. C correct A middleware tier mediates client requests across multiple independent database servers. D incorrect One centralized database server does not describe mediation across independent distributed servers.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 233 · NS0155
records.text: NS0155 Question 233 ADB36 ADB37 ADB11 ADB34 Hybrid fragmentation combines which two techniques? Identify whether rows or columns are split and reverse the split to reconstruct the original relation. A Full replication and no replication B Horizontal fragmentation and vertical fragmentation C Locking and timestamp-based concurrency control D Client-server and middleware architectures Horizontal and vertical fragmentation. ADB36 explicitly defines hybrid fragmentation as combining row and column splits in an appropriate order. B names those two operations. Replication changes copy placement, locking and timestamps control concurrent access, and client-server/middleware describe architecture responsibilities. They can coexist with hybrid fragmentation but are not its two component fragmentation techniques. A incorrect Full/no replication concerns copies rather than the row and column splits of hybrid fragmentation. B correct Hybrid fragmentation combines horizontal row subsets with vertical column subsets. C incorrect Locking and timestamps are concurrency-control mechanisms, not fragmentation types. D incorrect These are architecture forms rather than the two data-fragmentation operations.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 234 · NS0286
records.text: NS0286 Question 234 ADB34 ADB06 In client-server database architecture, what is the primary role of the server? Identify which tier submits, mediates or executes a request. A Provide the GUI for end users B Initiate all network connections and poll clients for updates C Store and manage shared data, enforce ACID properties, and process client requests D Cache all user sessions locally for offline access Manage shared data, process requests and enforce supported transaction/integrity guarantees. ADB34 assigns clients request submission and servers shared-data management, operation execution and supported integrity/transaction enforcement. C matches those responsibilities. User interfaces usually belong to clients, while initiating all connections, polling every client or caching all sessions for offline use are not the server role defined by this architecture. Guarantees still depend on supported mechanisms and correct application use. A incorrect The user-facing GUI is normally a client responsibility rather than the database server's primary role. B incorrect The server need not initiate every connection or poll clients for every update. C correct Shared-data management, query execution and supported integrity/transaction enforcement are server duties. D incorrect Caching every session for offline access is not the defined database-server responsibility.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 235 · NS0288
records.text: NS0288 Question 235 ADB12 ADB16 In two-phase locking (2PL), during which phase may a transaction acquire locks but not release any? Track the first lock release and the transaction-completion boundary. A Growing phase B Commit phase C Validation phase D Shrinking phase Growing phase. ADB12 allows acquiring or upgrading locks during growing and releasing or downgrading them during shrinking. Once any lock is released, a transaction may not acquire another. A is therefore the phase described. Commit is a transaction event, validation belongs to optimistic control and shrinking has the opposite lock-release role. A correct Growing permits acquisitions and upgrades before any release starts. B incorrect Commit is not the general 2PL phase for new lock acquisition. C incorrect Validation is an optimistic-control stage rather than the 2PL growing phase. D incorrect Shrinking releases or downgrades locks and forbids acquiring new ones.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 236 · NS0306
records.text: NS0306 Question 236 ADB24 ADB-S03 Assume that we are able to specify that Mr. Getahun can view the database record, but cannot change the value of the record. Which security management technique was used in this scenario? Identify whether the scenario concerns identity, permission, disclosure or valid values. A Access Control B Availability C Non-repudiation D Integrity Access control. ADB24 explicitly describes a user allowed to view but not change a record as having restricted access privileges. That is authorization/access control. Integrity concerns valid values, availability concerns readiness for use and non-repudiation concerns attributable actions rather than whether a particular read or write is permitted. A matches the actual permission distinction. A correct Access control grants reading while denying modification for the specified user. B incorrect Availability concerns service readiness rather than the read-versus-write privilege distinction. C incorrect Non-repudiation does not define whether this user is authorized to modify a record. D incorrect Integrity restricts valid data states rather than assigning user-specific read/update permissions.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 237 · NS0307
records.text: NS0307 Question 237 ADB30 ADB29 ADB11 ADB09 Suppose, a developer proposes using deferred update with no checkpoints in a high- transaction OLTP system. What is the most serious drawback? Identify which history a recovery boundary can safely exclude and whether active work spans it. A Log scans become prohibitively expensive after long uptime B Increased disk I/O due to frequent page copying C Shared locks cannot be used D View serializability cannot be ensured Long-running log scans can make recovery expensive. ADB30 warns that without checkpoints or another valid truncation boundary, a long-running system may scan expensive amounts of log history. Deferred update removes uncommitted persistent effects but does not remove that search problem. Page copying belongs to shadow approaches, while shared locks and serializability are independent concurrency concerns rather than consequences of omitting checkpoints. A correct High transaction volume and long uptime can produce costly recovery log scans without a valid boundary. B incorrect Frequent copy-on-write pages characterize shadow updating rather than the absence of checkpoints in deferred update. C incorrect Omitting checkpoints does not inherently prohibit shared locks. D incorrect View serializability is a concurrency-order property, not inherently lost by this checkpoint omission.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 238 · NS0321
records.text: NS0321 Question 238 ADB29 ADB31 Which listed techniques use transaction logs for recovery under the course model? Interpret Deferred Database Modification as conventional logged deferred update with no-force. Select all that apply. Separate update timing from update location and follow the commit boundary. A Recovery in Multi-database Systems B ARIES Recovery Algorithm C Shadow Paging Technique D Deferred Database Modification B. ARIES Recovery Algorithm; D. Deferred Database Modification ARIES relies on WAL and log-driven analysis, redo and undo. Conventional logged deferred update also uses recorded updates for redo of committed work, with no undo of uncommitted persistent changes. Both therefore belong to the requested category. Shadow paging preserves old page mappings instead, while recovery in multidatabase systems names an environment rather than a particular log-based technique. A incorrect Multidatabase recovery describes an environment rather than one specific recovery technique. B correct ARIES explicitly uses WAL and log-driven analysis, redo and undo. C incorrect Shadow paging preserves committed page maps rather than being the conventional log-based technique. D correct Deferred modification can use logged changes for redo after commitment.

records.title: Advanced Database Systems — Question 239 · NS0348
records.text: NS0348 Question 239 ADB36 ADB35 ADB37 Which type of fragmentation divides a relation into subrelations containing subsets of its columns, repeating a key or row identifier so the original rows can be reconstructed? Identify whether rows or columns are split and reverse the split to reconstruct the original relation. A Replication B Location C Horizontal D Vertical D. Vertical Vertical fragmentation divides a relation by columns. Repeating a key or row identifier allows corresponding pieces to be joined back into the original rows without spurious matches. Horizontal fragmentation divides rows instead. Replication creates copies, while location transparency hides where data resides. Hiding a column split would be fragmentation transparency, but the question asks for the split operation itself. A incorrect Replication copies data rather than dividing its columns. B incorrect Location transparency hides sites rather than splitting a relation. C incorrect Horizontal fragmentation selects row subsets. D correct Vertical fragmentation projects column subsets with a reconstruction identifier.

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Course module
records.text: Object Oriented Programming

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Study notes
records.text: Object Oriented Programming Design with objects, then trace the Java rules that make the design run. Java 17 is the baseline for these examples; modern interface rules and Java 25 constructor differences are explained where relevant. The official allocation is six items. Draw separate boxes for reference variables and objects, then trace constructor and field state changes. For a call, check visibility and declared type first, overload selection second, runtime overriding third. Practice one small interface hierarchy with valid implementations, a checked exception and a safe downcast; repair compiler errors before predicting output.

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Practice questions
records.text: Object Oriented Programming

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Revision outline
records.text: Object Oriented Programming

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Objects, classes and responsibilities
records.text: An object has identity, state and behavior. State is stored in fields; behavior is provided by methods. A Rectangle object may hold width and height and answer getArea() or getPerimeter(). Two objects can have equal fields and still be distinct objects. A class defines their common structure and behavior; an object is a particular instance. Choose classes around responsibilities: an account controls its own balance, a transaction records a payment, and a service coordinates them. Objects send messages through method calls such as obj.add(). They can delegate work to other objects; saying that objects cannot manage their own state is misleading. Procedural and object oriented designs both support reuse; global shared data is not compulsory in procedural programming. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Four principles and the difference between hiding and abstraction
records.text: Encapsulation groups related state and operations and controls access. Information hiding keeps implementation decisions behind a stable interface. Abstraction presents the essential operations while omitting details irrelevant to the caller. These ideas overlap: a private balance plus deposit(amount) can demonstrate all three, depending on what the question emphasizes. Inheritance forms a subtype relationship and may reuse implementation. Polymorphism lets code using a common type invoke behavior appropriate to different concrete objects. Prefer a precise mechanism over a vague slogan: wrapping fields and methods points to encapsulation; showing what an operation does while hiding how points to abstraction. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Create objects and distinguish references from instances
records.text: Student s; declares a reference variable; it creates no Student object. Student s=new Student(); allocates and initializes an instance. Member access uses s.name or s.study(), subject to visibility. Assignment t=s copies a reference, so both can refer to the same object; changing that object through t is observable through s. Java passes all arguments by value. Passing a reference copies it: a method may modify the shared object, but assigning its parameter to a new object does not reassign the caller’s reference. The runtime may reclaim unreachable objects; collection timing is unspecified. Reachable object cycles can matter for retention, but an unreachable cycle can be collected. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — UML class and instance notation
records.text: A UML class box normally contains name, attributes and operations. Visibility uses + public, - private and # protected. A field can be written name:String and an operation getName():String. A constructor Student(String,String,String,int) requires three strings and an integer, so an age argument "25" has the wrong type. An instance is conventionally labeled with an underlined instanceName:ClassName, such as sara:Student. Class notation describes a type; instance notation describes one particular object and may show its slot values. Underlining static class features has a different purpose; read the whole notation rather than assuming every underline means the same thing. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Variables, defaults, scope and initialization
records.text: The introductory three-way grouping is local, instance and class/static variables. Locals occur in methods, constructors or blocks; they must be definitely assigned before use and cannot have public/private/protected modifiers. Fields occur in a class outside method bodies; non-static fields belong to each instance, while static fields belong to the class. Declaration location alone does not distinguish instance and static fields. Java fields and array elements receive defaults: numeric zero, char '\u0000', boolean false and references null. A local int t; followed by printing t is a compilation error. Initializers such as int a=10,b=10; assign initial values. A final local is permitted; final is not an access modifier. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Primitive types, literals and conversions
records.text: Java has byte, short, int, long, float, double, char and boolean. Signed integer widths are 8,16,32,64 bits respectively. byte ranges from -128 to 127; short from -32768 to 32767. char is an unsigned 16-bit UTF-16 code unit and can hold a digit, letter or symbol, not a whole String. enum and String are reference types. A compatible widening conversion often needs no cast; narrowing usually needs an explicit cast and may lose information. Widening an int to float can lose precision, so “widening never loses information” is false. Arithmetic promotes char, byte and short to int in many expressions. boolean does not convert to or from numeric truth values; if(0) and for(...;0;...) are invalid. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Static members, static blocks and final
records.text: static gives one field per loaded class, shared by its instances. If count starts at zero and every constructor increments it, three creations leave count=3. Prefer ClassName.count and ClassName.utility(). A static method has no current instance, but can still use instance members through an explicit object reference. A static initializer runs during class initialization, before the class’s first relevant active use, not simply whenever a file is loaded. final prevents reassignment of a variable, overriding of a method or extension of a class. A final reference may still refer to a mutable object. A shared mathematical PI is a good static final candidate; a student name normally belongs to an instance. A calculation using only parameters may be static. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Access control and package boundaries
records.text: For ordinary members: private restricts access to the declaring class/nest; no modifier grants package access; protected grants same-package access plus qualified subclass access; public is widest, provided the declaring type itself is accessible. Top-level classes/interfaces may be public or package-private, not protected/private. Member types have additional visibility possibilities. Across packages, a subclass accessing a protected instance member must do so through its own inherited context or an appropriate subclass-typed receiver, not any arbitrary superclass object. protected therefore does not mean “subclasses only”: unrelated classes in the same package also have access. A class’s own main method can access private fields of an instance of that class. Object Oriented Programming module JLS 21: protected access

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Constructors and missing default constructors
records.text: A constructor has the class’s exact name and no return type, not even void. It initializes the new object and can be overloaded or private. A private constructor can support a factory or controlled singleton creation; it does not mean the class can never create an object internally. If a class declares no constructor, Java supplies a default constructor. If Circle(double r) is declared, new Circle() fails unless a no-argument constructor is also declared. Constructors are not inherited or overridden. They may contain return; but cannot return an expression. Fields get their default values before ordinary constructor initialization, rather than receiving defaults only because a default constructor was generated. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Constructor chaining and initialization order
records.text: Under Java 17 rules, an explicit this(args) or super(args) invocation must be the first constructor statement. this invokes another constructor in the same class; super invokes the immediate superclass constructor. A constructor cannot explicitly invoke both. If there is no explicit delegation, an implicit super() is inserted; a matching accessible no-argument parent constructor must exist. Trace parent construction first, then subclass field initializers and instance blocks in order, then the relevant subclass constructor body. With consistent class and constructor names and this(5) chaining in the FinalExam example, the parent sets num1=4, the subclass initializes num=3, this(5) sets num=25, and the no-arg body sets num1=num, leaving 25. Java 25 permits restricted statements before explicit constructor invocation; the older first-statement rule must be version qualified. Object Oriented Programming module Java 25: flexible constructor bodies

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Methods, getters and setters
records.text: A method has modifiers, return type, name, parameter list and body: public int getAge(){return age;}. A void method returns no value. Parameters name the inputs in the declaration; arguments supply values at a call. An instance method can be invoked as object.method(), or with an implicit this inside suitable instance context. An accessor/getter returns information; a mutator/setter changes state. Encapsulation does not require blindly generating setters for every field: validate changes and expose only useful operations. For a bank account, deposit must reject negative amounts. A private field cannot normally be accessed directly by a separately declared subclass, even with this.field; use a permitted parent operation. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Method overloading and compile-time selection
records.text: Overloaded methods share a name but have different parameter types, counts or type order. Return type alone is insufficient in Java and C++. Overloads can also arise through inherited methods; “same class only” is a teaching simplification. f(int), f(double) and f(int,int) are distinct, but changing a parameter name does not create an overload. The compiler selects the applicable signature from the declared argument types and conversions. int arguments usually choose an exact int overload rather than a wider double overload. A return type is not part of an ordinary Java method signature. Distinguish a different signature from overriding an inherited signature. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Inheritance and useful relationships
records.text: class Dog extends Animal declares a subclass/derived/child of a superclass/base/parent. A class extends one direct class and can implement multiple interfaces. Single, multilevel and hierarchical inheritance mean one parent, a chain, and several children of one parent. Java does not permit class Dog extends Animal,Mammal. Use inheritance when a subtype can satisfy the parent’s contract: Dog is an Animal. For shared Pet.name and speak(), put common state/contract in Pet, specialized fetch() in Dog, and appropriate speak() implementations in Dog and Cat. Composition represents has-a, such as Car containing Engine. Reuse alone does not justify an invalid is-a relationship. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Overriding and restrictions
records.text: A subclass overrides an eligible inherited instance method with the same signature and a compatible return type; a covariant reference return may be a subtype. Visibility cannot become more restrictive, and checked exceptions cannot be broadened incompatibly. @Override requests compiler checking; Java has no override keyword. Constructors, final methods, static methods and private parent methods are not overridden. A same-signature child method matching a private parent method is an independent declaration, not runtime overriding and not ordinary static-method hiding. An abstract inherited method is implemented by an overriding method in a concrete subclass. Merely reusing a name in two unrelated classes does not establish overriding. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Dynamic dispatch: declared type versus actual type
records.text: For Animal a=new Dog(), Animal is the declared type and Dog the actual type. The declared type determines which member operations compile. If fetch() exists only in Dog, a.fetch() fails compilation. For an eligible overridden sound(), a.sound() invokes Dog.sound() at runtime. To solve dispatch questions: check the declaration and visibility, determine the compile-time signature, then identify the object’s runtime class and its most specific override. An array Animal[]{new Dog(),new Cat()} can call speak() on each using one loop. New subclasses can supply behavior without rewriting this generic loop, which is the practical meaning of extensibility. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — this, super, fields and static hiding
records.text: Java this denotes the current object; this.name=name distinguishes a field from a parameter. super.name selects a hidden superclass field; super.sound() directly requests the parent implementation. It does not create a second parent object. An unqualified instance call may dispatch dynamically; an explicit super call is different. Fields are hidden rather than dynamically overridden, and same-signature static methods hide rather than override. With Animal a=new Dog(), a.staticMethod() resolves using Animal’s compile-time type. Prefer Animal.staticMethod() for clarity. Java this and super are unavailable as current-instance references in static context. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — C++ this and language-specific assumptions
records.text: In ordinary C++17 non-static member functions, this is a pointer to the object on which the function is called; this->field selects a member. It is often explained as an implicit object argument to a member function call. It is not an argument passed to member variables, and a static member function has no this pointer. C++ runtime polymorphism requires a virtual function when calling through a base pointer/reference. C++ may inherit multiple classes; Java permits multiple interface types instead. C++ object-value assignment can copy an object, whereas assigning Java class variables copies references. Never transfer Java dispatch or memory-management assumptions to a C++ question without checking the code. C++ draft: this pointer Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Abstract classes and concrete implementations
records.text: An abstract class cannot be directly instantiated but can define fields, constructors, abstract methods and concrete methods. It need not contain an abstract method. An abstract method has no body; abstract and final conflict because an operation cannot require overriding while forbidding it. A concrete subclass must provide or inherit implementations of all required abstract methods; otherwise it must itself be abstract. If parent declares abstract String welcome(), a String welcome() implementation is required; int welcome() is incompatible, and welcome(int) merely adds an overload. A valid class can contain both the required implementation and an unrelated overload. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Interfaces: contracts and modern Java
records.text: interface Payable{double getPaymentAmount();} declares an abstract public operation. class Invoice implements Payable must provide public double getPaymentAmount(), perhaps returning getQuantity()*getPricePerItem(). A class can extend a superclass and implement zero or more interfaces. An interface can extend several interfaces. No interface instance fields or constructors exist; fields are implicitly public static final. A method declaration without private, default or static is implicitly public abstract. Modern interfaces may also have default/static method bodies, and Java 9+ private helper methods. Not every interface method must lack a body in modern Java. Implementations must satisfy all inherited abstract contracts; they may inherit suitable public implementations. Interfaces cannot be instantiated directly, but references may hold implementing objects, anonymous implementations or suitable functional-interface lambdas. Object Oriented Programming module JLS 21: interface methods and conflicts

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Conflicting interface methods and abstract class choice
records.text: Use an abstract class for shared state, construction and common implementation; use an interface for a capability across unrelated classes and multiple type inheritance. A concrete inherited class method takes precedence over an interface default. An inherited abstract class declaration can require a concrete subclass to implement the operation rather than silently adopting a default. Unrelated interfaces providing conflicting defaults require an explicit resolution; interfaces do not remove every diamond ambiguity. If two compatible interfaces merely declare the same abstract signature, one public implementation can satisfy both. If return types or other contracts conflict, additional declarations may still be impossible. The answer to “same method in abstract class and interface” depends on whether each is abstract or implemented and whether their signatures are compatible. Object Oriented Programming module JLS 21: interface methods and conflicts

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Casts and instanceof
records.text: Upcasting a subclass reference to a superclass is implicit and does not change the object. A downcast may pass compile-time type checks yet fail at runtime. Car a=new Car(); Ferrari f=(Ferrari)a; throws ClassCastException before subsequent drive() or brake() calls. It does not turn a plain Car into a Ferrari. Use if(a instanceof Ferrari) before narrowing when the dynamic type is uncertain. null instanceof Ferrari is false; casting null yields null, although dereferencing it fails. For Object obj="Hello", (String)obj succeeds and (Integer)obj throws ClassCastException. A literal 'Hello' is invalid Java syntax; use double quotes for a string literal before tracing the program. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Identity, equals, toString and immutable strings
records.text: For object references, == tests identity; equals invokes the class’s equality policy. Object.equals uses identity unless overridden; String.equals compares character content. Equal objects must have equal hashCode values when that contract is implemented. toString gives a textual representation, not an equality test. Java String objects are immutable. text += " World" assigns a reference to a new concatenated result and can print Hello World without mutating the original String object. final class String prevents subclassing; final alone does not make arbitrary objects immutable. charAt(index) returns a char; length() counts UTF-16 units; substring(begin,end) excludes end. Character.toUpperCase(ch) converts a character, and matches(String regex) takes a regular-expression parameter named regex. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Expressions: numbers, bits and text output
records.text: Java evaluates operands left to right while respecting precedence. With n=6,m=15,p=3, n-=m then n*=p leaves -27. 6-2+10%4+7 is 13. In 8-2*5*(3+9/3)+6/3, the result is -50. Integer 6/4 is 1; double 6.0/4 is 1.5. Unlike C++, Java % also accepts floating-point operands. For bitwise values, write binary columns: 11&9=9; 9^3=10; 10|12=14. && and || short circuit Boolean operands; & and | can also operate on Boolean values without short circuiting. Printing Boolean true gives lowercase true, not 1 or uppercase TRUE. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Increment order and the character-space trap
records.text: Starting x=5, printing x++ then ++x gives 5 then 7. For int y=++x*x--, Java uses 6*6=36 and leaves x=5. System.out.println(x + ' ' + y) then adds char space’s numeric value 32, so it prints 73. To print separated values, use x + " " + y instead. Once a String operand is encountered, + concatenates in left-to-right groups: 1+2+"x" gives "3x", while "x"+1+2 gives "x12". When x and y are numeric, x + ' ' + y performs numeric addition; x + " " + y concatenates a separating space. Use the expression’s operand types to determine the result. JLS 21: expression order and string addition

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Control flow traces and exact printing
records.text: while and for pre-test and may execute zero times; do-while post-tests and executes once. break exits the loop; continue skips its remaining body and then runs a for update. Traditional colon-style switch labels fall through without break. Choice 1 printing Hello then case 2 printing you and breaking is followed by Goodbye outside the switch; default is skipped. Count executions independently from printing. For i=0..4, if(i%2==0) print(i+" "); followed unconditionally by print(i+1); produces "0 122 344 5". A loop summing j=1..10 yields 55. In if(a)... else if(a&&b)..., the second condition can never be true on a path reaching it because a is already false. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Arrays: creation, bounds and ragged rows
records.text: int[] a=new int[5]; and int a[]={1,2,3}; are valid. int[] a={}; creates a zero-length array; explicit new is unnecessary in a declaration initializer. int a[],b; makes only a an array; int[] c,d; makes both arrays. Array objects have fixed length after creation, although the reference may be reassigned. Elements have a declared common component type, which may be a superclass/interface. Valid indices are 0..a.length-1; an invalid access throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Java two-dimensional arrays are arrays of arrays and may be ragged: {{12,-9,8},{7,14},{-32,-1,0}} has row lengths 3,2,3. Java does not expose a portable physical contiguity guarantee, so a language-level answer should not rely on raw addresses. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Array algorithms, sort and copy APIs
records.text: For int[] a=new int[4], setting a[i]=i*3 and accumulating yields 0+3+6+9=18. To average an array, sum every element and divide by its length using floating arithmetic; handle zero length separately. Floating representations and printing can differ from a rounded mathematical result. For the six-value example, the mathematical average is 98.8/6, approximately 16.46666667; the exact printed string also depends on floating representation and formatting. java.util.Arrays.sort(a) sorts in place. System.arraycopy(src,srcPos,dst,dstPos,length) copies into an existing array; its exact spelling uses lowercase c. Arrays.copyOf(a,n) creates a copy. a=b merely aliases the same array. Random access is the reliable array advantage; size is bounded by implementation/resources, not unlimited. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Packages, imports and command-line tools
records.text: package p; precedes imports; imports precede top-level type declarations. import p.*; imports accessible types from p as needed, not types in p.sub automatically. Packages organize names and control access; hierarchical spelling does not grant special access between a package and its subpackages. java.lang is implicitly imported; java.util supplies utilities; java.io supplies I/O; java.awt includes Button and Checkbox. Ordinary compilation uses javac Test.java, producing bytecode, then java Test launches the class. Modern Java can also launch a source file using java Test.java; distinguish source-file launch from running a compiled class. For ordinary public top-level types, filename and type name match. Capitalized class names and lowercase method names are conventions, not universal syntax requirements. Java identifiers are case sensitive; $ is allowed but @ is not an identifier character. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Exception hierarchy and checked obligations
records.text: Throwable is the root of throwable values, with Exception and Error branches. RuntimeException and Error subclasses are unchecked; other throwable classes are checked. IOException, FileNotFoundException and SQLException are standard checked examples. ArithmeticException, NullPointerException, ClassCastException and array bounds exceptions are unchecked. A missing semicolon or undeclared variable is a compile-time source error, not a checked exception. Checked does not mean the exception occurs at compile time: the compiler checks an obligation to catch or declare it, while an actual throw occurs at runtime. A custom exception can extend Exception or RuntimeException. Error normally signals serious conditions for which routine recovery is inappropriate; it is not technically impossible to catch an Error. Object Oriented Programming module JLS 21: checked and unchecked exceptions

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — throw, throws and catch selection
records.text: throw new IOException("message") actively throws a value; throws IOException in a signature declares a possible checked exception. A caller must handle or propagate checked obligations. try encloses guarded operations; a matching catch handles the thrown type or a subtype. Execution skips the remainder of the try when a throw occurs. Catch blocks are considered in source order. Place FileNotFoundException before IOException and IOException before Exception; a general catch before a subtype catch makes that later handler unreachable and prevents compilation. If no catch matches, the exception propagates outward and an uncaught exception terminates its thread. Multiple catch blocks are allowed; catch(IOException | SQLException e) handles alternatives, which must not be related by subclassing. Object Oriented Programming module JLS 21: checked and unchecked exceptions

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — finally, cleanup and diagnostic information
records.text: finally normally executes after try and any selected catch, including when leaving by return or propagating an exception. It is not guaranteed if the process/JVM exits or crashes, or control never leaves the try. A return expression is evaluated before finally; a finally return overrides the pending return and can suppress an exception, so avoid that pattern. try-with-resources closes AutoCloseable resources even on exceptional exit. getMessage returns the message, toString normally includes type and message, and printStackTrace shows exception information and recorded call frames for diagnosis. Tests should cover expected success, caught failures and propagation. Exception handling does not replace validation or correct an algorithm’s logic automatically. Object Oriented Programming module JLS 21: try and finally

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Streams, GUI events and JDBC practice
records.text: InputStream/OutputStream read and write bytes; Reader/Writer handle text characters through an encoding. Close resources deterministically. A read returning -1 signals end-of-stream. A GUI event source notifies registered listeners; a button can call an ActionListener’s actionPerformed method. In Swing, update components on the event dispatch thread and keep handlers short so the interface remains responsive. Object Oriented Programming module Oracle: event dispatch thread

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — JDBC flow from user action to database
records.text: A JDBC operation obtains a Connection, prepares SQL, binds values, executes and processes results, then closes resources. For PreparedStatement ps=con.prepareStatement("SELECT name FROM Student WHERE id=?"), ps.setInt(1,id) binds the first parameter. executeQuery returns a ResultSet; rs.next() moves to each row before reading columns. executeUpdate returns an affected-row count for updates. Parameter binding keeps values separate from SQL syntax. Catch or declare SQLException. When several writes form one operation, disable auto-commit, commit on success and roll back on failure. A GUI handler should delegate a slow database operation away from its UI thread, then display the result through the appropriate UI mechanism. Oracle: prepared JDBC statements

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Legacy applets and lifecycle questions
records.text: In the historical applet model, Java code was embedded in an HTML document and executed by a compatible JVM host/plugin or applet viewer. init initializes once; start follows initialization and resumes activity; stop suspends activity when the host deactivates it; destroy performs final cleanup before unloading. paint draws content and is not a constructor. Study applets as historical Java concepts rather than modern browser deployment tools. destroy is not defined exclusively as “browser shuts down”: the host may destroy an applet on unloading, and abrupt process termination does not guarantee cleanup. A JVM alone is also not the complete browser embedding environment. Oracle: applet lifecycle callbacks

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Android Activity, Intent, manifest and layouts
records.text: An Android Activity is a component providing an entry point for user interaction, often corresponding to a screen. An Intent describes a requested action or explicit target; extras carry values between activities. For example, putExtra("id",17) attaches an ID for the destination to read. A content provider shares structured data, while a broadcast receiver handles broadcast messages; neither is the ordinary mechanism for starting an activity with parameters. Android: Intents and extras Android: Activities

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Android app declarations and packaging
records.text: AndroidManifest.xml declares essential app metadata such as components, permissions and intent filters. It is not executable code and does not contain all source or layout details. Traditional view-based layout containers such as LinearLayout and RelativeLayout derive from android.view.ViewGroup, which contains child views. An .apk is an Android package archive used for installation and runtime contents. “Android Package Kit” is a common exam expansion; Android’s documentation calls it an Android package. A manifest describes the package, while layout resources describe views. Use these distinctions to compare Android application structure with Java language concepts. Android: manifest Android: ViewGroup Android: packages

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Validate Java syntax before tracing
records.text: Check exact Java spelling and syntax: extends differs from Extends, println differs from printIn/printin, constructor names must match class names, and braces and operators such as <= and == affect validity and behavior. Java is case sensitive: an invalid program may not compile even when a possible trace seems clear. For a valid Java loop with i=2,4,6,8,10 that prints i*i only when i%4==0, the printed values are 16 and 64. A valid implementation can define public String welcome() and additionally overload welcome(int). Identify an implementation by its complete declarations and method bodies. Check the required signature before selecting an implementation. A rounded mathematical mean is not necessarily the exact Java printed output. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Apply Java rules under explicit assumptions
records.text: Several Java statements can be valid at once: a static constant and a parameter-only utility may both be suitable static members; multiple array declarations/initializers can be legal; an abstract class may contain a complete interface implementation. Encapsulation and abstraction overlap, so choose only when the requested emphasis is specific. An interface supports multiple type inheritance and abstraction. “All methods are public abstract” applies only under a restricted abstract-declaration or legacy interpretation. Java protected also grants access within the same package, so it cannot enforce “only subclasses.” No keyword implements overriding: it is recognized from compatible declarations, and @Override is an annotation. For C++ this, ordinary non-static member functions have an implicit object; variables do not receive a hidden argument. Object Oriented Programming module

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Language classifications and portability
records.text: Under the conventional introductory generation taxonomy, general-purpose high-level languages such as C++, Java, Python and Perl are third generation. The taxonomy is separate from object orientation and from compilation versus interpretation. Java source normally compiles to JVM bytecode, and a compatible JVM plus libraries supports portability across systems. Portability still depends on compatible APIs, versions and environment assumptions; it is not an unconditional guarantee for any program on any device. Java supports objects and classes but also primitive values. “Difficult to learn” is a subjective judgment rather than a technical language property. Syntax conventions, bytecode portability and runtime implementation must be distinguished. Object Oriented Programming module University of Rhode Island: conventional language generation taxonomy

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Identifiers, literals and source comments
records.text: An identifier is a programmer-chosen name for an entity such as a class, method or variable. A reserved keyword has a language-defined role and cannot be used as an ordinary identifier. A literal writes a value directly, such as an integer, floating-point number, quoted character, quoted string or Boolean value. A single-line Java comment begins with // and continues to the end of that line. A block comment begins with /* and ends with */. A documentation comment begins with /** and ends with */ and can be processed by Javadoc. Comment text does not execute as program statements. For ordinary ASCII Java identifiers, the first character is a letter, underscore or dollar sign; later characters may also be digits. A reserved keyword is not an ordinary identifier, and a lone underscore is not a valid identifier in Java 17. Object Oriented Programming module · page 4 Java SE 17 JLS — Identifiers

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Java 17 floating-point evaluation and printed doubles
records.text: Java 17 float uses IEEE 754 binary32, and double uses binary64. Successive multiplications group from left to right. Each floating-point operation rounds to its representable result, using nearest-value rounding with ties to even; regrouping a product can change its result. PrintStream.print(double) converts the stored value through String.valueOf and Double.toString. For finite nonzero magnitudes from 0.001 inclusive to 10000000 exclusive, the standard decimal form uses at least one fractional digit and only the further digits needed to distinguish the value from adjacent doubles. println(double) also adds a line terminator. This is not fixed-decimal-place formatting. A print call emits its value without inserting a separator or ending the line. A println call emits its value followed by a line terminator. Spaces must come from the supplied text or explicit output operations; adjacent calls do not automatically separate their values. Java SE 17 JLS — Floating-point expressions and multiplication Java SE 17 — Double.toString(double) Java SE 17 — PrintStream.print(double)

records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Expression results, assignment and control headers
records.text: Java relational comparisons (<, <=, >, >=) and equality tests (==, !=) produce primitive boolean truth values. Their result is not an integer truth code or a value of the numeric operand type. The conditional expression condition ? whenTrue : whenFalse requires a boolean or Boolean condition. It evaluates only the selected alternative. An integer or floating-point first operand is a compile-time error. Assignments group right to left: a=b=c assigns c to b, then the resulting value to a. A later assignment overwrites an earlier value. Compound assignments update the left variable using the indicated operation. Prefix ++ and -- update a variable before supplying its value; postfix forms supply the old value before the update. Multiplication, division and remainder bind before addition and subtraction; same-level binary arithmetic groups left to right. Integer division truncates toward zero. Unary plus preserves its numeric operand’s value. A while header is while(condition). A basic for header is for(initialization; condition; update). A do-while statement places its condition after the body. An if selects its true branch or, when present, its else branch; only the selected branch executes. For Boolean values, ! reverses true and false, && is true only when both operands are true, and || is true when at least one is true. Short-circuit evaluation skips an unnecessary right operand. For each binary column, integral & produces 1 only for two 1 bits, | produces 1 for either 1 bit, and ^ produces 1 for differing bits. An unlabeled break leaves the innermost enclosing loop or switch. continue moves to the next iteration step, while return leaves the current method and may supply a return value. These transfers have different destinations; return is not merely a loop exit. records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Core package membership and text values
records.text: The base Exception class is java.lang.Exception. It does not belong to java.io merely because some subclasses represent I/O failures. Package membership and position in an inheritance hierarchy are separate facts. Calendar and Date are classes in java.util; Collection is an interface in that package. java.util also contains Arrays and Scanner. java.net supplies networking facilities; java.awt supplies the Button and Checkbox UI controls described in the package overview. A String represents a sequence of UTF-16 code units. A single char represents one code unit rather than an entire String. String objects are immutable; changing a reference to another String does not modify the original text value. A double-quoted string literal denotes a String object. new String(existingString) creates a String with the same text; new String(charArray) copies the array’s characters into an immutable String. A single-quoted literal denotes one char, so several characters enclosed together in single quotes cannot supply a String. Character.toUpperCase(ch) supplies the uppercase equivalent where one exists; Character.toLowerCase(ch) supplies the lowercase equivalent. Character.isDigit(ch) tests whether a character is a digit and returns boolean. Character.toString(ch) supplies a one-character String rather than converting letter case. records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Inheritance boundaries and whole-part relationships
records.text: In Java’s class-declaration terminology, constructors are not members and are not inherited. A subclass can invoke superclass construction; this does not turn the superclass constructor into an inherited subclass method. Aggregation models one instance grouping other instances as a whole with parts. It is an object-relationship concept, not a method-dispatch rule. Inheritance instead relates a specialized class to a general class; overridden operations can then provide polymorphic behavior. records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Question 5 · SM0073
records.text: SM0073 Question 5 OOP23 What is the output of the following Java fragment code? int n = 6, m = 15, p = 3; n -= m; n *= p; System.out.print(n); Respect operator grouping and operand types, then trace each operation in evaluation order. A 27 B 3 C 24 D -27 -27. Start with n=6. The subtraction assignment n-=m computes 6-15, leaving n=-9. The multiplication assignment then uses that updated value: -9*3=-27. OOP23 includes this exact trace. The sign cannot become positive because only subtraction followed by multiplication by positive three occurs. A incorrect 27 discards the negative sign produced when 15 is subtracted from 6. B incorrect Three is the unchanged multiplier p, not the updated value of n that is printed. records.title: Object Oriented Programming — Question 85 · Q00492
records.text: Q00492 Question 85 OOP27 OOP26 OOP03 Which is an inherent property of Java arrays? Here “Code Optimization” means a guarantee that merely introducing an array makes every algorithm run faster. Check declared dimensions, initializer shape, fixed length and zero-based index bounds. A Code Optimization B Random access C Size No-Limit D Both A and B Random access is the concrete array advantage. Arrays provide indexed random access, so B states the inherent capability. They have a fixed length after creation and are bounded by implementation limits and available resources, so unlimited size is false. An array is a storage structure, not a guarantee that every algorithm becomes faster: allocating an unused array cannot improve a computation that does not need it. A therefore fails the stated guarantee, and combining it with B does not make D correct. A incorrect The stated universal speedup does not follow from array storage; adding an unused allocation does not improve the algorithm’s required computation. B correct Indexed random access is a direct array capability. C incorrect Array length is fixed after creation and constrained by implementation limits and resources. D incorrect This conjunction includes the false universal optimization guarantee, even though random access itself is true.
