records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Multiplexing and channelization
records.text: Multiplexing combines multiple input streams onto a shared link; demultiplexing separates them at the receiver. It differs from broadcasting one message to many destinations. FDM assigns distinct frequency bands with suitable guard spacing; WDM assigns different optical wavelengths. TDM allocates time slots: synchronous TDM reserves recurrent slots even if an input is idle, while statistical TDM allocates according to demand and needs identification. FDMA and TDMA allocate frequencies or time among users; CDMA separates coded signals. Physical multiplexing is different from transport port multiplexing. Combining signals onto a shared link is multiplexing; distinguish it from point-to-point connectivity, broadcast, synchronization and multicast. Data Communication and Computer Networking module

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Identify networking layers and addressing assumptions
records.text: First identify the exact layer, protocol and scope. Flow/error control can exist at both link and transport layers; MAC addresses can be locally administered; bridges and switches both operate at layer 2. A LAN can use public or private unicast space. UDP and IP are both connectionless. Session dialogs and TCP connections are distinct senses of connection. Distinguish the protocol, layer and scope before treating these descriptions as exclusive. A host address without a prefix does not determine capacity unless the question explicitly assumes historical classful addressing. A subnet count needs a parent block. Excluding subnet zero and the all-ones subnet is an obsolete convention; apply it only when explicitly stated. Choose a networking concept by its definition rather than by repeated distractors. Read complete, unambiguous option labels before matching them to networking concepts. Data Communication and Computer Networking module

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Independent routing classifications
records.text: Adaptive or dynamic routing changes routes in response to updated network information; nonadaptive or static routing uses configured choices. Distributed routing means routers perform computations using exchanged information instead of requiring one central route computation. These properties do not imply random next-hop selection: the path-selection rule is a separate classification. Data Communication and Computer Networking module · page 19 RFC 1058 — Distance-vector computation and topology changes

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Management, traffic service and application transport bindings
records.text: SNMP means Simple Network Management Protocol. Its management applications monitor and control managed devices, such as hosts and routers, by exchanging management information with their agents. This device-management role differs from transferring email, resolving names or mapping an IP address to a MAC address. In the conventional service bindings, FTP control, SMTP mail transfer and Telnet remote terminals use TCP. DNS supports both UDP and TCP on port 53; it is not exclusively a UDP service. The application protocol’s service role is distinct from the transport carrying its messages. Quality of service (QoS) controls traffic treatment to meet objectives such as throughput, delay, jitter or loss. Classification, queue scheduling and allocation of buffer or bandwidth resources implement such treatment. QoS concerns delivered service behavior; scalability concerns accommodating growth, and security concerns unauthorized actions. RFC 3411 — SNMP architecture, section 1.2 Data Communication and Computer Networking module · page 28 RFC 2475 — Differentiated-services architecture

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Why IPv4 conservation and IPv6 matter
records.text: The finite IPv4 address space has faced allocation scarcity. Private addressing with NAT conserves public IPv4 addresses, while IPv6 provides a much larger address space. Data Communication and Computer Networking module · page 19

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Computer networks and network interfaces
records.text: A computer network connects computers or other devices so they can exchange information and share resources such as files, storage and printers. The interconnection uses both hardware and software; neither hardware alone nor software alone is the definition of the whole network. NIC expands to Network Interface Card. It is the host’s network interface, providing the connection through which the host sends and receives network signals. A cable connector attaches the medium to that interface; it is distinct from an intermediary switch or router. CRC expands to Cyclic Redundancy Check. Data Communication and Computer Networking module · page 22 Data Communication and Computer Networking module · page 23 Data Communication and Computer Networking module · page 13

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Network-access technologies and geographic use
records.text: Ethernet and Token Ring are traditional LAN technologies. X.25 and Frame Relay are traditional WAN technologies. TCP/IP can run over different network-access technologies; its Internet-layer packet service does not require one particular link medium or frame format. Data Communication and Computer Networking module · page 26

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Interface addresses and transport-number namespaces
records.text: An IP address identifies a network interface rather than limiting a whole computer to one address. A computer or router can have several interfaces and addresses. Under a supplied IPv4 prefix, leading bits identify the network and the remaining bits identify an address within that network; a MAC address is a separate link-layer identifier. TCP and UDP port fields are 16 bits, allowing numbers from 0 through 65535. Well-known ports are 0–1023, registered ports are 1024–49151, and dynamic/private ports are 49152–65535. Client endpoints can use dynamically selected ports instead of every application requiring a well-known assignment. These port numbers are distinct from the IP version and upper-protocol fields. A bridge or switch’s MAC address table is its learned forwarding database: it associates MAC addresses with ports for frame forwarding. It differs from an ARP cache, which associates an IPv4 next hop with a link address, and from a routing table, which selects next hops for IP prefixes. A common IPv6 unicast subnet uses a 64-bit subnet prefix and a 64-bit interface identifier. This split does not make the complete address 64 bits: it remains 128 bits. Special uses and explicitly different prefix lengths must be considered separately. Data Communication and Computer Networking module · page 18 Data Communication and Computer Networking module · page 28 Cisco — Configure MAC address learning and forwarding tables RFC 7421 — Analysis of the 64-bit boundary in IPv6 addressing

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Physical signaling and legacy Ethernet cable roles
records.text: Fiber-optic links can use near-infrared light. The selected optical wavelength is part of the link’s physical signaling specification, just as connectors and electrical signal levels are physical-interface specifications. This does not require every fiber link to use the same wavelength. For legacy fixed Ethernet port roles, PCs and router Ethernet endpoints use the same endpoint role, while ordinary switch ports use the opposite role. Thus a direct router-to-PC link uses crossover wiring; PC-to-switch or router-to-switch uses straight-through wiring. Automatic MDI-X can remove the need to choose the crossover manually. Ethernet switches can have fiber-optic interfaces with suitable optical transceivers. A forwarding role therefore does not impose a copper-only restriction: distinguish what the device does with frames from the physical medium used by its ports. Intermodulation distortion occurs when multiple signals interact through a nonlinear component and generate unwanted combination-frequency products. Its mechanism differs from random thermal motion, adjacent-channel leakage and an isolated impulse disturbance. records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 1 · Q00016
records.text: Q00016 Question 1 NET32 NET08 NET06 Which term describes combining multiple analogue or digital input signals for transmission over one shared medium? Compare the signal mechanism, medium properties or transmission direction against the definitions and stated physical assumptions. A Point-to-point B Broadcasting C Synchronization D Multiplexing Multiplexing Multiplexing combines separate input streams so they can share a transmission link. The receiver uses demultiplexing to separate them again. This operation concerns sharing link capacity, whereas broadcasting concerns the recipients of a message. Point-to-point describes the endpoints of a link, and synchronization coordinates timing. The option supplies the required operation while preserving those distinctions. A incorrect Point-to-point joins two endpoints and does not mean combining input signals onto a shared link. B incorrect Broadcast sends a message to all destinations in scope rather than combining multiple input streams. C incorrect Synchronization coordinates timing; it is not the multiplexing operation defined by the stem. D correct Multiplexing combines multiple streams for a shared link and is precisely the operation described.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 2 · Q00036
records.text: Q00036 Question 2 NET31 NET32 A traditional phone call is an example of Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule. A Packet switching B Multiplexing C Broadcasting D Circuit switching Circuit switching A traditional circuit telephone call exemplifies establishment, continuous use of a dedicated path, and release. This applies to the traditional circuit service assumed by the stem, rather than all modern telephone implementations. Evidence: PDF 20, 20, 20. A incorrect Packets are discrete rather than the dedicated circuit described (PDF 20, 20, 20.) B incorrect Multiplexing shares a link and may underlie telephony but does not name its switching service (PDF 20, 20, 20.) C incorrect Broadcasting does not establish a dedicated pairwise call (PDF 20, 20, 20.) D correct Dedicated establishment, transfer and disconnect match the call (PDF 20, 20, 20.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 3 · Q00050
records.text: Q00050 Question 3 NET20 NET21 Assume you are searching for information and typed the domain name: www.mysearchexample.com on your browser, having an IP address 192.108.110.1. Since internet communication is based on an IP address, the domain name has to be translated to its corresponding IP address. Which of the following is responsible for the translation? Separate address width, syntax, reserved scope and the supplied prefix or historical classful convention. A DNS B SMTP C FTP D DHCP DNS The needed operation is name resolution. The module identifies DNS as Domain Name Service and contrasts external DNS naming with locally stored host addresses; together these support the name-to-address lookup. Evidence: PDF 18, 65, 18. A correct DNS is the named external naming service (PDF 18, 65, 18.) B incorrect SMTP is electronic mail, not name lookup (PDF 18, 65, 18.) C incorrect FTP is file transfer, not name lookup (PDF 18, 65, 18.) D incorrect Page28 explicitly expands DHCP as Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol, separately from DNS (Domain Name Service). The external naming service discussed on page65 is DNS, the operation requested, rather than the separately named host-configuration protocol. The expansion alone is not a full account of DHCP operation.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 4 · Q00061
records.text: Q00061 Question 4 NET03 NET19 Which one of the following is not correct about networking models? Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule. A TCP/IP model is a protocol model B A reference model has no implementation specification C A network designer can use either of TCP/IP or OSL, or both D Open system interconnection (OSI) is a protocol model OSI is a reference model, not itself an implemented protocol suite NET03 distinguishes an abstract reference model from an implemented protocol suite. D incorrectly calls OSI a protocol model in that distinction. TCP/IP supplies the implemented suite, and designers can use models as architectural guides. B is valid when understood as the model itself not providing executable implementation details, rather than denying all interface descriptions. A incorrect TCP/IP describes an implemented protocol suite, consistent with calling it a protocol model. B incorrect A reference model divides responsibilities/interfaces without itself being executable implementation software. C incorrect Models can guide network design; using one or both perspectives is compatible with their reference purpose. D correct OSI is the reference model in the stated contrast, not itself the implemented TCP/IP-style protocol suite.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 5 · Q00063
records.text: Q00063 Question 5 NET16 NET-S03 Which statement about IPv4 is incorrect? Separate address width, syntax, reserved scope and the supplied prefix or historical classful convention. A It uses 128-bit addresses. B Its finite address space has faced allocation scarcity. C Private addressing with NAT can conserve public IPv4 addresses. D It uses 32-bit addresses. It uses 128-bit addresses. IPv4 addresses contain 32 bits, whereas IPv6 uses a much larger address space. IPv4 allocation scarcity motivates conservation through private addressing and NAT. These are address-space properties, not a claim that every IPv4 router is intrinsically slow or memory-intensive. The incorrect statement assigns a 128-bit address width to IPv4. A correct IPv4 addresses are 32 bits, so the claimed 128-bit width is incorrect. B incorrect Finite IPv4 address allocation has faced scarcity; this statement is true. C incorrect Private addressing with NAT conserves public IPv4 addresses; this statement is true. D incorrect The stated 32-bit IPv4 address width is correct.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 6 · Q00073
records.text: Q00073 Question 6 NET06 Which item is not a transmission impairment? Compare the signal mechanism, medium properties or transmission direction against the definitions and stated physical assumptions. A Synchronization B Crosstalk C Impulse noise D Distortion Synchronization Distortion changes the signal’s shape, while crosstalk and impulse noise add unwanted disturbances. Crosstalk couples energy from a nearby channel; impulse noise is a brief disturbance. Synchronization instead aligns timing so the receiver can interpret transmitted symbols. Losing synchronization can cause errors, but synchronization itself is a desirable coordination process rather than one of these signal impairments. A correct Synchronization aligns timing and is not itself an impairment. B incorrect Crosstalk is unwanted coupling from nearby channels, a noise impairment. C incorrect Impulse noise is a short unwanted disturbance, a noise impairment. D incorrect Distortion changes the signal shape and is a transmission impairment.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 7 · Q00086
records.text: Q00086 Question 7 NET30 NET-S01 _____________ is a probabilistic algorithm where a data packet is sent by the router to any one of its neighbors randomly. Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions. A Adaptive routing algorithm B Flooding routing algorithm C Random walks routing algorithm D Distributed routing algorithm Random-walk routing NET30 defines a random walk by probabilistically choosing a neighbor, exactly the forwarding behavior in the stem. Flooding instead replicates packets. Adaptive and distributed describe broader properties of routing algorithms; neither alone specifies random single-neighbor selection. A incorrect Adaptive routing responds to network conditions; adaptation alone does not mean choosing a random neighbor. B incorrect Flooding sends copies on multiple eligible links rather than selecting just one neighbor randomly. C correct Random walk selects the next neighbor probabilistically, matching the stated packet-forwarding procedure. D incorrect Distributed routing spreads computation among routers; it does not specify the random choice described.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 8 · Q00087
records.text: Q00087 Question 8 NET29 NET20 Which network address translation protocol solves the task of address resolution using port number? Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule. A Network Address Translation B Port Address Translation C Dynamic Address Translation D Static address translation Port Address Translation (PAT/NAPT) The wording loosely calls translation “address resolution,” but its decisive qualifier is use of port numbers. NET29 identifies PAT/NAPT as translation of address-plus-port combinations, allowing shared public addresses. This is not hardware-address resolution by ARP, and ordinary static or pooled dynamic address mappings do not themselves describe port multiplexing. A incorrect NAT is the broad translation family; this option does not identify the port-based form specifically. B correct PAT translates address-and-port combinations, distinguishing simultaneous clients that share an external address. C incorrect Dynamic NAT allocates address mappings from a pool, without necessarily multiplexing transport ports. D incorrect Static NAT fixes an address mapping; port-based sharing is the separate PAT mechanism.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 9 · Q00088
records.text: Q00088 Question 9 NET20 Which protocol resolves a known on-link IPv4 next-hop address to its link-layer hardware address? Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule. A Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) B Reverse Address Resolution Protocol (RARP) C Bootstrap Protocol (BOOTP) D Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) ARP resolves an on-link IPv4 next hop to a link address, normally by broadcasting a request and receiving a reply. For an off-subnet destination, the next hop is usually the gateway rather than the remote destination itself. RARP reverses hardware-to-IP lookup; BOOTP supplies boot configuration, and ICMP carries network diagnostics. These distinct functions do not replace ARP’s local IPv4-to-link resolution. A correct ARP resolves the known local IPv4 next hop to its link address. B incorrect RARP performs the reverse hardware-to-IP lookup. C incorrect BOOTP supplies boot configuration rather than resolving a known next-hop IPv4 address to its link address. D incorrect ICMP reports network errors and diagnostics rather than resolving hardware addresses.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 10 · Q00089
records.text: Q00089 Question 10 NET26 NET25 A 172.16.0.0/16 parent network is divided into equal /19 broadcast subnets. Counting all subnets, which statement is correct? Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule. A It provides 8 subnets, 32 IP addresses each B It provides 8 subnets, 8,190 hosts each C It provides 8 subnets, 30 hosts each D It provides 8 subnets, 2,046 IP addresses each It provides 8 subnets, 8,190 hosts each Moving from /16 to /19 borrows three subnet bits, producing 2^3 = 8 equal subnets. Each /19 leaves thirteen host bits, so it contains 8192 addresses. Reserving the network and directed-broadcast addresses leaves 8190 usable hosts. Subnet counts describe subdivision of the stated parent; they must not be confused with addresses or hosts within a child subnet. A incorrect Eight subnets is correct, but each /19 has 8192 total addresses rather than 32. B correct Three borrowed bits yield eight subnets; thirteen host bits yield 8190 usable hosts per subnet. C incorrect Thirty usable hosts belongs to /27, not /19. D incorrect A /19 contains 8192 addresses, not 2046.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 11 · Q00090
records.text: Q00090 Question 11 NET09 NET10 NET11 A network device that provides the physical interface between computer and cabling is known as________. Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions. A Switch B Router C NIC D Repeater NIC The star-topology description places RJ-45 cable connections at the NIC of each computer; the physical address is imprinted on that NIC. This identifies the host cabling interface. Evidence: PDF 23, 17, 12, 12, 11. A incorrect A switch forwards among attached devices (PDF 23, 17, 12, 12, 11.) B incorrect A router interconnects networks (PDF 23, 17, 12, 12, 11.) C correct The module names Network Interface Card and connects cable to it (PDF 23, 17, 12, 12, 11.) D incorrect A repeater regenerates a signal on a LAN (PDF 23, 17, 12, 12, 11.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 12 · Q00141
records.text: Q00141 Question 12 NET14 NET17 NET19 In the OSI teaching model, which layers provide hop-local or end-to-end flow control and error recovery when the chosen protocols support them? Select all that apply; isolated header-error detection alone does not qualify. Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A Application B Presentation C Network D Transport E Session F Data link G Physical Transport; Data link Data-link protocols can provide hop-local flow control and recovery, such as acknowledgments and retransmission. Transport protocols such as TCP provide end-to-end flow control and reliable delivery. These capabilities depend on the protocol: Ethernet detection alone does not guarantee recovery, and UDP does not provide TCP reliability. IPv4 checks its header but remains best-effort and does not supply the requested end-to-end recovery and flow-control service. A incorrect Application supplies application-facing network services, not the specified OSI control role. B incorrect Presentation concerns representation, compression and encryption roles. C incorrect IPv4 header checks detect some errors, but IP lacks the requested recovery and flow-control service. D correct Transport protocols such as TCP provide end-to-end flow control and recovery. E incorrect Session manages dialog and checkpoints rather than the specified delivery controls. F correct Data-link protocols can provide hop-local flow control and recovery. G incorrect Physical signaling transmits symbols rather than implementing these delivery-control procedures.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 13 · Q00142
records.text: Q00142 Question 13 NET33 NET17 NET09 Which of the following statement(s) is/are WRONG? (Choose all that applies) Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule. A Internet/Network layer is responsible for routing B Physical address can be assigned by the network administrator. C Physical layer is concerned with specifying the characteristics of the transmission medium, the nature of the signals and the data rate. D Transport layer provides only unreliable data transmission. E Network layer is responsible for host to host communication. F None of the above The transport layer does not provide only unreliable transmission The question asks for WRONG statements. TCP is a transport-layer protocol with reliable ordered delivery, disproving the absolute “only unreliable” in D. The other substantive statements fit the layer model: network routing and host delivery, physical signaling specifications, and administratively assigned MAC addresses. NET33 explicitly permits locally administered MAC addresses, so B must not be rejected. A incorrect This statement is true: routing is a network/Internet-layer responsibility, so it is not a wrong statement. B incorrect NET33 permits locally administered MAC addresses; physical addresses need not always be factory assigned. C incorrect Physical signaling, transmission-medium characteristics and data rate belong to the physical layer. D correct The word only is false: TCP supplies reliable transport, whereas UDP lacks built-in delivery guarantees. E incorrect Host-to-host packet delivery is a network-layer function, distinct from transport process delivery. F incorrect At least D is wrong, so none of the above cannot answer the requested negative test.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 14 · Q00143
records.text: Q00143 Question 14 NET14 Which one of the following Medium Access Control protocols is supported by WLAN (802.11)? Compare the signal mechanism, medium properties or transmission direction against the definitions and stated physical assumptions. A ALOHA B CSMA/CA C Token Passing D FDMA E CSMA CSMA/CA NET14 names CSMA/CA as the 802.11 Wi-Fi access procedure. It combines carrier sensing, waiting/backoff and acknowledgments rather than Ethernet-style collision detection or token turns. Generic CSMA describes its family, but B gives the specifically supported WLAN mechanism requested by the stem; E omits its collision-avoidance procedure. A incorrect ALOHA sends opportunistically and is not the 802.11 contention mechanism identified in NET14. B correct CSMA/CA is the specifically identified WLAN mechanism, using waiting/backoff and acknowledgments. C incorrect Token passing is controlled access, unlike the contention procedure used by ordinary 802.11 WLANs. D incorrect FDMA divides frequency resources; it is not the stated WLAN medium-access protocol. E incorrect CSMA names the broader carrier-sensing family but omits the specific collision-avoidance WLAN protocol offered in B.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 15 · Q00144
records.text: Q00144 Question 15 NET11 NET09 NET10 Which device category can perform protocol conversion at higher OSI layers, potentially including application formats, rather than being limited to basic repeating, MAC bridging or IP routing? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A Hub B Switch C Router D Gateway E Bridge Gateway A protocol gateway translates between protocol or application representations, so its possible scope extends above basic link forwarding and IP routing. A hub repeats signals, a basic switch or bridge forwards using link-layer information, and a basic router forwards IP packets. Gateway is used in several senses: an ordinary default gateway is usually a router and need not implement conversion across every OSI layer. A incorrect A hub repeats physical signals rather than converting application protocols. B incorrect A basic layer-2 switch forwards frames by link-layer information. C incorrect A basic router chooses IP next hops rather than translating application formats. D correct A protocol-conversion gateway can translate higher-layer formats. E incorrect A bridge forwards between links using MAC information rather than higher-layer protocol conversion.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 16 · Q00145
records.text: Q00145 Question 16 NET23 NET25 NET22 Which listed address can be assigned as an RFC1918 private unicast host address on a correctly configured /24 LAN? Select one. Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule. A 127.0.0.0 B 9.0.0.1 C 192.168.1.256 D 172.16.1.27 E All of the above F None of the above 172.16.1.27 An ordinary host address must have valid octets, belong to the required address scope and avoid the subnet network and broadcast addresses. The address 172.16.1.27 belongs to private 172.16.0.0/12 and is an interior host of 172.16.1.0/24. The public address 9.0.0.1 does not meet the private-address requirement. Loopback and an octet of 256 fail the other checks. A incorrect 127/8 is reserved for loopback and is not an ordinary LAN interface assignment. B incorrect 9.0.0.1 is public unicast, so it fails the explicit RFC1918 private-address requirement. C incorrect An IPv4 octet must be 0–255; 256 makes this address syntactically invalid. D correct 172.16.1.27 is within private 172.16/12 and is neither the network nor broadcast of its /24. E incorrect All fails because loopback and the impossible .256 octet are not valid ordinary LAN host assignments. F incorrect A private usable host is offered, so none of the above is false.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 17 · Q00146
records.text: Q00146 Question 17 NET31 For the switching methods below, select all statements that are correct. In D, allocation on demand means reservation when a circuit is established. Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions. A Circuit Switching and Virtual Packet Switching methods reserve the required resources for the duration of the session during communication between end systems B Circuit switching technique uses store and forward method. C In message switching technique, it is not required to create a dedicated path. D In circuit switching techniques, resources are allocated on demand. E Packet switching can have nonuniform delay because packets share links and may queue. In message switching technique, it is not required to create a dedicated path.; In circuit switching techniques, resources are allocated on demand.; Packet switching can have nonuniform delay because packets share links and may queue. Message switching stores and forwards whole messages without a dedicated end-to-end path. Circuit switching instead reserves resources when a call is established and retains them through the session. Packet switching shares links, so queueing can produce variable delay, although packet voice remains possible. Virtual-circuit forwarding state alone does not require resource reservation. These distinctions support the three selected statements without equating all connection-oriented methods. A incorrect Circuit switching reserves resources, but virtual-circuit packet switching need not reserve them throughout a session. B incorrect Circuit switching uses an established reserved path; complete-message or packet buffering describes store-and-forward switching. C correct Message switching forwards stored messages without requiring a dedicated end-to-end circuit. D correct Circuit resources are allocated when a connection is requested and reserved for its session. E correct Shared links and queueing can give packets different delays.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 18 · Q00147
records.text: Q00147 Question 18 NET25 NET22 Which information is not correct about the IP address 172.16.35.72/27? Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule. A 172.16.35.64 is one of the subnet addresses. B The default mask for the network is 255.255.0.0. C Itis Class B address. D The number of bits used for the host address is 5. E The broadcast address of the second subnet is 172.16.35.255 The claimed second-subnet broadcast is wrong For /27, five host bits give blocks of 32 in the last octet. The block containing .72 is .64–.95, with broadcast .95. If second subnet means the second /27 inside .35.0/24, its broadcast is .63; neither reading gives .255. The historical class is B and default mask /16, although the actual subnet mask is /27. A incorrect The .64 boundary is a valid /27 subnet start and contains host .72. B incorrect As a historical Class B address, its default mask is /16, even though the supplied actual prefix is /27. C incorrect First octet 172 is in the historical Class B range 128–191. D incorrect A 32-bit IPv4 address with /27 leaves exactly five bits for the host portion. E correct The second /27 in the local /24 broadcasts at .63; the containing subnet broadcasts at .95, never .255.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 19 · Q00156
records.text: Q00156 Question 19 NET21 Which one of the following is false about HTTP protocol? Identify the requested service or delivery guarantee, then distinguish application roles, transport behavior and address configuration. A Itis a stateless protocol B An HTTP message body can be empty C Itis a protocol used for communication between a web browser and a web server D None of the above None of the listed HTTP claims is false All three substantive choices agree with NET21: HTTP is stateless, a message body may be absent, and HTTP defines web request/response exchanges such as those between browsers and servers. The negative stem therefore has no false statement among A–C; D is the offered none-of-the-above response. A incorrect Statelessness is an HTTP property given in NET21, so this statement is true rather than false. B incorrect An HTTP message can omit its body, making this statement true. C incorrect Browser-to-web-server requests and responses are an ordinary use of HTTP, consistent with its web semantics. D correct A, B and C are all true, so none supplies the false statement requested.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 20 · Q00204
records.text: Q00204 Question 20 NET21 NET-S02 NET20 POP3 is most commonly used for: Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule. A Managing devices (such as routers and switches) on a network B Mapping IP addresses to hardware addresses C Sending emails from an email client to an email server D Retrieving emails from an email server to an email client Retrieving emails from an email server to an email client The module explicitly says POP3 is used to receive mail. Retrieval from a mail server into a client is that receiving function. Evidence: PDF 28, 17, 18. A incorrect Management is associated with SNMP, not POP3 (PDF 28, 17, 18.) B incorrect Address-to-hardware mapping is ARP (PDF 28, 17, 18.) C incorrect Sending mail is the SMTP role (PDF 28, 17, 18.) D correct Receiving mail matches the explicit POP3 statement (PDF 28, 17, 18.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 21 · Q00205
records.text: Q00205 Question 21 NET20 NET17 The Address Resolution Protocol maps addresses between which layers? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A Application layer to Network layer B Application layer to Transport layer C Transport layer to Network layer D Transport layer to Data link layer E Network layer to Data link layer Network layer to Data link layer ARP takes a logical IP address and resolves the physical MAC address, connecting network addressing to data-link addressing. Evidence: PDF 17, 15, 15. A incorrect Application to network omits the MAC destination of the mapping (PDF 17, 15, 15.) B incorrect Application to transport is not IP-to-MAC resolution (PDF 17, 15, 15.) C incorrect Transport ports are not the known IP address (PDF 17, 15, 15.) D incorrect Transport to data link incorrectly starts with ports (PDF 17, 15, 15.) E correct Network IP to data-link physical address matches both ends (PDF 17, 15, 15.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 22 · Q00206
records.text: Q00206 Question 22 NET24 NET25 What is the first usable host addressing of prefix 172.105.180.0/21? Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule. A 172.105.180.1 B 172.105.170.1 C 172.105.175.1 D 172.105.176.1 E 172.105.172.1 172.105.176.1 A /21 mask is 255.255.248.0, giving third-octet blocks of eight. 180 lies in the 176–183 block; masking therefore yields network 172.105.176.0, not 172.105.180.0. The first usable ordinary host is one address above the network boundary: 172.105.176.1. NET24 explicitly explains this unaligned host/prefix example. A incorrect This address is inside the block but is not its first usable address; the block begins at third octet 176. B incorrect Third octet 170 lies below the 176–183 range of the actual /21 block. C incorrect Third octet 175 is outside the block, immediately below its network boundary. D correct The network is 172.105.176.0/21, so its first usable ordinary host is 172.105.176.1. E incorrect Third octet 172 belongs to a different /21 block and is outside the specified network.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 23 · Q00207
records.text: Q00207 Question 23 NET23 NET11 What is the special IP with all binary 1's used for? Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule. A A destination address to send to all devices on the same subnet B A destination address to send to all devices on another subnet C A destination address if a device is sending to itself D A source address when a device doesn't yet have an IP address E A source address if a device is sending to itself Limited broadcast on the local subnet All 32 one bits form 255.255.255.255, the limited-broadcast destination in NET23. Its scope is the local network; routers do not ordinarily forward it to another subnet. Self-reference uses loopback, while an unconfigured source can use 0.0.0.0. Thus the all-ones value is a destination broadcast, not either kind of source address. A correct The all-ones IPv4 address targets limited broadcast on the sender’s local network. B incorrect Limited broadcast is local in scope; it is not the destination for another subnet’s directed broadcast. C incorrect Sending to the host itself uses loopback, commonly 127.0.0.1, rather than the all-ones address. D incorrect An unconfigured source can use all-zero 0.0.0.0, not all-one 255.255.255.255. E incorrect The all-ones address is a broadcast destination, not a self-reference source address.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 24 · Q00208
records.text: Q00208 Question 24 NET29 NET30 Which of the following technologies can allow a host with IP address 10.0.0.1 to access the internet? Separate address width, syntax, reserved scope and the supplied prefix or historical classful convention. A NAT B Route import C Dynamic route D Static route NAT The module prescribes translation of private internal addresses to a public address for Internet access. Conditional on the stem treating 10.0.0.1 as private, NAT is the offered mechanism. Evidence: PDF 19, 48, 19. A correct Private-to-public translation is exactly NAT (PDF 19, 48, 19.) B incorrect Importing routing information is not address translation (PDF 19, 48, 19.) C incorrect Dynamic path selection does not itself translate an internal address (PDF 19, 48, 19.) D incorrect Static routes do not themselves translate an internal address (PDF 19, 48, 19.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 25 · Q00267
records.text: Q00267 Question 25 NET21 NET16 Which of the following protocol is used to define how messages are formatted and transmitted on the World Wide Web? Identify the requested service or delivery guarantee, then distinguish application roles, transport behavior and address configuration. A IP B FTP C SMTP D HTTP HTTP The question asks for the application protocol defining World Wide Web message exchange. HTTP defines web request/response semantics. IP supplies packet delivery beneath applications; FTP transfers files through its own protocol; SMTP submits and relays email. Those services do not define browser/server HTTP message formatting and exchange. A incorrect IP supplies best-effort packet delivery and does not define World Wide Web application-message semantics. B incorrect FTP is a file-transfer protocol with separate control and data connections, not the web-message protocol. C incorrect SMTP submits and relays mail rather than defining World Wide Web exchanges. D correct HTTP supplies web request/response semantics, matching the message formatting and transmission role asked about.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 26 · Q00347
records.text: Q00347 Question 26 NET22 What is the bit pattern for the first octet of a class -B network address? Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule. A 110XXXXX B 1110XXXXX C 10XXXXXX D 0XXXXXXX 10XXXXXX In historical classful IPv4 addressing, Class B starts with the two fixed bits 10; the remaining six bits of the first octet vary. This gives first-octet decimal values 128–191. The alternatives instead begin with the Class C, Class D and Class A patterns respectively; B also prints too many total bits for an octet. A incorrect The fixed prefix 110 identifies historical Class C rather than Class B. B incorrect The fixed prefix 1110 identifies multicast Class D; the printed pattern also exceeds eight positions. C correct Class B fixes the first two bits to 10 and permits six remaining first-octet bits. D incorrect A leading zero identifies historical Class A, not Class B.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 27 · Q00348
records.text: Q00348 Question 27 NET17 NET19 Which OSI model layer is responsible for flow control? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A Application Layer B Transport Layer C Session Layer D Presentation Layer Transport Layer Among these four layers transport explicitly provides end-to-end flow control. Data link also provides flow control but is not offered. Evidence: PDF 16, 16, 16, 16. A incorrect Application provides access to resources (PDF 16, 16, 16, 16.) B correct Transport explicitly carries out flow control (PDF 16, 16, 16, 16.) C incorrect Session manages dialogs and checkpoints (PDF 16, 16, 16, 16.) D incorrect Presentation handles translation, compression and encryption (PDF 16, 16, 16, 16.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 28 · Q00349
records.text: Q00349 Question 28 NET09 NET10 NET11 Which of the following networking device is used in physical layer? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A Bridge B Router C Switch D Hub Hub An active hub is a multiport repeater, and a repeater operates only at the physical layer. Evidence: PDF 12, 11, 12, 12, 12. records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 36 · Q00553
records.text: Q00553 Question 36 NET14 One of the following is false the characteristics of controlled access in datalink layer. records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 38 · Q00560
records.text: Q00560 Question 38 NET02 Which organizational networking term describes exposing selected internal services to approved users outside the organization? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A Internet B Extranet C intranet D All Extranet Access scope determines the answer: an extranet extends selected organizational services to approved outsiders. An intranet serves members internally, while the Internet is the global network of networks. Neither organizational term determines geographic size or requires a particular physical connection. The question therefore asks about controlled external access rather than treating every external link as the same network category. A incorrect The Internet is the global network of networks; it does not specifically name controlled access to an organization’s selected services. B correct An extranet exposes selected services to approved outsiders. C incorrect An intranet describes internal organizational access. D incorrect The three terms have different scopes, so all is not the requested category.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 39 · Q00564
records.text: Q00564 Question 39 NET23 NET22 Class B private IP address space ranges: Separate address width, syntax, reserved scope and the supplied prefix or historical classful convention. A 10.0.0.0-----------19.255.255.255 B 128.12.0.0--------191.24.255.255 C 172.16.0.0--------172.31.255.255 D 192.168.0.0------192.168.255.255 172.16.0.0 through 172.31.255.255 The private allocation within the historical Class B range is 172.16.0.0/12. Its twelve fixed bits leave first octet 172 and second octets 16–31, inclusive. The 192.168 range is also private but lies in historical Class C space; the other printed ranges are not RFC1918 private allocations. A incorrect The private 10/8 block ends at 10.255.255.255; extending it through first octet 19 includes public space. B incorrect This broad portion of historical Class B space is not a designated RFC1918 private allocation. C correct The 172.16/12 private block spans exactly 172.16.0.0 through 172.31.255.255. D incorrect 192.168/16 is private, but it lies in historical Class C space rather than Class B.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 42 · Q00579
records.text: Q00579 Question 42 NET02 For this hypothetical design, Debre Markos University’s main campus and its Burie agricultural branch are in different towns beyond a single metropolitan area. records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 47 · Q00596
records.text: Q00596 Question 47 NET26 How many equal /27 subnets can be created from 192.168.20.0/24, counting every subnet? Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule. A 8 B 16 C 32 D 64 8 Subnet counts depend on both the parent and child prefixes. Dividing a /24 parent into /27 children borrows three bits, giving 2^3 = 8 subnets. Each child has five host bits and therefore 32 total addresses, but that address count is a different quantity. Counting every subnet avoids the obsolete practice of excluding the first and last subnet. A correct Three borrowed bits produce eight /27 subnets. B incorrect Sixteen would require four borrowed bits, not three. C incorrect Thirty-two is the number of addresses in each /27, not the number of children of this /24. D incorrect Sixty-four requires six borrowed bits rather than three.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 48 · Q00601
records.text: Q00601 Question 48 NET24 Given an IP Address 172.16.28.252 with the subnet mask of 255.255.240.0 what is the correct network address? Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule. A 172.16.24.0 B 172.16.28.0 C 172.16.0.0 D 172.16.16.0 172.16.16.0 240=11110000 in the third mask octet. 28 (00011100) AND 240 (11110000)=16 (00010000); the last masked octet is zero. Thus the network is 172.16.16.0. Evidence: PDF 18, 19, 19. A incorrect 24 is not aligned to a 16-wide third-octet block (PDF 18, 19, 19.) B incorrect 28 retains host bits instead of masking them (PDF 18, 19, 19.) C incorrect 0 would discard the retained third-octet network bit (PDF 18, 19, 19.) D correct 16 is the result of the mask operation (PDF 18, 19, 19.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 49 · Q00602
records.text: Q00602 Question 49 NET31 One of the following is true about packet switching. Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions. A Packets travel around the network seeking out the most efficient route. B Packets should necessarily seek out the shortest route. C The message gets broken into small data packets. D All Packet switching divides a message into packets The defining packet-switching property is dividing data into packets for shared-link forwarding. Routing may seek good paths, but packets do not guarantee the most efficient or geometrically shortest path. C directly states the definition; D includes unsupported universal route claims and therefore fails. A incorrect Routing chooses next hops, but packet switching does not guarantee packets discover the globally most efficient route. B incorrect Packets are not guaranteed to take the geometrically shortest route. C correct Breaking a message into data packets is the packet-switching operation. D incorrect The all option includes unsupported route-optimality and necessary-shortest-path claims.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 50 · Q00603
records.text: Q00603 Question 50 NET19 NET03 Which statements correctly compare the seven-layer OSI reference model with the four-layer TCP/IP model? Select all that apply. Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A Both have application layers. B Both have comparable transport and network layers. C Both uses packet-switching instead of circuit-switching technology. D All Both have application layers.; Both have comparable transport and network layers. Both models include application responsibilities and corresponding transport and network functions. TCP/IP groups the OSI session, presentation and application responsibilities into its application layer, and calls its network layer the Internet layer. An abstract reference model does not itself execute a switching technology. Consequently, the claim that both models necessarily use packet switching is not a valid shared model property. A correct Both models include an application layer, although TCP/IP folds several OSI upper-layer functions into it. B correct TCP/IP retains transport and maps OSI network responsibilities to its Internet layer. C incorrect A reference model does not itself use a switching technology or restrict every implementation to one. D incorrect The implemented-technology claim in C is not a property established for both abstract models.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 51 · Q00604

This follows the assigned taxonomy rather than assuming that all taxonomies place ARP identically. Evidence: PDF 17, 17, 18, 18. A incorrect HTTP is an application service in the table (PDF 17, 17, 18, 18.) B incorrect FTP is application file transfer (PDF 17, 17, 18, 18.) C correct ARP is explicitly grouped under network/IP support (PDF 17, 17, 18, 18.) D incorrect TCP belongs to transport (PDF 17, 17, 18, 18.)

records.text: Q00629 Question 52 NET09 NET12 NET17 One of the following is responsible for receiving and transmitting the signals across the physical media. records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 53 · Q00636
records.text: Q00636 Question 53 NET09 NET10 NET11 Which listed device performs layer-1 signal regeneration without inspecting destination addresses? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A Router B Switch C Firewall D Repeater Repeater A repeater regenerates physical signals and therefore performs a layer-1 function. Routers decide where to forward network-layer packets, and ordinary Ethernet switches make link-layer decisions using MAC addresses. A firewall enforces a security policy rather than defining a physical signal-regeneration role. Replacing the duplicated firewall distractor restores a meaningful physical-layer choice without changing the layer-identification concept. A incorrect A router’s defining forwarding function is network-layer IP routing rather than layer-1 signal repetition. B incorrect An ordinary Ethernet switch performs layer-2 MAC frame forwarding. C incorrect A firewall enforces traffic policy rather than being the layer-1 repeater/hub requested. D correct A repeater regenerates layer-1 signals without inspecting destination addresses.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 54 · Q00637
records.text: Q00637 Question 54 NET01 A data communication component that helps to convert data into transmittable signal. Compare the signal mechanism, medium properties or transmission direction against the definitions and stated physical assumptions. A Transmission media B Transmitter C Receiver D Data source Transmitter NET01 separates creating data, converting it to a signal, carrying that signal and reconstructing the data. The stem asks specifically about the conversion into a transmittable signal, which is the transmitter’s role. A source supplies the data before this conversion, while the receiver performs the reconstruction at the far end. A incorrect The transmission medium carries the signal; it is not the component that converts source data into it. B correct The transmitter converts data into a signal suitable for transmission over the medium. C incorrect The receiver reconstructs data from the incoming signal, performing the opposite end’s role. D incorrect The data source creates the data; signal conversion is assigned separately to the transmitter.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 55 · Q00638
records.text: Q00638 Question 55 NET13 NET12 Among the following one is the responsibility of logical link control layer. Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A Identify the network layer protocol. B Marking the beginning and ending of the frame. C Addressing the frame. D All Identify or multiplex the network-layer protocol LLC identifies or multiplexes the upper-layer protocol carried over the link. NET13 assigns medium-dependent addressing/access and frame delivery to MAC, and says exact framing depends on the protocol. Therefore the specific LLC duty offered here is identifying the network-layer protocol; the other functions cannot all be attributed to LLC. A correct Identifying or multiplexing an upper-layer network protocol is an explicit LLC responsibility in NET13. B incorrect Beginning/end frame delimitation belongs to protocol-specific framing, not the distinguishing LLC upper-protocol identification function. C incorrect Medium-dependent frame addressing belongs to MAC rather than the LLC duty asked about. D incorrect The all option incorrectly includes frame addressing and delimitation as specifically LLC responsibilities.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 56 · Q00639
records.text: Q00639 Question 56 NET22 One of the following is ODD Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule. A 192.257.10.0 B 192.168.10.0 C 172.16.1.1 D 192.168.0.0 192.257.10.0 As a syntactic IPv4 address comparison, 257 exceeds the permitted 0-255 octet range. The others have four legal octets; no host mask is supplied to test host assignability. Evidence: PDF 19. A correct 257 violates the octet limit (PDF 19.) B incorrect All octets fall between 0 and 255 (PDF 19.) C incorrect All octets fall between 0 and 255 (PDF 19.) D incorrect All octets fall between 0 and 255 (PDF 19.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 57 · Q00640
records.text: Q00640 Question 57 NET15 NET11 The most commonly used method to convert analog data to digital form. Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule. A Line coding scheme B Data encoding C Pulse code modulation D Demodulation Pulse code modulation (PCM) NET15 identifies PCM as the analog-to-digital procedure of sampling the analog input, quantizing each sample and encoding its level as bits. The note does not establish comparative usage statistics, but PCM is the specific conversion method among the choices. Line coding maps existing digital bits to signals; demodulation recovers information from a carrier rather than necessarily digitizing analog data. A incorrect Line coding begins with digital bits and maps them to digital signal patterns, rather than digitizing analog input. B incorrect Data encoding is a broad description and does not identify the specific analog-digitization method supplied here. C correct PCM performs the sampling, quantization and binary encoding needed to turn analog input into digital data. D incorrect Demodulation removes carrier modulation; it does not itself specify analog-to-digital sampling and quantization.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 58 · Q00647
records.text: Q00647 Question 58 NET02 NET33 In a peer-to-peer architecture, which statements are false? Select all that apply. Interpret C as absence of a required client-server hierarchy. Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule. A Computers can function as both a client and a server. B A dedicated central administrator is required by peer-to-peer architecture. C There is no a hierarchy among the computers. D In peer - to - peer network security is not an issue. A dedicated central administrator is required by peer-to-peer architecture.; In peer - to - peer network security is not an issue. Peers may request and supply services without a required client-server hierarchy. That capability does not impose a dedicated central administrator, although people may still take responsibility for administration. Peer systems also continue to need security because they expose data and services. The false statements therefore concern mandatory centralized administration and the dismissal of security, while the capability and no-required-hierarchy statements are true. A incorrect True: peers can both request and supply services, so this is not a false statement. B correct False: a dedicated central administrator is not a requirement of peer architecture. C incorrect True: peers do not require a client-server hierarchy, so this is not a false statement. D correct False: peer networks still require security.

Identify the requested service or delivery guarantee, then distinguish application roles, transport behavior and address configuration. records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 60 · Q00654
records.text: Q00654 Question 60 NET10 NET09 Which single option gives the complete set of listed devices whose ordinary forwarding function is at the data-link layer? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A Switch B Access point C Hub D A & B A & B An ordinary Ethernet switch forwards frames at layer 2, and an ordinary wireless access point bridges wireless and wired link-layer traffic. A hub simply repeats physical signals at layer 1. The question requests the complete set, so either switch or access point alone omits another qualifying device. The combined response is therefore the one complete selection. A incorrect A switch is layer 2, but this selection omits the qualifying access point. B incorrect A bridging access point is layer 2, but this selection omits the switch. C incorrect A hub repeats physical signals and does not inspect destination MAC addresses as a data-link device does. D correct Both the ordinary switch and bridging access point are data-link devices; this gives the complete set.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 61 · Q00656
records.text: Q00656 Question 61 NET03 NET19 Which statement correctly describes the OSI reference model? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A It has fewer layer that TCP/IP model. B The model itself is executable software installed to implement a network. C Used as a guide to help students or learners understand the communication process. D All Used as a guide to help students or learners understand the communication process. OSI divides communication responsibilities into seven layers and serves as a framework for explaining interfaces and communication processes. The usual TCP/IP teaching model has four layers, so OSI does not have fewer. A reference model can guide design, but it is not itself executable networking software or an installed protocol implementation. That distinction makes the learning-guide statement the correct description. A incorrect OSI has seven layers, more than the usual four-layer TCP/IP teaching model. B incorrect A reference model is not itself executable networking software, although it can guide design. C correct The model helps learners understand layered communication responsibilities. D incorrect The incorrect layer count and executable-software claim prevent all statements from being true.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 62 · Q00699
records.text: Q00699 Question 62 NET01 NET06 Which listed item is not one of the five basic components of data communication? Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule. A Message B Medium C Sender D Distance Distance The five basic components are message, sender, receiver, medium and protocol. Message, medium and sender therefore belong to the required set. Distance affects transmission engineering, such as propagation delay and attenuation, but it is not a sixth component in that model. Replacing the original protocol option with distance supplies a meaningful exception while retaining the negative component-identification task. A incorrect Message is explicitly one of the required components. B incorrect The medium carries signals and is explicitly a communication component. C incorrect The sender is explicitly included among communication components. D correct Distance affects engineering but is not one of the five basic communication components.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 63 · Q00700
records.text: Q00700 Question 63 NET08 There are two types of network topologies from these topologies which one of the following defines how hosts access the media to send data. Draw the links and identify shared components, alternate paths and the effect of the specified failure or growth requirement. A Logical Topology B Bus Topology C Physical Topology D Star Topology Logical topology The distinction is between physical layout and communication/access relationships. NET08 defines logical topology in the latter sense, matching how hosts obtain medium access. Bus and star are particular arrangements rather than the general physical-versus-logical category requested. A correct Logical topology describes communication and medium-access relationships among hosts. B incorrect Bus is a particular shared-backbone arrangement, not the general category defining access relationships. C incorrect Physical topology describes link layout and connections rather than the logical rules for medium access. D incorrect Star describes endpoints around a central device; it does not name the general access-topology category.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 64 · Q00701
records.text: Q00701 Question 64 NET12 NET17 Segmentation of a data stream happens at which layer of the OSI model? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A Physical B Data Link C Network D Transport Transport Transport explicitly divides data into segments and reassembles sequence-numbered segments. Evidence: PDF 16, 14, 15, 15. A incorrect Physical delivers bits (PDF 16, 14, 15, 15.) B incorrect Data link handles frames (PDF 16, 14, 15, 15.) C incorrect Network handles packets (PDF 16, 14, 15, 15.) D correct Transport explicitly performs segmentation (PDF 16, 14, 15, 15.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 65 · Q00702
records.text: Q00702 Question 65 NET12 When data is encapsulated, which is the correct order? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A Data, frame, packet, segment, bit B Data, segment, packet, frame, bit C Segment, data, packet, frame, bit D Data, segment, frame, packet, bit Data, segment, packet, frame, bit Follow the sending path downward: upper data becomes transport segments, network packets, data-link frames, then physical bits. Evidence: PDF 16, 15, 15, 14. A incorrect Frames cannot precede network packets on the sending path B correct The encapsulation order is data, segment, packet, frame, then bit C incorrect Segmentation follows receipt of upper-layer data D incorrect Network packet must precede data-link frame

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 66 · Q00703
records.text: Q00703 Question 66 NET07 You want to implement a network medium that is not susceptible to EMI. Which type of cabling should you use? Compare the signal mechanism, medium properties or transmission direction against the definitions and stated physical assumptions. A Coaxial B Category 6 UTP C Microwave D Fiber-optic Fiber-optic cable NET07 identifies fiber as a light-guiding medium that resists electromagnetic interference. Coax and UTP carry electrical signals and can be affected by coupled interference. Microwave is wireless, so it is not a cabling answer even before considering interference in radio transmission. A incorrect Coax has shielding but still carries electrical signals; it does not offer fiber’s immunity to electromagnetic coupling. B incorrect Twisted pairs reduce interference but unshielded copper cable remains susceptible to electromagnetic coupling. C incorrect Microwave is an unguided wireless medium, not a cable matching the requested cabling choice. D correct Fiber carries light and resists electromagnetic interference rather than conducting the unwanted electrical coupling.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 67 · Q00704
records.text: Q00704 Question 67 NET13 Which responsibility belongs to the OSI network layer rather than the data-link layer? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A logical link control B Network Addressing C media access control D Hardware Addressing Network Addressing Logical network addressing, such as IP addressing, supports delivery across interconnected networks and belongs to the network layer. The data-link layer instead handles local frame delivery, hardware/MAC addressing, medium access and link-control functions. LLC identifies or multiplexes upper-layer protocols and may supply link control. The term hardware addressing here denotes frame-level MAC addressing, not an IP address. A incorrect LLC is a data-link sublayer role for upper-protocol identification and link control. B correct Logical network addressing is a network-layer responsibility. C incorrect Medium access control is a data-link role. D incorrect MAC hardware addressing is used for link-frame delivery.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 68 · Q00705
records.text: Q00705 Question 68 NET22 NET25 Which class of IP address provides a maximum of only 254 host addresses per network ID? Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule. A Class A B Class D C Class B D Class C Class C under the historical default mask The wording asks about historical address classes. Class C uses default /24, leaving eight host bits: 2^8−2=254 ordinary usable hosts. Classes A and B leave more bits, while Class D identifies multicast rather than an ordinary unicast host network. Under CIDR the actual prefix would replace these defaults. A incorrect Default Class A /8 leaves 24 host bits, far more than 254 usable hosts. B incorrect Class D is multicast space, not an ordinary classful unicast network with 254 hosts. C incorrect Default Class B /16 leaves sixteen host bits and 65534 ordinary usable hosts. D correct Default Class C /24 leaves eight host bits, giving 256 addresses minus network and broadcast.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 69 · Q00706
records.text: Q00706 Question 69 NET04 NET15 Which item is not a parameter or spatial characteristic of a continuous sinusoidal carrier wave? Compare the signal mechanism, medium properties or transmission direction against the definitions and stated physical assumptions. A Amplitude B Wavelength C phase D Discrete pulse Discrete pulse A sine wave has amplitude, frequency and phase. Given propagation speed, wavelength follows from frequency and describes its spatial repetition. A discrete pulse is a different waveform description, not a parameter of a continuous sine wave. This distinction concerns the specified carrier model; it does not claim that all pulse modulation is digital, since pulse amplitude and width can vary to carry analog information. A incorrect Amplitude specifies the sinusoid’s magnitude. B incorrect Wavelength specifies the spatial repetition of the propagating sinusoid. C incorrect Phase specifies displacement within the sinusoid’s cycle. D correct A discrete pulse is a waveform description rather than a sinusoidal parameter.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 70 · Q00707
records.text: Q00707 Question 70 NET06 Communication between a radio station and its listeners involves ______________ transmission. Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule. A full-duplex B Half-duplex C Simplex D Automatic Simplex An ordinary broadcast radio station transmits to listeners who only receive. The one-direction relationship matches simplex. Evidence: PDF 5. A incorrect Full duplex requires both sides simultaneously transmitting (PDF 5.) B incorrect Half duplex requires alternate two-way transmission (PDF 5.) C correct Simplex explicitly has one sender and one receiver direction (PDF 5.) D incorrect Automatic is not one of the module transmission modes (PDF 5.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 71 · Q00708
records.text: Q00708 Question 71 NET11 Which of the following does not describe router functions Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions. A Broadcast forwarding B Internetwork communication C Packet filtering D Packet switching Forwarding local broadcasts is not a normal router function Routers forward IP packets between networks and separate broadcast domains. Accordingly internetwork communication and packet forwarding/switching describe routing, whereas ordinary local link broadcasts are not propagated across routers. Packet filtering can accompany the traffic-control function, so A is the normal-function exception, not a claim that no specially configured broadcast relay can exist. A correct Ordinary routers bound broadcast domains rather than forwarding local link broadcasts between them. B incorrect Forwarding IP packets between different networks is the defining router function. C incorrect Traffic filtering can be implemented alongside routing; it is consistent with router security-policy controls. D incorrect A router forwards individual packets to next hops, a network-layer packet-switching function.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 72 · Q00709
records.text: Q00709 Question 72 NET14 NET17 Which OSI layer uses acknowledgments, sequencing and receiver flow control for end-to-end process delivery, as illustrated by TCP? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A Layer 2 B Layer 4 C Layer 3 D Layer 7 Layer 4 Scope separates otherwise similar mechanisms. Reliable link procedures can acknowledge frames and control a single hop, whereas TCP uses sequence numbers, acknowledgments and windows between transport endpoints. The explicit end-to-end process-delivery requirement identifies layer 4. IP at layer 3 offers best-effort delivery, and application services build on the transport service rather than defining this TCP reliability machinery. A incorrect Layer 2 can provide similar mechanisms only for hop-local link delivery, outside the requested scope. B correct Layer 4 transport provides TCP’s end-to-end sequencing, acknowledgments and receiver flow control. C incorrect IP best-effort delivery does not provide the indicated ordered acknowledgment/retransmission service. D incorrect Application services can build reliability, but the standard link/transport mechanisms named here are not layer-7 duties.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 73 · Q00710
records.text: Q00710 Question 73 NET32 NET30 What is the technique of combining multiple input signals or streams onto a shared transmission link? Compare the signal mechanism, medium properties or transmission direction against the definitions and stated physical assumptions. A Broadcast B Multicast C Multiplexing D demultiplexing Multiplexing Multiplexing combines input signals or streams so they share a link, using distinctions such as frequency, wavelength or time slots. Demultiplexing is the corresponding receiver operation that separates them. Broadcast and multicast instead describe recipient sets for a message. Link sharing and destination distribution therefore answer different questions, even though a network can use both mechanisms. A incorrect Broadcast distributes a message to all members of a broadcast domain rather than combining input streams. B incorrect Multicast distributes to a receiver group rather than combining inputs onto a link. C correct Multiplexing combines inputs onto the shared link. D incorrect Demultiplexing separates received multiplexed inputs; it is the reverse operation.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 74 · Q00912
records.text: Q00912 Question 74 NET03 NET19 How many layers are there in OSI reference model? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A 7 B 6 C 5 D 4 7 OSI is explicitly a seven-layer hierarchy. Evidence: PDF 14, 17. A correct Seven is the stated count (PDF 14, 17.) B incorrect Six omits one stated layer (PDF 14, 17.) C incorrect Five is not the stated OSI count (PDF 14, 17.) D incorrect Four is the original TCP/IP count (PDF 14, 17.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 75 · Q00921
records.text: Q00921 Question 75 NET22 NET24 Which one of the following ip address class uses first two octets for network addresses and last two for host addressing? Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule. A Class C B Class D C Class A D Class B Class B Two octets are sixteen bits. A historical Class B default /16 therefore uses the first two octets as network bits and the final two as host bits. Class A defaults to one network octet and Class C to three; Class D is multicast. Actual CIDR allocation can override the historical defaults. A incorrect Class C defaults to /24, using three network octets and one host octet. B incorrect Class D denotes multicast and does not use the described ordinary network/host division. C incorrect Class A defaults to /8, using one network octet and three host octets. D correct Class B defaults to /16, exactly the two-network-octet, two-host-octet division described.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 76 · Q00950

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 78 · Q00962
records.text: Q00962 Question 78 NET20 NET21 Which service used to translate domain names to ip address? Separate address width, syntax, reserved scope and the supplied prefix or historical classful convention.
