records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 79 · Q00968
records.text: Q00968 Question 79 NET17 NET21 Which scenario is best suited for UDP rather than TCP protocol? Identify the requested service or delivery guarantee, then distinguish application roles, transport behavior and address configuration. A Live video streaming B Email transmission C Downloading the files D Database update Live video streaming UDP is connectionless and omits flow/error control, fitting live streams where timely delivery matters more than repairing old data. Email/file/database transactions need the reliability contrast rather than that latency preference. Evidence: PDF 18, 18. A correct Live streaming fits the no-repair-delay tradeoff (PDF 18, 18.) B incorrect Mail transfer is an application for which reliable delivery is preferable (PDF 18, 18.) C incorrect File download generally needs intact reliable bytes (PDF 18, 18.) D incorrect Database updates require dependable ordered delivery (PDF 18, 18.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 80 · Q00976
records.text: Q00976 Question 80 NET22 Assume that you have IPv4 addresses in binary notation 11000001 10000011 00011011 11111111 and you are requested to change into dotted decimal notation. What is the equivalent IP address in decimal dotted notation? Sum the eight bit weights in each octet independently, then preserve their order in dotted-decimal notation. A 192.174.27.255 B 192.134.67.254 C ¢. 193.130.28.254 D 193.131.27.255 193.131.27.255 Compute each octet: 11000001=128+64+1=193; 10000011=128+2+1=131; 00011011=16+8+2+1=27; 11111111=255. Evidence: PDF 19. A incorrect First and second octets disagree with 193 and 131 (PDF 19.) B incorrect 192,134,67,254 disagree with the independently converted octets 193,131,27,255 (PDF19). C incorrect Only first octet matches; 130,28,254 do not (PDF 19.) D correct 193.131.27.255 matches all four converted octets (PDF 19.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 81 · Q00979
records.text: Q00979 Question 81 NET31 Which one of the following is disadvantage of circuit switching? Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions. A Predictable performance B Low latency C Guaranteed bandwidth D Limited scalability Limited scalability due to reserved resources Circuit switching reserves resources for an established path. NET31 explains that this offers predictable bandwidth but introduces setup, blocking and unused reservation during silence. Those costs constrain how many simultaneous circuits can be supported as demand grows, making limited scalability the disadvantage among the offered choices. A incorrect Predictable performance is a benefit of allocated circuit resources, not the disadvantage requested. B incorrect Low transfer latency after setup can be beneficial; the relevant costs include setup and resource reservation. C incorrect Guaranteed allocated bandwidth is an advantage, although reserving it consumes capacity during silence. D correct Finite reserved resources and blocking constrain simultaneous connections and therefore scalability as demand grows.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 82 · Q00997
records.text: Q00997 Question 82 NET31 In which case must a dedicated communication path between the sender and receiver be established? Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule. A Circuit switching B Packet switching C A and B D None of the above Circuit switching A dedicated path is explicitly required by circuit switching. Packet communication is contrasted with that continuous dedicated circuit. A correct Circuit establishment creates the dedicated path B incorrect Packet communication is discrete rather than the dedicated circuit C incorrect Both incorrectly adds a requirement not inherent to packet switching D incorrect None excludes the explicitly dedicated circuit

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 83 · Q00999
records.text: Q00999 Question 83 NET08 Which one of the following is a type of network topology in which all devices in the network are interconnected? Draw the links and identify shared components, alternate paths and the effect of the specified failure or growth requirement. A Star Topology B Ring Topology C Mesh Topology D Tree Topology Mesh Topology Interpret interconnected as every node directly connected to every other node: this is the module full-mesh definition. Without directly, all connected topologies would qualify. Evidence: PDF 23, 23, 23. A incorrect Star nodes connect through a central device (PDF 23, 23, 23.) B incorrect Ring nodes directly connect only to two neighbors (PDF 23, 23, 23.) C correct Full mesh explicitly connects every node to every other (PDF 23, 23, 23.) D incorrect Tree is listed but not defined as all-pairs direct connectivity (PDF 23, 23, 23.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 84 · Q01004
records.text: Q01004 Question 84 NET16 NET23 Which statements about IPv4 and IPv6 addresses are correct? Select all that apply. Separate address width, syntax, reserved scope and the supplied prefix or historical classful convention. A IPv4 is 128-bit and IPv6 is 28-bit B IPv4 is physical address C IPv6 is logical address D IPv4 is 32-bit and IPv6 is 128-bit IPv6 is logical address; IPv4 is 32-bit and IPv6 is 128-bit IPv4 addresses contain 32 bits, and IPv6 addresses contain 128 bits. Both are logical network-layer addresses, so IPv6 being logical is compatible with the width comparison. Physical or MAC addressing belongs to the link layer. The corrected selection instruction allows both true statements to be selected while retaining the original factual comparisons and the two incorrect distractors. A incorrect IPv4 is 32 bits and IPv6 is 128 bits; neither printed width is correct. B incorrect IPv4 is network-layer logical addressing, not a physical/MAC address. C correct IPv6 addresses identify network-layer endpoints logically rather than physical link interfaces. D correct This gives the correct address lengths: 32 bits for IPv4 and 128 for IPv6.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 85 · Q01006
records.text: Q01006 Question 85 NET07 NET06 Which one of the data communication mediums is used for direct transmission? Compare the signal mechanism, medium properties or transmission direction against the definitions and stated physical assumptions. A Induced B Crosstalk C A and B D None of the above Neither induced nor crosstalk names a transmission medium The note identifies cables and unguided radio/microwave/infrared as transmission media. Crosstalk instead names interference from nearby channels in NET06, and induced alone does not name a medium in the note. Regardless of the vague direct-transmission phrase, none of A–C supplies a listed medium, so D is the supported exclusion response. A incorrect Induced is not a transmission-medium category established here. B incorrect Crosstalk is unwanted coupling/interference, not a medium for intentional direct transmission. C incorrect Combining two nonmedium terms does not supply the requested transmission medium. D correct Neither induced nor crosstalk names a transmission medium among the choices.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 86 · Q01160
records.text: Q01160 Question 86 NET17 NET12 Which OSI layer is responsible for process-to-process delivery and segmentation? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A Network Layer B Transport Layer C Physical Layer D Data Link Layer Transport Layer Transport supplies process-to-process delivery and segmentation. The network layer handles logical addressing and routing, the data-link layer handles hop delivery of frames, and the physical layer transports bits or symbols. Restoring the four readable source rows gives the transport option its proper position. Reliability remains protocol-dependent: identifying transport does not imply that every transport protocol guarantees delivery. A incorrect Network handles routing and logical addressing rather than process delivery. B correct Transport supplies process delivery and segmentation. C incorrect Physical transports signals and bits rather than process messages. D incorrect Data link supplies hop-local frame delivery rather than process-to-process delivery.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 87 · Q01161
records.text: Q01161 Question 87 NET22 NET23 NET24 Which IP version uses 32-bit addresses and corresponding 32-bit subnet masks? Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule. A IPv6 B IPv4 C Addressing D None of the above IPv4 IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses, commonly written as four decimal octets, and its subnet mask selects a prefix within those 32 bits. IPv6 addresses instead contain 128 bits. The generic word addressing does not identify an IP version, and none of the above fails because the required version is listed. A incorrect IPv6 uses 128-bit addresses, not the required 32-bit addresses. B correct IPv4 addresses and their masks contain 32 bits. C incorrect Addressing is a general activity, not the IP version requested. D incorrect IPv4 is listed, so none of the above is false.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 88 · Q01195
records.text: Q01195 Question 88 NET19 NET30 What is the main goal of data compression while it paths in different network layers? Its goal is to: Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A Securing data B Minimize the size of data C Select the best path of destination devices D All of the above Minimize the size of data NET19 distinguishes reducing representation size from hiding content. Compression targets the amount of data needed to represent information, while encryption provides concealment and routing selects paths. Therefore minimizing size is the compression goal; combining it with security and path selection in the all option misattributes unrelated functions. A incorrect Securing or concealing content is an encryption/security function, not the primary goal of compression. B correct Compression reduces representation size, directly matching minimization of data size. C incorrect Path selection belongs to routing rather than the representation-size transformation performed by compression. D incorrect Only size reduction describes compression here; security and route selection are separate functions.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 89 · Q01218
records.text: Q01218 Question 89 NET21 Which single option gives the complete set of listed protocols used by end users to retrieve or synchronize stored mailboxes? Identify the requested service or delivery guarantee, then distinguish application roles, transport behavior and address configuration. A POP3 B IMAP C SMTP D Both POP3 and IMAP Both POP3 and IMAP POP3 retrieves stored messages, while IMAP accesses and synchronizes mailboxes held on the server. SMTP instead submits and relays messages between mail-system components. Since the question asks for the complete set of mailbox-access protocols, either POP3 or IMAP alone is incomplete. The combined choice correctly includes both without assigning mailbox retrieval to the mail transfer protocol. A incorrect POP3 retrieves messages but alone omits IMAP, so it is an incomplete selection. B incorrect IMAP accesses mailboxes but alone omits POP3, so it is incomplete. C incorrect SMTP submits and relays messages; it is not the end-user mailbox retrieval protocol described. D correct Both POP3 and IMAP provide the requested mailbox-access functions.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 90 · Q01229
records.text: Q01229 Question 90 NET12 The data link layer divides the stream of bits received from the physical layer into manageable data units called ________________? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A Bits B Frames C Packets D Segments Frames The receive-side data-link description explicitly regroups physical-layer bits into frames. Evidence: PDF 15, 16, 15, 14. A incorrect Bits are the incoming physical units, not the regrouped unit (PDF 15, 16, 15, 14.) B correct Frames are explicitly the regrouped units (PDF 15, 16, 15, 14.) C incorrect Packets are network-layer units (PDF 15, 16, 15, 14.) D incorrect Segments are transport-layer units (PDF 15, 16, 15, 14.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 91 · Q01258
records.text: Q01258 Question 91 NET25 NET24 What is the maximum number of IP addresses that can be assigned to hosts on a local subnet that uses the 255.255.255.224 subnet mask? Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule. A 14 B 32 C 24 D 30 30 usable host addresses The final mask octet 224 is 11100000, making the prefix /27 and leaving five host bits. There are 2^5=32 addresses in each block. For an ordinary broadcast subnet, one identifies the network and one the broadcast, leaving 30 assignable host addresses; total addresses must not be confused with usable hosts. A incorrect Fourteen usable hosts would correspond to /28, not this /27 mask. B incorrect Thirty-two is the total address count before reserving the network and broadcast addresses. C incorrect Twenty-four is not the usable count obtained from five host bits and two reservations. D correct Five host bits yield 32 total addresses minus two reserved addresses, leaving 30 hosts.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 92 · Q01270

Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule. A Token Ring B Ethernet C X.25 or Frame Relay D None X.25 or Frame Relay The module explicitly contrasts LAN Ethernet/Token Ring with WAN X.25/Frame Relay. Evidence: PDF 26. A incorrect Token Ring is explicitly a LAN technology (PDF 26.) B incorrect Ethernet is explicitly a LAN technology (PDF 26.) C correct X.25 and Frame Relay are explicitly WAN technologies (PDF 26.) records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 93 · Q01276
records.text: Q01276 Question 93 NET20 NET16 Which internet layer address is responsible for providing diagnostic functions and reporting errors or conditions regarding the delivery of IP packets? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A Internet Protocol (IP) B Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) C Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) D Internet Group Message Protocol (IGMP) Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP) ICMP reports transit problems and supports destination-unreachable, echo and timeout diagnostics. The stem calls it an address, but asks for a protocol by its functions. Evidence: PDF 17, 27, 17, 17. A incorrect IP supplies best-effort datagram delivery (PDF 17, 27, 17, 17.) B incorrect ARP resolves IP to hardware address (PDF 17, 27, 17, 17.) C correct ICMP explicitly provides error/diagnostic messages (PDF 17, 27, 17, 17.) D incorrect IGMP supports group recipients rather than these transit diagnostics (PDF 17, 27, 17, 17.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 94 · Q01277
records.text: Q01277 Question 94 NET26 NET25 Hana divides a 172.16.0.0/16 parent into equal /19 broadcast subnets. Counting every subnet, which option correctly gives the subnet count and usable hosts per subnet? Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule. A 7 subnets and 30 valid hosts B 8 subnets and 8190 usable hosts in each subnet C 8 subnets and 2046 valid hosts in each subnet D 7 subnets and 2046 valid hosts in each subnet 8 subnets and 8190 usable hosts in each subnet The /16-to-/19 subdivision borrows three bits, so it creates eight equal subnets. Each /19 leaves thirteen host bits, producing 8192 total addresses and 8190 usable hosts after network and broadcast reservations. Modern counting includes every subnet. The option changes only the obsolete subnet count; the calculation still requires distinguishing child subnet count from host capacity. A incorrect Neither seven subnets nor thirty usable hosts follows from /19; thirty hosts would require /27. B correct Three subnet bits give eight subnets and thirteen host bits give 8190 usable hosts. C incorrect Eight subnets is correct for the stated /16 parent, but a /19 has 8190 usable hosts rather than 2046. D incorrect Seven lacks a stated counting basis, and 2046 hosts corresponds to /21 rather than /19.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 95 · Q01494
records.text: Q01494 Question 95 NET10 NET09 A switch-based LAN is more efficient than a hub-based LAN because: Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions. A A switch can connect two different LANs together B A switch allows multiple computers to send at the same time C A hub uses reservation-based MAC protocols D A switch uses contention-based MAC protocols E A switch is easier to implement than a hub. A switch allows multiple computers to send at the same time Switches direct frames toward the MAC recipient instead of copying all traffic to every port. Independent point-to-point communication permits multiple simultaneous exchanges on suitable separate ports. Evidence: PDF 12, 12. A incorrect Connecting LANs is not the efficiency distinction in the switch/hub comparison (PDF 12, 12.) B correct Selective independent port communication explains the improvement (PDF 12, 12.) records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 96 · Q01496
records.text: Q01496 Question 96 NET31 Compare circuit switching versus datagram packet switching. An advantage of circuit switching is it: Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions. A Allows end hosts to use different line rates. B Can guarantee the performance delivered to end hosts. C Establishes a connection before sending data. D Sends packets instead of signals. E Is non-blocking. F Is efficient when the amount of traffic to be sent by end hosts varies over time. Reserved resources can guarantee performance The reserved-resource circuit supports predictable allocated bandwidth and performance, the advantage contrasted with datagram links shared statistically. Establishing a connection is a procedural characteristic and imposes setup cost rather than itself guaranteeing a benefit. The note explicitly identifies blocking and wasted reservation during silence, ruling out the nonblocking and variable-traffic-efficiency claims. A incorrect Different endpoint line rates are not the reserved-circuit advantage established in the note. B correct Reserved resources provide predictable allocated bandwidth and can guarantee the agreed performance to endpoints. C incorrect Setup is a characteristic of circuit operation, but is not itself the performance advantage requested. D incorrect Circuit switching establishes reserved resources; packet-versus-signal wording does not describe its advantage. E incorrect NET31 explicitly identifies blocking as a circuit-switching tradeoff. F incorrect Reservations can be wasted during silence, making highly variable traffic less efficient on fixed circuits.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 109 · Q01533
records.text: Q01533 Question 109 NET07 A new network backbone needs high capacity, long reach and immunity to electromagnetic interference in the transmission medium. records.text: Q01535 Question 111 NET09 The portion of physical layer that interfaces with the media access control sublayer is called ___________ Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 113 · Q01537
records.text: Q01537 Question 113 NET09 NET15 Which single option gives the complete set of listed operations that can be implemented as physical-layer transmission coding or modulation? Channel coding in this question means redundancy used in transmission coding, rather than every possible higher-layer error-control mechanism. Under that scope, all three operations can be physical-layer work. Each individual choice names only part of the qualifying set, so the inclusive option is the complete response. A incorrect Line coding is physical signaling work, but alone omits the other qualifying operations. B incorrect Physical channel coding adds transmission redundancy, but alone is incomplete. C incorrect Modulation is a physical transmission operation, but alone is incomplete. D correct Line coding, physical channel coding and modulation all qualify, making this the complete set.

records.text: Q01542 Question 118 NET13 NET14 NET09 Under the OSI role convention used here, which task belongs to physical transmission coding rather than data-link framing and control? records.text: Q01543 Question 119 NET13 Which sublayer of the data link layer performs data link functions that depend upon the type of medium? records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 120 · Q01544
records.text: Q01544 Question 120 NET13 Which listed field identifies source or destination endpoints in a link-frame header, rather than synchronization or frame/control identification? Select one. records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 122 · Q01546

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 123 · Q01547
records.text: Q01547 Question 123 NET14 NET13 Which option gives the complete set of listed CSMA multiple-access mechanisms for shared-channel contention? Identify the requested service or delivery guarantee, then distinguish application roles, transport behavior and address configuration. A CSMA/CD B CSMA/CA C Both CSMA/CD & CSMA/CA D HDLC Both CSMA/CD & CSMA/CA CSMA/CD and CSMA/CA both govern shared-medium access. Legacy half-duplex Ethernet uses collision detection and backoff, while Wi-Fi uses collision avoidance procedures with waiting, backoff and acknowledgments. Selecting only one omits another valid listed mechanism. HDLC is a link framing/control protocol rather than either of these CSMA contention mechanisms, so the combined CSMA option is complete. A incorrect CSMA/CD is a valid mechanism but omits the other listed CSMA mechanism. B incorrect CSMA/CA is a valid mechanism but omits the other listed CSMA mechanism. C correct This includes both listed CSMA contention mechanisms. D incorrect HDLC is a link framing/control protocol, not a listed CSMA medium-contention mechanism.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 125 · Q01549
records.text: Q01549 Question 125 NET16 NET17 NET30 For IPv4 as described in the note, which listed function is not provided by IP itself? Here “error control” means header checksum error detection. Separate address width, syntax, reserved scope and the supplied prefix or historical classful convention. A routing B inter-networking C congestion control D error control congestion control IPv4 supports logical packet delivery across networks, including routing, and checks its header with a checksum. The use of error control therefore refers to detection, not reliable end-to-end recovery. TCP supplies congestion control to protect network capacity; IPv4 itself does not provide TCP’s congestion-control service. The question separates those protocol services instead of denying that the network layer ever detects errors. A incorrect Routing is explicitly a network-layer function, so it cannot be the requested exception. B incorrect Forwarding packets between networks is an established network-layer responsibility. C correct Congestion control of the kind protecting network capacity is a TCP service rather than a service supplied by IPv4 itself. D incorrect IPv4 detects header corruption with its checksum, so error detection is present under the stated meaning.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 128 · Q01552
records.text: Q01552 Question 128 NET30 In a multi-destination scheme that carries an explicit list of multiple selected targets in each packet, which statements are incorrect as general descriptions? records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 131 · Q01555
records.text: Q01555 Question 131 NET12 NET18 At a sending host, transport identifies data from different application endpoints using ports and forms segments or datagrams. To which OSI layer does it pass these units directly? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A network layer B data link layer C application layer D physical layer network layer On the sending path, transport creates segments or datagrams and hands them to the network layer for packet delivery. The network layer then uses the data-link layer, which in turn uses physical signaling. Ports distinguish application endpoints; this multiplexing does not merge unrelated applications into one undifferentiated TCP byte stream. The answer follows the immediate downward interface in the OSI stack. A correct The network layer immediately receives transport units on the sending path. B incorrect Data link is below network, not immediately below transport. C incorrect Application is above transport rather than its downward delivery target. D incorrect Physical is below both network and data link.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 132 · Q01556
records.text: Q01556 Question 132 NET17 NET21 Which of the following are transport layer protocols used in networking? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A TCP and FTP B UDP and HTTP C TCP and UDP D HTTP and FTP TCP and UDP TCP and UDP are explicitly transport protocols; FTP and HTTP are application services. Evidence: PDF 18, 18. A incorrect FTP makes this pair include an application protocol (PDF 18, 18.) B incorrect HTTP makes this pair include an application protocol (PDF 18, 18.) C correct Both are explicitly transport protocols (PDF 18, 18.) D incorrect Both are application services, not transport protocols (PDF 18, 18.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 133 · Q01557
records.text: Q01557 Question 133 NET17 User datagram protocol is called connectionless because _____________ Identify the requested service or delivery guarantee, then distinguish application roles, transport behavior and address configuration. A all UDP packets are treated independently by transport layer B it sends data as a stream of related packets C it is received in the same order as sent order D it sends data very quickly UDP treats datagrams independently without connection setup Connectionless UDP sends independent datagrams without establishing a transport connection. NET17 explicitly separates this from TCP’s reliable ordered byte stream. Fast transmission may be desirable but is not the definition of connectionlessness, and UDP itself does not preserve send order or combine datagrams into an ordered related stream. A correct Independent datagram treatment without built-in setup directly explains why UDP is connectionless. B incorrect An ordered related byte stream describes TCP’s service rather than UDP’s independent datagrams. C incorrect UDP provides no built-in ordering guarantee, so reception need not match transmission order. D incorrect Speed is not the defining condition; connectionlessness concerns the absence of connection establishment and associated state.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 134 · Q01558
records.text: Q01558 Question 134 NET18 NET17 For one TCP connection, which single option gives the complete set of correct descriptions? Identify the requested service or delivery guarantee, then distinguish application roles, transport behavior and address configuration. A is a connection-oriented protocol B uses a three way handshake to establish a connection C receives data from application as a single stream D all of the mentioned all of the mentioned TCP establishes logical transport connection state through the SYN, SYN+ACK and ACK exchange. It then provides an ordered byte-stream service for that connection rather than preserving individual application message boundaries. All three descriptions apply to one TCP connection. Each individual response is therefore incomplete under the complete-set instruction, while the inclusive option collects all of the valid properties. A incorrect TCP is connection-oriented, but this choice alone omits its handshake and stream properties. B incorrect TCP uses a three-way handshake, but that alone is an incomplete set. C incorrect TCP accepts an application byte stream within a connection, but this alone is incomplete. D correct Connection orientation, three-way setup and a per-connection byte stream are all valid.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 135 · Q01559
records.text: Q01559 Question 135 NET17 A _____ is a TCP name for a transport service access point. Identify the requested service or delivery guarantee, then distinguish application roles, transport behavior and address configuration. A port B pipe C node D protocol port Ports identify source/destination applications or processes for transport delivery, fitting a transport service access point in this question. Evidence: PDF 28, 16. A correct Port is the module application/process identifier (PDF 28, 16.) B incorrect Pipe is not the described TCP endpoint identifier (PDF 28, 16.) C incorrect Node is a network device rather than application endpoint (PDF 28, 16.) D incorrect Protocol names rules, not the numeric process endpoint (PDF 28, 16.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 136 · Q01560
records.text: Q01560 Question 136 NET17 NET14 Which phrase names the precise transport-layer endpoint-delivery responsibility in the OSI model? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A application to application communication B process to process communication C node to node communication D man to man communication process to process communication Transport provides process-to-process delivery, with ports identifying transport endpoints. Application-to-application communication is a broader description of what that service supports, but it does not name the precise endpoint-delivery term requested here. Hop or node-to-node frame delivery belongs to the data-link layer. Human communication describes an application purpose rather than the protocol endpoint responsibility used to distinguish the OSI layers. A incorrect Applications use transport, but this broad description does not name the precise process-delivery term requested. B correct Process-to-process is the precise transport endpoint-delivery responsibility. C incorrect Hop/node-to-node frame delivery is a link-layer responsibility rather than transport process delivery. D incorrect Human-to-human interaction is not the protocol endpoint service defining transport.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 137 · Q01561
records.text: Q01561 Question 137 NET31 A local telephone network is an example of a _______ network. Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule. A Packet switched B Circuit switched C Bit switched D Line switched Circuit switched Assuming the traditional local circuit telephone network, call setup creates a dedicated circuit and teardown releases it. This identifies circuit switching. A incorrect Packet switching is discrete packet communication B correct Circuit switching matches the traditional dedicated-call assumption C incorrect Bit switched is not a listed switching category D incorrect Line switched is not a listed switching category

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 138 · Q01562
records.text: Q01562 Question 138 NET31 NET14 Most packet switches use this principle ____________ Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions. A Stop and wait B Store and forward C Store and wait D Stop and forward Store and forward Packet store-and-forward means receiving the complete packet or frame before forwarding it. That is the switching principle named by B. Stop-and-wait is instead a reliability procedure that sends one frame and waits for acknowledgment. Cut-through alternatives exist, so the answer identifies the conventional principle without claiming every switch must use it. A incorrect Stop-and-wait is a link reliability/flow procedure involving acknowledgments, not the switching-buffering principle. B correct Store-and-forward buffers the full packet or frame before sending it on the next link. C incorrect Store and wait is not the defined switching principle named in NET31. D incorrect Stop and forward is not the defined receive-complete-then-forward switching procedure.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 139 · Q01563
records.text: Q01563 Question 139 NET21 NET17 Which is not a application layer protocol? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A HTTP B SMTP C FTP D TCP TCP TCP is explicitly transport, whereas SMTP/FTP and the HTTP service belong to the application side. Evidence: PDF 18, 18, 28. A incorrect HTTP appears as an application service in the port table (PDF 18, 18, 28.) B incorrect SMTP is in the application protocol list (PDF 18, 18, 28.) C incorrect FTP is explicitly application file transfer (PDF 18, 18, 28.) D correct TCP is explicitly a transport protocol (PDF 18, 18, 28.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 140 · Q01564

Message is the suitable upper/application unit among these options. Evidence: PDF 5, 16, 16, 15, 15. A incorrect Packet is network-layer terminology B correct Message names the communicated upper data C incorrect Segment is transport terminology D incorrect Frame is data-link terminology

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 141 · Q01565
records.text: Q01565 Question 141 NET02 NET21 Which one of the following is an architecture paradigms? Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule. A Peer to peer B Client-server C HTTP D Both Peer-to-Peer & Client-Server Both Peer-to-Peer & Client-Server The architecture section explicitly describes client-server and peer-to-peer; HTTP is a protocol rather than that resource-service arrangement. Evidence: PDF 24, 18. A incorrect Peer-to-peer is an architecture, but the combined option includes the other valid architecture (PDF 24, 18.) B incorrect Client-server is an architecture, but the combined option includes the other valid architecture (PDF 24, 18.) C incorrect HTTP is a protocol/service, not either listed architecture paradigm (PDF 24, 18.) D correct Both named architectures are explicitly described (PDF 24, 18.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 142 · Q01566
records.text: Q01566 Question 142 NET17 Application developer has permission to decide the following on transport layer side Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A Transport layer protocol B Maximum buffer size C Both Transport layer protocol and Maximum buffer size D None of the mentioned Choose transport protocol and request buffer size, subject to OS limits NET17 permits an application to choose its transport protocol and request socket-buffer sizes. In that application-configuration sense, C combines both choices. “Maximum buffer size” must mean the requested socket limit, not authority to override the operating system’s enforced maximum; the note explicitly makes the request subject to OS limits. A incorrect Choosing a transport is permitted, but this option omits the also-permitted socket-buffer size request. B incorrect A buffer limit can be requested subject to OS limits, but this omits transport-protocol choice. C correct Both settings can be selected/requested by the application, with the buffer size constrained by the operating system. D incorrect At least transport choice and buffer-size requests are explicitly permitted, so none is false.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 143 · Q01567
records.text: Q01567 Question 143 NET19 NET17 Using “end-to-end” for application service and “process-to-process” for the transport service beneath it, which service does the application layer offer? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A End to end B Process to process C Both End to end and Process to process D None of the mentioned End to end The question explicitly separates an application service from the underlying transport service. The note describes end-to-end application service as building on process-to-process transport. Under those named scopes, the application layer offers the end-to-end service, while process delivery identifies the transport boundary. Combining both would collapse the distinction being tested; none of the mentioned fails because the application-service term is present. A correct End-to-end is the stated application-service scope. B incorrect Process-to-process names the underlying transport service in this question. C incorrect The combination assigns the underlying transport-service term to the application layer, contrary to the stated distinction. D incorrect The stated application-service term is offered in A.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 144 · Q01568

A IP B MAC C Port D None of the mentioned Port Port numbers explicitly identify the destination application/process, while IP identifies an interface and MAC a local physical endpoint. records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 145 · Q01572
records.text: Q01572 Question 145 NET18 In TCP connection establishment procedure, if a client chooses Initial Sequence Number of 395, and server chooses 260, then: Trace the handshake in order, keeping each endpoint’s sequence and acknowledgment fields separate. A The 1st segment sent will contain sequence number of 396 B The 2nd segment sent will contain acknowledgement number of 261 C The 3rd segment sent will contain sequence number of 261 D The 2nd segment sent will contain acknowledgement number of 396 E The 2nd segment sent will contain sequence number of 395 F The 3rd segment sent will contain acknowledgement number of 396 Second segment acknowledgment number 396 SYN consumes one sequence position. The first segment is client SYN seq395. The server’s second segment is SYN+ACK seq260 ack396, acknowledging the client SYN. The third is client ACK seq396 ack261. Comparing those fields shows only D matches; sequence numbers and acknowledgment numbers must not be swapped between endpoints. A incorrect The first client SYN uses its initial sequence number 395, not the next position 396. B incorrect The second segment acknowledges the client SYN with 396; 261 is the later acknowledgment of the server SYN. C incorrect The third segment’s sequence number is the client’s next position 396, not the server acknowledgment value 261. D correct The server’s SYN+ACK acknowledges client ISN 395 plus one, giving 396. E incorrect The second segment is sent by the server with its own sequence number 260. F incorrect The third segment acknowledges server ISN 260 plus one, giving 261 rather than 396.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 146 · Q01573
records.text: Q01573 Question 146 NET16 NET23 For IPv4 when fragmentation is permitted, which option gives the complete set of nodes that may fragment packets and the location of reassembly? Separate address width, syntax, reserved scope and the supplied prefix or historical classful convention. A Fragment at the source host; re-assemble at the destination host B Fragment at the source host and routers; re-assemble at the destination host C Fragment at the source host and routers; re-assemble at the routers and destination host D Fragment at the source host; re-assemble at the routers and destination host E IP does not support Fragmentation and Re-assembly. Fragment at the source host and routers; re-assemble at the destination host IPv4 permits both the source and a router to fragment packets when fragmentation is allowed and an outgoing MTU requires it. The destination reassembles the fragments. Source-only fragmentation omits a permitted IPv4 case; it instead resembles the IPv6 restriction. Adding intermediate-router reassembly is incorrect. Naming IPv4 and asking for the complete permitted set makes the version-specific distinction explicit. A incorrect A source may fragment, but this option omits permitted IPv4 router fragmentation. B correct IPv4 sources and routers may fragment; only the destination reassembles. C incorrect Neither cited IP fragmentation rule places reassembly at intermediate routers. D incorrect Destination reassembly is required; the additional router reassembly claim is unsupported for either version. E incorrect Both version-specific rules support fragmentation and reassembly, although the allowed fragmenting nodes differ.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 147 · Q01574
records.text: Q01574 Question 147 NET17 Packets in one TCP connection can be distinguished from packets in another TCP connection by: Identify the requested service or delivery guarantee, then distinguish application roles, transport behavior and address configuration. A Source port, destination port, protocol number B Source IP address, destination IP address, protocol number C Source port, destination port, source IP address, destination IP address D Source IP address, destination IP address E Source port, destination port F Protocol number Both IP addresses and both port numbers All packets under discussion are already TCP, so their protocol identity is common. Distinguishing arbitrary simultaneous connections needs the endpoint four-tuple: source IP, destination IP, source port and destination port. Addresses alone cannot distinguish separate applications between the same hosts; ports alone can repeat between different hosts. C supplies all four required fields. A incorrect Ports and protocol can repeat between different host pairs, so this omits necessary IP addresses. B incorrect Two hosts can have several simultaneous TCP connections; addresses and TCP protocol alone do not distinguish them. C correct The source/destination IP addresses and source/destination ports form the TCP connection four-tuple. D incorrect An IP-address pair cannot distinguish multiple connections between the same two hosts. E incorrect The same source/destination port pair can be used with different IP-address endpoints. F incorrect Every connection in the stem uses TCP, so protocol number alone distinguishes none of them.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 148 · Q01630
records.text: Q01630 Question 148 NET08 Compared to other common topologies in LANs (such as bus, mesh, ring), which of the following is a disadvantage of using a star topology for LAN? Draw the links and identify shared components, alternate paths and the effect of the specified failure or growth requirement. A Poor performance due to sharing of point-to-multipoint links between users B Failure of a single station results in no stations being able to communicate C Failure of a single link results in no stations being able to communicate D Each station requires many network interfaces E Too many links needed in the network F Failure of a special node results in no stations being able to communicate Failure of a special node results in no stations being able to communicate The star description explicitly calls its hub/switch a single point of failure: failure of that central device brings the whole system down. Ordinary station/link failure is isolated. Evidence: PDF 23, 23, 23, 23. A incorrect Star has separate central links, not the bus shared-backbone defect (PDF 23, 23, 23, 23.) B incorrect Failure of an ordinary station does not remove the central device (PDF 23, 23, 23, 23.) C incorrect The module says a link failure affects only its attached device (PDF 23, 23, 23, 23.) D incorrect Many interfaces per station is the full-mesh burden (PDF 23, 23, 23, 23.) E incorrect Star uses more cable than bus/ring but less than mesh, so this is not the distinctive universal comparison (PDF 23, 23, 23, 23.) F correct The special central node is explicitly a single point of failure (PDF 23, 23, 23, 23.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 149 · Q01631
records.text: Q01631 Question 149 NET-S06 NET16 For IPv4 networks, distinguish interface IP addresses, transport port numbers and the IPv4 Protocol header field. Which statement is true? Identify the requested service or delivery guarantee, then distinguish application roles, transport behavior and address configuration. A The protocol number commonly used by web server applications is 80 B Every application must use a well-known port number C Each host and router in the Internet has only a single IP address D Client applications may dynamically select port numbers E A protocol number is used to indicate the version of IP being used Client applications may dynamically select port numbers Client applications commonly use dynamically selected ephemeral ports. Ports identify transport endpoints, whereas the IPv4 Protocol field identifies the carried upper-layer protocol, such as TCP or UDP. The separate Version field identifies the IP version. Port 80 is a usual HTTP service port, not an IP protocol number. Hosts and routers can have multiple addressed interfaces, so they are not restricted to one IP address. A incorrect 80 is a usual HTTP port number, not the IPv4 Protocol value for HTTP. B incorrect Clients may use ephemeral ports, so a well-known port is not mandatory for every application. C incorrect A device can have multiple addressed interfaces and therefore multiple IP addresses. D correct Clients may dynamically select ephemeral transport ports. E incorrect The IPv4 Protocol field identifies the upper-layer protocol; the Version field identifies the IP version.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 150 · Q01632
records.text: Q01632 Question 150 NET26 NET24 If you would like to give IP address to 57 hosts from your IP prefix which subnet mask do you use most effectively? Convert the mask to a prefix, separate network and host bits, and apply the relevant subnet-count or usable-host rule. A 255.255.255.248 B 255.255.255.240 C 255.255.255.224 D 255.255.255.128 E 255.255.255.192 255.255.255.192 For 57 hosts choose the smallest offered block with at least 57 total addresses: /26 (192=11000000) has 64. The next smaller /27 has only 32, and /25 wastes twice the space. Even the conventional two reserved addresses leave /26 sufficient. Evidence: PDF 19, 19. A incorrect 248 gives only eight total addresses (PDF 19, 19.) B incorrect 240 gives only 16 (PDF 19, 19.) C incorrect 224 gives only 32 (PDF 19, 19.) D incorrect 128 gives 128 and uses more space than necessary (PDF 19, 19.) E correct 192 gives 64, the smallest offered sufficient block (PDF 19, 19.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 151 · SM0021
records.text: SM0021 Question 151 NET21 NET16 Which one of the following is NOT correct about POP3 and SMTP? Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule. A A sender can send email using SMTP B Both are application layer protocols C A sender can receive emails using POP3 D Both are network layer protocols Both are network layer protocols The application-layer list includes SMTP and POP3; POP3 is explicitly for receiving mail. They are not network-layer protocols. Evidence: PDF 28, 18. A incorrect SMTP mail transfer supports sending (PDF 28, 18.) B incorrect Both appear in the application list (PDF 28, 18.) records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 152 · SM0022
records.text: SM0022 Question 152 NET02 A university’s private LANs and WANs provide services only to its staff, students and administrators. Which term best describes this system by its access scope? Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule. A Local Area Network B Intranet C Wide Area Network D Metropolitan Area Network Intranet The relevant distinction is who can access organizational services, rather than how far the links extend. An intranet serves an organization internally, so it can include both local and wide-area components. LAN, WAN and MAN describe geographic reach and cannot replace that access-scope classification. The option identifies an intranet without assuming a particular geographic footprint. A incorrect LAN describes geographic reach of local components rather than the organizational access scope requested. B correct An intranet serves the university’s internal members across its constituent networks. C incorrect WAN describes geographic reach of some components rather than the internal-access scope requested. D incorrect MAN describes metropolitan geographic reach rather than internal organizational access.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 153 · SM0025
records.text: SM0025 Question 153 NET09 NET10 At which layer of the OSI model are devices such as bridges, switches and Network Interface Cards used? Match the requested scope or data unit to the layer duties in the note; distinguish hop delivery from end-to-end process delivery. A Physical layer B Application layer C Network layer D Data link layer Data-link forwarding functions, with NICs also implementing PHY Bridges and ordinary switches inspect MAC frames at layer 2. A NIC commonly implements both physical and data-link functions, as NET09 explains; listing NICs here does not force all NIC work into one layer. D is the common frame/addressing layer for the listed devices’ relevant network-interface forwarding functions. A incorrect A NIC has physical functions, but bridges/switches make layer-2 forwarding decisions beyond signal repetition. B incorrect These devices’ MAC/frame operations are below application-service semantics. C incorrect Ordinary bridges and Ethernet switches do not route IP prefixes as their defining function. D correct Bridges/switches operate at layer 2, and NICs also implement link-layer MAC/frame functions.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 154 · SM0035
records.text: SM0035 Question 154 NET09 NET10 NET-S04 Which listed device is an end resource used by clients, rather than an intermediary that forwards, bridges or repeats network traffic? Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule. A Routers B Network printer C Wireless access point D Hubs Network printer A network printer is an endpoint resource that receives client jobs. A router forwards packets between networks, a wireless access point normally bridges wireless and wired link traffic, and a hub repeats physical signals among ports. These are intermediary roles in the comparison. The question classifies their normal function rather than claiming that an intermediary cannot also expose a management endpoint. A incorrect Routers forward traffic between networks and are intermediaries. B correct A network printer is the client-facing end resource. C incorrect A wireless access point normally bridges wireless and wired link traffic. D incorrect A hub repeats signals between attached devices and is an intermediary.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 155 · SM0036
records.text: SM0036 Question 155 NET01 NET-S02 ______ is a network architecture characteristic that states a network can expand quickly to address needs of new users and applications without having impact on the services delivered to existing users. Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule. A Security B Quality of service C Fault tolerance D Scalability Scalability Scalability is explicitly continued predictable function as system size grows, matching expansion without undermining existing service. Evidence: PDF 32. A incorrect Security concerns authorized access, not size growth (PDF 32.) B incorrect Quality of service is not the named growth principle (PDF 32.) C incorrect Fault tolerance is continued operation through failures rather than growth (PDF 32.) D correct Scalability is the explicit size-growth principle (PDF 32.)

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 156 · SM0038
records.text: SM0038 Question 156 NET02 Which network type is the largest as compared to the rest? Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule. A Wide Area Network B Metropolitan Area Network C The Internet D Local Area Network The Internet The Internet names the particular global network of networks, while WAN, MAN and LAN name scope categories. NET02 explicitly gives the Internet as the largest common WAN example. Thus C is the intended largest actual network in the comparison, even though WAN includes Internet-scale networks rather than being a disjoint smaller category. A incorrect WAN is a category that includes the Internet, not a separate specific network shown to be larger. B incorrect MAN spans a metropolitan area rather than the global network of networks. C correct NET02 identifies the global Internet as the largest common WAN example. D incorrect LAN covers a local building/campus and is much narrower in geographic scope.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 157 · SM0057
records.text: SM0057 Question 157 NET31 Which statement is incorrect when packet switching means connectionless datagram switching? Compare signal repetition, frame forwarding, packet routing and policy enforcement using the stated device or traffic assumptions. A In packet switching, messages are sent in small blocks B In packet switching, an end-to-end connection has to be established C In circuit switching, a channel is dedicatedly used D For bursty traffic, statistical packet sharing can use capacity that dedicated circuits would reserve while idle. In packet switching, an end-to-end connection has to be established Datagram switching divides messages into packets and forwards those packets independently without requiring end-to-end connection establishment. Circuit switching reserves resources along a path. Statistical sharing lets bursty packet traffic use capacity that would otherwise remain reserved but idle; this is a conditional utilization advantage, not a universal claim that packets outperform circuits for every workload or metric. A incorrect Packet switching divides messages into smaller packets. B correct Connectionless datagrams do not require end-to-end connection setup. C incorrect Circuit switching reserves channel resources for the connection. D incorrect For bursty traffic, shared packet links can avoid idle dedicated reservations; the qualified statement is true.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 158 · SM0062

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 162 · SM0274
records.text: SM0274 Question 162 NET08 In which network topology should every computer have N-1 I/O ports when there are N computers in the network? records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 163 · SM0291
records.text: SM0291 Question 163 NET05 NET06 In data communication, data rate refers how fast we can send data and is measured in bits per second. Which one of the following is not a factor for data rate? Use the cited note definitions to identify the requested function or scope, then check each alternative against that same rule. A Travel distance B Levels of the signals [SS C Bandwidth available D Level of noise Travel distance is not an explicit channel-capacity formula variable NET05 gives Nyquist in terms of bandwidth and signal states, and Shannon in terms of bandwidth and signal-to-noise ratio. Distance is not an independent variable in those simplified capacity formulas, so A is the intended comparison. It can still affect practical achievable rate through attenuation and delay. The image confirms travel distance despite noise in another extracted option. A correct Distance is absent as an independent variable in the simplified formulas, although it affects real links indirectly. B incorrect The number of signal levels appears explicitly in Nyquist through log2(M). C incorrect Available bandwidth directly appears as B in both Nyquist and Shannon capacity expressions. D incorrect Noise affects signal-to-noise ratio and therefore the Shannon capacity limit.

records.title: Data Communication and Computer Networking — Question 164 · SM0292
