records.text: Q00607 Question 21 OS37 Which directory implementation is used in most Operating System? Follow namespace structure and distinguish names, underlying files and mounted filesystems. A Single level directory structure B Two level directory structure C Tree directory structure D Acyclic directory structure Tree directory structure, in the usual general-purpose OS sense. OS37 states that modern general-purpose systems commonly present hierarchical namespaces and defines a tree as allowing nested directories and absolute/relative paths. That directly supports the conventional tree-directory choice. This is a general-purpose namespace convention, not a measured claim about every OS ever built; links can add graph structure without replacing the hierarchy as the basic user-visible organization. A incorrect A single namespace without nested directories does not match the common hierarchical organization described. B incorrect Separating user directories alone is less general than the nested hierarchy specified for modern general-purpose systems. C correct Nested directories and paths form the tree/hierarchical organization the note identifies as commonly presented. D incorrect Links can add graph sharing, but acyclic sharing is not the basic common directory organization identified.

records.title: Operating System — Question 22 · Q00696
records.text: Q00696 Question 22 OS30 OS31 In the basic virtual-memory models, which technique divides the address space into fixed-size units mapped to equal-size physical frames? Split the address into page and offset, then apply the mapping and access checks. A Paging B Segmentation C A&B D All Paging Paging divides addresses into fixed-size pages and maps them to physical frames of the same size. Segmentation instead uses variable-length logical units such as code and stack. Thus the fixed-size condition selects paging alone. Both combined alternatives include segmentation and therefore fail that condition; fixed partitions elsewhere in an operating system are outside the page-versus-segment comparison. A correct Paging uses fixed-size pages and corresponding equal-size frames. B incorrect Segments are variable-length logical units, so segmentation does not satisfy the fixed-unit condition. C incorrect Including segmentation makes this combined choice fail the fixed-size requirement. D incorrect All includes the variable-size segmentation alternative and is therefore incorrect.

records.title: Operating System — Question 23 · Q00731
records.text: Q00731 Question 23 OS32 When does a page fault occur? Separate a permitted nonresident access from an illegal access and trace the required handling steps. A The page is present in memory. B Deadlock occurs. C The page does not present in memory. D Buffering occurs. The page does not present in memory. A demand-paging access to a nonresident page causes the trap (PDF p38). PDF p39 distinguishes a valid but absent page, which is brought in, from an invalid address, which terminates the process. C presupposes an actual reference to that page. A incorrect Resident page access proceeds normally (p38). B incorrect Deadlock is not the page-residency test on p38. C correct An accessed valid page absent from RAM causes demand paging (pp38–39). D incorrect Buffering is not the fault-triggering residency condition.

records.title: Operating System — Question 24 · Q00732
records.text: Q00732 Question 24 OS22 Which of the following is a condition that causes deadlock? Trace the resource dependencies and distinguish necessary conditions from evidence of an actual deadlock. A Mutual exclusion B Hold and wait C Circular wait D No preemption E All of these All four are standard necessary deadlock conditions. OS22 lists mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no-preemption and circular wait as the four necessary conditions in the standard reusable-resource model. Each substantive choice therefore names a valid deadlock condition, making all of these the comprehensive answer. The wording causes must not be read as saying one condition alone is sufficient; actual allocation/request dependencies still require inspection. A incorrect Mutual exclusion is one necessary condition, but the other three named conditions also belong to the standard set. B incorrect Hold-and-wait is necessary, but selecting it alone leaves out the other valid conditions. C incorrect Circular wait is part of the condition set, but it is not the sole valid listed condition. D incorrect No-preemption is necessary in this model, alongside the other three substantive choices. E correct All four substantive choices are standard necessary conditions; together their names give the complete condition set.

records.title: Operating System — Question 25 · Q00733
records.text: Q00733 Question 25 OS01 OS04 What is an operating system? Separate broad resource-management goals from individual services or applications. A System service provider to the application programs B Collection of programs that manages hardware resources C Interface between the hardware and application programs D All of above All of above The OS manages hardware and mediates users/program execution (PDF p5), and provides services to programs (p10). Thus each of A–C is a valid aspect of the definition and D collects them. A incorrect Program services are explicitly provided (p10). B incorrect Hardware and resource management are explicit (p5). C incorrect The mediation/interface role is explicit (p5), including program execution. D correct All three descriptions agree with pp5 and 10.

records.title: Operating System — Question 26 · Q00735
records.text: Q00735 Question 26 OS06 What is the ready state of a process? Decide whether the process is eligible, running or waiting, then identify the responsible queue or scheduling role. A When process is unable to run until some task has been completed B When process is scheduled to run after some execution C When process is using the CPU D None of the mentioned When process is scheduled to run after some execution Ready means waiting to be assigned a processor (PDF p16). B is the nearest paraphrase, provided scheduled to run means eligible and waiting, not already executing. A incorrect Waiting for an event is the Waiting state. B correct Eligible to receive CPU next matches Ready under the stated reading. C incorrect Using the CPU defines Running. D incorrect Ready is represented by B under the stated interpretation.

records.title: Operating System — Question 27 · Q00736
records.text: Q00736 Question 27 OS22 OS07 In the standard reusable-resource model, a set of processes is deadlocked when ____________. Trace the resource dependencies and distinguish necessary conditions from evidence of an actual deadlock. A Each process is terminated B All processes are trying to kill each other C Each process is blocked waiting for an event or resource that only another blocked member of the set can provide D None of the mentioned Each process is blocked waiting for an event or resource that only another blocked member of the set can provide Deadlock requires blocked participants whose needed event or resource can be supplied only by another blocked participant in the same set. The closed dependency prevents any member from progressing without intervention. Terminated processes are no longer waiting, and attempts to kill one another do not establish a resource dependency. The revised blocking option states the necessary relationship rather than merely predicting permanent delay. A incorrect Termination ends execution and does not define a set of blocked dependent processes. B incorrect Attempts to kill other processes do not establish deadlocked resource waits. C correct This states the closed dependency among blocked members that defines deadlock. D incorrect The revised C explicitly gives the deadlock definition, so none is false.

records.title: Operating System — Question 28 · Q00737
records.text: Q00737 Question 28 OS16 OS17 OS18 In Operating Systems, which of the following is/are CPU scheduling algorithms? Compare the ready jobs using the stated burst or remaining-time rule. A Priority B Round Robin C Shortest Job First D All of the mentioned All of the mentioned PDF pp23–25 explicitly cover priority, RR and SJF in the scheduling chapter, so D collects three genuine CPU scheduling policies. A incorrect Priority ordering is defined on p24. B incorrect Quantum-based scheduling is defined on p25. C incorrect Duration-based SJF is defined on p23. D correct All three belong to the chapter’s scheduling methods.

records.title: Operating System — Question 29 · Q00738
records.text: Q00738 Question 29 OS28 OS-S03 In which of the storage placement strategies a program is placed in the largest available hole in the main memory? Apply the stated hole-selection or base-and-bound rule with its explicit convention. A Best fit B First fit C Worst fit D Buddy Worst-fit. OS28 defines worst-fit as selecting the largest hole, directly matching the stem. Best-fit chooses the smallest adequate hole, and first-fit stops at the first adequate one rather than comparing all sizes. The buddy label does not state this largest-hole rule in the provided note. No numeric trace is necessary because the selection criterion itself is explicit. A incorrect Best-fit chooses the smallest adequate hole, which is the opposite size-selection criterion from the stem. B incorrect First-fit selects the first adequate hole in search order, not necessarily the largest available hole. C correct Worst-fit is explicitly the policy that selects the largest available adequate hole. D incorrect The supplied largest-hole criterion is defined as worst-fit; the buddy label is not that rule.

records.title: Operating System — Question 30 · Q00916
records.text: Q00916 Question 30 OS01 OS06 Which one of the following function of operating system is categorized under process management? Separate broad resource-management goals from individual services or applications. A Allocates the device in the efficient way B De-allocates the resources. C . Allocates the memory when the process requests it to do so. D Allocates the processor (CPU) to a process Allocates the processor (CPU) to a process CPU allocation is explicitly process/processor management (PDF p6). Memory requests belong to memory management (p5), and device allocation belongs to device management (p6). A incorrect Device allocation is listed under device management. B incorrect Resource deallocation is too broad and appears in several management categories, not this precise processor task. C incorrect Memory allocation is explicitly under memory management (p5). D correct Allocating CPU to a process is explicitly listed under processor management (p6).

records.title: Operating System — Question 31 · Q00928
records.text: Q00928 Question 31 OS01 OS03 What is the primary function of an operating system? Separate broad resource-management goals from individual services or applications. A To connect to the internet B To create documents and spreadsheets C . To design computer hardware D To act as an intermediary between users and computer hardware To act as an intermediary between users and computer hardware PDF p5 defines the OS as intermediary between users and hardware and controller of program execution. D states this general role; the other options are particular applications or other activities. A incorrect Internet connection is narrower than the whole OS definition. B incorrect Document authoring is a program activity, not the definition on p5. C incorrect Hardware design is not managing hardware during execution. D correct Directly matches the intermediary definition on p5.

records.title: Operating System — Question 32 · Q00935
records.text: Q00935 Question 32 OS34 A user installs a new printer. The OS automatically detects and configures it. This is an example of: Separate device hardware, device-specific software and general event or transfer mechanisms. A Plug-and-play functionality B Manual driver installation C . Manual hardware management D Resource allocation Plug-and-play functionality. OS34 defines plug-and-play as discovering and configuring compatible new hardware, with the qualification that a driver may still be required. That is exactly the printer scenario. The automatic wording excludes the two manual alternatives. Resource allocation may occur during configuration, but it is broader than the specific automatic detection/configuration feature requested by the question. A correct Automatically discovering and configuring the installed printer is precisely the plug-and-play behavior described. B incorrect The scenario explicitly says automatic detection/configuration rather than manual driver installation by the user. C incorrect Manual hardware management conflicts with the automatic configuration behavior specified in the scenario. D incorrect Resources may be assigned during setup, but the specific automatic discovery feature is plug-and-play.

records.title: Operating System — Question 33 · Q00944
records.text: Q00944 Question 33 OS22 In asystem, resources cannot be forcibly taken from processes; they must be released voluntarily. Which deadlock condition does this represent? Trace the resource dependencies and distinguish necessary conditions from evidence of an actual deadlock. A No Preemption B Hold and Wait C . Mutual Exclusion D Circular Wait No preemption. OS22 directly defines no resource preemption as requiring voluntary release. The stem repeats that resources cannot be forcibly taken, so the match is exact. Hold-and-wait concerns retaining one resource while requesting another, mutual exclusion concerns exclusive possession, and circular wait concerns a closed dependency chain. None of those separately states the prohibition on forced withdrawal. A correct Prohibiting forced withdrawal and requiring voluntary release is exactly the no-preemption resource condition. B incorrect Hold-and-wait concerns retaining a resource while requesting another, not whether forced removal is permitted. C incorrect Mutual exclusion limits concurrent holders; it does not itself require voluntary release. D incorrect Circular wait describes a closed chain of dependencies rather than the resource-withdrawal rule.

records.title: Operating System — Question 34 · Q00984
records.text: Q00984 Question 34 OS02 OS20 How does an operating system improve efficiency in a multi-user environment? Compare interaction, CPU sharing and deadline requirements under the stated system model. A By allowing only one user to access the system at a time B By disabling all background services C . By using time-sharing and process scheduling to allocate CPU time fairly among users and processes D By requiring manual intervention for each task . By using time-sharing and process scheduling to allocate CPU time fairly among users and processes Time-sharing switches CPU among users and gives each a small portion of time (PDF p7), reducing idle time and giving quick response. C captures that scheduling-based allocation. A incorrect One user at a time contradicts the simultaneous time-sharing service on p7. B incorrect Disabling background services is not the mechanism described. C correct CPU scheduling and time-sharing are explicitly the mechanism on p7. D incorrect Manual intervention per task is not the CPU-switching mechanism.

records.title: Operating System — Question 35 · Q00994
records.text: Q00994 Question 35 OS07 Which exits are involuntary? Here “Terminate exit” means an externally imposed kill, “Fatal exit” means an unrecoverable execution fault, and “Error exit” means the program chooses to exit after detecting bad input. Select all that apply. Separate creation, image replacement and termination; classify termination by its cause. A Normal exit B Terminate exit C Fatal exit D Error exit Terminate exit; Fatal exit An externally imposed kill and an unrecoverable execution fault stop a process involuntarily. Normal completion is chosen by the program, and detecting an input error then exiting is also a voluntary program decision. The meanings separate causes of termination instead of treating every use of the word terminate as one category. Thus the external-kill and fatal-fault choices are selected. A incorrect Normal completion is a voluntary exit. B correct The defined external kill imposes termination and is involuntary. C correct An unrecoverable execution fault imposes termination and is involuntary. D incorrect The program-detected error exit is a voluntary decision under the stated meaning.

records.title: Operating System — Question 36 · Q01085
records.text: Q01085 Question 36 OS08 How do we define the term Thread? Compare per-thread execution context with shared process resources and the stated thread mapping. A Device that controls input B Variable that controls movement C Controlled execution of applications D None of the above None of the above A thread is a separate flow of execution through process code with its own PC, registers and stack (PDF p27). None of A–C states that definition; controlled execution of applications is too broad to identify a thread. A incorrect A device is not the defined flow of execution. B incorrect A variable is not a flow of control with a stack and PC. C incorrect Generic controlled application execution does not distinguish thread from process or scheduler. D correct None of A–C gives the thread definition on p27.

records.title: Operating System — Question 37 · Q01186
records.text: Q01186 Question 37 OS06 Where are the list of processes that are prepared to be executed and waiting placed? Decide whether the process is eligible, running or waiting, then identify the responsible queue or scheduling role. A Job queue B Ready queue C Execution queue D Process queue Ready queue PDF p19 says processes wait in the ready queue for CPU allocation. That is exactly prepared to execute but awaiting a processor. A incorrect Job queue contains all processes in the system (p18), rather than specifically ready ones. B correct Ready queue is the explicit CPU-waiting queue (p19). C incorrect No separate execution queue is defined for this purpose. D incorrect Process queue is generic and not the specific named queue on p19.

records.title: Operating System — Question 38 · Q01192
records.text: Q01192 Question 38 OS02 OS06 CPU scheduling is the basis of ___________ Compare interaction, CPU sharing and deadline requirements under the stated system model. A Multiprogramming operating systems B Larger memory-sized systems C Multiprocessor systems D None of the mentioned Multiprogramming operating systems Process scheduling is explicitly essential to a multiprogramming OS (PDF p18), enabling loaded processes to time-share one CPU; multiple processors or unusually large RAM are not required. A correct Multiprogramming explicitly needs this CPU sharing (pp13,18). B incorrect Large RAM is not the defining scheduling basis. C incorrect Multiprogramming can assume a single shared processor (p13). D incorrect The module explicitly names multiprogramming.

records.title: Operating System — Question 39 · Q01251
records.text: Q01251 Question 39 OS26 An OS designer must choose between checking for deadlock after every resource request and checking periodically. No detection cost, request rate or acceptable delay is specified. Which conclusion about a universally best checking schedule is justified? Separate handling before allocation from actions taken after detection, and consider the cost of checking. A Both checking on every request and checking periodically are always equally optimal B Checking at fixed time intervals is always optimal C Checking on every resource request is always optimal D Neither schedule is universally best; the choice trades detection overhead against delay Neither schedule is universally best; the choice trades detection overhead against delay Checking after every request can discover a problem promptly but incurs repeated detection overhead. Periodic checking reduces check frequency while allowing a deadlock to persist until the next check. Which tradeoff is suitable depends on workload and acceptable detection delay. Without those criteria neither schedule is universally optimal, nor is there a basis for claiming they are always equally good. A incorrect The two policies need not have equal overhead or detection delay. B incorrect Fixed intervals may suit some workloads, but no universal optimum follows. C incorrect Per-request checks can impose excessive overhead despite earlier detection. D correct This states the overhead-versus-delay tradeoff without asserting an unsupported universal optimum.

records.title: Operating System — Question 40 · Q01265
records.text: Q01265 Question 40 OS35 OS03 Which listed operation is directly an OS/tool task? Here “bad-block recovery” specifically means autonomous drive-internal sector remapping, and “booting from disk” means the initial power-on stage before the kernel has been loaded. Identify whether data is in transit, retained for reuse or queued for a device. A bad-block recovery B booting from disk C disk initialization D all of the mentioned disk initialization Disk initialization and filesystem creation are identified as OS/tool work. Firmware starts the boot sequence before the kernel takes control, while a drive may use its own firmware to remap defective sectors. The question asks about that direct responsibility boundary, rather than broad coordination of every disk-related activity. Consequently disk initialization is the only matching choice, and the aggregate is too broad. A incorrect The specified bad-sector remapping is drive-firmware work, not the requested OS/tool operation. B incorrect The stage beginning boot is firmware work before kernel control. C correct Disk initialization/filesystem preparation is OS/tool work. D incorrect The other operations include firmware responsibilities, so all is too broad.

records.title: Operating System — Question 41 · Q01274
records.text: Q01274 Question 41 OS11 OS05 OS06 Which method is used to prevent threads or processes from accessing a single resource? Track available permits and blocked operations using the stated semaphore model. A PCB B Semaphore C Job Scheduler D Non-Contiguous Memory Allocation A semaphore can enforce one-at-a-time access. OS11 describes a binary semaphore as one permit and gives wait(m); critical work; signal(m) with m initialized to 1. This prevents competing threads/processes from entering the protected resource operation simultaneously; it does not mean nobody can ever use the resource. A PCB stores process state, a scheduler selects jobs, and allocation layout does not enforce this resource-access rule. A incorrect A PCB records execution and resource state rather than supplying atomic mutual-exclusion operations. B correct A one-permit semaphore with atomic wait/signal can serialize entry to the protected resource operation. C incorrect A job scheduler selects admitted or ready work; it does not by itself protect shared resource accesses. D incorrect Noncontiguous memory placement changes allocation layout rather than synchronizing access to one shared resource.

records.title: Operating System — Question 42 · Q01283
records.text: Q01283 Question 42 OS40 Which of the following is not a type of operating system? Use the stated historical or platform scope and distinguish origin from technical capability. A Windows B Linux C macOS D Microsoft Office Microsoft Office is an application suite. OS40 explicitly identifies Microsoft Office as an application suite and discusses Windows, Linux and macOS as OS/kernel families. Office runs using OS services rather than providing the core resource-management platform. Thus Office is the exclusion in this list. The kernel-versus-distribution distinction for Linux does not turn it into an office application or invalidate the conventional OS-family contrast. A incorrect Windows is identified as the Microsoft operating-system family, so it is not the application-suite exclusion. B incorrect Linux names a kernel used with distributions as operating systems, unlike the Office application suite. C incorrect macOS is an operating-system product rather than a user application suite in this classification. D correct Microsoft Office is explicitly described as an application suite, not an operating system.

records.title: Operating System — Question 43 · Q01284
records.text: Q01284 Question 43 OS01 What is the main function of an operating system? Separate broad resource-management goals from individual services or applications. A To manage hardware resources B To manage software applications C To manage user accounts D To manage network connections To manage hardware resources Hardware resource management is the general technical definition on PDF p5. Applications, accounts and connections are narrower services and cannot replace that umbrella definition. A correct Matches the hardware-management definition (p5). B incorrect Application execution is a service within that broader role. C incorrect Accounts are one aspect of network/user administration (p8). D incorrect Network connection management is narrower than OS-wide hardware management (p8).

records.title: Operating System — Question 44 · Q01285
records.text: Q01285 Question 44 OS04 OS27 OS30 OS31 Which of the following is not a memory management technique used in operating systems? Identify the abstraction layer and separate a protected service request from an application task. A Paging B Segmentation C Swapping D Virtualization Virtualization, in the virtual-machine sense. OS04 defines virtualization as presenting virtual machine environments and distinguishes it from virtual memory. OS27 describes swapping, OS30 paging and OS31 segmentation as memory-management mechanisms. Under the guest-machine sense used here, virtualization is therefore the option outside that list. The answer depends on that stated sense; the broader phrase memory virtualization would describe a different use of the word. A incorrect Paging maps fixed-size virtual pages to physical frames and is explicitly a memory-management mechanism. B incorrect Segmentation maps variable-length logical regions and is explicitly a memory-management mechanism. C incorrect Swapping moves a process to backing store and is a memory-management operation described here. D correct In the note’s guest-machine sense, virtualization presents virtual computers rather than naming these process-memory techniques.

records.title: Operating System — Question 45 · Q01286
records.text: Q01286 Question 45 OS19 OS15 OS16 OS18 Which of the following is not a process scheduling algorithm? Separate class assignment, movement between queues and the rule for choosing work. A First-Come-First-Serve (FCFS) B Round-Robin C Shortest-Job-First (SJF) D Binary Search Tree (BST) Binary Search Tree is a data structure. OS19 explicitly states that a binary search tree may implement a queue but is not itself a CPU selection policy. FCFS, Round Robin and SJF are actual scheduling algorithms described in OS15, OS18 and OS16. Consequently BST is the exclusion. Using a tree internally to maintain priorities would not change the selection policy into an algorithm called BST. A incorrect FCFS is a scheduling policy that runs ready bursts in their arrival order. B incorrect Round Robin is a scheduling policy assigning cyclic ready-queue turns bounded by a quantum. C incorrect SJF is a scheduling policy selecting the shortest next burst among ready jobs. D correct BST is a data structure that can support queue operations rather than a CPU scheduling policy.

records.title: Operating System — Question 46 · Q01287
records.text: Q01287 Question 46 OS36 Which of the following is not a type of file system? Distinguish a file operation, a resource handle, an offset and file metadata. A FAT32 B NTFS C EXT4 D HTTP HTTP is an application communication protocol. OS36 explicitly names FAT32, NTFS and ext4 as filesystem formats and contrasts HTTP as an application communication protocol. Filesystems organize stored file content and metadata; a communication protocol does not become a filesystem merely because it transfers file contents. Therefore HTTP is the single option outside the stated filesystem-format category. A incorrect FAT32 is explicitly identified as a filesystem format, making it a member of the requested category. B incorrect NTFS is explicitly identified as a filesystem format, not a communication-protocol exclusion. C incorrect ext4 is explicitly identified as a filesystem format in the complete study note. D correct HTTP is an application communication protocol rather than a filesystem format for organizing stored files.

records.title: Operating System — Question 47 · Q01288
records.text: Q01288 Question 47 OS34 What is the purpose of a device driver in an operating system? Separate device hardware, device-specific software and general event or transfer mechanisms. A To manage user accounts B To manage hardware resources C To manage software applications D To manage network connections To manage hardware resources A driver implements I/O behavior for a device class and hides hardware peculiarities (PDF pp10,47). B is the closest option when hardware resources means its particular device; it should not imply one driver manages every resource. A incorrect Account administration is not the device-specific I/O job. B correct Device hardware I/O management is supported (pp10,47). C incorrect Applications use driver services but the driver does not manage applications generally. D incorrect Only a network-device driver concerns a network adapter; that is not every driver’s purpose.

records.title: Operating System — Question 48 · Q01289
records.text: Q01289 Question 48 OS39 Which listed forms can serve as user interfaces to an operating system? Treat possible interface forms generally, rather than features of a particular product. Select all that apply. Distinguish identity checks, permission checks and the particular security property at issue. A Command-line interface (CLI) B Graphical user interface (GUI) C Natural language interface (NLI) D Virtual reality interface (VRI) Command-line interface (CLI); Graphical user interface (GUI); Natural language interface (NLI); Virtual reality interface (VRI) Command lines, graphical interfaces, speech or natural-language interaction, and virtual-reality interaction are possible interface forms. An OS need not implement all of them for each form to count as a possible interface. Because the stated question asks about capability in general rather than a particular product’s installed features, all four listed forms satisfy it. A correct A CLI accepts text commands as a user interface. B correct A GUI provides graphical controls for user interaction. C correct Natural-language or speech interaction is a possible interface form. D correct VR interaction is also a possible interface form.

records.title: Operating System — Question 49 · Q01290
records.text: Q01290 Question 49 OS03 OS01 Which of the following is not a component of an operating system kernel? Distinguish command interfaces, privileged core services and the stages of booting. A Process scheduler B Memory manager C File system D Web browser Web browser. OS03 defines the kernel through core resource management, protection and system-call handling, while explicitly calling browsers applications. Scheduling, memory management and filesystem service are core resource-management functions in the textbook kernel sense. Some systems move services outside a kernel, but a web browser remains the clear application-level exclusion from the listed ordinary kernel responsibilities. A incorrect Process scheduling is a core resource-management function in the textbook kernel model used here. B incorrect Memory management is a core resource-management function rather than the listed user application. C incorrect Filesystem service belongs to ordinary OS resource management in this textbook kernel-level comparison. D correct The note explicitly identifies browsers as applications rather than components implementing the kernel’s core role.

records.title: Operating System — Question 50 · Q01291
records.text: Q01291 Question 50 OS04 Which of the following is not a type of system call used in operating systems? Identify the abstraction layer and separate a protected service request from an application task. A Process control B File management C Network communication D Video editing Video editing is an application operation. OS04 lists process control, file/device management, information retrieval and communication as service categories. It explicitly distinguishes video editing as an application operation. Network communication falls within communication services, so it is not excluded merely because it uses sockets rather than local files. The category outside generic system calls is video editing. A incorrect Process control is explicitly included among protected operating-system service categories. B incorrect File management is explicitly included among operating-system services requested through system calls. C incorrect Network communication falls within the communication service category rather than being excluded from system calls. D correct Video editing is an application-level operation, not a standard generic system-call service category.

records.title: Operating System — Question 51 · Q01292
records.text: Q01292 Question 51 OS03 What is the purpose of a shell in an operating system? Distinguish command interfaces, privileged core services and the stages of booting. A To manage user accounts B To manage hardware resources C To manage software applications D To provide a user interface To provide a user interface PDF p54 calls the shell an interface to the kernel that takes user commands. D captures its interface role rather than an individual resource-management service. A incorrect Account management may be requested through shell commands, but is not its defining role. B incorrect Kernel provides low-level hardware services (p54). C incorrect Invoking applications is supported, but does not replace the general interface role. D correct Directly follows the user-command interface description (p54).

records.title: Operating System — Question 52 · Q01293
records.text: Q01293 Question 52 OS40 Which listed systems are proprietary OS products rather than open-source systems as a whole? Interpret Linux as the open-source kernel and Android as AOSP without vendor additions. Select all that apply. Use the stated historical or platform scope and distinguish origin from technical capability. A Linux B Android C macOS D Windows macOS; Windows Windows and macOS are proprietary products. The existence of open-source components within macOS does not make the complete product open source. Linux is treated here as the open-source kernel, and Android is explicitly restricted to AOSP, excluding proprietary applications or services bundled by device vendors. With that component-versus-product scope fixed, both macOS and Windows belong in the selected set. A incorrect Linux is the open-source kernel under the stated scope. B incorrect AOSP is open source; vendor additions are explicitly excluded. C correct macOS is a proprietary product even though some components are open source. D correct Windows is a proprietary OS product.

records.title: Operating System — Question 53 · Q01294
records.text: Q01294 Question 53 OS03 What is the purpose of a bootloader in an operating system? Distinguish command interfaces, privileged core services and the stages of booting. A To load the operating system kernel into memory B To manage hardware resources C To manage software applications D To provide a user interface Load the OS kernel into memory. OS03 places firmware/bootloader stages before transfer of control to a kernel loaded into RAM. This identifies loading the kernel as the bootloader purpose among the alternatives. Resource management is subsequently a kernel role, application management is a running-system function, and user interfaces are provided by shells/GUI components rather than defining the bootloader’s purpose. A correct The bootloader prepares the kernel in memory and transfers control to it during the boot sequence. B incorrect Core hardware-resource management is the kernel’s role after the bootloader hands over control. C incorrect Managing running applications belongs to the operating system’s runtime services rather than defining the bootloader. D incorrect Shells and GUIs provide user interfaces; that is not the bootloader’s principal role here.

records.title: Operating System — Question 54 · Q01295
records.text: Q01295 Question 54 OS08 OS-S02 What is the difference between a kernel-level thread and a user-level thread? Compare per-thread execution context with shared process resources and the stated thread mapping. A Kernel-level threads are faster than user-level threads B Kernel-level threads are managed by the operating system, while user- level threads are managed by the application C Kernel-level threads can access hardware resources directly, while user-level threads cannot D There is no difference between a kernel-level thread and a user-level thread Kernel-level threads are managed by the operating system, while user- level threads are managed by the application Application management of user threads is explicit on PDF p28; kernel management is explicit on p29. Kernel threads are generally slower to create/manage, and management location does not automatically grant application thread code kernel privilege. A incorrect Opposes the p29 slower-to-create/manage comparison. B correct Exactly matches management location on pp28–29. C incorrect Confuses scheduling/management by the kernel with execution privilege; p53 distinguishes user code from kernel code. D incorrect Management location and costs explicitly differ.

records.title: Operating System — Question 55 · Q01296
records.text: Q01296 Question 55 OS25 OS23 OS19 Which listed item is a general data structure rather than a deadlock-specific avoidance method or dependency-graph analysis? Compute remaining needs and simulate feasible completions before deciding whether an allocation is safe. A Banker's algorithm B Wait-for graph algorithm C Resource allocation graph algorithm D Binary search tree algorithm Binary search tree algorithm Banker’s algorithm checks whether tentative allocations leave a safe completion sequence and is an avoidance method. Wait-for and resource-allocation graphs represent dependencies used in deadlock reasoning. A binary search tree is a general data structure and does not, by its name alone, specify deadlock handling. The broader category distinguishes the unrelated item without misclassifying avoidance or detection as strict prevention. A incorrect Banker is a deadlock-avoidance method, so it belongs to the stated handling category. B incorrect A wait-for graph directly represents process dependencies for deadlock analysis. C incorrect A resource-allocation graph represents resource requests and assignments for deadlock reasoning. D correct A binary search tree is a general search structure rather than a deadlock-specific method.

records.title: Operating System — Question 56 · Q01297
records.text: Q01297 Question 56 OS05 OS01 What is the general execution role of a process in an operating system, regardless of the application it runs? Distinguish stored instructions, an executing instance and its saved execution state. A To manage user accounts B To manage hardware resources C To execute a program instance with its own address space and resources D To provide a user interface To execute a program instance with its own address space and resources A process is an executing instance of a program, accompanied by an address space and resources. Its application may administer accounts, interact with hardware through services, or display a user interface, but none of those specialized jobs defines every process. The execution option expresses the general role. It also distinguishes a running instance from a program stored as instructions. A incorrect Account administration is only one possible application responsibility. B incorrect Hardware management is an OS responsibility rather than the general role of every process. C correct Executing a program instance with an address space and resources is the process abstraction. D incorrect Many processes run without providing a user interface.

records.title: Operating System — Question 57 · Q01298
records.text: Q01298 Question 57 OS06 Which of the following is not a type of process state in an operating system? Decide whether the process is eligible, running or waiting, then identify the responsible queue or scheduling role. A Ready B Running C Blocked D Sleeping Beauty Sleeping Beauty The state list on PDF p16 contains Ready, Running and Waiting. Interpret Blocked as the waiting-for-event state. Sleeping Beauty is not one of this module’s five named states. A incorrect Ready is explicitly listed. B incorrect Running is explicitly listed. C incorrect Blocked is the conventional paraphrase of waiting for an event; Waiting is the module’s exact term. D correct Not present in the five-state model, and not a defined state term.

records.title: Operating System — Question 58 · Q01299
records.text: Q01299 Question 58 OS08 What is the difference between a process and a thread in an operating system? Compare per-thread execution context with shared process resources and the stated thread mapping. A A process is a unit of execution, while a thread is a unit of scheduling B A process is a unit of scheduling, while a thread is a unit of execution C There is no difference between a process and a thread D A process can have multiple threads, while a thread can only belong to one process A process can have multiple threads, while a thread can only belong to one process PDF p27 says every thread belongs to exactly one process and separate flows improve parallel execution; p29 supports multiple threads within one process. D directly expresses that relationship. A incorrect Processes and threads can both be scheduled (pp20,29); this is not an exclusive distinction. B incorrect Both may participate in scheduling and execution; reversal does not define their containment. C incorrect PDF p27 explicitly distinguishes heavy processes from light threads. D correct Directly follows the one-process-per-thread and multithreaded-process definitions (pp27,29).

records.title: Operating System — Question 59 · Q01300
records.text: Q01300 Question 59 OS11 OS10 OS34 Which of the following is not a type of synchronization mechanism used in operating systems? Track available permits and blocked operations using the stated semaphore model. A Mutex B Semaphore C Monitor D Keyboard Keyboard. OS10 describes monitors as protected operations with condition synchronization, and OS11 explains mutex/semaphore exclusion mechanisms. These coordinate concurrent execution. A keyboard is an input device rather than such a coordination abstraction. Interrupts generated by hardware may participate in event handling, but that does not make the keyboard itself a mutex, semaphore or monitor mechanism. A incorrect A mutex provides owned mutual exclusion and is a synchronization mechanism in the note. B incorrect A semaphore coordinates participants through atomic wait and signal operations, so it is a synchronization mechanism. C incorrect A monitor combines protected operations and condition synchronization, making it a genuine synchronization abstraction. D correct A keyboard is a physical input device rather than a process/thread synchronization abstraction.

records.title: Operating System — Question 60 · Q01301
records.text: Q01301 Question 60 OS05 OS08 What is the purpose of a context switch in an operating system? Distinguish stored instructions, an executing instance and its saved execution state. A To save the state of a process or thread and switch to another process or thread B To manage hardware resources C To manage software applications D To provide a user interface To save the state of a process or thread and switch to another process or thread PDF p21 defines saving/restoring CPU context so execution can resume, enabling multiple processes to share a CPU. A identifies that specific operation. A correct Directly states save state and switch execution (p21). B incorrect Resource management is the wider OS purpose, not the specific state operation. C incorrect Application management is broader and omits saved execution state. D incorrect A user interface is not what a context switch provides.

records.title: Operating System — Question 61 · Q01302
records.text: Q01302 Question 61 OS09 Which item is an application-layer protocol rather than a primitive OS IPC mechanism such as a stream, shared region or message queue? Identify how data moves, which participant waits and what event allows the operation to continue. A Pipes B Shared memory C Message queues D HTTP requests HTTP requests Pipes provide streams, shared memory provides a common region, and message queues preserve messages. These are primitive IPC mechanisms in the stated classification. HTTP is an application protocol that can use an underlying communication mechanism such as sockets. It can certainly carry interprocess communication, but it is the only listed application-layer protocol rather than one of the primitive mechanisms requested here. A incorrect Pipes are primitive stream-based IPC mechanisms. B incorrect Shared memory is a primitive common-region IPC mechanism. C incorrect Message queues are primitive message-preserving IPC mechanisms. D correct HTTP requests use an application-layer protocol over an underlying mechanism.

records.title: Operating System — Question 62 · Q01303
records.text: Q01303 Question 62 OS04 What is the general purpose of a system call in an operating system? Identify the abstraction layer and separate a protected service request from an application task. A To manage user accounts B To request a protected kernel service C To manage software applications D To provide a user interface To request a protected kernel service A system call is the mechanism through which executing code requests a protected kernel service. Process creation, file reads and socket operations are examples. A program that manages accounts, applications or a user interface may use system calls, but those tasks are not the mechanism’s general purpose. The option captures the common role without restricting it to one kind of resource. A incorrect Account management can use system calls but does not define their general purpose. B correct Requesting a protected kernel service states the general purpose. C incorrect Managing applications is a possible use rather than the system-call mechanism’s definition. D incorrect A UI may issue calls, but providing a UI is not the general system-call role.

records.title: Operating System — Question 63 · Q01305
records.text: Q01305 Question 63 OS14 OS19 Which of the following is not a type of scheduling policy used in operating systems? Check whether the running burst can be interrupted before completion or blocking. A Preemptive B Non-preemptive C Cooperative D Infinite Infinite is not a scheduling-policy category. OS14 distinguishes preemptive and non-preemptive scheduling and explains cooperative scheduling as relying on voluntary release. OS19 explicitly rejects Infinite as a standard scheduling-policy category. Thus the first three labels describe genuine scheduling approaches, whereas infinite does not identify a selection or preemption rule. It should not be confused with a possible unbounded waiting-time outcome. A incorrect Preemptive scheduling can interrupt running work and return it to the ready state. B incorrect Non-preemptive scheduling retains a running burst until completion, blocking or voluntary release. C incorrect Cooperative scheduling is the recognized approach relying on voluntary release of execution. D correct Infinite names no scheduling selection or preemption policy in the provided note.

records.title: Operating System — Question 64 · Q01306
records.text: Q01306 Question 64 OS30 24.What is the purpose of a page table in memory management? Split the address into page and offset, then apply the mapping and access checks. A To translate virtual addresses to physical addresses B To manage user accounts C To manage software applications D To provide a user interface To translate virtual addresses to physical addresses Page number indexes a table containing physical page bases (PDF p34); combining the base with the page offset yields the physical address (p35). Thus a page table participates in virtual-to-physical translation, A. A correct Matches page-table address lookup (pp34–35). B incorrect User accounts are not the page-number-to-frame mapping. C incorrect Application management is broader than the translation data structure. D incorrect An execution address map does not provide the user interface.

records.title: Operating System — Question 65 · Q01308
records.text: Q01308 Question 65 OS35 What is the purpose of a system monitor in an operating system? Identify whether data is in transit, retained for reuse or queued for a device. A To manage user accounts B To manage hardware resources C To manage software applications D To provide information about system performance and resource usage Report performance and resource usage. OS35 says a system monitor reports CPU, memory, storage and network usage and measures rather than creating more resources. This matches providing information about performance and usage. User-account administration, hardware allocation and application management are broader OS/administration functions, not the monitor’s defining reporting role. Observing a resource is distinct from allocating or increasing it. A incorrect Account management is an administration function, not the monitor’s specified performance-reporting purpose. B incorrect The monitor measures hardware usage rather than serving as the general resource-allocation manager. C incorrect Application management is broader than the monitor’s role of reporting system performance and consumption. D correct Reporting system performance and resource usage directly matches the monitor definition in the note.

records.title: Operating System — Question 66 · Q01309
records.text: Q01309 Question 66 OS03 What is the difference between a kernel and a shell in an operating system? Distinguish command interfaces, privileged core services and the stages of booting. A A kernel is the core of the operating system, while a shell provides a user interface B A kernel provides a user interface, while a shell manages hardware resources C There is no difference between a kernel and a shell D A kernel manages hardware resources, while a shell manages software applications A kernel is the core of the operating system, while a shell provides a user interface The kernel is the core interacting with hardware (PDF p53); the shell takes user commands and interfaces to the kernel (p54). A preserves both roles. A correct Both halves match pp53–54. B incorrect Reverses the explicit roles. C incorrect The module lists and distinguishes the two layers. D incorrect First half is supported; invoking applications is only part of shell use, and omits its defining command interface.

records.title: Operating System — Question 67 · Q01310
records.text: Q01310 Question 67 OS36 OS04 Which of the following is not a type of system call used in file management? Distinguish a file operation, a resource handle, an offset and file metadata. A open() B close() C read() D write_database() write_database() is not a standard generic file-management system call. OS36 identifies open, close and read as ordinary file operations, and OS04 explicitly distinguishes database-specific write_database() as an application operation rather than a standard generic syscall name. A database operation may internally use actual file syscalls, but that composition does not make its application-specific name a generic kernel file-management call. A incorrect open obtains an open-file reference and is a standard file-management operation described here. B incorrect close releases an open-file reference and is a standard file-management operation. C incorrect read transfers bytes from an open resource and is a standard generic file operation. D correct write_database is an application-specific database operation rather than a standard generic file-management syscall.

records.title: Operating System — Question 68 · Q01311
records.text: Q01311 Question 68 OS10 OS11 OS34 Which item is a hardware/CPU event-notification mechanism rather than a high-level lock, participant rendezvous, or protected-operation abstraction? Identify conflicting shared accesses and the safety or progress property required. A Locks B Barriers C Monitors D Interrupts Interrupts Locks coordinate entry to protected state, barriers wait for participants to reach a common point, and monitors encapsulate protected operations with conditions. Interrupts notify the CPU of events and may help coordinate work, but belong to a different abstraction level. The classification therefore selects interrupts without denying that interrupts can participate in synchronization or completion notification. A incorrect A lock is a high-level mutual-exclusion abstraction. B incorrect A barrier is a participant rendezvous abstraction. C incorrect A monitor encapsulates protected operations and condition synchronization. D correct An interrupt is a CPU event-notification mechanism, the different abstraction level requested.

records.title: Operating System — Question 69 · Q01312
records.text: Q01312 Question 69 OS04 What is the purpose of a virtual machine in an operating system? Identify the abstraction layer and separate a protected service request from an application task. A To manage user accounts B To manage hardware resources C To manage software applications D To provide a virtualized environment for running multiple operating systems on a single physical machine A virtualized environment can run guest operating systems on one physical host. OS04 defines virtualization as presenting a virtual machine environment, often allowing guest operating systems on one host through a hypervisor. That is exactly the complete description in D. Account, hardware and application management may occur within host or guest systems, but those broad administrative roles do not define why a virtual machine is provided. A incorrect User-account management is not the defining purpose of presenting a virtual machine environment. B incorrect Hardware is mediated, but general hardware management alone omits the guest-machine environment requested. C incorrect Application management does not define a virtual machine or distinguish it from an ordinary running OS. D correct Providing guest-machine environments on one physical host directly matches the note’s virtualization definition.

records.title: Operating System — Question 70 · Q01313
records.text: Q01313 Question 70 OS09 Which item coordinates access but does not itself transfer arbitrary data payloads or request an operation in another process? Identify how data moves, which participant waits and what event allows the operation to continue. A Message passing B Shared memory C Remote procedure call (RPC) D File locking File locking Message passing transfers messages, shared memory carries data through a common region, and RPC requests an operation in another process or machine. File locking instead coordinates who may access a file or region. Locks can therefore be part of IPC synchronization while not being a payload-transfer mechanism themselves. The narrower wording makes file locking the unique match without denying its coordination role. A incorrect Message passing transfers data using send/receive operations. B incorrect Shared memory carries data in a common accessible region. C incorrect RPC communicates a request to perform another process’s operation. D correct File locking coordinates access rather than carrying arbitrary payloads itself.

records.title: Operating System — Question 71 · Q01314
records.text: Q01314 Question 71 OS36 OS37 What is the purpose of a file system in an operating system? Distinguish a file operation, a resource handle, an offset and file metadata. A To manage user accounts B To manage hardware resources C To manage software applications D To manage files and directories on storage devices To manage files and directories on storage devices The file system tracks file information and locations and organizes directories (PDF p6); files store information on secondary storage (p48). D captures these functions. A incorrect Account administration manages user identities and accounts, rather than organizing stored file contents and directory names. B incorrect Hardware-resource management spans processors, memory and devices; it is broader than the file system’s file-and-directory responsibility. C incorrect Application management does not describe file/directory organization. D correct Matches locations, directory organization and secondary storage (pp6,48).

records.title: Operating System — Question 72 · Q01315
records.text: Q01315 Question 72 OS08 OS05 In this question only, “task” means a thread within a process. Which statement describes the process–task ownership relationship? Compare per-thread execution context with shared process resources and the stated thread mapping. A There is no difference between a process and a task B A process is a unit of execution, while a task is a unit of scheduling C A process can have multiple tasks, while a task can only belong to one process D A task is a unit of execution, while a process is a unit of scheduling A process can have multiple tasks, while a task can only belong to one process With task explicitly defined to mean thread, a process may contain several tasks while each task belongs to one process at a time. The tasks share the process address space but have their own execution context. This ownership relationship does not follow from the word task universally; it follows from the definition supplied here. Execution-versus-scheduling slogans do not state that relationship. A incorrect A thread/task is not identical to its containing process under this definition. B incorrect The execution-versus-scheduling description does not express the defined ownership relationship. C correct A process can contain multiple threads/tasks, each belonging to one process at a time. D incorrect The reversed execution/scheduling labels do not describe thread ownership.

records.title: Operating System — Question 73 · Q01316
records.text: Q01316 Question 73 OS28 Which of the following is not a type of memory allocation algorithm used in operating systems? Apply the stated hole-selection or base-and-bound rule with its explicit convention. A First-Fit B Best-Fit C Next-Fit D Binary-Fit Binary-Fit is not one of the standard fit-policy names. OS28 defines first-fit, next-fit, best-fit and worst-fit, then explicitly says binary-fit is not one of these standard names. First-fit, best-fit and next-fit therefore belong to the allocation-policy category used by the question. Binary-fit is the supported exclusion; it should not be invented as a synonym for another algorithm merely because the word binary is familiar. A incorrect First-fit selects the first adequate hole and is an explicitly defined memory-allocation policy. B incorrect Best-fit chooses the smallest adequate hole and is an explicitly defined memory-allocation policy. C incorrect Next-fit resumes search from the previous position and is an explicitly defined allocation policy. D correct The note explicitly excludes binary-fit from the standard memory-allocation fit-policy names.

records.title: Operating System — Question 74 · Q01317
records.text: Q01317 Question 74 OS04 What is the purpose of a system call interface in an operating system? Identify the abstraction layer and separate a protected service request from an application task. A To manage user accounts B To manage hardware resources C To manage software applications D To provide a standardized interface for application programs to make system calls Provide the interface through which applications request system calls. OS04 defines a system call as requesting a protected kernel service and distinguishes an API/library wrapper from the direct boundary. Option D describes the interface that applications use to make those requests. Account, hardware and application management can be services reached through it; they are not the general purpose of the interface itself. A incorrect Account operations may be exposed as services, but account management does not define the interface itself. B incorrect Hardware operations may be requested through services; general hardware management is not the interface definition. C incorrect Application management is a possible service use rather than the purpose of the syscall interface. D correct The interface supplies the application-to-system-call request path for protected kernel services.

records.title: Operating System — Question 75 · Q01319
records.text: Q01319 Question 75 OS06 OS05 What is the purpose of a dispatcher in an operating system? Decide whether the process is eligible, running or waiting, then identify the responsible queue or scheduling role. A To manage user accounts B To manage hardware resources C To manage software applications D To switch the context of execution from one process to another To switch the context of execution from one process to another PDF p19 describes the dispatcher transferring execution to a queued process; p21 defines the context save/restore mechanism. D is the specific execution handoff rather than a broad management service. A incorrect Account management does not identify execution handoff. B incorrect Hardware management is a broad OS responsibility. C incorrect Application management is not the specific handoff operation. D correct Switching saved execution contexts matches pp19,21.

records.title: Operating System — Question 76 · Q01320
records.text: Q01320 Question 76 OS01 OS34 Which listed item is not a hardware resource managed by an operating system? Separate broad resource-management goals from individual services or applications. A CPU B Memory C Keyboard D User account User account CPU time, memory and input devices such as a keyboard are hardware resources allocated or controlled by the OS. A user account is an identity used in administration and protection, rather than a hardware device. The OS may manage accounts too, but that does not put them in the hardware-resource category. Completing the stem and replacing one option gives a unique exclusion. A incorrect The CPU is a managed processing resource. B incorrect Memory is a managed storage resource used during execution. C incorrect A keyboard is a managed input device. D correct A user account is an identity rather than a hardware resource.

records.title: Operating System — Question 77 · Q01321
records.text: Q01321 Question 77 OS05 39.What is the difference between a process and a program in an operating system? Distinguish stored instructions, an executing instance and its saved execution state. A There is no difference between a process and a program B A process is a running instance of a program, while a program is a set of instructions C A program is a running instance of a process, while a process is a set of instructions D A program is a unit of execution, while a process is a unit of scheduling A process is a running instance of a program, while a program is a set of instructions PDF p16 directly contrasts a dynamic executing process with a static program containing processor instructions. B states that distinction. A incorrect Contradicted by the explicit static/dynamic contrast. B correct Matches the definitions on p16. C incorrect Reverses program and process. D incorrect Program is static instructions, not itself an executing unit (p16).

records.title: Operating System — Question 78 · Q01322
records.text: Q01322 Question 78 OS36 OS-S04 Which listed operation can receive bytes from a socket while also serving as a generic file-input operation in the descriptor model? Distinguish a file operation, a resource handle, an offset and file metadata. A socket() B connect() C read() D send() read() Sockets can support the ordinary read/write interface as well as specialized socket operations. A read therefore need not be confined to disk files: it can receive bytes from a socket descriptor. socket creates an endpoint, connect establishes a connection, and send transmits data. Only read matches both the generic file-input role and the ability to receive socket data in this model. A incorrect socket creates a communication endpoint rather than reading bytes from it. B incorrect connect establishes a connection rather than receiving its data. C correct read is generic descriptor input and can receive bytes from a socket. D incorrect send transmits data rather than performing the requested input operation.

records.title: Operating System — Question 79 · Q01323
records.text: Q01323 Question 79 OS35 OS-S04 What is the purpose of a system clock in an operating system? Identify whether data is in transit, retained for reuse or queued for a device. A To manage user accounts B To manage hardware resources C To manage software applications D To provide a reference for measuring time and scheduling processes and events To provide a reference for measuring time and scheduling processes and events The clock driver maintains time and decrements the quantum counter to invoke the scheduler (PDF p46, section 12.3 Clocks). D is the matching time-and-scheduling purpose. A incorrect Accounts are not the clock’s task. B incorrect Generic resource management omits the clock’s time reference. C incorrect Software management is not its stated task. D correct Time of day and quantum expiration are both clock-driver functions on p46.

records.title: Operating System — Question 80 · Q01324
records.text: Q01324 Question 80 OS34 OS39 42.Which of the following is not a type of device managed by an operating system? Separate device hardware, device-specific software and general event or transfer mechanisms. A Input devices B Output devices C Storage devices D User accounts User accounts PDF p43 lists storage, transmission and human-interface hardware. User accounts concern authentication (p50), rather than physical I/O device categories. A incorrect Human input devices are listed (p43). B incorrect Screens and related human-interface devices are listed (p43). C incorrect Disks and tapes are storage devices (p43). D correct A user identity/account is authenticated, not a physical device (p50).

records.title: Operating System — Question 81 · Q01325
records.text: Q01325 Question 81 OS36 What is the purpose of a file descriptor in an operating system? Distinguish a file operation, a resource handle, an offset and file metadata. A To manage user accounts B To manage hardware resources C To manage software applications D To provide a reference to an open file or communication endpoint A process-local reference to an open file or communication endpoint. OS36 defines a file descriptor as a process-local integer handle and separately places offset and access mode in associated open-file state. It also describes sockets supporting ordinary descriptor I/O. The descriptor therefore refers to an open resource or endpoint; it is not an account manager, hardware manager or application manager. D is the specific role matching that definition. A incorrect A descriptor identifies an open resource within a process, rather than managing user accounts. B incorrect A descriptor is a handle used to access a resource, not a general hardware-management component. C incorrect Descriptors support resource I/O and do not manage application lifecycles or software installations. D correct An open-file or socket reference is the resource-handle purpose of a file descriptor.

records.title: Operating System — Question 82 · Q01454
records.text: Q01454 Question 82 OS03 OS04 What is the main function of the command interpreter? Distinguish command interfaces, privileged core services and the stages of booting. A to provide the interface between the API and application program B to handle the files in the operating system C to get and execute the next user-specified command D none of the mentioned to get and execute the next user-specified command The shell is a special interpreter that executes OS commands and application programs (PDF p54), taking user commands to kernel functions. C states that command-interpreter loop role. A incorrect The module places the shell between user commands and kernel, not API and application. B incorrect File handling is one possible command activity, not the interpreter’s general function. C correct Getting and executing user commands matches p54. D incorrect C already matches the supplied definition.

records.title: Operating System — Question 83 · Q01458
records.text: Q01458 Question 83 OS34 Which failures can OS software report or handle while it continues executing on powered hardware? C means complete power loss with no backup supply or advance notification. Select all that apply. Separate device hardware, device-specific software and general event or transfer mechanisms. A lack of paper in printer B connection failure in the network C power failure D all of the mentioned lack of paper in printer; connection failure in the network OS I/O services can report or respond to a printer running out of paper and to a network connection failure. Complete unannounced loss of power without backup prevents the processor from continuing to run the OS, so software alone cannot handle it during continued execution. The aggregate option includes that unsupported case. Under the explicit power assumptions, the printer and network choices are selected. A correct The OS can report or handle an out-of-paper printer condition while running. B correct The OS can report or handle a network connection failure while running. C incorrect Complete unannounced power loss without backup prevents continued software execution. D incorrect All includes the excluded total-power-loss case and is therefore incorrect.

records.title: Operating System — Question 84 · Q01459
records.text: Q01459 Question 84 OS-S01 Who among the following is credited as a co-creator of the UNIX operating system at Bell Labs, together with Ken Thompson? Compare the stated historical clues and distinguish origin, characteristic era and technical capability. A Charles Babbage B Alan Turing C Tim Berners-Lee D Dennis Ritchie Dennis Ritchie Dennis Ritchie is credited alongside Ken Thompson in Bell Labs’ account of UNIX’s creation. The other listed people are not that co-creator. A incorrect Babbage is not the UNIX co-creator alongside Thompson identified by Bell Labs. B incorrect Turing is not the UNIX co-creator alongside Thompson identified by Bell Labs. C incorrect Berners-Lee is not the UNIX co-creator alongside Thompson identified by Bell Labs. D correct Dennis Ritchie is the Bell Labs co-creator associated with Ken Thompson.

records.title: Operating System — Question 85 · Q01460
records.text: Q01460 Question 85 OS40 Which operating system was developed by Microsoft as a successor to MS-DOS? Use the stated historical or platform scope and distinguish origin from technical capability. A macOS B Windows C Linux D Solaris Windows. OS40 explicitly identifies Windows as the Microsoft family commonly described as succeeding the MS-DOS desktop era. That directly matches the stem’s company and predecessor clues. Linux is separately attributed to Linus Torvalds, Solaris to Sun, and macOS is a different proprietary OS product. No additional market-history claim is needed to resolve the listed alternatives. A incorrect macOS is not the Microsoft family identified as succeeding the MS-DOS desktop era. B correct The note explicitly identifies Windows as Microsoft’s successor family to the MS-DOS desktop era. C incorrect Linux is separately attributed to Linus Torvalds, not the Microsoft MS-DOS desktop succession. D incorrect Solaris originated at Sun rather than being Microsoft’s MS-DOS successor family.

records.title: Operating System — Question 86 · Q01461
records.text: Q01461 Question 86 OS-S01 Which listed operating-system family originated at Bell Labs in 1969 and later provided multiuser time-sharing with asynchronous processes? This asks for that system’s identity, not the first-ever invention of multitasking. Compare the stated historical clues and distinguish origin, characteristic era and technical capability. A MS-DOS B macOS C Windows D UNIX UNIX UNIX began at Bell Labs in 1969. Ritchie and Thompson’s primary paper describes the later system as multiuser and interactive, with asynchronous processes. These historical identifying facts come from the supplementary sources. OS40 supplies the related caution that UNIX was not the first system ever to multitask. The revised question preserves the history and multitasking focus while dropping that false priority claim. A incorrect MS-DOS is not the Bell Labs system originating in 1969. B incorrect macOS is not the original Bell Labs system identified by that history. C incorrect Windows is not the Bell Labs system described by Ritchie and Thompson. D correct UNIX matches the Bell Labs origin and the later multiuser time-sharing description.

records.title: Operating System — Question 87 · Q01462
records.text: Q01462 Question 87 OS40 Which operating system was developed by Linus Torvalds and is based on the UNIX operating system? Use the stated historical or platform scope and distinguish origin from technical capability. A Linux B Windows C macOS D Solaris Linux, Unix-compatible and written from scratch. OS40 attributes Linux to Linus Torvalds and calls it a Unix-compatible kernel written from scratch. The developer clue therefore uniquely identifies Linux. The phrase based on UNIX must be read as compatible/inspired in interface and design, rather than asserting copied UNIX source. The other named families do not match the explicit creator attribution given here. A correct Linux matches Linus Torvalds and Unix compatibility; the note explicitly says it was written from scratch. B incorrect Windows is the Microsoft family, not the kernel explicitly attributed here to Linus Torvalds. C incorrect macOS does not match the note’s explicit Torvalds attribution for the Unix-compatible kernel. D incorrect Solaris originated at Sun rather than being the kernel developed by Linus Torvalds.

records.title: Operating System — Question 88 · Q01463
records.text: Q01463 Question 88 OS40 Which operating system was developed by Sun Microsystems and is known for its scalability and reliability? Use the stated historical or platform scope and distinguish origin from technical capability. A Linux B Windows C macOS D Solaris Solaris. OS40 directly states that Solaris originated at Sun. That developer clue resolves the choices even though the note does not quantify Solaris’s reliability or scalability relative to other systems. The answer relies on the explicit origin, not on assuming those broad positive attributes uniquely distinguish one OS. Linux and Windows have separately identified developer lineages in the same section. A incorrect Linux is attributed to Linus Torvalds rather than being the Sun-originated OS requested here. B incorrect Windows is identified as the Microsoft family, not the Sun-originated product. C incorrect macOS does not match the explicit Sun-origin attribution provided by the complete note. D correct Solaris is explicitly stated to have originated at Sun, matching the decisive developer clue.

records.title: Operating System — Question 89 · Q01464
records.text: Q01464 Question 89 OS40 Which listed mobile operating-system platform uses Linux as its base kernel layer and has an open-source base called AOSP? Use the stated historical or platform scope and distinguish origin from technical capability. A iOS B Android C Windows Phone D BlackBerry OS Android Android uses Linux at its base kernel layer, with framework and application layers above it. Its open-source base is AOSP, although shipped devices may contain proprietary services or applications. Those architectural facts identify Android without needing an unspecified population or a dated market-share claim. The other listed mobile systems are not the platform identified by this particular combination of Linux and AOSP. A incorrect iOS is not the platform identified by the Linux/AOSP combination. B correct Android has the Linux base layer and the AOSP open-source base. C incorrect Windows Phone is not the Linux/AOSP platform described. D incorrect BlackBerry OS is not the Linux/AOSP platform described.

records.title: Operating System — Question 90 · Q01471
records.text: Q01471 Question 90 OS-S01 Using the first four generations described in NYU’s OS-history notes (vacuum tubes; transistors; integrated circuits; personal computers), which generation is associated with resident uniprogrammed batch operating systems, following the manual/no-resident-OS era? Compare the stated historical clues and distinguish origin, characteristic era and technical capability. A First Generation B Second Generation C Third Generation D Fourth Generation Second Generation The first four generations in NYU’s historical taxonomy associates second-generation transistor machines with uniprogrammed batch systems whose OS remains resident between jobs. The first era has no separate resident OS; the third emphasizes ICs and multiprogramming, and the fourth personal computers. OS02 explains batch operation, while the generation mapping is supplied by the supplementary university notes. This is a scoped teaching convention rather than a universal first-OS claim. A incorrect The first era is the manual/no-separate-resident-OS era in this taxonomy. B correct The second era pairs transistor machines with resident uniprogrammed batch systems. C incorrect The third era emphasizes ICs and multiprogramming rather than the initial resident batch stage. D incorrect The fourth era emphasizes personal computers and follows the batch-monitor era.

records.title: Operating System — Question 91 · Q01475
records.text: Q01475 Question 91 OS03 What is the primary function of a kernel in an operating system? Distinguish command interfaces, privileged core services and the stages of booting. A Provide a user-friendly interface B Manage system resources and provide core services C Run user applications D Facilitate communication with external devices Manage system resources and provide core services The kernel is the core, responsible for major activities and direct hardware interaction (PDF p53), providing services with privileged access. B summarizes this rather than a particular interface or device subset. A incorrect The shell supplies the user-command interface (p54). B correct Core services and resource access match p53. C incorrect The kernel runs processes, but application execution alone omits its wider central role. D incorrect External-device communication is one hardware activity, not the entire primary role.

records.title: Operating System — Question 92 · Q01476
