records.text: Q01476 Question 92 OS03 OS01 OS06 OS-S05 Which component of an operating system is responsible for memory management and process scheduling? Distinguish command interfaces, privileged core services and the stages of booting. A Kernel B User program C Compiler D File system Kernel Kernel is the major-activity core (PDF p53); memory management and ready-process selection are OS functions (pp31,20). Under the module’s architecture, A is the component responsible for these core services. A correct Kernel provides the core resource services (p53). B incorrect User programs request services rather than being the core manager (p53). C incorrect Compilation is not the ready-process or memory manager described. D incorrect File organization does not substitute for memory/CPU management.

records.title: Operating System — Question 93 · Q01477
records.text: Q01477 Question 93 OS03 OS-S02 In the module’s conventional architecture, where device drivers are kernel components and ordinary applications run with restricted privilege, which item normally executes in kernel mode? Distinguish command interfaces, privileged core services and the stages of booting. A User programs B Device drivers C Text editors D Web browsers Device drivers Kernel components perform privileged operating-system work. In the stated architecture, device drivers are such components, so they execute in kernel mode. User programs, text editors and web browsers are ordinary applications and execute in restricted user mode, requesting protected services when needed. User-space driver designs exist, which is why the architecture is stated rather than treating every driver implementation as privileged. A incorrect Ordinary user programs execute in restricted user mode. B correct The specified drivers are kernel components and therefore execute with kernel privilege. C incorrect A text editor is an ordinary application, so it runs in user mode under this architecture. D incorrect A web browser is an ordinary application and does not acquire kernel privilege merely by using OS services.

records.title: Operating System — Question 94 · Q01478
records.text: Q01478 Question 94 OS-S02 OS03 In the operating system’s user/kernel privilege model, which standard term names the restricted level used by ordinary application code? Classify execution privilege, rather than processor addressing modes. Distinguish where threads are managed from the privilege of the code they execute. A Kernel mode B Supervisor mode C User mode D Protected mode User mode Ordinary application code runs at the restricted user level and obtains protected services through libraries and system calls. Kernel mode is the privileged level; supervisor mode is commonly another name for that privileged level. Protected mode is not the name of the restricted application privilege level in the stated user/kernel classification. The question therefore selects User mode without making a claim about every processor’s architectural modes. A incorrect Kernel mode permits privileged OS operations and is not the restricted application level. B incorrect Supervisor mode denotes the privileged context in this model, rather than ordinary application privilege. C correct User mode is the restricted application level in the user/kernel privilege model. D incorrect The requested restricted privilege level is user mode; an architectural mode label does not name that level in this classification.

records.title: Operating System — Question 95 · Q01479
records.text: Q01479 Question 95 OS03 OS36 OS34 OS-S05 In the teaching module’s architecture, which broad core component provides protected file-system operations for applications? Distinguish command interfaces, privileged core services and the stages of booting. A Kernel B User program C Device driver D Compiler Kernel The kernel provides core protected services and handles system calls, including the operating system’s file operations in this architecture. Applications request those services. A device driver translates requests into device-specific operations beneath the file-service layer, while a compiler translates program source. These supporting roles do not make either the broad core provider of protected file-system operations. A correct The kernel provides the protected OS service and system-call layer in the stated architecture. B incorrect Applications request file services rather than being the protected core service provider. C incorrect Drivers perform device-specific operations beneath the broader file-service layer. D incorrect A compiler translates program source; it is not the runtime protected file-service provider.

records.title: Operating System — Question 96 · Q01480
records.text: Q01480 Question 96 OS03 OS35 During a conventional disk-based boot, the bootloader reads the kernel image from disk. Into which main execution-memory region is it loaded before control is transferred to it? Distinguish command interfaces, privileged core services and the stages of booting. A RAM B Hard disk C CPU cache D ROM RAM In the stated boot sequence, firmware and bootloader stages run before control passes to the kernel loaded into RAM. The disk supplies the stored image, while RAM is its main execution-memory destination. CPU cache can retain copies of memory contents for faster reuse, but that is distinct from the image’s main-memory loading location. ROM is not the RAM destination specified by this conventional boot model. A correct RAM is the main execution-memory destination for the loaded kernel image in the stated boot sequence. B incorrect The hard disk is the source of the stored image here, not its main-memory loading destination. C incorrect Cache retains copies for reuse; it is not the bootloader’s main-memory image region. D incorrect ROM does not identify the writable RAM destination of the kernel image in this stated disk-boot model.

records.title: Operating System — Question 97 · Q01481
records.text: Q01481 Question 97 OS03 OS-S02 In a conventional monolithic OS, which listed utilities can have user-space program components that invoke privileged OS services, even if the complete product also includes privileged helpers? Treat “device driver” and “interrupt handler” here as kernel-resident components. Select all that apply. Distinguish command interfaces, privileged core services and the stages of booting. A Device driver B Antivirus software C Disk partition manager D Interrupt handler Antivirus software; Disk partition manager Antivirus and disk-management products can combine ordinary user processes with privileged helper components. Their user-space components count as user programs even though some work requires kernel services. The stem explicitly confines the driver and interrupt-handler options to kernel-resident components, avoiding architectures with user-space drivers. Thus antivirus software and the partition-manager utility are both valid examples under the stated component-level interpretation. A incorrect The driver is explicitly kernel-resident in this question. B correct Antivirus software can have a user-process component alongside privileged helpers. C correct A disk partition manager can have a user-process component invoking privileged services. D incorrect The interrupt handler is explicitly kernel-resident in this question.

records.title: Operating System — Question 98 · Q01482
records.text: Q01482 Question 98 OS-S02 OS-S05 In the module’s operating-system architecture, which broad core component performs privileged interaction with underlying hardware? Distinguish where threads are managed from the privilege of the code they execute. A Kernel B User program C Compiler D File system Kernel The kernel performs privileged low-level hardware operations and supplies protected services. Ordinary applications use those services from user mode. A compiler translates source code, and the file system provides a particular family of storage services rather than naming the broad hardware-facing OS core. The question asks for that broad core component, not a particular device-specific driver. A correct The kernel is the privileged OS core that performs permitted low-level hardware operations. B incorrect Ordinary user programs request protected services rather than directly obtaining kernel privilege. C incorrect A compiler performs source translation, a development-tool role rather than privileged OS-core hardware management. D incorrect A file system supplies specific storage services, not the broad hardware-facing OS core requested.

records.title: Operating System — Question 99 · Q01483
records.text: Q01483 Question 99 OS03 OS-S02 In a two-level privilege model where “kernel mode” and “supervisor mode” are synonymous names for the privileged execution level, which listed names denote that level? “Protected mode” denotes a processor operating mode that can include restricted user execution. Select all that apply. Distinguish command interfaces, privileged core services and the stages of booting. A Kernel mode B User mode C Supervisor mode D Protected mode Kernel mode; Supervisor mode The note states that kernel mode permits privileged operations and that supervisor mode commonly denotes the same privileged mode. The stated model makes those names explicitly synonymous. User mode is restricted. Protected mode is defined here as a broader processor mode that can still run user code, so its name alone does not identify the privileged execution level. Both kernel and supervisor are selected. A correct Kernel mode denotes the privileged execution level. B incorrect User mode is the restricted level. C correct Supervisor mode is explicitly synonymous with kernel mode in this model. D incorrect Protected mode is not a privilege level under the supplied definition.

records.title: Operating System — Question 100 · Q01484
records.text: Q01484 Question 100 OS03 OS04 OS-S05 Which of the following is responsible for handling system calls made by user programs? Distinguish command interfaces, privileged core services and the stages of booting. A Kernel B User program C Compiler D File system Kernel PDF p53 says the kernel provides system services and protected hardware access to processes; libraries let user code reach kernel functions. Thus the handling component is the kernel, not the application caller or compiler. A correct Kernel provides the requested process services (p53). B incorrect User program is the requester using libraries (p53). C incorrect Compiler is not the runtime service handler. D incorrect File system handles one service category, not all kernel requests.

records.title: Operating System — Question 101 · Q01506
records.text: Q01506 Question 101 OS06 A scheduler selects the next process to be executed from one of the following. Decide whether the process is eligible, running or waiting, then identify the responsible queue or scheduling role. A Ready queue B Job queue C Device queue D None of the choices is correct Ready queue PDF pp19–20 place processes waiting for CPU in the ready queue and select among ready processes. The question is about the next CPU execution, hence A rather than job admission. A correct Ready queue contains eligible CPU waiters. B incorrect Job queue includes all processes/admission work, not just eligible CPU contenders. C incorrect Device queue contains I/O waiters (p18). D incorrect Ready queue is explicitly supplied.

records.title: Operating System — Question 102 · Q01507
records.text: Q01507 Question 102 OS06 OS17 Under preemptive priority scheduling, which event sends a currently running, unfinished process back to the ready state? Decide whether the process is eligible, running or waiting, then identify the responsible queue or scheduling role. A Arrival of a higher-priority ready process that preempts it B Completion of its final CPU burst C Suspension while waiting for an event D Issuing a blocking I/O request Arrival of a higher-priority ready process that preempts it Preemption removes the CPU from a running process that can still execute, returning it to ready. In the stated priority policy, arrival of a higher-priority ready process triggers that handoff. Final completion ends execution, while a blocking I/O request makes the process wait for an event. Suspension while waiting also does not describe ordinary readiness, so only the explicit preemption event fits. A correct The higher-priority arrival preempts the runnable process and returns it to ready. B incorrect Final completion transitions to terminated, not ready. C incorrect Suspended waiting work is not eligible for the ordinary ready queue. D incorrect Blocking I/O transitions running to waiting.

records.title: Operating System — Question 103 · Q01508
records.text: Q01508 Question 103 OS26 OS24 One of the following deadlock handling methods is used if it occurs rarely and is insignificant. Separate handling before allocation from actions taken after detection, and consider the cost of checking. A Prevention B waiting C recovery D Ignorance Ignorance, the intentional ignoring/ostrich policy. The ostrich or ignoring policy accepts the risk of a sufficiently rare, insignificant deadlock problem when systematic handling is not worthwhile. That is the intended meaning of Ignorance. Prevention instead constrains requests to break a necessary deadlock condition, and recovery acts after detection. Merely waiting is not the same as deliberately choosing to tolerate the rare problem. A incorrect Prevention constrains resource requests to remove a necessary deadlock condition; it does not deliberately ignore the problem. B incorrect Waiting describes a process behavior, not the deliberate policy of accepting rare deadlocks. C incorrect Recovery takes action after deadlock detection rather than choosing to ignore the rare problem. D correct Ignorance names the intentional ignoring or ostrich policy in this context.

records.title: Operating System — Question 104 · Q01587
records.text: Q01587 Question 104 OS38 One of the following is false about linked allocation. Trace how logical file blocks reach physical blocks and account for pointer metadata. A Is based on sequential file access B Use pointer concept C No external fragmentation D The size of the file should be set in advanced The size of the file should be set in advanced PDF p49 says linked allocation carries links to disk blocks, is effective for sequential access and has no external fragmentation. No advance contiguous size reservation is part of that linked structure; D confuses it with a fixed extent requirement. A incorrect Sequential access effectiveness is explicitly stated on p49. B incorrect Links/pointers are explicitly stated on p49. C incorrect No external fragmentation is explicitly stated on p49. D correct A chain can link another block without requiring one pre-sized contiguous extent; no advance-size requirement follows from the p49 linked structure.

records.title: Operating System — Question 105 · Q01588
records.text: Q01588 Question 105 OS08 Consider three specified implementations: an Excel application process with several worker threads, a client-browser process with multiple threads sharing its address space, and a server process using only its single main thread. Which listed process does not use multithreading? Compare per-thread execution context with shared process resources and the stated thread mapping. A Excel application B Client browser C Server D None of the choices is correct Server Multithreading means that one process contains multiple threads of execution. The described spreadsheet and browser processes each have several threads sharing their process resources. The specified server implementation has only its main thread and therefore is not multithreaded. This conclusion follows from the supplied designs, not from a universal claim about every version of Excel, every browser, or every server. A incorrect The specified Excel process has several worker threads and is multithreaded. B incorrect The specified browser process has multiple threads and is multithreaded. C correct The specified server has only one thread and is not multithreaded. D incorrect C is a valid non-multithreaded implementation, so none is incorrect.

records.title: Operating System — Question 106 · Q01589
records.text: Q01589 Question 106 OS39 One of the following security techniques is not supported by modern operating systems. Distinguish identity checks, permission checks and the particular security property at issue. A Cryptography B Authentication C Firewall D None of the above None: modern OS families can support all three techniques. OS39 states that modern OS families can support cryptography, authentication and firewalls, while support/configuration depends on product. Therefore none of the three is categorically unsupported by modern operating systems. The answer is a capability-category statement, not a guarantee that every installation includes every feature or enables it by default. Each technique has a distinct security role. A incorrect Cryptography is explicitly a capability that modern OS families can support, though configuration varies. B incorrect Authentication is explicitly supported as a modern OS capability for verifying identity. C incorrect Firewalls are explicitly within modern OS support capabilities, even though product and configuration matter. D correct All three techniques can be supported; none is categorically outside modern operating-system security capabilities.

records.title: Operating System — Question 107 · Q01627
records.text: Q01627 Question 107 OS31 Under the basic fixed-page and variable-length-segment memory models, which listed differences are correct? Select all that apply. Check the logical region and offset bound before computing its physical location. A Paging leads to internal fragmentation whereas segmentation leads external fragmentation B The size of block is fixed in the case of paging but variable in the case of segmentation C Paging use page table whereas segmentation use segmentation table D Paging is visible to user whereas segmentation is invisible to user Paging leads to internal fragmentation whereas segmentation leads external fragmentation; The size of block is fixed in the case of paging but variable in the case of segmentation; Paging use page table whereas segmentation use segmentation table Basic paging uses fixed-size pages and page tables, and its final allocated page can contain unused space. Basic segmentation uses variable-length logical units and segment tables, so free holes can cause external fragmentation. Those properties make A, B and C valid contrasts. D reverses the usual abstraction relationship: segments reflect program structure, while ordinary page placement is largely transparent to the application. A correct Paging can waste space internally; variable-length segmentation can fragment externally. B correct Pages have a fixed size while segments have variable lengths. C correct Paging uses page tables and segmentation uses segment tables. D incorrect Segments reflect program structure; ordinary pages are largely transparent, reversing this option.

records.title: Operating System — Question 108 · Q01628
records.text: Q01628 Question 108 OS35 OS06 One of the following IO services is used store data in memory while transferring between devices. Identify whether data is in transit, retained for reuse or queued for a device. A Buffering B Scheduling C Caching D Spooling Buffering PDF p47 defines buffering as retaining data while transferred between devices or an application and device. This is A; caching stores reusable copies and spooling queues a noninterleavable output stream. A correct Directly matches transfer-time storage (p47). B incorrect Scheduling reorders requests, rather than providing transfer storage. C incorrect Caching keeps copies for more efficient access, not specifically transfer mismatch handling. D incorrect Spooling holds queued device output, a specialized buffer use; no printer/output serialization is specified in the stem.

records.title: Operating System — Question 109 · Q01629
records.text: Q01629 Question 109 OS37 Which directory structure describes the commonly presented namespace of modern general-purpose operating systems, with nested directories and absolute or relative paths? Choose the structural category, not every simpler arrangement that might also be implemented. Follow namespace structure and distinguish names, underlying files and mounted filesystems. A multi-level B All choices are correct C two level D Single level multi-level A multilevel or tree namespace supports nested directories and paths that can be absolute or relative. That is the structure the notes identify as commonly presented by modern general-purpose systems. A two-level structure separates users but does not express arbitrary nesting, and a single-level structure has only one namespace level. The aggregate therefore includes structures that do not match the requested hierarchical category. A correct Multilevel describes the hierarchical nested namespace. B incorrect Single-level and two-level arrangements do not both describe the requested nested tree, so all is incorrect. C incorrect Two-level separates users without providing the general nested hierarchy asked for. D incorrect Single-level has no nested directory hierarchy.

records.title: Operating System — Question 110 · SM0001
records.text: SM0001 Question 110 OS-S01 For the first four generations described in NYU’s OS-history notes, which pairings incorrectly identify the defining historical characteristic of the named generation? Judge characteristic era, not whether a feature could also exist later. Select all that apply. Compare the stated historical clues and distinguish origin, characteristic era and technical capability. A Second generation -> multiprogramming B Fourth generation -> real time systems C First generation → manual single-user operation without a separate resident OS D Third generation → uniprogrammed batch systems Second generation -> multiprogramming; Fourth generation -> real time systems; Third generation → uniprogrammed batch systems The first four generations in NYU’s teaching taxonomy associates the first era with one user and no separate OS, the second with uniprogrammed batch systems, the third with IC-based multiprogramming, and the fourth with personal computers. Thus A, B and D mismatch the characteristic eras, while C fits. OS02 supplies the operating-mode background; the generation associations come from the supplementary university history notes rather than the unchanged master note. A correct Multiprogramming characterizes the third era, so pairing it with the second is wrong. B correct The fourth-era heading is personal computers, not the introduction of real-time systems. C incorrect Manual single-user operation without a separate OS matches the first era. D correct Uniprogrammed batch characterizes the second era, not the defining third-era advance.

records.title: Operating System — Question 111 · SM0002
records.text: SM0002 Question 111 OS09 OS-S04 Which one of the following is asynchronous in message communication? Identify how data moves, which participant waits and what event allows the operation to continue. A Non-block receive B Blocking receive C Blocking send D Direct message Nonblocking receive. OS09 defines nonblocking operations as returning promptly with data, progress or a would-block result. Among the options, nonblocking receive therefore supplies the asynchronous/non-waiting behavior being contrasted. Blocking receive waits for a message, blocking send waits for its defined completion condition, and direct message concerns how endpoints are addressed rather than whether the call blocks. A correct Nonblocking receive returns promptly instead of waiting until a message arrives, matching this asynchronous contrast. B incorrect Blocking receive waits for a message rather than providing the non-waiting behavior requested. C incorrect Blocking send waits for its defined handoff or receipt condition rather than returning promptly. D incorrect Direct messaging describes endpoint addressing, not whether sending or receiving blocks.

records.title: Operating System — Question 112 · SM0011
records.text: SM0011 Question 112 OS08 Which one of the following is NOT correct about threads? Compare per-thread execution context with shared process resources and the stated thread mapping. A Threads are the entities scheduled for execution on the CPU B It is a group of processes C Threads have program counters D Threads have registers to hold their working memory It is a group of processes PDF p27 defines a thread as a flow within one process, with its own PC and registers; p29 says kernel scheduling occurs on a thread basis. B incorrectly inverts containment by calling a thread a group of processes. A incorrect Thread-basis scheduling is explicit on p29. B correct Each thread belongs to exactly one process, not a collection of processes (p27). C incorrect Own program counter is explicit (p27). D incorrect Own system registers are explicit (p27); working memory should mean saved execution values rather than all shared process memory.

records.title: Operating System — Question 113 · SM0029
records.text: SM0029 Question 113 OS13 A computer expert would like to know the number of processes that are completed per hour to assess the performance of a machine. Which one of the following best describes the expert's assessment? Construct a timeline and distinguish completion rates from individual elapsed-time measures. A Waiting time B System throughput C Turnaround time D Response time System throughput. OS13 defines throughput as completed jobs divided by elapsed time. Counting process completions per hour is exactly that rate. Waiting, turnaround and response are delays associated with an individual process or an average of such delays; they are not completion counts per hour. The stated measurement therefore identifies system throughput without any scheduling trace. A incorrect Waiting time measures ready-queue delay, not the number of processes completed in an hour. B correct Completed processes divided by hours elapsed is system throughput here’s definition. C incorrect Turnaround measures arrival-to-completion duration for a process rather than a system completion rate. D incorrect Response measures arrival-to-first-start delay, not the number of jobs finished per unit time.

records.title: Operating System — Question 114 · SM0075
records.text: SM0075 Question 114 OS07 A process is terminated by the operating system due to a reference to non-existing memory. Which one of the following best explains the process termination? Separate creation, image replacement and termination; classify termination by its cause. A Normal exit B Error exit C Terminated by another process D Fatal exit Fatal exit. OS07 explicitly identifies a reference to nonexistent/protected memory as a fatal fault. Here the OS terminates the process because of that fault, so this is involuntary fatal termination. It is not the program’s voluntary error exit, normal completion or a kill request by another ordinary process. The cause in the stem resolves the otherwise loose exit terminology. A incorrect Normal exit is voluntary completion, unlike OS-enforced termination for an invalid memory reference. B incorrect A program-detected error exit is voluntary; the stem specifies an unrecoverable memory-access fault. C incorrect The stated cause is a fault handled by the OS, not a kill request from another process. D correct The note explicitly classifies nonexistent-memory access as a fatal fault causing involuntary termination.

records.title: Operating System — Question 115 · SM0207
records.text: SM0207 Question 115 OS18 OS17 OS16 What is a characteristic feature of round-robin scheduling? Trace bounded turns in ready-queue order and include the stated overhead and arrivals. A It assigns priorities to tasks based on their relative importance B It always selects the task with the shortest remaining time C It favors short tasks over long tasks D It guarantees fairness by providing each task with an equal time slice It guarantees fairness by providing each task with an equal time slice PDF p25 gives each process a fixed quantum and preempts after it. D identifies that equal-turn mechanism; it guarantees equal-sized opportunities, not identical lifetime CPU totals for unequal jobs. A incorrect Priority rank is the p24 policy, not the RR criterion. B incorrect Remaining-time selection is not RR’s fixed quantum. C incorrect Short-job preference is not RR’s fixed quantum rule. D correct Equal quantum per turn is precisely the p25 definition.

records.title: Operating System — Question 116 · SM0220
records.text: SM0220 Question 116 OS01 Which objective of modern operating systems involves providing a consistent and convenient environment for running applications? Separate broad resource-management goals from individual services or applications. A Maximizing hardware utilization B Ensuring fault tolerance C Providing security and protection D Providing a user-friendly interface Providing a user-friendly interface PDF p5 emphasizes a convenient program-execution environment; p14 supplies a user interface with short interactive response. D is the option specifically about user convenience. A incorrect Utilization concerns efficiency rather than the stated convenient interaction goal. B incorrect Fault tolerance concerns failure behavior, not ordinary interaction convenience. C incorrect Security controls authorization (p6), not the named convenience goal. D correct Interface support is the module’s interaction/convenience role (pp5,14).

records.title: Operating System — Question 117 · SM0228
records.text: SM0228 Question 117 OS13 All of the following are scheduling criteria EXCEPT: Construct a timeline and distinguish completion rates from individual elapsed-time measures. A CPU utilization B Min Turnaround Time C Max Throughput D Max Response Time Maximizing response time is the wrong optimization direction. OS13 says to minimize response, turnaround and waiting while maximizing useful throughput/utilization under the chosen objective. Thus maximum response time is the mismatched criterion: making first response later worsens responsiveness. The other alternatives name a standard metric or its conventional optimization direction. The question is about preferred direction, not whether response time itself is measurable. A incorrect CPU utilization is a standard scheduling metric measuring the fraction of elapsed time the CPU is busy. B incorrect Minimizing turnaround is the conventional goal for reducing arrival-to-completion delay. C incorrect Maximizing useful throughput is a conventional goal for increasing completed work per unit time. D correct Response delay should ordinarily be minimized; maximizing it reverses the responsiveness objective.

records.title: Operating System — Question 118 · SM0241
records.text: SM0241 Question 118 OS01 OS06 OS36 OS39 Which umbrella function of modern operating systems allocates and coordinates hardware resources such as CPU time, memory and I/O devices? Separate broad resource-management goals from individual services or applications. A File Management B Resource Management C Process Management D Security Management Resource Management An OS allocates CPU time, memory, storage, devices and communication resources. The umbrella term for coordinating these allocations is resource management. File, process and security management cover narrower responsibilities, so none alone names the full scope of the question. Replacing device management with the umbrella category preserves the combined CPU/memory/I/O concept and gives the item one complete answer. A incorrect File management concerns files and storage abstractions rather than all named resources. B correct Resource management spans CPU time, memory and I/O devices. C incorrect Process management covers execution and CPU scheduling but is narrower than the combined scope. D incorrect Security management controls protection and permissions rather than naming all allocation functions.

records.title: Operating System — Question 119 · SM0268
records.text: SM0268 Question 119 OS17 OS18 OS16 Which scheduling algorithm is commonly associated with the concept of aging, where the priority of a task increases the longer it waits in the ready queue? Check priority direction, preemption and whether waiting can change effective rank. A Round Robin (RR) B Shortest Job Next (SJN) C Priority Scheduling D Shortest Remaining Time First (SRTF) Priority scheduling. OS17 describes aging as increasing waiting jobs’ effective priority to reduce indefinite postponement. That is a direct adjustment within a priority scheme and matches the stem exactly. RR rotates turns, SJN selects the shortest next burst, and SRTF selects the shortest remaining work. Those policies may be modified, but they are not the named priority-aging mechanism requested. A incorrect RR cycles ready jobs by quantum rather than defining aging through increasing priority. B incorrect SJN chooses shortest next bursts; aging refers specifically to adjusting the effective priority of waiting work. C correct Priority scheduling can raise a waiting task’s effective priority through aging to reduce starvation. D incorrect SRTF compares remaining bursts rather than increasing priority solely because a task has waited longer.

records.title: Operating System — Question 120 · SM0278
records.text: SM0278 Question 120 OS22 OS24 In a system susceptible to deadlock, what does the 'no preemption' condition imply? Trace the resource dependencies and distinguish necessary conditions from evidence of an actual deadlock. A Resources can be preempted and assigned to other processes B Processes cannot request additional resources while holding others C Resources cannot be preempted while they are in use D Processes must release all resources when blocked Allocated resources cannot be forcibly withdrawn. OS22 defines no resource preemption as requiring voluntary release by the holder. C states that resources cannot be preempted while in use and therefore matches. A reverses the condition. B and D describe policies attacking hold-and-wait by limiting requests or requiring release; they are different from the no-preemption property itself. A incorrect Permitting withdrawal and reassignment is resource preemption, directly reversing the condition requested. B incorrect Forbidding additional requests while holding resources attacks hold-and-wait rather than defining no-preemption. C correct The holder retains the resource until voluntary release, so it cannot simply be forcibly withdrawn. D incorrect Requiring release when blocked removes holding-while-waiting; it is not the no-preemption definition.

records.title: Operating System — Question 121 · SS106
records.text: SS106 Question 121 OS06 When a process is in a "Blocked" state waiting for some Input-Output services and afterthe service is completed, it will goes to a state known as: Decide whether the process is eligible, running or waiting, then identify the responsible queue or scheduling role. A Terminated B Suspended C Ready D Running Ready After I/O completion the process no longer waits for that event but must obtain CPU allocation, so it becomes Ready (PDF pp16,19–20). Running follows only when the scheduler actually selects it. A incorrect Completion of an I/O request is not completion of the process. B incorrect Suspension concerns memory removal/swapping, not an inevitable I/O-completion transition. C correct Ready means eligible and waiting for processor assignment (p16). D incorrect It can run after scheduling; I/O completion alone does not allocate CPU (p20).

records.title: Operating System — Question 122 · SS107
records.text: SS107 Question 122 OS33 OS-S03 A memory management policy that decisions must be made as to which page or pages are to be supplanted when a memory is full is known as: Trace every reference, distinguish hits from faults and update the policy state consistently. A Cleaning policy B Fetch policy C Load policy D Replacement policy Replacement policy Page replacement chooses which memory pages to swap out when allocation requires unavailable free space (PDF p40). D names that victim-selection policy. A incorrect Cleaning concerns writing dirty contents; it does not identify victim selection in the p40 definition. B incorrect Fetching concerns bringing data in, rather than selecting a resident victim. C incorrect Loading concerns admission/bringing in work, rather than selecting pages to evict. D correct Replacement is explicitly the decision of which pages to swap out (p40).

records.title: Operating System — Question 123 · SS122
records.text: SS122 Question 123 OS07 Which of the following is not a principal event that cause processes to be created? Separate creation, image replacement and termination; classify termination by its cause. A Multiple execution of processes B Execution of a process-creation system call by a running process C System initialization D Auser request to create a new process Multiple execution is not itself a process-creation event. OS07 lists initialization, user requests, service requests and a running process’s creation call as creation causes. B, C and D match that list. Multiple execution of processes describes work being run, not an explicit request or initialization event creating a new process. Existing processes can execute repeatedly without creating a child, so A is the unsupported creation trigger. A correct Executing existing processes multiple times is not itself the explicit creation trigger identified here. B incorrect A running process’s creation system call is explicitly one of the listed process-creation causes. C incorrect System initialization is explicitly listed as a time when processes are created. D incorrect A user request to create a process is explicitly a valid process-creation cause.

records.title: Operating System — Question 124 · SS125
records.text: SS125 Question 124 OS25 Which statement about Banker’s algorithm is false? Compute remaining needs and simulate feasible completions before deciding whether an allocation is safe. A It is a CPU scheduling algorithm B It uses each process’s declared maximum resource claims C Its safety test simulates completions to check whether every process can finish D It checks a received resource request before granting it It is a CPU scheduling algorithm Banker’s algorithm is a deadlock-avoidance technique, not a CPU scheduling policy. It requires maximum resource claims, computes remaining needs, and simulates possible completions to check for a safe sequence. A request is evaluated after receipt and before being granted, including checks against need and availability. The factual alternatives therefore describe the supported safety procedure, leaving only the CPU-scheduling classification false. A correct Banker is deadlock avoidance rather than CPU scheduling, so this statement is false. B incorrect Maximum resource claims are required input, so this statement is true. C incorrect The safety test repeatedly simulates feasible completions, so this statement is true. D incorrect A request is checked before granting it, so this statement is true.

records.title: Operating System — Question 125 · SS138
records.text: SS138 Question 125 OS22 OS24 A set of processes is blocked: each holds a resource and waits for another resource that only another blocked member of the set can release. No member can proceed without intervention. This state is called: Trace the resource dependencies and distinguish necessary conditions from evidence of an actual deadlock. A Deadlock B Queuing C Preemption D Overloading Deadlock The specified set has a closed dependency: every member is waiting for something only another blocked member can provide. None can reach the release operation needed by another, so the state is deadlock. Queuing can occur during ordinary waits that eventually finish; preemption withdraws or reallocates a resource; overload concerns excessive demand. The added dependency condition makes the deadlock interpretation definite. A correct The closed dependency among blocked members defines deadlock. B incorrect Ordinary queuing does not require a dependency that prevents every member from progressing. C incorrect Preemption is resource withdrawal or reassignment rather than this blocked state. D incorrect Overload does not by itself create the specified closed dependency.

records.title: Operating System — Question 126 · SS183
records.text: SS183 Question 126 OS40 Identify the lowest layer of Android architecture. Use the stated historical or platform scope and distinguish origin from technical capability. A Application B Application Framework C Database D Linux Kernel Linux kernel. OS40 directly states that Android’s base kernel layer is Linux and places framework and applications above it. Thus Linux Kernel is the lowest offered layer. A database is not identified as the kernel foundation in this model. The answer rests on Android’s architecture, not on a separate claim about Android’s current market share. A incorrect Applications sit above the framework and kernel rather than forming Android’s base layer. B incorrect The application framework is explicitly a higher layer than the Linux kernel foundation. C incorrect A database is not the base kernel layer identified here’s Android architecture description. D correct The note explicitly names Linux as Android’s base kernel layer beneath framework and applications.

records.title: Operating System — Question 127 · AM0654
records.text: AM0654 Question 127 OS01 OS39 Which objective specifically concerns efficient allocation of CPU time, memory, storage and devices among competing programs? Separate broad resource-management goals from individual services or applications. A To provide an interface for users to interact with the hardware B To manage and allocate system resources efficiently C To ensure data security and protection D To optimize program execution speed To manage and allocate system resources efficiently Resource management allocates CPU time, memory, storage, devices and communications to programs. That directly matches efficient management and allocation in B. User interfaces support convenience, protection controls permitted access, and execution speed is a performance concern. Those are related goals, but the stated question asks specifically for the allocation objective rather than ranking every legitimate OS goal as universally most important. A incorrect Providing an interface concerns convenience rather than the specific allocation objective. B correct Efficient management and allocation directly names the requested resource objective. C incorrect Security and protection concern access control rather than allocation efficiency itself. D incorrect Program speed is a performance concern and is not equivalent to efficient allocation of all resources.

records.title: Operating System — Question 128 · AM0655
records.text: AM0655 Question 128 OS01 OS04 Which of the following is not a function of an operating system? Separate broad resource-management goals from individual services or applications. A Process management B File management C Network management D Application development Application development is not a core OS resource-management function. OS01 explicitly distinguishes application-development tools using OS services from application development itself as a core OS function. Processes, files and communication resources are managed by the OS. Therefore D is the exclusion in the intended resource-management scope. Providing compilers, editors or development APIs does not mean the operating system itself performs application development as its defining resource function. A incorrect Managing execution/process resources belongs to the OS’s core resource-management responsibilities. B incorrect File and storage management are core OS services rather than the requested non-function. C incorrect Communication/network resource management belongs to the OS responsibilities described in the note. D correct The note explicitly separates developing applications from the OS functions used by development tools.

records.title: Operating System — Question 129 · AM0656
records.text: AM0656 Question 129 OS-S03 OS28 OS03 OS06 OS39 What is the purpose of memory management in an operating system? Read the cited conceptual rules, state the model, and apply them before comparing the alternatives. A To provide an interface for users to interact with the computer system B To manage the execution of multiple processes simultaneously C To allocate and deallocate memory for processes and data D To ensure data integrity and security To allocate and deallocate memory for processes and data PDF pp5 and 31 say memory management tracks primary memory, decides allocations, and updates status when memory is freed. C is the specific allocation/deallocation function. A incorrect User interaction is a separate interface function. B incorrect Multiple-process execution is process/scheduling work; memory management supports it but does not define execution control. C correct Allocation and deallocation are the direct memory-management tasks (pp5,31). D incorrect Protection is supported by base/limit registers, but data integrity/security is too broad to identify the principal allocation role.

records.title: Operating System — Question 130 · AM0657
records.text: AM0657 Question 130 OS34 OS03 OS06 Which OS component converts generic I/O requests into operations specific to a particular device, rather than naming the kernel as a whole? Separate device hardware, device-specific software and general event or transfer mechanisms. A Kernel B Scheduler C File system D Device drivers Device drivers A device driver translates OS I/O requests into the particular operations a device requires. The kernel provides broader resource management and can contain drivers, but the question asks for that specific hardware-facing component. The scheduler selects runnable work and the filesystem organizes file abstractions. Neither performs the general per-device request translation described, making device drivers the precise answer. A incorrect The kernel is the larger system containing or coordinating the specific component. B incorrect The scheduler chooses runnable CPU work rather than translating device commands. C incorrect The filesystem organizes files rather than translating requests for every device type. D correct Drivers convert OS requests into device-specific operations.

records.title: Operating System — Question 131 · AM0658
records.text: AM0658 Question 131 OS36 OS37 What is the role of the file system in an operating system? Distinguish a file operation, a resource handle, an offset and file metadata. A To manage system resources and allocate them to processes B To provide a user interface for interacting with the computer system C To store and organize files on secondary storage devices D To schedule and prioritize the execution of processes To store and organize files on secondary storage devices Files are related information on secondary storage (PDF p48); file management tracks locations and organizes directories (p6). C gives that role. A incorrect System-wide allocation is broader than organizing files. B incorrect A user interface is not the file system’s stored-information role. C correct Matches secondary storage and organization (pp6,48). D incorrect Process execution ordering belongs to schedulers (p20), not file organization.

records.title: Operating System — Question 132 · AM0659
records.text: AM0659 Question 132 OS18 OS15 OS16 OS17 Which scheduling algorithm is based on assigning a fixed time slice to each process in a round-robin manner? Trace bounded turns in ready-queue order and include the stated overhead and arrivals. A First-Come, First-Served (FCFS) scheduling B Shortest Job Next (SJN) scheduling C Priority scheduling D Round-Robin scheduling Round-Robin scheduling PDF p25 explicitly defines a fixed execution quantum followed by preemption and another process’s turn. D is that round-robin policy. A incorrect FCFS uses arrival order without this specified repeating quantum (p23). B incorrect SJN selects short jobs using known execution length (p23). C incorrect Priority uses assigned rank (p24). D correct Fixed quantum plus repeated turns is the p25 RR definition.

records.title: Operating System — Question 133 · AM0660
records.text: AM0660 Question 133 OS39 What is the primary goal of file-access authorization in an operating system? Distinguish identity checks, permission checks and the particular security property at issue. A To ensure the availability of files for authorized users B To prevent unauthorized access to files and data C To optimize file storage and retrieval performance D To minimize the impact of system failures on file operations To prevent unauthorized access to files and data Authorization checks whether a user or other principal is permitted to perform an operation on a file. Preventing unauthorized access is therefore the direct goal. Availability and recovery protect access through failures or disruption, while storage optimization concerns performance. Those are useful objectives, but they are distinct from deciding who may read, write or otherwise access a particular file. A incorrect Availability keeps files accessible when needed; it is distinct from deciding whether an attempted access is authorized. B correct Preventing unauthorized access directly follows from checking permitted operations and file rights. C incorrect Storage and retrieval performance do not determine a caller’s access rights. D incorrect Limiting failure impact concerns resilience and recovery, rather than the access-permission decision.

records.title: Operating System — Question 134 · AM0661
records.text: AM0661 Question 134 OS32 OS04 What is the purpose of virtual memory in an operating system? Separate a permitted nonresident access from an illegal access and trace the required handling steps. A To provide a virtualized environment for running multiple operating systems B To increase the physical memory capacity of a computer system C To allow the execution of programs without any memory constraints D To create a separate memory space for each running process Provide translated, protected per-process address spaces. OS32 defines virtual memory as translated/protected address spaces with nonresident portions backed by storage. D is the option matching separate process memory spaces. A describes machine virtualization; B falsely adds physical RAM and C falsely removes all memory constraints. Isolation and translation are the supported purpose, with backing storage providing flexibility within finite resource limits. A incorrect Running multiple guest OSs describes machine virtualization, explicitly distinguished from process virtual memory. B incorrect Virtual memory does not physically add RAM; it maps address spaces using existing RAM and backing storage. C incorrect The note explicitly retains capacity constraints; virtual memory does not make execution memory-unlimited. D correct Separate translated/protected process address spaces match the virtual-memory purpose described here.

records.title: Operating System — Question 135 · AM0662
records.text: AM0662 Question 135 OS03 What is the role of the shell in an operating system? Distinguish command interfaces, privileged core services and the stages of booting. A To manage and allocate system resources B To provide a graphical user interface for interacting with the system C To act as an interface between the user and the operating system kernel D To schedule and prioritize the execution of processes To act as an interface between the user and the operating system kernel The shell takes user commands and invokes kernel functions (PDF p54), making C the exact interface relationship. A and D describe other core functions; B imposes a GUI-only restriction absent from the command-interpreter definition. A incorrect System resources are the kernel/OS management role, not the shell’s defining interface. B incorrect The module describes command interpretation, not a requirement that the shell be graphical. C correct Directly matches the user-to-kernel interface (p54). D incorrect CPU ordering is scheduling, not the shell definition.

records.title: Operating System — Question 136 · AM0663
records.text: AM0663 Question 136 OS10 What is the primary purpose of process synchronization when processes perform conflicting accesses to shared state? Identify conflicting shared accesses and the safety or progress property required. A To prevent deadlock situations B To ensure fair allocation of system resources C To enable parallel execution of multiple processes D To coordinate shared-state access and required operation ordering safely To coordinate shared-state access and required operation ordering safely Conflicting accesses need coordination so interleaving does not corrupt shared state or violate required operation order. Critical-section protection provides mutual exclusion, with progress and bounded waiting required under the stated solution assumptions. Synchronization does not automatically eliminate deadlock; inconsistent lock acquisition can introduce it. It may also serialize work rather than create parallelism, so safe shared-access coordination is the precise primary purpose. A incorrect Locking can itself deadlock, so universal deadlock prevention is not the primary definition. B incorrect General resource-allocation fairness is broader than coordinating shared-state operations. C incorrect Synchronization can serialize conflicting operations and does not itself create parallel execution. D correct Coordinating shared accesses and required ordering safely captures the primary purpose.

records.title: Operating System — Question 137 · AM0664
records.text: AM0664 Question 137 OS01 What is the main function of an operating system in terms of convenience? Separate broad resource-management goals from individual services or applications. A Providing an easy-to-use graphical user interface B Optimizing program execution speed C Managing system resources efficiently D Ensuring data security and protection An easy-to-use interface is the convenience example. OS01 defines convenience as making tasks easy through consistent interfaces and abstractions. A directly exemplifies that user-facing goal, although a GUI is one possible interface rather than a universal requirement. B and C concern speed/resource efficiency, and D protection. Those are worthwhile OS objectives but do not match the convenience dimension specifically named in the stem. A correct An easy-to-use GUI is an example of making user tasks convenient through an interface. B incorrect Optimizing execution speed concerns performance rather than the user-facing convenience dimension requested. C incorrect Efficient allocation is a resource-use objective, distinguished from convenience in the note. D incorrect Security/protection is a separate OS objective rather than the interface-usability example of convenience.

records.title: Operating System — Question 138 · AM0665
records.text: AM0665 Question 138 OS01 How does an operating system improve efficiency in a computer system? Separate broad resource-management goals from individual services or applications. A By allocating system resources to processes effectively B By providing a wide range of software applications C By supporting multiple programming languages D By ensuring data integrity and security By allocating system resources to processes effectively Efficient use follows the module’s allocation of processor time and memory to processes (PDF pp5–6,31). A states this mechanism rather than the quantity of applications or languages. A correct Directly matches resource allocation and scheduling responsibilities. B incorrect More applications alone does not establish allocation efficiency. C incorrect Language variety alone does not establish allocation efficiency. D incorrect Security is a distinct access-control function, not the stated allocation mechanism.

records.title: Operating System — Question 139 · AM0666
records.text: AM0666 Question 139 OS01 OS04 What does it mean for an operating system to have the ability to evolve? Separate broad resource-management goals from individual services or applications. A It can adapt to changing hardware configurations B It can support multiple operating systems simultaneously C It can run legacy software without compatibility issues D It can automatically update itself with new features and bug fixes Adapt to changing hardware configurations. OS01 defines ability to evolve as adding hardware support, features and repairs through maintainable interfaces/modules. Adaptation to hardware configurations is therefore the direct example. Running multiple guest OSs describes virtualization. Backward compatibility preserves supported behavior rather than guaranteeing every legacy binary, and automatic updating is not a defining property of all operating systems. A correct Adding support for changing hardware is a direct example of maintainable OS evolution. B incorrect Supporting multiple guest operating systems describes virtualization rather than the definition of ability to evolve. C incorrect The absolute absence of compatibility issues is not guaranteed by evolution or supported backward compatibility. D incorrect Automatic updates may be provided, but the note explicitly rejects them as a defining property of every OS.

records.title: Operating System — Question 140 · AM0667
records.text: AM0667 Question 140 OS37 OS39 Which file-management feature directly helps users locate files and navigate among organized groups of files? Follow namespace structure and distinguish names, underlying files and mounted filesystems. A By providing advanced encryption techniques for file security B By allowing users to organize files in a hierarchical structure C By automatically backing up files to remote servers D By optimizing file storage to maximize disk space utilization By allowing users to organize files in a hierarchical structure A hierarchical directory tree gives users nested groups and paths for locating files and navigating between directories. This directly supplies the requested organizational convenience. Encryption protects confidentiality, backups preserve additional copies for recovery, and storage optimization concerns space utilization. Those functions may also be useful, but they do not themselves define the navigable directory organization asked for here. A incorrect Encryption protects confidentiality; it does not supply nested directory paths for navigation. B correct Hierarchical directories organize files into nested groups reachable through paths. C incorrect Remote backup concerns additional stored copies, rather than the structure used to navigate the working file namespace. D incorrect Maximizing disk-space utilization is an allocation goal rather than a directory-navigation feature.

records.title: Operating System — Question 141 · AM0668
records.text: AM0668 Question 141 OS34 What is the role of device drivers in an operating system's convenience factor? Separate device hardware, device-specific software and general event or transfer mechanisms. A They allow users to customize the appearance of the graphical user interface. B They provide compatibility with a wide range of hardware devices. C They optimize system performance for resource-intensive applications. D They enhance data security and encryption for sensitive files. They provide compatibility with a wide range of hardware devices. Drivers hide peculiarities of device hardware (PDF p10); p47 even explains a terminal driver supporting differing brands. Standard interfaces on p45 let applications use differing controllers, matching B. A incorrect GUI appearance is not the device-specific I/O abstraction. B correct Device compatibility through hardware-specific implementation and common interfaces matches pp10,45,47. C incorrect Application performance may benefit, but optimizing all resource-intensive applications is not the driver definition. D incorrect Encryption is not the driver’s general stated I/O responsibility.

records.title: Operating System — Question 142 · AM0669
records.text: AM0669 Question 142 OS02 OS08 How does an operating system improve efficiency in terms of process management? Compare interaction, CPU sharing and deadline requirements under the stated system model. A By providing a comprehensive programming environment B By executing processes in parallel on multiple CPUs C By automatically compressing files to reduce storage space D By enabling users to schedule program execution at specific times By executing processes in parallel on multiple CPUs PDF p29 says the kernel can simultaneously schedule threads from one process across multiple processors, while p27 explains parallel performance benefits. B is the relevant offered mechanism when suitable parallel work and CPUs exist. A incorrect A programming environment does not itself describe parallel process execution. B correct Scheduling work across multiple CPUs exploits parallelism (pp27,29). C incorrect File compression is unrelated to CPU process management here. D incorrect User-chosen execution times are not the multiprocessor-efficiency mechanism.

records.title: Operating System — Question 143 · AM0670
records.text: AM0670 Question 143 OS01 In the context of operating systems, what is the meaning of scalability? Separate broad resource-management goals from individual services or applications. A The ability to run on different hardware platforms B The ability to support multiple programming languages C The ability to handle increasing workloads and resources D The ability to provide a user-friendly interface Handle increasing workloads and resources. OS01 directly defines scalability as handling greater workloads/resources. Running on different hardware platforms is portability, and providing an easy interface is convenience. Programming-language support does not itself establish either increasing capacity or workload handling. The wording in C matches the supplied definition without assuming scalability guarantees limitless growth or unchanged performance. A incorrect Adapting to other hardware platforms is portability, explicitly distinguished from scalability. B incorrect Supporting programming languages does not define the ability to handle growing workload or resources. C correct Handling increasing workloads and resources directly matches the note’s definition of scalability. D incorrect A user-friendly interface concerns convenience rather than scaling capacity as demand grows.

records.title: Operating System — Question 144 · AM0671
records.text: AM0671 Question 144 OS01 How does an operating system ensure convenience in terms of software installation and management? Separate broad resource-management goals from individual services or applications. A By providing an intuitive software development environment B By offering automatic software updates and patches C By optimizing the execution speed of software applications D By allowing users to customize the appearance of the graphical user interface Automatic updates and patches can make software maintenance convenient. OS01 defines convenience as making tasks easy and notes that updates help administration. Among the alternatives, offering automatic updates and patches directly reduces routine software-management effort. This is an example of a convenience feature, not a universal guarantee that every OS updates automatically. Development environments, speed optimization and appearance customization address different activities from installation/maintenance in the stem. A incorrect A development environment assists creating software rather than directly providing installation and maintenance convenience. B correct Automating updates and patches can reduce routine software-management work, though the feature is not universal. C incorrect Execution-speed optimization concerns performance, not the installation/maintenance convenience specifically requested. D incorrect Customizing GUI appearance changes presentation rather than automating software installation or maintenance tasks.

records.title: Operating System — Question 145 · AM0672
records.text: AM0672 Question 145 OS01 What does it mean for an operating system to provide fault tolerance? Separate broad resource-management goals from individual services or applications. A It continues correct service despite the specified failures it is designed to tolerate B It can handle multiple user requests simultaneously. C It can optimize system performance for resource-intensive tasks. D It can provide a secure environment for sensitive data. It continues correct service despite the specified failures it is designed to tolerate Fault tolerance means that correct service continues despite specified failures within the system’s fault model. Recovery restores service after a failure and may be useful without providing uninterrupted correct service. Multiple-user handling concerns concurrency, resource-intensive performance concerns efficiency, and sensitive-data protection concerns security. The revised continuation option therefore states the specific property rather than substituting quick recovery for fault tolerance. A correct Continued correct service despite specified faults is the fault-tolerance property. B incorrect Simultaneous user requests concern concurrency rather than surviving failures. C incorrect Performance optimization does not define continued service under faults. D incorrect Security protects data but does not itself define fault tolerance.

records.title: Operating System — Question 146 · AM0673
records.text: AM0673 Question 146 OS01 How does an operating system support the ability to evolve in terms of software compatibility? Separate broad resource-management goals from individual services or applications. A By providing a wide range of pre-installed software applications B By offering backward compatibility for legacy software C By optimizing the execution speed of software applications D By allowing users to customize system settings and preferences Backward compatibility for supported legacy software. OS01 defines backward compatibility as preserving supported older application behavior. That is the software-compatibility aspect of evolution asked here. Preinstalled applications, execution speed and preference customization do not establish that older software’s supported behavior remains available. The answer must retain the support qualification; it does not promise all legacy binaries run without any compatibility issues. A incorrect Preinstalling many applications does not establish compatibility with older applications or their supported behavior. B correct Backward compatibility preserves supported legacy behavior, directly matching the software-compatibility aspect of evolution. C incorrect Faster execution does not by itself preserve interfaces or behavior required by legacy software. D incorrect Customizing preferences changes configuration rather than establishing compatibility with older application behavior.

records.title: Operating System — Question 147 · AM0674
records.text: AM0674 Question 147 OS22 OS06 What is deadlock in the standard process/resource model? Trace the resource dependencies and distinguish necessary conditions from evidence of an actual deadlock. A A state in which each member of a blocked set waits for an event or resource that only another blocked member can provide B It is a state where a process is terminated abruptly. C It is a state where multiple processes are executing concurrently. D It is a state where the operating system crashes due to a software bug. A state in which each member of a blocked set waits for an event or resource that only another blocked member can provide Deadlock describes a blocked set whose members depend on one another for the events or resources required to continue. Because each provider is itself blocked within the same dependency, normal execution cannot resolve the waits. A process being terminated, multiple processes executing, or an OS crash describes a different condition. The revised definition also distinguishes deadlock from starvation caused by unfair repeated bypass. A correct This states the closed dependency that defines the deadlocked set. B incorrect Abrupt termination ends execution rather than defining blocked dependencies. C incorrect Concurrent execution is normal and does not imply deadlock. D incorrect An OS crash is a different failure; deadlocked processes can exist while the OS remains active.

records.title: Operating System — Question 148 · AM0675
records.text: AM0675 Question 148 OS22 Which of the following conditions must be present for deadlock to occur? Trace the resource dependencies and distinguish necessary conditions from evidence of an actual deadlock. A Mutual exclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, and circular wait. B Mutual exclusion, hold and wait, preemption, and circular wait. C Mutual inclusion, hold and wait, no preemption, and circular wait. D Mutual inclusion, hold and wait, preemption, and circular wait. Mutual exclusion, hold-and-wait, no-preemption and circular wait. OS22 lists the four necessary conditions in the standard reusable-resource model. A preserves the exact set: exclusion, holding while requesting more, no forced resource withdrawal, and a wait cycle. B introduces preemption in place of no-preemption; C and D replace exclusion with inclusion. These are not harmless wording changes because they remove or reverse the relevant restrictions. A correct This option states all four standard necessary conditions with their correct meanings and polarity. B incorrect It substitutes preemption for no-preemption, reversing the required resource-withdrawal restriction. C incorrect It substitutes mutual inclusion for mutual exclusion, losing the nonshareable-resource condition. D incorrect It reverses both exclusion and no-preemption, so it is not the required condition set.

records.title: Operating System — Question 149 · AM0676
records.text: AM0676 Question 149 OS22 What is mutual exclusion in the context of deadlock? Trace the resource dependencies and distinguish necessary conditions from evidence of an actual deadlock. A It is the condition where multiple processes can access the same resource simultaneously. B It is the condition where a resource can be accessed by only one process at a time. C It is the condition where a process holds a resource while waiting for another resource. D It is the condition where a process waits indefinitely for a resource. At most one process holds the nonshareable resource at a time. OS22 defines mutual exclusion as allowing at most one holder of a nonshareable resource. B states that one-at-a-time condition. A describes concurrent sharing, C describes holding while requesting another resource, and D describes indefinite waiting without establishing exclusivity. The definition concerns access safety, not a guarantee that every waiting process eventually obtains the resource. A incorrect Simultaneous access by several processes contradicts the exclusive-holder condition for a nonshareable resource. B correct Only one process at a time may hold or use the nonshareable resource. C incorrect Retaining one resource while requesting another defines hold-and-wait rather than mutual exclusion. D incorrect Indefinite waiting describes a possible failure outcome and does not define exclusive resource possession.

records.title: Operating System — Question 150 · AM0677
records.text: AM0677 Question 150 OS22 What is hold and wait in the context of deadlock? Trace the resource dependencies and distinguish necessary conditions from evidence of an actual deadlock. A It is the condition where a process holds a resource while waiting for another resource. B It is the condition where a process waits indefinitely for a resource. C It is the condition where multiple processes can access the same resource simultaneously. D It is the condition where a resource can be accessed by only one process at a time. Retain a resource while waiting for another. OS22 directly defines hold-and-wait as retaining a resource while requesting another. A contains both parts of that definition. Merely waiting indefinitely does not establish a retained allocation, simultaneous sharing contradicts exclusion, and one-at-a-time access describes mutual exclusion rather than a process holding one resource while requesting more. A correct The process simultaneously retains an allocated resource and waits to acquire a further one. B incorrect Indefinite waiting does not establish that the process still holds another resource. C incorrect Simultaneous shared access is not the retained-allocation-plus-request condition defining hold-and-wait. D incorrect One process accessing a resource at a time defines mutual exclusion, not hold-and-wait.

records.title: Operating System — Question 151 · AM0678
records.text: AM0678 Question 151 OS24 OS22 What is preemption in the context of deadlock prevention? Identify the resource-request restriction and which necessary condition it removes. A It is the condition where a process holds a resource while waiting for another resource. B It is the condition where a process waits indefinitely for a resource. C It is the condition where multiple processes can access the same resource simultaneously. D It is the condition where a resource can be forcibly taken from a process. A resource may be forcibly taken from its holder. OS22 defines no-preemption as voluntary release only, while OS24 permits safe withdrawal/restart as a way to attack that restriction. Preemption is the opposite permission: a resource can be forcibly reclaimed. D directly states it. The answer concerns resources that can safely be withdrawn, not a claim that every device or lock can be preempted without corruption. A incorrect Holding one resource while waiting for another describes hold-and-wait rather than forced resource withdrawal. B incorrect Indefinite waiting is a possible outcome, not the permission to reclaim a held resource. C incorrect Concurrent sharing concerns resource shareability rather than withdrawing an existing allocation from its holder. D correct Forcibly taking a held resource is resource preemption, subject to safe withdrawal/restart support.

records.title: Operating System — Question 152 · AM0679
records.text: AM0679 Question 152 OS22 What is circular wait in the context of deadlock? Trace the resource dependencies and distinguish necessary conditions from evidence of an actual deadlock. A It is the condition where a process waits indefinitely for a resource. B It is the condition where multiple processes can access the same resource simultaneously. C It is the condition where a process holds a resource while waiting for another resource. D It is the condition where a circular chain of processes exists, each holding a resource requested by the next process in the chain. A closed chain of resource waits. OS22 defines circular wait as a closed chain of waits. D specifies that each process holds a resource requested by the next in a circular chain, which returns the dependency to the starting participant. C describes only one hold-and-wait relationship, which need not be cyclic. Indefinite waiting and simultaneous sharing likewise fail to establish a closed chain. A incorrect Indefinite waiting does not identify a closed cycle of dependencies among resource holders. B incorrect Simultaneous resource sharing is not a chain of blocked requests and does not define circular wait. C incorrect One process holding while requesting another establishes hold-and-wait but not necessarily a cycle. D correct The circular chain of holdings and requests explicitly forms the required closed wait dependency.

records.title: Operating System — Question 153 · AM0680
records.text: AM0680 Question 153 OS26 OS24 OS25 Which listed policy does not actively prevent an unsafe allocation or detect and recover from an existing deadlock? Interpret “deadlock acceptance” as deliberately ignoring sufficiently rare deadlocks. Separate handling before allocation from actions taken after detection, and consider the cost of checking. A Deadlock avoidance B Deadlock detection and recovery C Deadlock prevention D Deadlock acceptance Deadlock acceptance Prevention constrains requests to break a necessary condition; avoidance keeps tentative allocations safe; detection and recovery identifies and resolves an existing deadlock. Deliberate acceptance, as defined here, instead ignores a sufficiently rare problem rather than actively applying those controls. It is still a possible policy choice, but is the only listed one outside the active-control category specified by the revised stem. A incorrect Avoidance actively restricts grants to preserve a safe state. B incorrect Detection and recovery actively identifies and resolves deadlock. C incorrect Prevention actively removes a necessary deadlock condition. D correct Intentional ignoring is a policy choice but does not actively apply the specified controls.

records.title: Operating System — Question 154 · AM0681
records.text: AM0681 Question 154 OS23 In a resource-allocation graph with one instance of each resource type, which listed roles are valid? Read B as direct resource-to-resource edges and D as showing permission to forcibly withdraw resources. Select all that apply. Follow request and assignment arrows and check how many instances each resource has. A To represent the allocation of resources to processes. B To represent the dependencies between resources. C To represent the circular wait condition. D To represent the preemption of resources. To represent the allocation of resources to processes.; To represent the circular wait condition. An assignment edge records which process holds a resource instance, and a request edge records what a process is waiting for. Following alternating edges can form a circular wait. In the stated single-instance model a cycle establishes deadlock. The graph does not use direct resource-to-resource dependency edges and does not encode a general permission to preempt resources, so A and C are the valid listed roles. A correct Assignment edges represent resource holdings by processes. B incorrect Standard graph edges connect processes and resources, not resources directly to other resources. C correct A cycle of request and assignment edges represents circular wait. D incorrect Resource-preemption permission is not encoded by the stated request/assignment edges.

records.title: Operating System — Question 155 · AM0682
records.text: AM0682 Question 155 OS25 OS14 Which resource allocation policy can help prevent deadlock? Compute remaining needs and simulate feasible completions before deciding whether an allocation is safe. A First-Come, First-Served (FCFS) B Round Robin (RR) C Shortest Job Next (SJN) D Banker's Algorithm Banker’s algorithm, technically an avoidance policy. OS25 states that Banker grants requests only while preserving a safe state.
