records.title: Software Engineering — Question 1 · Q00003
records.text: Q00003 Question 1 SE04 SE06 A company delivers registration first, then adds payments and reporting, each as a usable delivery. Which model specifically names this addition-of-functionality strategy, independent of whether earlier features are also refined? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Waterfall B Incremental C Spiral D Evolutionary Incremental The delivery strategy adds usable capabilities in stages so that end users receive a valuable subset before the complete product is ready. Incremental development names that addition of functionality. Evolutionary development broadly emphasizes refinement and can overlap with increments, but does not specifically name the stated delivery distinction. Spiral is organized around risk-reduction cycles, and classical waterfall normally delays usable delivery until its planned development phases are complete. A incorrect Classical waterfall organizes sequential phases rather than prioritizing staged usable subsets. B correct Incremental development adds usable capability in successive deliveries. C incorrect Spiral names risk-driven cycles; those may contain increments without defining this delivery strategy. D incorrect Evolutionary refinement can overlap with increments, but the question asks the specific name for adding usable functionality.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 2 · Q00010
records.text: Q00010 Question 2 SE35 If you want to test individual sub-systems of software, which phase of software testing is appropriate? Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A Integration testing B Unit testing C System testing D Acceptance testing Unit testing Unit testing tests isolated building blocks, including objects and subsystems; integration begins when individually tested components are combined. A incorrect Combines components rather than isolating a subsystem. See PDF p. 148, 144. B correct Directly tests an individual object or subsystem. See PDF p. 148, 144. C incorrect Tests components together as one system. See PDF p. 148, 144. D incorrect Checks the delivered system against the client agreement. See PDF p. 148, 144.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 3 · Q00019
records.text: Q00019 Question 3 SE11 Which characteristic of requirements specifies that the requirement should be phrased so that there is one and only one interpretation for it? Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity. A Unambiguous B Correct C Feasible D Verifiable Unambiguous A single interpretation is the unambiguous property. Correctness, feasibility and verifiability answer different questions. A correct Rules out two or more interpretations. See PDF p. 68, 70. B incorrect Accuracy to the client's view does not guarantee a unique reading. See PDF p. 68, 70. C incorrect Realism concerns implementation within constraints. See PDF p. 68, 70. D incorrect Requires a repeatable test, not a unique interpretation alone. See PDF p. 68, 70.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 4 · Q00082
records.text: Q00082 Question 4 SE09 Which option most completely summarizes the listed observable behaviors that functional requirements may specify? Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity. A specifies the tasks the program must complete B Specifies observable tasks the program must not perform C Specifies required observable responses to invalid input D All of the mentioned All of the mentioned Functional requirements describe observable services and behavior, including what must happen, what is prohibited and how the system responds to errors. Each individual choice gives one of these forms. The all-of-the-mentioned option is therefore the complete summary. Selecting only A, B or C would omit other valid functional obligations; negative wording alone does not make a requirement nonfunctional. A incorrect Required tasks are functional, but A alone omits the other listed forms. B incorrect Prohibited tasks can be functional, but B alone is incomplete. C incorrect Required error responses are functional, but C alone is incomplete. D correct All three listed observable behavior forms can be functional requirements.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 5 · Q00083
records.text: Q00083 Question 5 SE02 SE06 A team has little experience with a project’s unfamiliar technology. Major feasibility risks must be evaluated before each further commitment, and experienced risk-analysis support is available. Which lifecycle is selected specifically by that risk-driven criterion? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Iterative Enhancement Model B RAD C Spiral D Waterfall Spiral Spiral organizes each cycle around objectives, alternatives, risk assessment and reduction before further commitment. That directly addresses the specified major feasibility risks and supported risk-analysis capability. Iterative enhancement can aid learning but does not make risk assessment its defining organizer; RAD needs rapid construction and skilled support. Classical waterfall fits stable requirements and familiar technology, which the scenario does not supply. A incorrect Iteration supports feedback but is not defined by risk-driven commitments. B incorrect RAD emphasizes rapid construction rather than the specified risk cycle. C correct Spiral explicitly organizes commitment around major risk reduction. D incorrect Unfamiliar technology and unresolved risks do not fit the stated classical waterfall rationale.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 6 · Q00084
records.text: Q00084 Question 6 SE02 In which step of SDLC actual programming of software code is done? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Development and Documentation B Maintenance and Evaluation C Design D Analysis Development and Documentation Programming translates the design into source code in implementation. A corresponds to the development stage of implementation and unit testing. A correct Development is the option corresponding to producing source code; documentation accompanies the process. See PDF p. 18, 18, 19. B incorrect Maintenance modifies an operational product. See PDF p. 18, 18, 19. C incorrect Design derives implementation structure rather than source code. See PDF p. 18, 18, 19. D incorrect Analysis establishes and organizes requirements. See PDF p. 18, 18, 19.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 7 · Q00094
records.text: Q00094 Question 7 SE09 SE10 Which offered requirement is nonfunctional, specifying a measurable quality rather than required or prohibited observable tasks? Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity. A specifies the tasks the program must complete B Specifies observable tasks the program must not perform C Specifies the required error response to invalid input D Search shall respond within two seconds under 100 concurrent users. Search shall respond within two seconds under 100 concurrent users. The response-time limit under a defined concurrent-user workload is a measurable performance requirement, a nonfunctional quality constraint. Required services, prohibited actions and specified error responses are all forms of observable functional behavior. Their positive or negative wording does not determine the category. D instead constrains how well the search service must perform, making it the unique nonfunctional example. A incorrect Required observable tasks are functional. B incorrect Prohibited observable tasks can be functional. C incorrect An observable error response specifies functional behavior. D correct The time threshold and workload constrain performance quality.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 8 · Q00098
records.text: Q00098 Question 8 SE08 Which of the following is the understanding of software product limitations, learning system related problems or changes to be done in existing systems beforehand, identifying and addressing the impact of project on organization and personnel etc.? Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity. A Software Design B Feasibility Study C Requirement Gathering D System Analysis Feasibility study. SE08 asks whether a proposal is worth doing and deliverable, considering existing limitations, impacts on organization and personnel, benefits, costs, skills and integration risk. That matches the stem’s preliminary impact and constraint investigation. System analysis studies the detailed problem and behavior and informs feasibility, but the broad early viability assessment is the more specific match here. A incorrect Design chooses solution structures rather than primarily assessing preliminary viability and organizational impacts. B correct Feasibility investigates existing limitations, impacts and whether the proposal is worthwhile and deliverable. C incorrect Gathering needs is useful input but does not by itself cover the full viability assessment. D incorrect System analysis examines detailed problem behavior; feasibility is the more specific preliminary impact/viability activity.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 9 · Q00120
records.text: Q00120 Question 9 SE01 For a software product developed to meet a client’s requirements, which choice most completely describes its scope? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Software product refers any software created to meet the client's requirements. B Software product includes design and test documentation. C Software product includes requirement specifications, and user manuals. D All of the above All of the above SE01 explicitly includes executable code plus requirements, designs, test assets, configuration and user documentation in a software product. A describes the implemented software, while B and C name relevant accompanying artifacts. All three descriptions are therefore compatible; none limits the product to code alone. D is the inclusive answer among these options. A incorrect True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Software built to meet client requirements forms part of the product. B incorrect True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Relevant design and testing documentation are included product artifacts. C incorrect True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Requirements specifications and user manuals are relevant product documentation. D correct All three descriptions are compatible with the complete software-product scope.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 10 · Q00121
records.text: Q00121 Question 10 SE10 One of the followings is type of requirements associated with quality features of a software. Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity. A Business requirements B Functional requirements requirements C Non-functional D User requirements Non-functional Quality and user-visible constraints beyond functional behavior are nonfunctional requirements; user and business are viewpoints rather than this quality classification. A incorrect Business objectives do not identify the stated quality category. See PDF p. 66, 78. B incorrect Specifies provided interactions and services. See PDF p. 66, 78. C correct Matches nonfunctional quality constraints. See PDF p. 66, 78. D incorrect User requirements can contain several types, so this is broader than quality features. See PDF p. 66, 78.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 11 · Q00122
records.text: Q00122 Question 11 SE08 A type of requirement that describes why the software project is needed and used to define the objective of the software is . Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity. A Business requirements B Functional requirements C Non-functional requirements D User requirements Business requirements. SE08 distinguishes the business reason and objectives of a project from user needs and detailed system obligations. The question asks why the project is needed and what objectives it serves, so business requirements match directly. Functional requirements describe behavior, while nonfunctional requirements describe qualities or constraints; neither primarily states the project's business justification. A correct Business requirements state the project's purpose, justification and intended organizational goals. B incorrect Functional requirements specify observable system services rather than the overall business reason for the project. C incorrect Nonfunctional requirements specify qualities or constraints rather than why the project exists. D incorrect User requirements describe stakeholder needs at a high level rather than the project's business justification.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 12 · Q00123
records.text: Q00123 Question 12 SE14 SE-S03 SE24 Which of the following is used to model the functionality of software? Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A Use case diagram B Class diagram C E-R diagram D Deployment diagram Use case diagram Use-case diagrams model external roles and their goals or interactions with the system. This is the functional view requested. Class diagrams instead emphasize static classes, features and relationships. Entity–relationship diagrams organize entity types, attributes and data relationships. Deployment diagrams map software artifacts to execution nodes. Each can contribute to understanding a system, but only the use-case view directly presents the actor-goal functionality in this comparison. A correct Use-case diagrams show external actors and the system goals they use. B incorrect Class diagrams describe static types and their relationships. C incorrect ER diagrams describe entity types, attributes and data relationships. D incorrect Deployment diagrams map software artifacts onto execution nodes.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 13 · Q00124
records.text: Q00124 Question 13 SE23 Which of the following refers to the deployment platform? i Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Use case B Tier C Layer D Component Tier. SE23 explicitly separates logical abstraction from deployment separation. A layer organizes responsibilities logically, whereas a tier describes their deployment separation or platform arrangement. A use case models an actor goal, and a component is a software building block. Neither is the term for the deployment distinction asked for here. A incorrect A use case models a goal or interaction rather than the deployment platform separation. B correct A tier identifies deployment separation, contrasting with logical layering. C incorrect A layer is a logical abstraction level and need not occupy a distinct deployment platform. D incorrect A component is a software element and does not itself denote a deployment tier.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 14 · Q00125
records.text: Q00125 Question 14 SE03 SE05 SE07 When requirements will change substantially and frequent early feedback is needed, which classical process organization is least accommodating among these choices? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Waterfall B Scrum C RAD D Agile Waterfall Classical waterfall commits to planned phases and reviewed deliverables, making late feedback and changed requirements costly. Agile and Scrum plan and inspect work incrementally, allowing later content to adapt. RAD also uses rapid construction and user participation to obtain feedback. The comparison therefore favors waterfall as the least accommodating under the stated conditions, without claiming that a waterfall project is physically unable to authorize any change. A correct Late feedback and phase commitments make major requirement changes costly in classical waterfall. B incorrect Scrum inspects usable increments and adapts later work within its planning framework. C incorrect RAD uses rapid construction and user participation to obtain feedback. D incorrect Agile explicitly values responding to changing needs.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 15 · Q00126
records.text: Q00126 Question 15 SE34 Which of the following aims to find errors? Distinguish process assurance from product evaluation, and compare specified obligations with actual stakeholder needs. A Requirement Analysis B Design C Testing D None of the above Testing Testing systematically attempts to expose errors in the implementation; the other named activities primarily construct specifications and designs. A incorrect Structures requirements, although validation may reveal requirement defects. See PDF p. 140, 100, 18. B incorrect Constructs the solution design. See PDF p. 140, 100, 18. C correct Explicit planned fault detection activity. See PDF p. 140, 100, 18. D incorrect Testing is present, so none is false. See PDF p. 140, 100, 18.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 16 · Q00239
records.text: Q00239 Question 16 SE23 Which among the following focuses on the way the elements interact with each other at runtime during architectural design? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A All choices are correct B Component-and-connector (C&C) structures C Allocation structures D Module decomposition structure Component-and-connector structures. The runtime interaction of software elements is the subject of component-and-connector structures in SE23. Module structures instead organize the code, while allocation structures relate software to hardware, teams or environments. These are different architectural views, so the inclusive choice fails: only the C&C option specifically answers the runtime-interaction focus. A incorrect The alternatives address different architectural concerns, so not every choice focuses on runtime interaction. B correct C&C structures show runtime elements and the connectors through which they interact. C incorrect Allocation structures map software to hardware, teams or environments rather than primarily describing runtime exchanges. D incorrect Module decomposition shows code organization rather than the runtime interactions emphasized by the stem.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 17 · Q00240
records.text: Q00240 Question 17 SE27 SE22 Which option combines both explicitly specified testability mechanisms among A, C and D? Treat refactoring alone as behavior-preserving restructuring with no stated testability improvement. Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Sand box B A and D C Refactoring D Limiting structural complexity A and D A sandbox can isolate execution, giving control over the test environment. Limiting structural complexity also supports testability by making behavior easier to control and observe. Refactoring preserves behavior while changing structure, but without a stated improvement it does not automatically supply either testability effect. The combination A and D therefore includes both explicitly supported mechanisms; the individual choices each give only one. A incorrect Sandbox isolation is valid but only one of the two mechanisms. B correct A and D include both explicitly supported mechanisms. C incorrect Unspecified refactoring need not improve testability. D incorrect Limited structural complexity is valid but only one of the two mechanisms.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 18 · Q00241
records.text: Q00241 Question 18 SE27 Which choices explicitly provide architectural variability through selectable elements or defined extension interfaces? Select all that apply. Treat overloading as alternate code signatures only. Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Overloading B Omission or inclusion of elements C Extension point D All of the above Omission or inclusion of elements; Extension point Omitting or including selected elements permits configured architectural variation, and extension points define places where additional behavior can be supplied. Overloading by itself supplies alternate code signatures and does not establish either architectural mechanism. Thus B and C meet the specified architectural scope. The all-of-the-above choice includes that insufficient code-level case and therefore cannot be selected as a correct aggregate. A incorrect Alternate signatures alone do not define the specified architectural variability. B correct Selectable omission or inclusion changes architectural configuration. C correct Extension points explicitly support variation at defined boundaries. D incorrect It incorrectly includes overloading alone as an architectural mechanism.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 19 · Q00242
records.text: Q00242 Question 19 SE27 Which choice most completely describes the stated advantages of the Factory Method pattern? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Allows the sub-classes to choose the type of objects to create B Promotes loose coupling C A and B D None of the above A and B SE27 describes Factory Method as letting subclasses choose a concrete product through a creation operation, reducing dependence on concrete constructors. Those are exactly the two benefits in A and B, so C is the inclusive answer. The reference is to Factory Method; a simple factory is related but does not necessarily delegate product choice to subclasses. A incorrect True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Factory Method lets subclasses select the concrete product through the creation operation. B incorrect True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Depending on the creation abstraction reduces coupling to concrete product constructors. C correct Both listed benefits hold for Factory Method, making this the inclusive answer. D incorrect The note explicitly supports both benefits, so none is false.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 20 · Q00243
records.text: Q00243 Question 20 SE23 Which statements correctly distinguish architectural structures and views? Select all that apply. Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A B and D only B Views design structures whereas architects document the structures. C A structure is the set of elements and their relations as they exist in software or hardware. D A view is a representation of a structure A structure is the set of elements and their relations as they exist in software or hardware.; A view is a representation of a structure An architectural structure consists of elements and their relations in the modeled software or hardware. A view represents selected aspects of a structure for a particular purpose. Both C and D therefore express compatible definitions. Views are representations, not agents that design structures, so B is false. The aggregate A includes that false statement and incorrectly excludes the true structure definition. A incorrect The B-and-D-only combination includes false B and excludes true C. B incorrect Views represent structures rather than acting as their designers. C correct A structure is the underlying set of elements and relations. D correct A view represents selected aspects of a structure.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 21 · Q00244
records.text: Q00244 Question 21 SE35 SE36 Which testing level isolates one function or class, using stubs or mocks for called dependencies, so its internal branches can be tested directly? Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A System testing B Integration testing C System and integration testing together D Unit testing Unit testing Unit testing isolates a function, class or small component and may replace dependencies with stubs or mocks. That matches the stated test scope. White-box cases can then target its internal branches, but white-box is a technique rather than a testing level. Integration and system tests cover combined interactions or the full system, so neither matches the isolation specified here. A incorrect System testing evaluates the complete integrated system. B incorrect Integration testing targets interactions among combined parts. C incorrect Combining system and integration levels does not give isolated unit scope. D correct Unit testing isolates the function or class with replaceable dependencies.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 22 · Q00245
records.text: Q00245 Question 22 SE20 SE14 Which offered UML diagram models external behavioral goals and actor interactions at a high level, rather than detailed message timing or state evolution? Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A Component diagram B Use case diagram C Deployment diagram D Class Diagram Use case diagram A use-case diagram presents external roles, their goals and relationships within a chosen system boundary. It therefore matches the specified high-level behavioral scope. Component, deployment and class diagrams describe structural organization, allocation or static types. Sequence, activity and state diagrams would be appropriate for detailed interactions, workflows or state changes, but those finer-grained dynamic questions are explicitly outside this stem. A incorrect Component diagrams describe components and interfaces. B correct Use-case diagrams show actor roles and high-level goals. C incorrect Deployment diagrams allocate artifacts to nodes. D incorrect Class diagrams show static types and relationships.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 23 · Q00246
records.text: Q00246 Question 23 SE11 SE-S01 Which choice most completely identifies the listed reasons requirements elicitation can be difficult? Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity. A All choices are correct B Problem of scope C Problem of understanding D Problem of volatility All choices are correct SE11 identifies scope, understanding and volatility as distinct elicitation difficulties. Scope concerns agreeing what belongs in the system; understanding concerns discovering and interpreting actual needs; volatility concerns needs changing as the project progresses. Since all three listed problems are valid, the inclusive answer is appropriate rather than choosing just one source of difficulty. A correct All three listed difficulties are explicitly recognized in the complete note. B incorrect True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Unclear system boundaries make agreeing on included and excluded requirements difficult. C incorrect True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Different interpretations and tacit stakeholder needs complicate accurate understanding. D incorrect True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Changing needs make elicitation an ongoing activity rather than a one-time capture.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 24 · Q00247
records.text: Q00247 Question 24 SE02 Which development activity primarily recognizes and clarifies the problem, required behavior and related constraints before choosing the solution architecture or algorithms? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Implementation B Testing C Analysis D Design Analysis Analysis clarifies the problem, required behavior and constraints. Design then chooses architecture, interfaces and algorithms for a solution; implementation writes it, and testing evaluates its behavior. The revised scope keeps these responsibilities distinct instead of mixing problem recognition with selecting methods to overcome it. Creativity can occur in several activities, so the activity’s purpose, rather than that adjective, determines the answer. A incorrect Implementation writes the selected solution. B incorrect Testing evaluates behavior. C correct Analysis clarifies the problem and constraints. D incorrect Design selects the solution architecture and mechanisms.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 25 · Q00248
records.text: Q00248 Question 25 SE17 _______ is a set of notations and conventions used to describe and model an application. Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A All choices are correct B Unified approach (UA) C Unified modeling language (UML) D Jacobson's use case Unified modeling language (UML) UML provides modeling notations and conventions; it is distinct from a development methodology. A incorrect UA and use cases are not both equivalent to the language. See PDF p. 32. B incorrect UA specifies steps for development. See PDF p. 32. C correct The exact defined modeling notation language. See PDF p. 32. D incorrect A use case is an interaction model inside the approach. See PDF p. 32.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 26 · Q00249
records.text: Q00249 Question 26 SE01 SE40 SE22 SE43 Which structural risk can arise when repeated software changes are made without coherent design or refactoring? Classify the motive for the change before its implementation: repair, environment, useful capability or reduced future risk. A Reduced user engagement B Increased software complexity C Increased automation D Elimination of maintenance costs Increased software complexity Repeated changes without coherent boundaries can accumulate dependencies and make the evolving system harder to understand. Refactoring and good subsystem design help control that structural complexity while maintenance still requires impact analysis and regression checks. User engagement is a product-use outcome rather than the structural risk asked for. Automation is an execution technique, not itself structural deterioration, and ongoing evolution does not eliminate maintenance costs. A incorrect Engagement concerns user behavior rather than the internal structural deterioration asked for. B correct Accumulated poorly coordinated changes can increase structural complexity. C incorrect Automation does not itself describe deterioration of responsibilities or dependency structure. D incorrect Changing software still requires maintenance and regression work.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 27 · Q00250
records.text: Q00250 Question 27 SE30 Which of the following best describes the difference between CPM and PERT? Write out the supplied quantities and dependency constraints. Compute and compare values under the stated metric, finish condition and assumptions. A CPM focuses on minimizing cost, while PERT focuses on minimizing time. B CPM is used for projects with uncertain activity durations, while PERT is used for projects with known activity durations. C PERT is used for projects with uncertain activity durations, while CPM is used for projects with known activity durations. D PERT is deterministic, whereas CPM is probabilistic. PERT models uncertain durations; traditional CPM uses point durations. SE30 gives traditional CPM point estimates and PERT optimistic, most-likely and pessimistic duration estimates. PERT therefore represents duration uncertainty, whereas the traditional CPM calculation uses known or fixed activity durations. The cost-versus-time contrast is not the defining distinction here, and the other two choices reverse the described treatment of uncertainty. A incorrect The note's defining contrast concerns duration uncertainty rather than assigning cost exclusively to CPM. B incorrect This reverses the models: PERT explicitly represents uncertain activity durations. C correct PERT uses uncertain three-point estimates, while traditional CPM uses fixed point durations. D incorrect The probabilistic/deterministic characterization is reversed relative to the note.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 28 · Q00251
records.text: Q00251 Question 28 SE28 A key benefit of using a project management tool in software development is: Distinguish the planning or organization goal from the tool or structure used to support it. Apply the stated project conditions. A Automatic bug detection and fixing. B Replacing the need for human project managers. C Improved communication and collaboration within the team. D Increased coding efficiency for developers. Improved team communication and collaboration. SE28 says planning tools coordinate ownership, dependencies and progress while leaving judgment to people. That coordination supports communication and collaboration. The tool does not automatically detect and repair code faults, replace project managers or directly guarantee faster coding. Those benefits would require other capabilities and evidence beyond project-management tooling itself. A incorrect Project-management tools do not automatically detect and repair software defects. B incorrect They support planning and coordination while human managers still supply judgment. C correct Shared ownership, dependency and progress information helps the team communicate and collaborate. D incorrect A direct increase in coding efficiency is not the general coordination benefit established here.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 29 · Q00252
records.text: Q00252 Question 29 SE33 A software development team is setting up a configuration management process. They need to identify the configuration items (CIs) for their project. Which of the following would not typically be considered a configuration item? Separate artifact history and controlled changes from scheduling, collaboration benefits and automated execution. A Internet browsers used by the development team B Source code files C User manuals D Test plans Ordinary browsers used by the team are usually tools, not product configuration items. Controlled configuration items include source files, requirements, manuals and test plans. A team's ordinary browser is normally just a tool. A particular browser version can become an environment CI if the project deliberately controls it for reproducible testing, but the word typically makes A the appropriate exception in the stated scenario. A correct An ordinary team browser is usually a tool; a deliberately controlled test-browser version would be an exception. B incorrect Source code files are standard controlled product configuration items. C incorrect User manuals can be versioned and baselined alongside the software product. D incorrect Test plans are controlled project artifacts whose versions must match the tested configuration.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 30 · Q00253
records.text: Q00253 Question 30 SE28 Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a well-defined Work Breakdown Structure (WBS)? Distinguish the planning or organization goal from the tool or structure used to support it. Apply the stated project conditions. A It can be used to assign ownership and track the progress of project tasks. B It clearly defines deliverables for each level of the breakdown. C It includes activities that are outside the project scope. D It is organized in a hierarchical manner, with the overall project at the top and smaller tasks at the bottom. It includes activities that are outside the project scope. Planning breaks down the work needed to complete this project. Work outside project scope is therefore not part of its WBS; hierarchy and assignable tasks are consistent with decomposition. A incorrect Task assignment and tracking serve project management. See PDF p. 90, 95. B incorrect Deliverables constrain and clarify project work. See PDF p. 90, 95. C correct Outside-scope activities do not belong to the work needed to complete the defined project. See PDF p. 90, 95. D incorrect Breaking large tasks into smaller activities supports the hierarchy described. See PDF p. 90, 95.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 31 · Q00254
records.text: Q00254 Question 31 SE33 A project team is working on a software project with multiple developers. They decided to implement a version control system (VCS). Which of the following scenarios best describes the use case for a distributed VCS like Git? Separate artifact history and controlled changes from scheduling, collaboration benefits and automated execution. A The team prefers to avoid merge conflicts by locking files so only one developer can work on a file at a time. B The team is large, geographically distributed, and each developer needs to work on features independently and merge changes later. C The team is small, and all developers work in the same physical location on a single branch. D The project requires strict control over who can make changes, and all changes must be approved by a central authority before being committed. Independent distributed development followed by merging. SE33 says a distributed Git clone contains local history and allows independent branches that can later be merged. B matches that working arrangement directly. Git does not require everyone to lock files, use one local branch or obtain central permission before every local commit. Additional review policies can be imposed, but they do not define distributed version control. A incorrect Exclusive file locking is not the defining distributed Git collaboration model. B correct Local histories and independent branches support geographically distributed work followed by merging. C incorrect A colocated team can use Git, but this scenario does not express its independent distributed-work benefit. D incorrect Central approval policies can exist, but they do not define or require distributed local commits.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 33 · Q00256
records.text: Q00256 Question 33 SE08 SE21 SE-S06 In the ordinary software lifecycle terminology used here, which document organizes the agreed user and detailed system requirements? records.title: Software Engineering — Question 34 · Q00257
records.text: Q00257 Question 34 SE04 Which listed statements describe supported advantages or uses of incremental delivery? Select all that apply. Interpret easier testing/debugging as a potential benefit of smaller changes, not a guarantee. Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Easier to test and debug B Easier to test and debug & It is used when there is a need to get a product to the market early C Customer can respond to each increment D It is used when there is a need to get a product to the market early Easier to test and debug; Easier to test and debug & It is used when there is a need to get a product to the market early; Customer can respond to each increment; It is used when there is a need to get a product to the market early Incremental delivery adds usable capability in stages. Smaller changes can be easier to test and debug, users can provide feedback after increments, and prioritized partial capability can reach the market early. Thus A, C and D each describe a supported benefit, and B is also true because it combines two true points. These benefits still require architecture, integration and testing effort. A correct Smaller increments can be easier to test and debug. B correct Both the smaller-change and early-delivery points are supported. C correct Users can respond to each usable increment. D correct Early delivery of prioritized capability is a supported use.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 35 · Q00258
records.text: Q00258 Question 35 SE07 Use a process diagram whose named stages are requirements gathering, quick design, prototype construction, prototype refinement and engineering the production product. Which offered activity is not a separately named stage, although it can occur within prototype construction? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Coding B Prototype Refinement C Engineer Product D Quick Design Coding Coding can be part of building an executable prototype even if the process diagram labels that work construction. It is therefore the offered activity that is not a separately named stage in the stated convention. Quick design, refinement and production engineering are named stages there. This answer concerns the diagram’s labels and does not claim that prototyping excludes coding or always follows one universal phase taxonomy. A correct Coding can occur inside construction without a separate stage label. B incorrect Prototype refinement is a named stage. C incorrect Engineering the production product is a named stage. D incorrect Quick design is a named stage.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 36 · Q00259
records.text: Q00259 Question 36 SE07 What is the major drawback of using the RAD Model? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Increases reusability of components, Highly specialized & skilled developers/designers are required B Increases reusability of components C Highly specialized & skilled developers/designers are required D Encourages customer/client feedback The need for highly skilled developers and designers. SE07 describes RAD as rapid construction using timeboxes, user participation and often reusable components, but requiring skilled designers and developers. That staffing prerequisite is the listed drawback. Reuse and customer feedback are useful features. A combines the genuine prerequisite with a benefit, so C states the drawback accurately without misclassifying reuse. A incorrect It bundles a genuine staffing drawback with component reuse, which is generally a benefit. B incorrect Component reuse helps rapid construction and is not the drawback asked for. C correct RAD depends on skilled designers and developers, which can constrain staffing and feasibility. D incorrect Customer feedback supports learning and fit rather than being the stated RAD disadvantage.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 38 · Q00261
records.text: Q00261 Question 38 SE34 Which of the following is not a SQA plan for a project? Distinguish process assurance from product evaluation, and compare specified obligations with actual stakeholder needs. SE34 identifies assurance responsibilities, evaluations, reviews, audits and assurance records as SQA-plan contents. The documents produced by SQA are assurance records; evaluations, audits and reviews are assurance activities. The amount of general technical development work belongs primarily to project scope and effort planning rather than defining the SQA activities listed here. A incorrect Assurance documents and records are legitimate SQA-plan deliverables. B incorrect Planned evaluations are explicitly part of an SQA plan. records.title: Software Engineering — Question 39 · Q00262
records.text: Q00262 Question 39 SE39 Which of the below is not a part of the Test Plan? Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A Schedule B Incident reports C Entry and exit criteria D Risk Incident reports are execution outputs, rather than the test plan itself. SE39 places objectives, scope, resources, schedule, risks and entry/exit criteria in test planning. Incident reports document observed problems during execution and are normally outputs of that work. They may be referenced by later plans, but that does not make actual incident reports an intrinsic part of the prospective test plan. A incorrect The test schedule is planned work and belongs in a test plan. B correct Incident reports normally record execution findings rather than describing the planned testing work. C incorrect Entry and exit criteria define when testing can start or finish and belong in planning. D incorrect Testing risks influence scope and priorities and are legitimate test-plan content.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 40 · Q00263
records.text: Q00263 Question 40 SE36 Exploratory testing is a -----? Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A Experience-based Test Design Technique B Black Box Test Design Technique C White Box Test Design Technique D Grey Box Test Design Technique Experience-based testing. SE36 explicitly classifies exploratory testing as experience based because learning, test design and execution occur together. It may use knowledge of specifications or internals, but black-box, white-box and grey-box describe different bases of test derivation. None of them replaces the defining experience-based classification asked for in this question. A correct Exploratory testing uses experience while learning, designing and executing tests together. B incorrect It may use external behavior, but black-box alone is not its defining classification. C incorrect Exploratory testing does not require test cases to be derived from internal code structure. D incorrect Partial internal knowledge can help exploration, but it does not define the technique.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 42 · Q00308
records.text: Q00308 Question 42 SE21 SE22 When comparing internal subsystem-grouping criteria with an external user perspective, which option names the external perspective rather than an internal structural or responsibility criterion? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. User workflows can still inform architecture; the distinction does not claim users have no influence on design or that internal boundaries should ignore their needs. A incorrect Coupling directly measures inter-subsystem dependency. B incorrect Functionality guides internal responsibility grouping. C incorrect Cohesion measures how well elements grouped inside a subsystem serve a related purpose. D correct This names the external user perspective rather than an internal structural measure or responsibility criterion.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 44 · Q00310
records.text: Q00310 Question 44 SE02 SE21 SE08 Under the course’s distinction between problem analysis and solution design, which statement is false? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A System Analysis Focuses on the user's view of the system B Design focuses on the developer point of view. C Result of system analysis is a model that includes a subsystem decomposition D Requirements elicitation establishes externally visible stakeholder needs and constraints before internal solution design. Result of system analysis is a model that includes a subsystem decomposition Analysis clarifies the domain and externally required behavior; system design chooses the solution architecture and subsystem responsibilities. Attributing subsystem decomposition to the principal analysis result therefore confuses these stages. Requirements elicitation establishes stakeholder needs and constraints before the internal solution is selected. The revised elicitation option avoids the stronger claim that only one user’s viewpoint matters, while retaining the intended external-needs versus internal-design distinction. A incorrect Analysis clarifies the user/domain view of required behavior. B incorrect Design develops the solution structure and implementation-facing decisions. C correct Subsystem decomposition is principally a system-design result, so attributing it to analysis is the false claim. D incorrect Elicitation establishes externally visible stakeholder needs and constraints before choosing internal design.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 45 · Q00311
records.text: Q00311 Question 45 SE13 Which of the following heuristics is not used to identify Entity objects Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity. A Real-world entities B Real-world activities C Forms D Data sources Forms normally identify boundary objects. SE13 defines entity objects as domain information and gives ReportForm as a boundary mediating interaction. Thus forms normally suggest boundary objects rather than entity objects. Real-world things, domain activities represented as information and relevant stored data can suggest entity candidates; those are heuristics, not mechanical rules guaranteeing a class for every noun or activity. A incorrect Real-world domain entities are natural candidates for entity objects. B incorrect A domain activity represented as persistent domain information can suggest an entity candidate. C correct A user-interface form normally mediates interaction and is modeled as a boundary object. D incorrect Relevant domain data sources can suggest information-holding entities, subject to analysis rather than automatic conversion.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 51 · Q00554
records.text: Q00554 Question 51 SE32 Which team organization shares development decisions among team members rather than centralizing technical coordination in a chief programmer? Distinguish the planning or organization goal from the tool or structure used to support it. Apply the stated project conditions. A Functional B Project C Democratic D Chief programmer Democratic Democratic teams share decisions, whereas chief-programmer teams centralize technical coordination. Functional and project organizations classify how people are grouped, not how authority is distributed. Asking about shared decision-making therefore makes democratic the unique answer. It does not require every individual to perform every lifecycle task; a democratic team can still divide work by expertise and responsibilities. A incorrect Functional organization groups specialists by discipline. B incorrect Project organization groups people by project rather than defining shared authority. C correct Democratic teams share decisions. D incorrect Chief-programmer teams centralize technical coordination.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 52 · Q00555
records.text: Q00555 Question 52 SE32 Which capability maturity model level an organization must master the requirements management software quality assurance, and software project planning Distinguish the planning or organization goal from the tool or structure used to support it. Apply the stated project conditions. A Repeatable level B Initial level C Defined level D Managed level Historical CMM Level 2: Repeatable. SE32 explicitly assigns requirements management, software project planning, quality assurance and configuration management to historical Software CMM Level 2. Its name is Repeatable, rather than the later CMMI label Managed. The other named choices correspond to levels 1, 3 and 4 in this historical model, so A matches both practices and terminology. A correct Repeatable is historical Software CMM Level 2, which establishes the listed basic project practices. B incorrect Initial is historical Level 1, before the repeatable project discipline specified here. C incorrect Defined is historical Level 3, not the level associated with this basic practice list. D incorrect Managed is historical Software CMM Level 4; modern CMMI terminology must not be substituted.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 53 · Q00558
records.text: Q00558 Question 53 SE32 All are the advantages of functional format structure, except Distinguish the planning or organization goal from the tool or structure used to support it. Apply the stated project conditions. A Ease of staffing B Production of good quality documents C No need job specialization D Efficient handling manpower turnover No need for job specialization is false of a functional organization. SE32 defines functional organizations as grouping specialists by discipline. Claiming that specialization is unnecessary contradicts that organizing principle. Ease of staffing and knowledge continuity are benefits of specialization; continuity can help with turnover. Specialist expertise can also support documentation quality, although no organizational form guarantees good documents. C is the clear exception. A incorrect Grouping specialists supports staffing within established disciplines, so this is a plausible benefit. B incorrect Specialist expertise can support good documentation; this is not the direct contradiction of functional grouping. C correct This contradicts the defining use of specialist disciplines in a functional organization. D incorrect Knowledge continuity within a functional group can help absorb staff turnover.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 56 · Q00575
records.text: Q00575 Question 56 SE07 SE06 Requirements and technical feasibility are unclear. The immediate goal is to build an exploratory version for user feedback and feasibility learning, then discard it rather than deliver it as production software. Which model best names that immediate activity? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Incremental model B Prototype model C Spiral model D Waterfall model Prototype model A throwaway prototype explores requirements, usability or technical feasibility and is discarded after learning. That exactly matches the immediate purpose specified. Incremental delivery would provide usable production capability; spiral would organize broader commitments around risk-driven cycles and might use a prototype within them. Classical waterfall favors understood requirements and familiar technology. The specific learning-and-discard goal therefore identifies the prototype model. A incorrect Incremental delivery targets usable capability rather than a discarded exploratory artifact. B correct A throwaway prototype explores needs and feasibility before being discarded. C incorrect Spiral may use a prototype, but names the broader risk-driven process. D incorrect The stated uncertainty lacks classical waterfall’s stable, familiar conditions.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 57 · Q00580

A incorrect Actor interaction is part of some sequences but is less precise than object-message order. See PDF p. 54. B incorrect Broadly describes behavior without identifying temporal interaction. See PDF p. 54. C incorrect Activity flow is represented by activity diagrams. See PDF p. 54. D correct Matches time-ordered messages and activations. See PDF p. 54.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 59 · Q00597

A incorrect Efficiency is useful, but it is not the defining organizing feature of spiral cycles. B incorrect Time management matters in many processes and does not distinguish spiral. records.title: Software Engineering — Question 61 · Q00612

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 63 · Q00649
records.text: Q00649 Question 63 SE40 ______a software product is necessary to rectify the bugs observed while the system is in use. Classify the motive for the change before its implementation: repair, environment, useful capability or reduced future risk. A Adaptive maintenance B Corrective maintenance C Perfective maintenance D Preventive maintenance Corrective maintenance The purpose of the change determines the maintenance category. Corrective maintenance repairs faults observed during use. Adaptive maintenance handles environmental changes, perfective maintenance improves useful capability or performance, and preventive maintenance reduces future risk before a corresponding failure occurs. Because the scenario starts with observed bugs that need repair, corrective maintenance is the direct category rather than one of the other three motives. A incorrect Adaptive maintenance responds to a changed environment. B correct Corrective maintenance repairs observed defects. C incorrect Perfective maintenance improves useful capability or performance. D incorrect Preventive maintenance reduces future risk rather than primarily fixing the stated observed bugs.

records.text: Q00740 Question 66 SE22 Which are supported modularization benefits? Select all that apply. Read D as a claim that modularization alone guarantees security. records.title: Software Engineering — Question 73 · Q00750
records.text: Q00750 Question 73 SE22 SE01 Which maintenance risk can arise from poorly designed objects with complex or poorly separated responsibilities? records.title: Software Engineering — Question 74 · Q00897
records.text: Q00897 Question 74 SE18 In a class diagram, a filled diamond is at Car’s end of its Engine association. In this model an Engine remains owned by its Car for its entire lifetime, with no detachment or transfer. What does the relationship imply? Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A Car uses Engine temporarily B Engine can exist independently of the Car C Engine is part of Car and cannot exist independently under the stated lifetime policy. D Car inherits from Engine Engine is part of Car and cannot exist independently under the stated lifetime policy. The filled diamond at Car denotes composition: Car is the whole and Engine is its strongly owned part. Composition destroys parts that remain owned when the whole is destroyed. Because this model forbids detachment or transfer, the Engine’s lifetime cannot continue independently of its Car. Temporary use would be a dependency, and inheritance would use a hollow generalization triangle instead. A incorrect Temporary use is a dependency, not composition. B incorrect The stipulated permanent ownership excludes an independent Engine lifetime. C correct Engine is the owned part and cannot outlive Car under the stated policy. D incorrect Inheritance uses a hollow triangle rather than a filled diamond.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 76 · Q00948
records.text: Q00948 Question 76 SE10 Which statement specifically constrains response-time performance under a stated workload? Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity. A The system allow user to generate PDF report. B The system respond to user's request within 2 second under normal load C . The system allow user to store data on relational database D The system allow user to submit emergency report The system respond to user's request within 2 second under normal load The two-second response obligation bounds the speed of a service under the stated load, so it is a performance requirement. Generating a PDF and submitting an emergency report describe services the system provides. The database clause describes storage behavior together with an implementation choice; it does not impose a response-time threshold. The explicit performance scope removes the broader taxonomy overlap between nonfunctional requirements and technology constraints. A incorrect Report generation specifies a service, not its response-time limit. B correct A two-second response bound under normal load is a quantitative speed target. C incorrect This specifies storage behavior and a database technology, without a timing bound. D incorrect Submitting an emergency report specifies a function rather than its speed.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 80 · Q01197
records.text: Q01197 Question 80 SE21 Which choice most completely lists candidate heuristics for grouping objects into subsystems? Treat them as starting guidance, not mandatory boundaries. Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Assign objects identified in one use case into the same subsystem. B Create a dedicated subsystem for objects used for moving data among subsystems. C Minimize the number of associations crossing subsystem boundaries. D All of the above All of the above SE21 recommends grouping related functionality, minimizing cross-subsystem associations and isolating communication infrastructure where useful. Grouping objects serving one use case can be a starting heuristic, though workflows do not dictate every boundary. B and C directly support isolation and low coupling. Since the question asks what can be a heuristic, the inclusive option is appropriate. A incorrect True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Objects collaborating on one use case can be grouped as a starting heuristic, subject to other design constraints. B incorrect True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Communication infrastructure can be isolated in a dedicated subsystem when useful. C incorrect True as one component, but incomplete as the requested full selection. Reducing cross-boundary associations reduces coupling between subsystems. D correct All three can guide decomposition, provided use-case grouping is not treated as an absolute rule.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 81 · Q01205
records.text: Q01205 Question 81 SE21 Which statement is false about a logical software subsystem? Interpret complexity reduction as managing solution-design complexity, not changing the inherent application domain. Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A A physical and replaceable part of the system. B It helps manage the complexity of the solution design. C Decompose a system into simpler parts. D Well-defined interfaces that encapsulate the state and behavior of its contained classes. A physical and replaceable part of the system. A subsystem is a manageable logical collection of responsibilities with services and an interface. It need not be a physical replaceable artifact, so A is false as a definition. Decomposing the designed solution into simpler groups helps manage complexity, and defined interfaces can encapsulate implementation state and behavior. These design benefits concern the solution organization rather than reducing the inherent complexity of its problem domain. A correct A logical subsystem need not be physical or independently replaceable. B incorrect Managing solution-design complexity is a supported decomposition benefit. C incorrect Decomposition groups the system into simpler responsibilities. D incorrect Defined interfaces encapsulate contained implementation details.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 82 · Q01208
records.text: Q01208 Question 82 SE10 SE-S07 Which of the following is an example of Usability requirements? Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity. A A new user shall complete the main interface task within one minute without help. B Robustness C Mean time to failure D Adaptability A new user shall complete the main interface task within one minute without help. A usability requirement states an observable target for successful and learnable use. Requiring a new user to finish a main interface task without help within one minute gives a task, user context, success condition and threshold. Robustness concerns dependable behavior under adverse conditions, mean time to failure is a reliability measure, and adaptability concerns change. Merely naming a user interface would not itself specify an obligation, so the option supplies a genuine requirement. A correct The task-success and unaided-learning target is a measurable usability obligation. B incorrect Robustness concerns dependable behavior under adverse conditions rather than ease of learning a task. C incorrect Mean time to failure measures reliability rather than user task ease. D incorrect Adaptability concerns accommodating change rather than the stated user task target.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 84 · Q01261
records.text: Q01261 Question 84 SE11 SE09 Which of the following is false about functional requirement? Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity. A Requirements should complete B Requirement should be accurate as possible. C Each requirement should state a clear, independently verifiable obligation. D A requirement can be interpreted in many exclusive ways. A requirement can be interpreted in many exclusive ways. Requirements should accurately reflect stakeholder needs, cover the agreed scope and express clear, verifiable obligations. Unambiguity requires one intended interpretation; mutually exclusive readings violate that property. The revised third option states the useful single-obligation writing rule without claiming that duplicate requirements can never be consolidated. Thus the multiple-interpretation option is the single false quality claim, while completeness, accuracy and clarity remain valid goals. A incorrect Completeness requires coverage of the agreed behavior and exceptional cases. B incorrect Accuracy requires requirements to reflect the actual stakeholder needs. C incorrect A clear independently verifiable obligation supports precise specification. D correct Mutually exclusive readings violate the unambiguity requirement.

See PDF p. 62, 100.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 86 · Q01512
records.text: Q01512 Question 86 SE07 SE06 Which named approach develops an experimental version specifically to explore unclear requirements or feasibility, and can therefore serve both as a development approach and an elicitation technique? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Spiral process model B Waterfall process model C Prototype process model D Agile process model Prototype process model Prototyping uses an early experimental representation or working version to discover requirements, usability needs or technical feasibility. It can be organized as a development approach and also used within elicitation. Spiral may contain a prototype to reduce risk, but risk-driven cycles define spiral itself. Waterfall names phased development, while Agile names a broader adaptive approach. The question asks the named experimentation technique that directly serves both purposes. A incorrect Spiral may employ prototypes but is itself defined by risk-driven cycles. B incorrect Waterfall is a phased lifecycle rather than the experimentation technique described. C correct Prototyping directly explores requirements or feasibility using an experimental version. D incorrect Agile is a broad adaptive approach and can use several elicitation techniques.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 88 · Q01514
records.text: Q01514 Question 88 SE22 Evaluate statements A–C about subsystem decomposition. Which is false? Select D if none is false. Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A In designing the desirable effect is low coupling and high cohesion in sub system decomposition B Cohesion refers to the dependency of classes with in subsystem C Coupling refers to the dependency between sub systems D None of statements A–C is false. None of statements A–C is false. Low coupling limits dependencies between subsystems, while high cohesion keeps related responsibilities together inside each subsystem. The first statement recommends this combination, the second identifies cohesion within the subsystem, and the third identifies coupling across subsystems. All three substantive statements are therefore true. The final alternative is explicitly the response for finding no false statement among those three, rather than a self-referential assertion about all choices. A incorrect Low coupling and high cohesion are the stated decomposition goals. B incorrect Cohesion concerns relatedness and dependencies among elements within a subsystem. C incorrect Coupling concerns dependencies between subsystems. D correct None of the substantive statements A–C is false, so this is the required response.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 89 · Q01593

D correct None of A–C is inherently excluded; all can be reused.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 90 · Q01594
records.text: Q01594 Question 90 SE43 SE25 SE23 A software design model states exact withdraw preconditions and balance equations but omits physical implementation detail. Compare it with an informal mathematical sketch that leaves those constraints unspecified and a fully detailed engine drawing. Which statement is FALSE for these particular models? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A This software model is less precise than the specified mathematical sketch. B This software model is more abstract than the fully detailed engine drawing. C A main role of this model is to represent the software designer’s ideas. D None of A–C is false. This software model is less precise than the specified mathematical sketch. The software model states exact preconditions and balance equations, whereas the informal mathematical sketch omits those constraints. It is therefore not less precise in the stated comparison, making A false. Omitting implementation detail makes it more abstract than the specified detailed engine drawing, and representing design ideas remains a legitimate purpose. These are scenario-specific judgments rather than universal rankings of all software and mathematical models. A correct Its exact constraints make the stated less-precise comparison false. B incorrect The software model omits implementation detail retained in the detailed drawing. C incorrect A design model can represent the designer’s ideas and decisions. D incorrect A is false, so the no-false-statements alternative is wrong.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 91 · Q01595
records.text: Q01595 Question 91 SE20 SE-S03 Which among the following designing models show sequence functional transformation done on inputs into outputs? Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A ER diagrams B DFD diagrams C Component diagrams D None of the choices are correct Data-flow diagrams. SE20 defines a DFD through data flows, stores and transformations from inputs to outputs. That matches the functional-transformation focus in the stem. An ER diagram focuses on domain data relationships, while a component diagram describes software components and dependencies. A DFD need not show detailed control timing merely because it depicts connected transformations. records.title: Software Engineering — Question 93 · Q01597
records.text: Q01597 Question 93 SE01 SE-S02 Which choice gives the most complete supported comparison of object-oriented model continuity and transitions between different development models? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Object-oriented development can use a consistent vocabulary of objects and classes across analysis and design. B Reuse and consistent models in object-oriented development can reduce development effort and duration on suitable projects. C Moving between different representations in a traditional phased approach can add translation complexity and errors. D All statements A–C are correct. All statements A–C are correct. A consistent object vocabulary across development stages can reduce errors from translating between unrelated models. Reuse and continuity can also reduce effort on suitable projects, while transitions between different representations can add complexity. These are potential benefits and risks, not guarantees that every OO project is shorter or every traditional project is worse. With those qualifications, all three substantive statements are supported, making their aggregate the most complete answer. A incorrect True but incomplete alone: a consistent object/class vocabulary can connect analysis and design. B incorrect True but incomplete alone: reuse and model continuity can reduce effort, without guaranteeing it. C incorrect True but incomplete alone: translation between different representations can add complexity or errors. D correct All three qualified statements hold, so the aggregate is the complete selection.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 94 · Q01598
records.text: Q01598 Question 94 SE33 Which of the following process model is concerned with how changes are incorporated in software? Separate artifact history and controlled changes from scheduling, collaboration benefits and automated execution. A Configuration management process B Change management process C Inspection management process D Project management process Change management process. SE33 assigns handling change requests, impact assessment, decisions, implementation and validation to change management. Configuration management coordinates versions and baselines of affected artifacts, which supports that work but is a different focus. Inspection and general project management also contribute, yet B specifically names how proposed software changes are evaluated and incorporated. A incorrect Configuration management maintains controlled versions and baselines rather than primarily deciding and incorporating requested changes. B correct Change management evaluates, approves/prioritizes, implements and validates proposed changes. C incorrect Inspection evaluates artifacts rather than defining the complete change-handling process. D incorrect Project management is broader than the specific process for handling software change requests.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 95 · Q01599
records.text: Q01599 Question 95 SE40 After a maintenance change request has been received, which is the earliest listed technical activity before release planning and implementation? Classify the motive for the change before its implementation: repair, environment, useful capability or reduced future risk. A Release planning B Change management C Impact analysis D Testing Impact analysis A typical evolution sequence is change request, impact analysis, release planning, implementation/testing and release. Once the request has arrived, impact analysis is the earliest listed technical step, assessing consequences before scheduling and implementation. Change management names the broader handling process rather than that next step. Release planning and testing occur later, so neither starts the specified post-request technical sequence. A incorrect Release planning follows impact analysis. B incorrect Change management is the overarching process. C correct Impact analysis is the first listed technical activity after the request. D incorrect Testing follows analysis, planning and implementation.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 96 · Q01600
records.text: Q01600 Question 96 SE29 A takes 5 days. B takes 3 days and C takes 4 days; both depend only on A and may run in parallel with sufficient resources. The project finishes when all three complete. What is its earliest duration? Write out the supplied quantities and dependency constraints. Compute and compare values under the stated metric, finish condition and assumptions. A 3 days B 4 days C 5 days D 9 days 9 days A completes at day five. B and C then start together, finishing at days eight and nine respectively. The project must wait for both required tasks, so its earliest finish is 5+max(3,4)=9 days. Adding all durations would ignore the permitted parallelism, while using eight days would count only the shorter A–B path and leave C incomplete. A incorrect Three counts B alone and omits its predecessor. B incorrect Four counts C alone and omits A. C incorrect Five stops after A, before both successors. D correct A followed by the longer parallel branch takes nine days.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 97 · Q01601
records.text: Q01601 Question 97 SE30 A project starts at day 0 and must finish at day 9. It consists of exactly two parallel paths, A → B and C → D. A and C have no predecessors, B depends only on A, D depends only on C, and the project finishes when both B and D are complete. Activity durations and early times are: A: duration 4 days, ES=0, EF=4; B: duration 5 days, ES=4, EF=9; C: duration 3 days, ES=0, EF=3; D: duration 6 days, ES=3, EF=9. What is the total slack (float) of Activity C? Write out the supplied quantities and dependency constraints. Compute and compare values under the stated metric, finish condition and assumptions.
