A 0 days B 1 day C 3 days D 6 days 0 days. Each complete path takes 9 days: A→B is 4+5 and C→D is 3+6. Working backward from day 9, D must start by day 3. Therefore C must finish by day 3 and start by day 0. C has LS=0 and ES=0, so total slack = LS−ES = 0 days (equivalently LF−EF = 3−3). A is correct. Delaying C would delay its successor D and the required project finish. A correct C has latest start 0 and earliest start 0, giving zero total slack. B incorrect A one-day delay would make the C→D path finish on day 10, beyond the day-9 finish. C incorrect C’s three-day duration is not its slack; a three-day delay would finish this path on day 12. D incorrect D’s six-day duration is not C’s slack; a six-day delay to C would finish the path on day 15.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 98 · Q01602
records.text: Q01602 Question 98 SE30 PERT considers which of the following time estimates for each activity? Write out the supplied quantities and dependency constraints. Compute and compare values under the stated metric, finish condition and assumptions. A Ideal time only B Worst-case time only C Three-point estimates (optimistic, most likely, pessimistic) D Average of historical data (if available) statement. Optimistic, most likely and pessimistic estimates. SE30 defines the classic PERT inputs as optimistic a, most-likely m and pessimistic b. These feed the weighted expected time (a+4m+b)/6 and an uncertainty estimate. Neither a single ideal or worst-case time nor an unqualified historical average supplies the three-point representation of uncertainty described by PERT. A incorrect An ideal estimate alone omits the most-likely and pessimistic values needed by classic PERT. B incorrect A worst-case estimate alone omits the optimistic and most-likely possibilities. C correct Classic PERT uses optimistic, most-likely and pessimistic duration estimates. D incorrect Historical data may inform estimates, but an average alone is not the PERT three-point input model.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 99 · Q01603
records.text: Q01603 Question 99 SE20 __________diagram is not supported by UML considering Data-driven modeling. Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A Activity B Data Flow Diagram (DFD) C State Chart D Component Data Flow Diagram (DFD) The traditional nine UML diagram types include activity, statechart and component diagrams; DFD is not a UML diagram type. Thus DFD is the offered non-UML notation. A incorrect Listed UML activity diagram. See PDF p. 101, 56, 55. B correct Not included among the module's nine UML diagrams on PDF p.47. See PDF p. 101, 56, 55. C incorrect Listed UML statechart diagram. See PDF p. 101, 56, 55. D incorrect Listed UML component diagram on PDF p.47. See PDF p. 101, 56, 55.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 100 · Q01604
records.text: Q01604 Question 100 SE07 What defining intention distinguishes a throwaway prototype from an evolutionary prototype? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A It involves successive steps B It involves just one task C The prototype is built with the idea that it will eventually be converted into final system D It is intended to be discarded after learning, rather than refined into the production system. It is intended to be discarded after learning, rather than refined into the production system. A throwaway prototype is built to learn about requirements, usability or feasibility and is discarded after serving that purpose. An evolutionary prototype is deliberately refined toward production. Either may involve successive steps, multiple tasks and varying development time, so those features do not define the difference. The artifact’s intended future, rather than how quickly it was built, distinguishes the approaches. A incorrect Either kind may involve successive steps. B incorrect Either kind can explore more than one task. C incorrect Intended refinement into the final system describes evolutionary prototyping. D correct Discard after learning is the defining throwaway intention.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 101 · Q01605
records.text: Q01605 Question 101 SE11 SE40 Which factors can cause requirements, scope or priorities to evolve during a project? Select all that apply. Classify the motive for the change before its implementation: repair, environment, useful capability or reduced future risk. A Changing needs of stakeholders B Advances in technology C Market dynamics D Lack of project funding Changing needs of stakeholders; Advances in technology; Market dynamics; Lack of project funding Stakeholder needs can change the services required, technology can introduce new constraints or opportunities, and market dynamics can alter business priorities. A funding shortfall can also reduce scope or force reprioritization. The note explicitly includes all four sources of change. Their effects depend on the project, but each can cause evolution, so none is an unconditional exception. A correct Changed stakeholder needs can revise required behavior. B correct Technology changes can alter constraints or opportunities. C correct Market changes can alter goals and priorities. D correct Funding limits can reduce scope or reorder requirements.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 102 · Q01606
records.text: Q01606 Question 102 SE36 Used when a large amount of testing is needed and the changes, while small, can affect many parts of the system Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A Preventive testing B Unit Testing C Regression Testing D Acceptance Testing Regression testing. The concern is that small changes may disturb other previously working parts of the software. Regression testing means checking unintended effects after change, rather than only confirming the defect. Such testing can span multiple levels and a large scope; the question describes its purpose, not the size of a unit or an acceptance decision. A incorrect Preventive testing is not the defined technique for detecting unintended effects of a specific software change. B incorrect Unit testing isolates a small component and does not by itself define the cross-system change-impact purpose. C correct Regression tests check whether changes unintentionally damage previously working behavior elsewhere. D incorrect Acceptance testing supports a user acceptance decision rather than specifically checking unintended change effects.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 103 · Q01607
records.text: Q01607 Question 103 SE37 The Decision table testing is a ----------? Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A White box Test Design Technique B Black Box Test Design Technique C Experience-based Test Design Technique D Grey Box Test Design Technique Black-box, specification-based testing. SE37 derives decision-table cases from combinations of specified conditions and resulting actions. This is specification-based rather than code-structure-based testing. It therefore belongs to black-box techniques. Experience or partial internal knowledge may help a tester, but they do not define the decision-table method or change its condition/action test basis. A incorrect White-box techniques derive tests from internal implementation structure rather than specified condition/action rules. B correct Decision tables derive cases from specified conditions and expected actions, making them black-box. C incorrect The technique has an explicit specification-based structure rather than being defined by tester experience. D incorrect Partial knowledge of internals is not required to derive decision-table test cases.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 104 · Q01608
records.text: Q01608 Question 104 SE37 Which of the following testing is related to the boundary value analysis? Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A White & black box testing B White-box testing C Black box testing D None of the above Black box testing Boundary testing is a special case of equivalence testing, a black-box testing technique. A incorrect The cited classification does not require both white and black knowledge. See PDF p. 149, 149. B incorrect Internal path knowledge is not required by input-class edges. See PDF p. 149, 149. C correct Follows by boundary being a special case of black-box equivalence testing. See PDF p. 149, 149. D incorrect The black-box option is supported. See PDF p. 149, 149.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 105 · Q01636
records.text: Q01636 Question 105 SE22 During initial design, a component with three unrelated responsibilities is split into three cohesive components. Which concept most specifically names the resulting decomposition into responsibility-based modules, rather than a general restructuring activity? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Refactoring B Modularization C Information hiding D Refinement Modularization Separating unrelated responsibilities into cohesive components is modularization: the design is divided into modules with focused purposes. Refactoring can describe behavior-preserving restructuring of an existing solution, but that broader activity is not the specific decomposition concept requested. Information hiding concerns concealed decisions behind interfaces, while refinement is a general elaboration concept. The stated split primarily establishes better module responsibility boundaries. A incorrect Refactoring names behavior-preserving restructuring rather than the specific module decomposition principle. B correct Modularization separates responsibilities into cohesive components. C incorrect No particular hidden implementation decision defines the stated split. D incorrect Refinement is broader than the specified module-boundary decomposition.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 106 · Q01637
records.text: Q01637 Question 106 SE25 Which design approach characteristically starts with available reusable components and assembles them into a larger system, rather than starting from high-level decomposition? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Both can be used B Top down C Bottom up D None of the choices are correct Bottom up Bottom-up design begins with existing components and assembles them into a larger solution. Top-down design instead starts with high-level structure and refines it, although it can still reuse components later. A hybrid combines the two directions, but the question asks which approach characteristically begins with the parts. Reuse by itself would not distinguish them; the explicit starting direction does. A incorrect A hybrid may use both directions but does not name the specifically described starting approach. B incorrect Top-down begins with high-level structure. C correct Bottom-up assembles existing components into the larger system. D incorrect Bottom-up directly matches, so none is false.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 107 · Q01638
records.text: Q01638 Question 107 SE23 Processes and threads are element types we find in ____________ software structure. Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Service software structure B Use software structure C Layer software structure D Concurrent software structure Concurrent software structure. SE23 explicitly puts processes and threads in concurrency views because they represent independently scheduled execution. Layer structure instead describes logical abstraction levels, while uses and service relations describe different dependencies or interfaces. Thus the concurrent structure is the offered category that directly matches these runtime execution elements. A incorrect Service structure emphasizes provided behavior or interfaces rather than processes and threads as execution elements. B incorrect Uses structure emphasizes dependencies rather than the concurrency entities named in the stem. C incorrect Layers organize logical abstraction levels rather than identifying independently scheduled execution units. D correct Concurrent structure models execution elements such as processes and threads.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 108 · Q01639
records.text: Q01639 Question 108 SE34 Which statements correctly describe verification and validation? Select all that apply. Distinguish process assurance from product evaluation, and compare specified obligations with actual stakeholder needs. A Verification consists of checking of documents/files and is performed by human where as validation consists of execution of program and is performed by computer. B All choices are correct C Validation assesses whether the built software meets intended stakeholder needs. D Verification refers to the set of activities that ensure software correctly implements the specific function. Validation assesses whether the built software meets intended stakeholder needs.; Verification refers to the set of activities that ensure software correctly implements the specific function. Verification checks whether specified functions and obligations have been implemented correctly. Validation checks whether the built product meets intended stakeholder needs. Both can use reviews, analysis and execution, so the claimed human-only versus computer-only split is false. Traceability can support these activities but does not alone establish satisfaction. If C states that validation checks whether software meets intended stakeholder needs, C and D are correct. A incorrect Both activities can use human reviews and execution; the exclusive split is false. B incorrect A is false, so all choices are not correct. C correct Validation assesses whether the product meets intended stakeholder needs. D correct Verification assesses correct implementation of specified obligations.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 109 · Q01640
records.text: Q01640 Question 109 SE24 Which architectural style is more suitable for if a system has to have successive transformation of streams of data? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Pipe and filter B Layered architecture C Client server architecture D All choices are correct Pipe and filter Pipe-and-filter architecture explicitly applies transformations to streams without user intervention. A correct Direct match to successive stream transformations. See PDF p. 126, 127, 124. B incorrect Layers organize levels, but the module does not identify them as the stream transformation style. See PDF p. 126, 127, 124. C incorrect Client/server organizes requests/services, not the requested transformation pipeline. See PDF p. 126, 127, 124. D incorrect Client/server is not equally established for the specific stream criterion. See PDF p. 126, 127, 124.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 110 · Q01641
records.text: Q01641 Question 110 SE34 Which of the following is quality measure for software? Distinguish process assurance from product evaluation, and compare specified obligations with actual stakeholder needs. A Reliability B Low cost C Productivity D Low development time Reliability Reliability is a software quality attribute characterized by behavior conformance and failure probability. A correct Explicit quality metric. See PDF p. 91, 140. B incorrect A project cost consideration rather than the offered software-behavior quality metric. See PDF p. 91, 140. C incorrect An output/effort process measure, not the specific product quality attribute. See PDF p. 91, 140. D incorrect A schedule measure rather than product reliability. See PDF p. 91, 140.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 111 · Q01642
records.text: Q01642 Question 111 SE30 A project manager is using PERT to estimate the duration of a project activity. The optimistic time (a) is 3 days, the most likely time (m) is 6 days, and the pessimistic time (b) is 15 days. What is the expected time (TE) for the activity? Write out the supplied quantities and dependency constraints. Compute and compare values under the stated metric, finish condition and assumptions. A 8 days B 10 days C 7 days D 9 days 7 days. Use TE=(a+4m+b)/6 from SE30 with a=3, m=6 and b=15. The numerator is 3+24+15=42, so TE=42/6=7 days. A simple average would give 8, but that discards the fourfold weighting of the most-likely estimate. The expected duration is an estimate, not a guaranteed actual completion time. A incorrect Eight is the simple mean of 3, 6 and 15, not the weighted PERT estimate. B incorrect Ten does not result from substituting the three given values into the PERT formula. C correct The weighted sum is 42 and dividing by six gives 7 days. D incorrect Nine does not equal the PERT weighted expected time for these estimates.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 112 · Q01643
records.text: Q01643 Question 112 SE29 Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a critical path in a CPM network diagram for software development? Write out the supplied quantities and dependency constraints. Compute and compare values under the stated metric, finish condition and assumptions. A Any delay in tasks on this path delays the entire project. B It identifies tasks with strict dependencies. C It represents the longest sequence of tasks. D It has the most slack (buffer time) compared to other paths. It has the most slack (buffer time) compared to other paths. The critical path is the chain determining project duration. The maximum-slack claim contradicts this: freely postponable tasks would not determine the earliest completion under a fixed network. A incorrect Delaying a controlling chain delays completion. See PDF p. 95. B incorrect Dependency order constrains the chain, though noncritical tasks can also have strict dependencies. See PDF p. 95. C incorrect The duration-determining chain is the longest required chain in the fixed-duration network. See PDF p. 95. D correct Maximum slack is inconsistent with a path that controls completion; no resource constraints are assumed. See PDF p. 95.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 113 · Q01644
records.text: Q01644 Question 113 SE29 A zero-duration start A leads to parallel paths B(5)→C(6) and D(8)→E(3), both ending at a zero-duration finish. Which critical-path statements are true? Select all that apply. Multiple critical paths are allowed. Write out the supplied quantities and dependency constraints. Compute and compare values under the stated metric, finish condition and assumptions. A A→B→C is a critical path with total duration 11 days. B A→D→E is a critical path with total duration 11 days. C A→D→E is a critical path with total duration 14 days. D A→B→C is a critical path with total duration 14 days. A→B→C is a critical path with total duration 11 days.; A→D→E is a critical path with total duration 11 days. The B–C branch totals 5+6=11 days and the D–E branch totals 8+3=11 days. With zero-duration start and finish, both are equally longest complete paths, so both are critical and the project duration is eleven days. There is no rule requiring a unique critical path. The alternatives using fourteen days miscalculate the corresponding branch totals. A correct The B–C branch totals eleven and is critical. B correct The D–E branch also totals eleven and is critical. C incorrect Eight plus three is eleven, not fourteen. D incorrect Five plus six is eleven, not fourteen.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 114 · Q01645
records.text: Q01645 Question 114 SE11 How can market dynamics influence the evolution of requirements? Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity. A By introducing new competitors with innovative products B By stabilizing existing market conditions C By reducing the need for frequent updates D By minimizing consumer demands By introducing new competitors with innovative products Product competition is a business risk. A competitor introducing a product can alter customer needs and thus motivate evolution. A correct Direct concrete competitive stimulus consistent with the risk table on PDF p.97. See PDF p. 96, 41. B incorrect Stabilization does not supply the change stimulus described. See PDF p. 96, 41. C incorrect Reduced updates does not explain new competitive requirements. See PDF p. 96, 41. D incorrect Minimizing demands is not the described competitive pressure. See PDF p. 96, 41.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 115 · Q01646
records.text: Q01646 Question 115 SE17 The static nature of the system is represented by which model? Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A Context Model B Data Model C Structural Model D Behavioral Model Structural Model The class/object model describes structure rather than temporal behavior; structural model is the offered general category. A incorrect Context concerns system boundaries, not all internal static structure. See PDF p. 51, 101. B incorrect Data is one aspect of structure but narrower than the overall static model. See PDF p. 51, 101. C correct Best matches the system's static classes/relationships. See PDF p. 51, 101. D incorrect Behavioral models describe interactions and changes over time. See PDF p. 51, 101.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 116 · Q01647
records.text: Q01647 Question 116 SE11 How does backward traceability help in requirements management? Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity. A By identifying redundant requirements B By mapping requirements to design documents C By ensuring that each requirement can be traced back to its source D By linking requirements to future project phases Trace each requirement back to its source and rationale. SE11 directs requirements backward to their source or rationale and forward to design, code and tests. Backward traceability therefore establishes why a requirement exists and where it came from. It can assist reviews, but redundancy detection is not its definition. Design mappings and future phases primarily describe the forward direction. A incorrect Redundancy detection can benefit from traceability, but it is not the definition of backward tracing. B incorrect Mapping toward design documents is forward traceability from the requirement. C correct Backward tracing establishes the source or rationale from which each requirement originated. D incorrect Links toward later project artifacts describe forward rather than backward traceability.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 117 · Q01648
records.text: Q01648 Question 117 SE39 SE11 SE28 Which artifact primarily serves project budgeting rather than specifying, planning or tracing tests? Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A Test strategy B Test Case C Project-wide cost estimate D Requirements Traceability Matrix [RTM] Project-wide cost estimate A test strategy describes how testing will be approached, a test case supplies actions or inputs with expected results, and an RTM links requirements to tests to support coverage and impact analysis. A project-wide cost estimate instead budgets the broader project. It may include testing costs and inform a test plan, but its primary purpose is project planning rather than specifying or tracing tests. The distractor uses that explicit distinction. A incorrect A test strategy defines the intended testing approach. B incorrect A test case specifies inputs or actions and expected results. C correct A project-wide cost estimate is a budgeting artifact, not primarily a testing specification or trace. D incorrect An RTM links requirements to tests and supports test coverage.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 118 · Q01649
records.text: Q01649 Question 118 SE34 Degree to which design specifications are followed in manufacturing the product is called Distinguish process assurance from product evaluation, and compare specified obligations with actual stakeholder needs. A Quality Control B None of the mentioned C Quality of conformance D Quality Assurance Quality of conformance. SE34 defines quality of conformance as following the design or specification. That is exactly the degree asked for in the stem. Quality control evaluates work products and quality assurance establishes and checks processes, but neither is the name of this conformance property. A conforming product may still follow an inadequate specification. A incorrect Quality control evaluates products rather than naming their degree of adherence to the design. B incorrect The exact property is offered as quality of conformance. C correct Conformance measures how faithfully the product follows its design or specification. D incorrect Quality assurance concerns processes and standards rather than the named degree of product conformance.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 119 · Q01650
records.text: Q01650 Question 119 SE36 Which of the below testing is related to Non-functional testing? Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A Performance Testing B Unit Testing C Black-box Testing D None of the choices are correct Performance Testing Performance testing explicitly checks nonfunctional requirements and additional design goals. A correct Directly tests nonfunctional qualities. See PDF p. 144. B incorrect A test level that can use several techniques and requirement types. See PDF p. 144. C incorrect A knowledge-based technique category, not specifically nonfunctional scope. See PDF p. 144. D incorrect The performance option is supported. See PDF p. 144.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 120 · Q00034B
records.text: Q00034B Question 120 SE25 First design the very high level structure of the system. Then gradually work down to detailed decisions about low-level constructs. Which design approach follows the given strategy? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Bottom-up B System design C Top-down D Hybrid Top-down design. The described direction starts with high-level structure and refines it into lower-level decisions. SE25 explicitly calls that top-down design. Bottom-up starts from existing components and assembles them; a hybrid combines directions. System design names a design activity or level, not the specific refinement direction requested by the question. A incorrect Bottom-up proceeds from components toward a larger structure, reversing the described direction. B incorrect System design names an architectural activity rather than the specific high-to-low refinement approach. C correct Top-down begins with high-level structure and progressively refines implementation details. D incorrect A hybrid combines both directions; the stem describes only top-down refinement.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 121 · SM0006
records.text: SM0006 Question 121 SE35 If you plan a software test to be done by clients to demonstrate that the system satisfies their requirements, which phase of software testing is appropriate? Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A Acceptance testing B Integration testing C System testing D Unit testing Acceptance testing Acceptance testing checks requirements against the project agreement and is performed by the client, matching both actor and purpose in the stem. A correct Direct client agreement/acceptance check. See PDF p. 145, 144. B incorrect Combines individually tested components. See PDF p. 145, 144. C incorrect Tests the complete system, but the specified client acceptance purpose identifies the narrower level. See PDF p. 145, 144. D incorrect Isolates building blocks, not client acceptance. See PDF p. 145, 144.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 122 · SM0027
records.text: SM0027 Question 122 SE36 Assume you make modification to your software. Then you want to make sure that the modification has not introduced new errors. Which software testing level is required? Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A Regression testing B Static testing C Beta testing D Dynamic testing Regression testing. Regression testing means checking for unintended effects after a software change. That matches the stated goal of finding newly introduced errors. Static and dynamic describe execution-related approaches rather than this change-focused purpose; beta describes an external-user test setting. Although the stem says level, regression is more accurately a testing purpose/type. A correct Regression testing checks whether a modification damages behavior that previously worked. B incorrect Static testing examines artifacts without execution and does not specifically define the change-impact purpose. C incorrect Beta testing involves external users in their environments rather than specifically checking every change's unintended effects. D incorrect Dynamic testing means executing software; it is broader than the regression purpose described.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 123 · SM0066
records.text: SM0066 Question 123 SE40 After deep analysis if your software requires major change to the architecture of the system, which strategy of software change should be applied? Classify the motive for the change before its implementation: repair, environment, useful capability or reduced future risk. A Preventative maintenance B Architectural transformation C Software reengineering D Software maintenance Architectural transformation. SE40 names major restructuring reengineering and identifies architectural transformation as the more specific term when the architecture itself changes. The stem expressly requires major architecture change, making B the best match. Maintenance and reengineering are broader categories, while preventive maintenance describes a motive and need not involve architectural restructuring. A incorrect Preventive maintenance reduces future risk but does not specifically denote a major architectural change. B correct Architectural transformation directly names the major architecture change required by the scenario. C incorrect Reengineering is a broader restructuring category; architectural transformation is more specific here. D incorrect Maintenance is the broad activity family rather than the particular architecture-change strategy.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 124 · SM0078
records.text: SM0078 Question 124 SE09 Which one of the following does NOT show a non-functional requirement of software systems? Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity. A Response time B Memory requirement C Reliability D Displaying information Displaying information Response time, memory constraints and reliability are nonfunctional qualities. Displaying information specifies a service rather than a quality bound. A incorrect Quantitative speed constraint. See PDF p. 65, 66, 127. B incorrect Space/resource constraint. See PDF p. 65, 66, 127. C incorrect Dependability quality. See PDF p. 65, 66, 127. D correct Observable function of presenting information. See PDF p. 65, 66, 127.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 125 · SM0079
records.text: SM0079 Question 125 SE28 Which one of the following is false about project planning stage? Distinguish the planning or organization goal from the tool or structure used to support it. Apply the stated project conditions. A Risk analysis is done during project planning B Preparing time schedule is done during project planning C Cost estimation is done during project planning D Project planning is a one-time task in software development life cycle Project planning is a one-time task in software development life cycle Planning is explicitly continuous from initial concept through delivery and revised as information changes. Therefore the one-time statement is false. A incorrect Risk analysis is in the plan structure. See PDF p. 90. B incorrect Schedule is in the project plan. See PDF p. 90. C incorrect Plans concern schedule and budget, so cost estimation belongs in planning. See PDF p. 90. D correct Direct contradiction of continuous revision. See PDF p. 90.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 126 · SM0090
records.text: SM0090 Question 126 SE01 Which phase of software development process refers to modification of software to reflect changing customer and market requirements? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Validation B Evolution C Development D Specification Evolution Changing existing software to meet new requirements is software evolution. A incorrect Checks conformance and customer expectations. See PDF p. 41. B correct Exact ongoing change activity. See PDF p. 41. C incorrect Produces a software implementation. See PDF p. 41. D incorrect Defines required services and constraints. See PDF p. 41.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 127 · SM0203
records.text: SM0203 Question 127 SE06 When is it appropriate to use the Spiral model? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Where business modeling is clearly understood and in use B When it is too risky to develop the overall system as one block C When requirements are understood early but can change during the project's life cycle D When requirements are unstable and constantly changing When major risks make one-block development unsafe. SE06 uses explicit risk assessment and reduction to distinguish spiral development from other iterative approaches. B directly states that risk makes a single overall commitment inappropriate. Changing or unstable requirements can occur in several processes and do not alone identify spiral; clear business modeling likewise does not supply the distinctive risk-based reason. A incorrect Understanding business modeling alone does not identify the need for risk-driven spiral cycles. B correct Important risks justify staged investigation and commitment rather than building the entire system in one block. C incorrect Possible requirement changes fit multiple processes and omit spiral's distinguishing explicit risk emphasis. D incorrect Unstable requirements alone do not uniquely select spiral over other adaptive approaches.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 128 · SM0235
records.text: SM0235 Question 128 SE22 A module is said to have logical cohesion if: Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A All the functions of the module are executed within the same time span B All elements of the module depend on their interface complexity C It performs a set of tasks that relate to each other very loosely D All elements of the module perform similar operations The module groups similar-category operations. SE22 defines logical cohesion as grouping operations in a similar category, often selected through a flag. D matches that shared logical category. A instead describes temporal cohesion, where operations occur at the same time. Interface complexity concerns dependencies, and a loose collection of unrelated tasks does not state the defining category-based relationship. A incorrect Grouping operations because they occur at the same time is temporal cohesion. B incorrect Interface complexity concerns dependencies and does not define logical cohesion inside a module. C incorrect Loose task relatedness alone does not establish the shared operation category defining logical cohesion. D correct Grouping similar-category operations is the defining feature of logical cohesion.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 129 · SM0244
records.text: SM0244 Question 129 SE22 Which software engineering principles are used to help reduce programming complexity? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Structured and unstructured B Object Oriented Design C Abstraction and Decomposition D Functional and Non-functional Abstraction and Decomposition Abstraction lets developers reason about objects at a higher level while decomposition divides a complex system into simpler subsystems; both directly control complexity. A incorrect Structured/unstructured names do not identify the paired techniques. See PDF p. 31, 118. B incorrect OO design employs these mechanisms but is the broader methodology. See PDF p. 31, 118. C correct Combines the two explicit complexity-management mechanisms. See PDF p. 31, 118. D incorrect These classify requirements, not techniques for decomposing a program. See PDF p. 31, 118.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 130 · SM0271
records.text: SM0271 Question 130 SE03 SE06 Which listed model organizes repeated cycles around risk assessment and can select prototyping, incremental or sequential activities as appropriate within those cycles? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Spiral model B Prototyping model C Classical Waterfall model D Iterative Waterfall model Spiral model Spiral development repeatedly identifies objectives, assesses and reduces risks, develops an appropriate result and plans further commitment. Its cycles can incorporate prototyping, incremental work or sequential activities according to the risks. The other listed models name particular exploratory or staged organizations rather than this risk-driven choice framework. This explains the conventional general-model reading without claiming that every process is formally a specialization of spiral. A correct Spiral selects cycle work through risk assessment. B incorrect Prototyping is one learning activity that a spiral cycle may use. C incorrect Classical waterfall is a planned sequential organization. D incorrect Iterative waterfall adds feedback without defining the risk-driven cycle.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 131 · SM0293
records.text: SM0293 Question 131 SE10 Which system requirement specification includes human-computer interface issues from the system? Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity. A Functional requirements of the system B Non-functional requirements of the system C Goals of implementation D System Testing Non-functional requirements of the system User-interface look/feel and user expertise are explicitly nonfunctional concerns, under user interface and human factors. Particular interaction services can still be functional; the question is read as interface quality issues. A incorrect Specific interface functions can be functional, but this is not the broad human-factor quality category. See PDF p. 78, 66. B correct Explicitly includes user interface and human factors. See PDF p. 78, 66. C incorrect Implementation goals are not the stated requirement category. See PDF p. 78, 66. D incorrect Testing is an activity, not a requirement category. See PDF p. 78, 66.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 132 · SM0294
records.text: SM0294 Question 132 SE03 In a classical waterfall model, which phase precedes the design phase? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Requirements analysis and specification B Maintenance C Feasibility study D Coding and unit testing Requirements analysis and specification The sequential waterfall establishes the requirements specification before deriving the software design from the SRS. A correct The immediate input and preceding phase. See PDF p. 15, 18, 26. B incorrect Occurs after delivery and operation. See PDF p. 15, 18, 26. C incorrect A prior viability activity, not the immediate specification input to design. See PDF p. 15, 18, 26. D incorrect Implements a design after it has been produced. See PDF p. 15, 18, 26.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 133 · SM0300
records.text: SM0300 Question 133 SE06 When to use the Spiral Model? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Where business modeling is clearly understood and in use. B When it is too risky to develop the overall system as one block. C When requirements are understood in the early stages but can change during the project's life cycle. D When requirements are unstable and constantly changing. When major risks make whole-system development in one block unsafe. A spiral cycle identifies objectives, assesses and reduces important risks, develops an appropriate result and plans further commitment. B directly supplies the risk-based reason for choosing that process. Clear business understanding, potentially changing requirements and continuously unstable requirements do not alone distinguish spiral from other staged or adaptive models. The explicit risk is the decisive feature. A incorrect Clear business modeling does not by itself create a reason for risk-driven spiral development. B correct Risk makes staged assessment and commitment preferable to building the whole system in one block. C incorrect Requirements that may change fit several processes and do not specifically identify spiral. D incorrect Unstable requirements alone do not distinguish spiral without its explicit risk-analysis need.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 134 · SS096
records.text: SS096 Question 134 SE28 The process that generates activities such as project schedule, cost estimations and work breakdown structures is described as: Distinguish the planning or organization goal from the tool or structure used to support it. Apply the stated project conditions. A Project Executing B Project Initiating C Project Closing D Project Planning Project Planning The project plan explicitly sets out resources, work breakdown and schedule and concerns budget; these are outputs of project planning. A incorrect Execution carries out planned tasks. See PDF p. 90, 95. B incorrect Initiation frames a project but does not best identify this full planning output set. See PDF p. 90, 95. C incorrect Closing concerns completion/acceptance, not scheduling future work. See PDF p. 90, 95. D correct Directly corresponds to the listed plan contents. See PDF p. 90, 95.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 135 · SS103
records.text: SS103 Question 135 SE05 Which slogan is against the agile method philosophy? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Working software over comprehensive documentation B Following a plan over responding to changes C Individuals and interactions over processes and tools D Customer collaboration over contract negotiation Following a plan over responding to changes Agile values working software, people interacting, customer collaboration and responsiveness to change over the respective items on the other side of each comparison. It still recognizes value in documentation, tools, contracts and plans. The reversed preference for following a plan over responding to changes conflicts with this ordering. The other three alternatives retain the Agile ordering and therefore are not slogans against its philosophy. A incorrect This preserves the Agile preference for working software while still valuing documentation. B correct This reverses Agile’s preference for responding to change over following a plan. C incorrect This preserves the preference for individuals and interactions. D incorrect This preserves the preference for customer collaboration.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 136 · SS105
records.text: SS105 Question 136 SE11 What would be the most likely consequence if every software stakeholder were rushing to be approved for their requirements without discussing with other stakeholders? Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity. A Results in excess requirement B Attains the project schedule C Requirements become unambiguous D Leads to conflicting requirement Leads to conflicting requirement JAD brings stakeholders together to negotiate a mutually acceptable specification; without discussion, incompatible local demands can remain unresolved. A incorrect Excess scope is possible but not the most direct consequence of unnegotiated differences. See PDF p. 81, 68. B incorrect Rushing approvals does not prove the schedule is met. See PDF p. 81, 68. C incorrect Clarity is not obtained automatically by separate approvals. See PDF p. 81, 68. D correct Competing viewpoints can yield contradictions, precisely what consensus and consistency checks address. See PDF p. 81, 68.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 137 · SS113
records.text: SS113 Question 137 SE31 If the estimate for total discounted benefits for a project is Birr 120,000 and total discounted cost is Birr 100,000, what is the estimated return on investment (ROI) percentage? Write out the supplied quantities and dependency constraints. Compute and compare values under the stated metric, finish condition and assumptions. A 30% B 12% C 10% D 20% 20%. The benefits and costs are already discounted to a common date, so use SE31 directly: ROI=(120000−100000)/100000×100%. Net benefit is Birr 20000, and dividing by Birr 100000 gives 0.20, or 20%. Dividing total benefits by costs would report a benefit-cost ratio, not the net return percentage requested. A incorrect Thirty percent does not follow from the given net benefit and cost. B incorrect Twelve percent is not 20000 divided by 100000 as a percentage. C incorrect Ten percent understates the calculated net return of twenty percent. D correct Net benefit is Birr 20000, which is 20% of the Birr 100000 cost.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 138 · SS114
records.text: SS114 Question 138 SE23 In a closed layered architecture with A,B,C,D from top to bottom, a pair (X,Y) means X directly calls Y. Calls may go only to the immediately lower layer. Which pair obeys this policy? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A (A,C) B (D,A) C (A,B) D (C,B) (A,B) Closed layering permits a layer to call only the immediately lower layer. A→B follows that adjacency and direction, so C is valid. A→C skips B and violates the closed policy even though it would be possible in a suitably open architecture. D→A and C→B point upward, which the stipulated dependency policy also forbids. The ordered pair is interpreted as caller then callee. A incorrect A→C skips B. B incorrect D→A points upward. C correct A→B calls the immediately lower layer. D incorrect C→B points upward.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 139 · SS124
records.text: SS124 Question 139 SE39 Which listed roles should document a fault if they discover it during development? Select all that apply. Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A Tester B Requirement engineer C Developer D Scrum master Tester; Requirement engineer; Developer; Scrum master Anyone discovering a fault should record it with enough evidence to reproduce and assess it. Testers often coordinate reporting, but requirements engineers, developers and Scrum masters should also document faults they discover. The report should identify the relevant environment, steps and expected versus actual behavior. Therefore all four roles meet the stated discoverer-based responsibility rather than only the dedicated tester. A correct A tester discovering a fault should record it. B correct A requirements engineer discovering a fault should record it. C correct A developer discovering a fault should record it. D correct A Scrum master discovering a fault should record it.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 140 · SS127
records.text: SS127 Question 140 SE18 SE-S02 Select the one that is not correct related to generalization in system modeling. Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A Ingeneralization, the attributes and operations associated with higher-level classes are also associated with the lower-level classes B Facilitate easy modification of data C The higher-level classes are more specific than the lower-level classes by adding specific attributes and operations D Common information will be maintained in one place The higher-level classes are more specific than the lower-level classes by adding specific attributes and operations Generalization puts common features in more general superclasses; subclasses add or override details and are more specialized. C reverses the direction. A incorrect Inherited attributes and methods are available on subclasses. See PDF p. 104. B incorrect Common definitions can reduce duplicated modification; the wording is broad. See PDF p. 104. C correct Higher-level classes are more general, not more specific. See PDF p. 104. D incorrect Consolidating common features in a superclass removes redundancy. See PDF p. 104.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 141 · SS135
records.text: SS135 Question 141 SE34 Which statement accurately describes the main evidential goal of software testing within quality assurance? Distinguish process assurance from product evaluation, and compare specified obligations with actual stakeholder needs. A To achieve project timelines and deadlines. B To monitor the entire SDLC. C To generate software requirement and design documentation. D To assess conformance to specified requirements, reveal defects and increase confidence through evidence. To assess conformance to specified requirements, reveal defects and increase confidence through evidence. Testing evaluates behavior against required results, revealing failures and increasing confidence in conformance. It does not generally guarantee correctness over every possible input or environment. Meeting schedules and monitoring the whole lifecycle are broader management or assurance activities, while requirements and design documentation usually form part of the test basis. Option D states the supported evidential purpose without promising certainty. A incorrect Timelines are a project-management goal rather than the test evidence goal. B incorrect Whole-lifecycle monitoring is broader assurance/control work. C incorrect Requirements and design documents are typically inputs to testing. D correct Tests assess conformance, reveal defects and increase confidence.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 142 · SS137
records.text: SS137 Question 142 SE24 What component hides the distinction or boundaries between various microservices from end-client application? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Alayered system B API gateway C API logging D API proxy API gateway. SE24 defines an API gateway as one entry point that routes or combines service calls and hides service boundaries from clients. That directly matches the stated role. Logging records activity and a layered system describes broader organization; a generic proxy label alone does not establish the multi-service routing and composition role given in the note. A incorrect Layering organizes abstraction levels rather than naming this single microservice-facing entry component. B correct An API gateway hides service boundaries behind a unified entry point and routes or combines requests. C incorrect API logging records activity rather than routing clients across hidden service boundaries. D incorrect A generic proxy forwards requests; the note names the broader multi-service entry-point role an API gateway.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 143 · SS139
records.text: SS139 Question 143 SE23 SE21 Which question is outside the architectural abstraction level and instead asks for every source-level execution detail? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Which architectural organization is best for delivering the functional requirements? B How the system will be distributed across a number of cores or processors C Which variable is assigned at every individual source-code execution step? D Which architectural patterns or styles to use Which variable is assigned at every individual source-code execution step? Architecture addresses major organization, responsibilities, allocation and style decisions. Selecting an arrangement for required behavior, mapping work to processors and choosing patterns are therefore valid architectural concerns. Enumerating every source-level assignment on every execution step is implementation-level tracing, beyond the abstraction of architecture documentation. Option C supplies that genuine exception while preserving the question’s comparison of architectural and detailed concerns. A incorrect Organization supporting required behavior is architectural. B incorrect Processor allocation is an architectural concern. C correct Every source-level execution step exceeds the architectural abstraction. D incorrect Style and pattern selection is architectural.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 144 · SS144
records.text: SS144 Question 144 SE21 Select the one that is not related with the purpose of properly documenting software architectures Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A to Know how the system is organized and interoperate B For Stakeholder communication C For critical system design decisions D To easily figure out the source code flow To easily figure out the source code flow The SDD documents goals, subsystem organization, mapping and interfaces to support teams and architecture decisions. Detailed source-code control flow is a lower-level implementation concern than the document's architectural control-flow mechanisms. A incorrect Subsystem decomposition and interfaces expose organization/interoperation. See PDF p. 130. B incorrect Defines interfaces between development teams and supports communication. See PDF p. 130. C incorrect Serves as reference when architecture-level decisions are revisited. See PDF p. 130. D correct Detailed source-level flow is not the purpose of an architecture description; global control mechanisms may still be documented. See PDF p. 130.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 145 · SS147
records.text: SS147 Question 145 SE38 Given the following fragment of code, how many tests are required for 100% decision coverage? if width > length then biggest_dimension = width if height > width then biggest_dimension = height end_if else biggest_dimension = length if height > length then biggest_dimension = height end_if end_if Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A ona. 4 B 6 C Ole 2 D 3 Four tests for 100% decision coverage. There are three decisions: width>length and one separate height comparison inside each outer branch. Covering both inner outcomes requires two tests with outer true and two with outer false. For example (w,l,h)=(3,2,4),(3,2,1),(2,3,4),(2,3,1) covers all outcomes. One execution cannot visit both outer branches, so two or three tests cannot suffice; six are unnecessary. A correct Four tests cover true/false of the inner decision on each of the two outer branches. B incorrect Six can cover the decisions, but four suffice; it is not the required minimum. C incorrect Two cover the outer decision but cannot cover both outcomes of both separate inner decisions. D incorrect Three leave at least one inner decision outcome uncovered because each outer branch needs two tests.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 146 · SS148
records.text: SS148 Question 146 SE05 Using classical up-front waterfall planning, usable incremental additions and timeboxed adaptive Agile, which lifecycle statements are NOT true? Select all that apply. Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Ina waterfall life cycle, the project scope, time, and cost are determined in the early phases of the life cycle B Inagile life cycle the project scope is generally determined early in the project life cycle, but time and cost estimates are routinely modified C Inanincremental life cycle, the deliverable is produced through a series of iterations that successively add functionality within a predetermined time frame D Inagile life cycles, the project scope cannot be outlined and agreed before the start of iteration. Inagile life cycle the project scope is generally determined early in the project life cycle, but time and cost estimates are routinely modified; Inagile life cycles, the project scope cannot be outlined and agreed before the start of iteration. Classical waterfall establishes planned baselines early, and incremental work adds functionality in successive deliveries. Agile instead adapts content while its timeboxes tend to remain fixed, so B misstates the general organizing pattern. D is also false because Agile permits outlining and agreeing scope before an iteration; planning continues as evidence changes. Adaptation does not mean that scope discussion or early agreement is prohibited. A incorrect Early planned baselines fit classical waterfall. B correct The claim reverses the timeboxed/adaptive-content characterization. C incorrect Successive additions of usable functionality fit incremental delivery. D correct Agile permits scope discussion and agreement before an iteration.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 147 · SS151
records.text: SS151 Question 147 SE27 Which design pattern is used to restore the state of an object to its previous state? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Iterator pattern B Observer pattern C Momento pattern D Visitor pattern Memento, printed as Momento. SE27 explicitly identifies Memento as storing and restoring state while hiding representation, and notes that Momento in this question bank is a spelling error for Memento. That makes C the intended pattern name. Iterator traverses a collection and Observer notifies subscribers; neither supplies the state-snapshot restoration responsibility asked for here. A incorrect Iterator traverses elements rather than storing a restorable snapshot of object state. B incorrect Observer notifies subscribers about changes rather than restoring an earlier object state. C correct Momento refers here to Memento, the state capture-and-restoration pattern. D incorrect Visitor is not the state-snapshot restoration pattern; the note assigns that role to Memento.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 148 · SS153
records.text: SS153 Question 148 SE32 Which of the following shows the five stages in Tuckman's model of team development, in sequential order? Distinguish the planning or organization goal from the tool or structure used to support it. Apply the stated project conditions. A forming, storming, performing, norming, and adjourning B norming, forming, storming, performing, and adjourning C storming, forming, norming, performing, and adjourning D forming, storming, norming, performing, and adjourning Forming → storming → norming → performing → adjourning. SE32 lists orientation first, then conflict, development of norms, effective performance and closure. Their stage names are forming, storming, norming, performing and adjourning. D preserves that order. The other alternatives either put performance before norms or move orientation after later stages, contradicting the taught sequence. A incorrect It places performing before norming, reversing the stated development sequence. B incorrect It starts with norming before the initial forming and storming stages. C incorrect It places storming before the initial forming stage. D correct It matches the taught progression from orientation through conflict, norms, performance and closure.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 149 · SS154
records.text: SS154 Question 149 SE34 Which one of the following is not among the purposes of software testing? Distinguish process assurance from product evaluation, and compare specified obligations with actual stakeholder needs. A Requesting more design and implementation time B Identifying shortcomings C Improving product acceptance D Enhancing reliability Requesting more design and implementation time Testing detects faults, supports client acceptance and enables corrections that improve reliability. Requesting more implementation time is a possible project consequence, not a testing purpose. A correct A request for time is not the fault-detection or confidence purpose. See PDF p. 140, 140, 145. B incorrect Identifying faults/shortcomings is the explicit goal. See PDF p. 140, 140, 145. C incorrect Client acceptance is checked through acceptance tests. See PDF p. 140, 140, 145. D incorrect Fault discovery permits corrections and increased reliability. See PDF p. 140, 140, 145.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 150 · SS155
records.text: SS155 Question 150 SE33 SE39 During which listed activity should the test plan define configuration-management procedures alongside objectives, resources and schedule, before those procedures are applied during execution? Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A During test execution B During test planning C During test closing D During test initiation During test planning Test planning specifies intended work, objectives, resources and schedule; configuration-management procedures should be defined early as part of that preparation. They then apply throughout testing to preserve reproducible builds, data and environments. Execution and closing use those procedures rather than being their exclusive establishment point. Initiation may set context, but the question specifically asks for the activity that defines them in the test plan. A incorrect Execution applies the planned procedures to tested versions. B correct Test planning defines procedures with the other planned work. C incorrect Closing preserves final artifacts under established control. D incorrect Initiation sets context rather than the specified test-plan definition activity.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 151 · SS156
records.text: SS156 Question 151 SE43 "The system architecture should be designed using fine-grain, self-contained components. Producers of data should be separated from consumers and shared data structures should be avoided". For which requirement this architecture description applies? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Performance B Availability C Maintainability D Security Maintainability Independent self-contained subsystems and avoiding shared attribute data reduce coupling, limiting the impact of future changes. That directly serves maintainability. A incorrect Fine-grained separation can carry overhead and is not primarily the stated speed optimization. See PDF p. 120, 118. B incorrect Availability requires continuity/failure treatment beyond component separation alone. See PDF p. 120, 118. C correct Matches minimizing change impact through low coupling. See PDF p. 120, 118. D incorrect Security needs explicit access-control policy; independence alone does not establish it. See PDF p. 120, 118.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 152 · SS159
records.text: SS159 Question 152 SE38 Which of the following is a process of selecting program paths in such a manner that certain branches (i.e., outgoing edges of nodes) of a control flow graph are covered by the execution of those paths? Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A Branch boundary B Branch coverage C Branch control D Branch expansion Branch coverage. The stem explicitly defines branches as outgoing control-flow edges. SE38 identifies branch coverage as counting exercised control-flow edges under the declared convention. This differs from merely counting executed statements or evaluating decision outcomes. Branch boundary, branch control and branch expansion are not the coverage criterion described by selecting paths that exercise graph edges. A incorrect Branch boundary is not the defined edge-coverage criterion in the note. B correct Branch coverage measures whether control-flow edges are exercised by the selected test paths. C incorrect Branch control is not the name of the specified structural coverage measure. D incorrect Branch expansion does not name the outgoing-edge coverage criterion described.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 153 · SS161
records.text: SS161 Question 153 SE40 Which of the following is the correct sequence that will be followed during software evolution process? Classify the motive for the change before its implementation: repair, environment, useful capability or reduced future risk. A Change request, release planning, change implementation, impact analysis, system release B Change request, impact analysis, release planning, change implementation, system release C Impact analysis, Change request, change implementation, release planning, system release D Change request, impact analysis, change implementation, release planning, system release Change request → impact analysis → release planning → implementation → release. SE40 gives the sequence directly. A requested change is analyzed before commitment to a release, then planned, implemented and tested, and finally released. B preserves those dependencies. The alternatives analyze consequences too late, begin analysis before a request exists, or implement before release planning. Implementation here includes the testing work omitted from the abbreviated options. A incorrect It postpones impact analysis until after implementation, too late to guide planning and commitment. B correct It preserves request, analysis, planning, implementation/testing and release in the taught order. C incorrect It begins impact analysis before identifying a change request and implements before release planning. D incorrect It places implementation before release planning instead of planning the analyzed change first.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 154 · SS162
records.text: SS162 Question 154 SE20 SE19 SE17 Which of the following UML element is wrongly applied? Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A Use case diagram represents an interaction with the system B Sequence diagram shows the sequence of interactions required to complete some operation C An activity diagram primarily specifies the persistent lifecycle states of one object and the event-triggered transitions between those states. D Class diagram shows the object classes in a system and their relation An activity diagram primarily specifies the persistent lifecycle states of one object and the event-triggered transitions between those states. Use-case diagrams summarize actor goals, sequence diagrams order interactions across participants, and class diagrams describe static types and relationships. An activity diagram models workflow and action/control flow. Persistent lifecycle states and event-triggered transitions of a particular object instead call for a state machine. The revised third statement makes that mismatch explicit; the original generic event wording was too broad because activities can also respond to events. A incorrect Use-case diagrams summarize external roles and system goals/interactions. B incorrect Sequence diagrams show ordered participant interactions. C correct The specified lifecycle-state behavior belongs to a state machine rather than an activity workflow. D incorrect Class diagrams describe static classes and their relationships.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 155 · SS163
records.text: SS163 Question 155 SE11 Select the wrong statement regarding traceability in software development projects. Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity. A Traceability shows the dependency among two or more requirements if any B Requirements should be linked to the respective stakeholder who generated them D Every design element(component) should be linked back to the requirement G Traceability traces the overall cost and schedule of every activity in the requirement Traceability traces the overall cost and schedule of every activity in the requirement Traceability records where requirements came from, how requirements depend on one another, and how each requirement is realized and checked in design, code and tests. Source links support rationale, and forward or backward links support change-impact analysis. A cost-and-schedule ledger instead belongs to project planning and control. It can reference requirements, but recording every activity’s cost and schedule is not the definition of requirements traceability. A incorrect Dependency links among requirements are a valid traceability relation. B incorrect Source or stakeholder links record a requirement’s provenance. D incorrect Design-to-requirement links support realization and impact analysis. G correct An overall activity cost-and-schedule ledger is project control, not the defining traceability relation.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 156 · SS164
records.text: SS164 Question 156 SE43 Which named prioritization heuristic suggests that a small subset of causes may account for much of the observed impact, often summarized as 80/20? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Pareto principle B Pairwise principle C Partition principle D Parametric principle Pareto principle Pareto’s 80/20 idea is a prioritization heuristic: a relatively small set of causes may account for a large share of observed impact. It encourages examining evidence to focus improvement effort. It does not promise that exactly one fifth of the effort fixes exactly four fifths of all defects. The revised question asks for this named heuristic, so the other principle names do not identify the rule described. A correct Pareto names the small-subset/large-impact heuristic often expressed as 80/20. B incorrect This is not the name of the described 80/20 prioritization heuristic. C incorrect Partitioning does not name the described concentration-of-impact heuristic. D incorrect Parametric reasoning does not name the described concentration-of-impact heuristic.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 157 · SS166
records.text: SS166 Question 157 SE05 SE06 A business expects changing requirements and organizes development around repeated customer collaboration and incremental replanning; risk-analysis cycles are not its organizing priority. Which offered approach most directly matches these priorities? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Code and run B Spiral model C Agile development method D Water fall model Agile development method The scenario’s organizing emphasis is repeated customer collaboration and adaptive planning as needs change, which identifies Agile. Spiral can also accommodate change, but organizes its cycles around explicit risk assessment and reduction. Classical waterfall relies more heavily on stable requirements and planned phase commitments. Code-and-run lacks the described disciplined planning and feedback organization. Changing requirements alone would not uniquely determine a process, so the added priorities matter. A incorrect Code-and-run does not supply the disciplined adaptive planning and feedback organization stated. B incorrect Spiral is specifically organized around risk assessment and reduction rather than the stated primary emphasis. C correct Agile makes customer collaboration and adaptation central to planning. D incorrect Classical waterfall is a poorer fit for repeated replanning of evolving needs.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 158 · SS168
records.text: SS168 Question 158 SE10 Which statement is correct about the differences between functional and non-functional requirements? Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity. A Functional requirements are the services the system provide while non-functional requirements are constraints on the services or functions offered by the system B Functional requirements are decided by the customer while non-functional requirements are decided by developers C Both are the same most of the time and only vary under certain contexts D Unlike functional requirement, nonfunctional requirements are stable Functional requirements are the services the system provide while non-functional requirements are constraints on the services or functions offered by the system Required interactions are distinct from user-visible quality constraints such as response time and accuracy; users and clients participate in defining both. A correct Correct service-versus-constraint distinction. See PDF p. 65, 66, 78. B incorrect Both types involve users/clients and developers; they are not separated by who decides. See PDF p. 65, 66, 78. C incorrect The module explicitly distinguishes their subject matter. See PDF p. 65, 66, 78. D incorrect No immunity to changing stakeholder needs is stated for nonfunctional requirements. See PDF p. 65, 66, 78.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 159 · SS169
records.text: SS169 Question 159 SE39 Which paired activity assesses requirements/system testability and then designs test cases and expected results? Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A Test analysis and requirements B Test analysis and design C Test analysis and planning D Test analysis and Implementation Test analysis and design Test analysis examines the test basis, identifies what can be tested and evaluates testability. Test design then specifies how to test it through cases and expected results. The analysis-and-design pair therefore covers both responsibilities. Requirements work, planning and implementation are relevant elsewhere, but do not replace case design: planning addresses resources and scope, while implementation prepares data, scripts and the environment. A incorrect Requirements work does not supply the requested case-design half. B correct Analysis assesses testability and design specifies cases and expected results. C incorrect Planning addresses intended work, resources and schedule rather than case design. D incorrect Implementation prepares scripts, data and environment rather than being the design half.
