records.title: Software Engineering — Question 161 · SS176
records.text: SS176 Question 161 SE31 In software risk management, accepting risk happening but don not do anything is known as: Write out the supplied quantities and dependency constraints. Compute and compare values under the stated metric, finish condition and assumptions. A Risk transfer B Risk Retention C Risk Reduction D Risk avoidance Risk retention, specifically passive acceptance. SE31 distinguishes removing a risk, reducing it, transferring consequences and retaining or accepting it. It explicitly says passive acceptance may take no action. The stem describes recognizing the risk and allowing it to remain without action, so retention matches. The other responses all involve a deliberate change to the risk or its consequences. A incorrect Transfer assigns consequences contractually rather than simply keeping the risk without action. B correct Retention or passive acceptance keeps the risk and may involve no immediate action. C incorrect Reduction actively lowers likelihood or impact instead of merely accepting exposure. D incorrect Avoidance changes the plan to remove the risk rather than allowing it to remain.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 162 · SS182
records.text: SS182 Question 162 SE04 SE06 Which software process model will you use if you want to deliver different functionalities (modules) of the software product that have different priority at different time? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Waterfall model B Spiral model C Incremental model D Linear model Incremental model Incremental development delivers prioritized functionality in usable stages. Earlier increments provide value while later increments add further capability. This is a delivery organization, distinct from a strict single-pass waterfall sequence. Spiral cycles are organized around risks and may use increments, but risk-driven development is not the specific name of the stated delivery strategy. A generic linear sequence also does not describe prioritized usable subsets. A incorrect Classical waterfall organizes phases before the principal usable delivery. B incorrect Spiral is defined by risk-driven cycles, even when an increment is produced. C correct Incremental development names the successive delivery of usable functionality. D incorrect A linear model does not name prioritized delivery of separate usable subsets.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 163 · SS184
records.text: SS184 Question 163 SE31 Which of the following is a resource optimization techniques in which start and finish dates are adjusted based on resource constraints with the goal of balancing the demand for resources with the available supply? Write out the supplied quantities and dependency constraints. Compute and compare values under the stated metric, finish condition and assumptions. A Resource smoothing B Responsibility assignment matrix C Resource leveling D Resource grouping Resource leveling. SE31 defines resource leveling as adjusting dates to respect resource availability, potentially changing the project finish. That matches balancing resource demand against supply by moving starts and finishes. Smoothing instead works within available float and schedule constraints. A responsibility matrix assigns ownership, and resource grouping is not the defined date-adjustment technique. A incorrect Smoothing uses available float while retaining schedule constraints rather than generally leveling against availability. B incorrect A responsibility assignment matrix maps work to owners rather than adjusting task dates for resource capacity. C correct Resource leveling changes dates to balance required resources against available supply. D incorrect Resource grouping is not the defined schedule-adjustment method described by the stem.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 164 · SS190
records.text: SS190 Question 164 SE25 Identify the design principle that does not apply to software systems Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A design should be structured to accommodate change B design should exhibit uniformity and integration C design should be reinventing the wheel from scratch D design should be traceable to the analysis model design should be reinventing the wheel from scratch Reusable classes, controlled change and traceability to requirements support software engineering. B incorrect Consistent interfaces and integrated structures support the system, though this exact slogan is not quoted. See PDF p. 32, 120, 70. records.title: Software Engineering — Question 166 · AM0002
records.text: AM0002 Question 166 SE25 Which design principle suggests that software components should have a single, well-defined responsibility? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) principle B SOLID principle C KISS (Keep It Simple, Stupid) principle D YAGNI (You Ain't Gonna Need It) principle Single Responsibility, within SOLID. SE25 includes Single Responsibility among the SOLID principles. That principle assigns a component one well-defined responsibility. DRY limits duplicated knowledge, KISS avoids unnecessary complexity and YAGNI avoids speculative work. Those can complement focused responsibilities, but none is the named principle directly described by the question. A incorrect DRY limits duplication of knowledge rather than specifically assigning one responsibility per component. B correct SOLID includes the Single Responsibility principle that the stem describes. C incorrect KISS favors simplicity, a different design concern from the specific single-responsibility rule. D incorrect YAGNI avoids speculative work rather than defining responsibility boundaries.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 167 · AM0003
records.text: AM0003 Question 167 SE05 Which of the following is an agile development methodology? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Waterfall model B Scrum C V-model D Spiral model Scrum. SE05 presents Scrum through timeboxed Sprints, a Sprint Goal and a usable Increment, in the Agile context. Waterfall and the V-model organize planned stages and corresponding tests, while spiral is defined by risk-driven cycles. Therefore Scrum is the specifically Agile approach among the listed alternatives; iteration alone does not make every process Scrum. A incorrect Classical waterfall organizes planned phases rather than the Agile Scrum approach described. B correct Scrum is the Agile framework using Sprints and usable Increments. C incorrect The V-model pairs development stages with test levels rather than being the listed Agile framework. D incorrect Spiral is risk driven and is not the specifically Agile methodology named among these choices.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 168 · AM0004
records.text: AM0004 Question 168 SE04 SE06 SE05 A team delivers small usable capabilities, replans the next work with customers and treats adaptation as a central value rather than organizing cycles around risk analysis. Which broad approach best fits? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Waterfall model B Agile methodology C Prototype model D Spiral model Agile methodology The team adds small usable capabilities and repeatedly replans with customers. Agile makes this combination of working results, customer participation and adaptation central. A prototype’s immediate purpose is learning about requirements or feasibility; a spiral cycle is organized around risk reduction. Classical waterfall instead emphasizes planned phase commitments. Increments by themselves can occur in several processes, so the collaboration and planning priorities establish the intended comparison. A incorrect Classical waterfall does not make repeated adaptive replanning its organizing emphasis. B correct Agile combines working increments with ongoing customer collaboration and adaptation. C incorrect Prototyping primarily explores uncertainty rather than naming this ongoing delivery-and-planning organization. D incorrect Spiral’s defining emphasis is risk analysis and reduction.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 169 · AM0005
records.text: AM0005 Question 169 SE36 Which software testing technique focuses on finding defects by executing the software without knowledge of its internal structure? A incorrect Requires code/data-structure knowledge for path selection. See PDF p. 149, 149. B correct Matches behavior testing without internal-structure knowledge. See PDF p. 149, 149. C incorrect A test level that can combine techniques. See PDF p. 149, 149. D incorrect A complete-system scope rather than the knowledge-based distinction. See PDF p. 149, 149.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 170 · AM0006
records.text: AM0006 Question 170 SE20 Which diagrams describe detailed behavioral evolution over time through either ordered participant interactions or event-triggered state changes? Select all that apply. Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A Use case diagrams B Class diagrams C Sequence diagrams D State machine diagrams Sequence diagrams; State machine diagrams Sequence diagrams show ordered messages across participant lifelines, while state machines show event-triggered transitions through an object’s lifecycle states. Both therefore describe behavioral evolution over time under the stated scope. A use-case diagram summarizes external roles and goals without that detailed temporal evolution, and a class diagram describes static types and relationships. Neither replaces the two detailed dynamic views requested. A incorrect Use-case diagrams summarize roles/goals rather than detailed temporal evolution. B incorrect Class diagrams are static. C correct Sequence diagrams show ordered participant interactions. D correct State machines show event-triggered lifecycle changes.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 171 · AM0007
records.text: AM0007 Question 171 SE05 SE03 SE06 Which software development methodology promotes adaptive planning, evolutionary development, and continuous improvement? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Waterfall model B Agile methodology C V-model D Spiral model Agile methodology Adaptive planning, evolutionary improvement and responsiveness to customer feedback characterize Agile as a broad development approach. Waterfall emphasizes planned phase progression; the V-model pairs development stages with corresponding test levels. Spiral can evolve a product as well, but its defining organization is repeated risk assessment and reduction. The question asks for the approach whose core emphasis matches the stated planning and collaboration values. A incorrect Waterfall emphasizes planned phase progression rather than adaptive planning. B correct Agile places adaptive planning and ongoing improvement at the center. C incorrect The V-model emphasizes correspondence between development and test stages. D incorrect Spiral is organized primarily around risk reduction, even when development is evolutionary.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 173 · AM0009
records.text: AM0009 Question 173 SE07 SE06 Developers build a quick interface version solely to discover how users perform an unfamiliar task; it is not a production release. Which named approach describes the immediate purpose of that version? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Waterfall model B Agile methodology C Prototype model D Spiral model Prototype model The early version is built to learn how users understand and carry out a task, not to deliver a production increment. That exploratory purpose identifies a prototype. Agile can use prototypes but its broader definition centers on collaboration and adaptation. Spiral may prototype to reduce a risk, but risk cycles are not the specific technique requested. Classical waterfall does not itself name early experimental versions. The purpose of the artifact distinguishes these overlapping practices. A incorrect Waterfall is a phased lifecycle rather than the named exploratory artifact technique. B incorrect Agile may use prototypes but does not specifically name the described usability experiment. C correct Prototyping uses an experimental version to discover requirements or usability needs. D incorrect Spiral may employ a prototype, but its defining method is organizing cycles around risk reduction.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 174 · AM0010
records.text: AM0010 Question 174 SE35 SE36 Which testing technique focuses on testing the interaction between different components or modules of a software system? Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A Unit testing B Integration testing C System testing D Regression testing Integration testing Integration testing targets interfaces and interactions among components that have been combined. Unit testing isolates a smaller function or component, while system testing evaluates the complete integrated product against its requirements. Regression testing is triggered by a change and looks for unintended effects; it can be performed at several levels. The scenario is categorized by its interaction scope, so integration is the specific level requested. A incorrect Unit testing isolates a function or small component. B correct Integration testing exercises interactions among combined components. C incorrect System testing evaluates the complete product rather than specifically the component interfaces. D incorrect Regression names the after-change purpose, not a particular component-combination level.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 175 · AM0011
records.text: AM0011 Question 175 SE25 Which design principle suggests that software entities should depend on abstractions, not on concrete implementations? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) principle B SOLID principle C KISS (Keep It Simple, Stupid) principle D YAGNI (You Ain't Gonna Need It) principle Dependency Inversion, within SOLID. SE25 lists Dependency Inversion within SOLID and explicitly directs designs to depend on abstractions. That reduces dependence on concrete implementation details and matches the stem. DRY, KISS and YAGNI address duplication, simplicity and speculative functionality respectively; none is the principle defining the abstraction-based dependency relationship. A incorrect DRY addresses duplicated knowledge rather than the direction and target of dependencies. B correct SOLID includes Dependency Inversion, which directs dependencies toward abstractions. C incorrect KISS addresses unnecessary complexity rather than specifying abstraction-based dependencies. D incorrect YAGNI limits speculative work rather than defining dependency direction.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 176 · AM0012
records.text: AM0012 Question 176 SE03 SE06 Which software development approach follows a linear, sequential flow from requirements gathering to testing and maintenance? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Waterfall model B Agile methodology C Prototype model D Spiral model Waterfall model Classical waterfall organizes development as planned sequential phases such as requirements, design, implementation and testing. Agile instead adapts work through feedback, prototyping uses experimental versions to learn, and spiral cycles organize work around risk reduction. Real waterfall projects can revisit work under change control, but the idealized linear organization described by the question is its characteristic model rather than one of the feedback-centered alternatives. A correct The idealized waterfall model follows the stated planned phase sequence. B incorrect Agile emphasizes adaptation and incremental planning. C incorrect Prototyping learns through experimental versions and feedback. D incorrect Spiral organizes repeated cycles around risk assessment and reduction.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 178 · AM0014
records.text: AM0014 Question 178 SE28 Which tool is used to track and manage software issues, bugs, and tasks throughout the development process? Distinguish the planning or organization goal from the tool or structure used to support it. Apply the stated project conditions. A Git B Jira C Jenkins D Docker Jira. SE28 distinguishes version tracking, issue tracking, automated checks and container packaging. It names Jira as an issue tracker for work and defects, matching bugs and tasks across development. Git records versions, Jenkins automates checks and Docker packages runtime dependencies; those tools may integrate with issue tracking but have different primary roles. A incorrect Git tracks source versions and history rather than serving as the named issue/task tracker. B correct Jira tracks work items, defects and tasks through their development workflow. C incorrect Jenkins automates checks and integration work rather than primarily managing issue records. D incorrect Docker packages runtime dependencies into containers rather than tracking bugs and tasks.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 179 · AM0015
records.text: AM0015 Question 179 SE25 Which design principle suggests that software entities should be open for extension but closed for modification? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) principle B SOLID principle C KISS (Keep It Simple, Stupid) principle D YAGNI (You Ain't Gonna Need It) principle Open–Closed, within SOLID. SE25 lists Open–Closed within SOLID and recommends adding compatible extensions. The stem quotes that principle's central idea: support extension while keeping established code stable. DRY, KISS and YAGNI address other concerns. Open–Closed is a design goal achieved through suitable abstractions, rather than a claim that software can never need modification. A incorrect DRY limits duplicated knowledge rather than defining openness for extension. B correct SOLID includes the Open–Closed principle explicitly described by the stem. C incorrect KISS favors simple solutions rather than the specific extension-versus-modification relationship. D incorrect YAGNI avoids speculative functionality rather than defining the Open–Closed design goal.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 181 · AM0017
records.text: AM0017 Question 181 SE05 SE03 SE06 Customer representatives stay in close contact with developers and use feedback to reshape the next timeboxed work. Which methodology makes this collaboration and adaptation a foundational priority? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Waterfall model B Agile methodology C V-model D Spiral model Agile methodology Frequent stakeholder communication alone is possible in several lifecycles. The scenario additionally gives customer representatives ongoing access to the team and lets feedback reshape the next timeboxed body of work, matching Agile’s collaboration and adaptation values. Waterfall and the V-model primarily organize planned stages, while spiral organizes commitments around risk reduction. The combination of priorities, rather than communication frequency by itself, identifies the intended methodology. A incorrect Waterfall is defined by planned phase progression, not the stated adaptive collaboration priority. B correct Agile explicitly prioritizes customer collaboration and responding to change. C incorrect The V-model is defined by linked development and testing stages. D incorrect Spiral’s organizing priority is risk assessment and reduction, though stakeholders can participate.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 182 · AM0018
records.text: AM0018 Question 182 SE14 SE-S05 Which technique documents an actor’s goal with preconditions, a main success flow, alternative flows and postconditions? Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A Use case modeling B Storyboarding C Wireframing D Pair programming Use case modeling A use-case description captures an actor’s goal together with preconditions, main flow, alternatives and postconditions. This provides the structured behavioral requirements record in the scenario. Storyboards illustrate moments in an interaction and wireframes sketch interface structure; either can help discovery without supplying that full behavioral contract. Pair programming organizes two people’s implementation work. It is therefore use-case modeling that directly names the requested requirements representation. A correct Use-case modeling records actors, goals and structured successful and alternative flows. B incorrect Storyboarding sketches interaction moments rather than necessarily supplying the full goal-and-flow description. C incorrect Wireframing sketches interface structure and layout. D incorrect Pair programming is collaborative implementation work.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 183 · AM0019
records.text: AM0019 Question 183 SE36 Which testing technique focuses on retesting modified or affected parts of the software to ensure that changes do not introduce new defects? Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A Unit testing B Integration testing C Regression testing D System testing Regression testing. SE36 defines regression testing by the purpose of detecting unintended effects after change. That includes retesting changed and affected areas to find newly introduced faults. Unit, integration and system testing describe levels or scope; regression tests can be run at any of them, so the change-driven purpose uniquely identifies C. A incorrect Unit testing defines a small-component scope rather than the purpose of checking change-induced defects. B incorrect Integration testing focuses on interfaces and interactions, which may be regression-tested but do not define regression. C correct Regression testing retests previously working behavior to detect unintended effects of modifications. D incorrect System testing addresses the complete integrated system rather than specifically the after-change purpose.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 184 · AM0020
records.text: AM0020 Question 184 SE28 Which tool is used to package an application and its dependencies into a container for easy deployment and scalability? C incorrect Jenkins automates checks and pipelines but is not the named container-packaging tool. D correct Docker packages the application and runtime dependencies into a deployable container.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 187 · AM0023
records.text: AM0023 Question 187 SE05 SE03 SE06 Which broad approach explicitly centers its values on collaboration, working results and responding to change, using frequent feedback to improve later work? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Waterfall model B Agile methodology C Spiral model D V-model Agile methodology The stated priorities combine short feedback cycles, collaboration and adaptation as central development values. Agile names that broad approach. Waterfall and the V-model emphasize planned stages, with the V-model additionally relating stages to test levels. Spiral can also iterate and consult stakeholders, but its defining cycle is risk-driven. Distinguishing the core emphasis avoids incorrectly claiming that only Agile can communicate or revisit work. A incorrect Classical waterfall emphasizes planned phase commitments. B correct Agile makes collaboration and responsiveness to change central values. C incorrect Spiral is defined by explicit risk-reduction cycles rather than this value-based emphasis. D incorrect The V-model is defined by development–test correspondences.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 188 · AM0024
records.text: AM0024 Question 188 SE22 A team separates a reusable reporting component behind a stable interface so other applications can use it and its implementation can change without rewriting clients. Which benefit most directly captures both goals? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A To improve the readability of the code B To ensure efficient memory management C To facilitate code reuse and maintenance D To minimize the number of software defects To facilitate code reuse and maintenance A module with a stable interface can be reused in another application, and hiding its implementation allows localized changes without rewriting its clients. Those are reuse and maintenance benefits. Readability may improve as well, but it does not fully describe the two goals stated in the scenario. Modularization does not automatically optimize memory use or eliminate defects; good boundaries and verification still matter. A incorrect Readability may improve, but it does not fully describe reuse across applications and localized change. B incorrect Memory efficiency is not guaranteed by separating modules. C correct Reuse and maintenance directly match the two stated goals. D incorrect Reducing defects can be a benefit, but it does not name the stated reuse-and-change objective.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 189 · AM0025
records.text: AM0025 Question 189 SE35 SE36 Which type of testing aims to uncover defects in the interaction between different components of a software system? Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A Unit testing B Integration testing C System testing D Regression testing Integration testing The defects sought are in communication or interfaces among combined components, so the applicable level is integration testing. Unit tests concentrate on isolated units and system tests assess the complete product. Regression testing instead describes checking for unintended effects after a change, and can include unit, integration or system tests. The distinction is between the scope of combination and the purpose that triggers a test run. A incorrect Unit testing concentrates on an isolated function or small component. B correct Integration testing targets interactions among combined parts. C incorrect System testing checks the whole integrated system against requirements. D incorrect Regression is an after-change objective that can occur at several testing levels.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 190 · AM0026
records.text: AM0026 Question 190 SE01 Which programming paradigm is based on the concept of objects and their interactions? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Functional programming B Procedural programming C Object-oriented programming D Event-driven programming Object-oriented programming Object-oriented programming organizes a system around objects that combine state and behavior and interact through operations. Procedural programming decomposes work into functions or procedures that manipulate data. Functional programming emphasizes function evaluation and controlled side effects, while event-driven programming organizes reactions to events. An object-oriented program may also use events or functions, but the question asks which paradigm is defined by objects and their interactions. A incorrect Functional programming emphasizes evaluation of functions and controlled side effects. B incorrect Procedural programming emphasizes functions or procedures operating on data. C correct Object-oriented programming centers on objects with state and behavior. D incorrect Event-driven programming centers on reactions to events, independent of object-based decomposition.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 191 · AM0027
records.text: AM0027 Question 191 SE33 SE28 What is the defining artifact-management function of version control, distinguishing it from collaboration benefits and CI services? Separate artifact history and controlled changes from scheduling, collaboration benefits and automated execution. A To manage project schedules and milestones B To facilitate collaboration among team members C To track and control changes to source code and files D To automate the testing and deployment processes To track and control changes to source code and files Version control records artifact versions and their history, making it possible to inspect changes, maintain branches and combine compatible work. Collaboration is an important benefit, but it is broader than the defining version-history function. Scheduling belongs to project planning, while automated testing and deployment belong to CI or delivery tooling that can use version-control events. These roles can be integrated without becoming the same activity. A incorrect Scheduling and milestones belong to project planning and tracking. B incorrect Collaboration is a benefit enabled by shared versions and merging, rather than the defining artifact-history function. C correct Tracking and controlling file changes is the direct version-control function. D incorrect Testing and deployment automation is CI/delivery work that may integrate with version control.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 192 · AM0028
records.text: AM0028 Question 192 SE03 Which conventional lifecycle is described by a simple linear requirements→design→implementation→testing sequence with reviewed phase completion, without the V-model’s explicit development-to-test pairing? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Waterfall model B Agile methodology C Spiral model D V-model Waterfall model Classical waterfall organizes work as separated planned phases with reviewed deliverables, matching the stated linear sequence. The V-model additionally pairs development artifacts with later test levels, which this question excludes. Agile emphasizes adaptation and feedback, while spiral organizes repeated risk-driven cycles. Explicitly distinguishing the test-pairing structure removes the overlap between two staged processes without denying their relationship. A correct Classical waterfall matches the specified simple linear organization. B incorrect Agile emphasizes adaptive content and feedback. C incorrect Spiral uses risk-driven cycles. D incorrect The V-model adds explicit development-to-test pairing excluded here.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 193 · AM0029
records.text: AM0029 Question 193 SE34 What is the primary purpose of software documentation? Distinguish process assurance from product evaluation, and compare specified obligations with actual stakeholder needs. A To serve as a record of code authorship B To provide instructions for end-users C To assist in software maintenance and understanding D To ensure compliance with coding standards To assist in software maintenance and understanding Documentation records requirements and architecture so developers can understand decisions, revisit designs and coordinate later change. A user manual is one audience-specific part of this broader purpose. A incorrect Authorship alone does not capture system decisions or behavior. See PDF p. 130, 83, 32. B incorrect End-user instructions are a valid subset, not the overall technical purpose. See PDF p. 130, 83, 32. C correct Matches understanding, revisiting and maintaining documented structures. See PDF p. 130, 83, 32. D incorrect Coding-standard compliance is narrower than the general understanding purpose. See PDF p. 130, 83, 32.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 194 · AM0030
records.text: AM0030 Question 194 SE04 SE03 SE06 SE05 After each short usable release, customers reorder the remaining work and the team adapts the next release’s content while keeping its timebox. Which broad approach most directly fits this planning behavior? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Waterfall model B Agile methodology C Spiral model D V-model Agile methodology A fixed short timebox with usable results and customer-driven adaptation of later content fits Agile planning. Classical waterfall and the V-model organize planned development stages, with the latter pairing stages to tests. Spiral cycles organize commitments around risk assessment and reduction. All can incorporate some staged work, so the stated treatment of feedback and later scope is what makes the Agile option the most direct match. A incorrect Classical waterfall emphasizes planned phases and later delivery feedback. B correct Agile adapts later work from customer feedback while producing usable increments. C incorrect Spiral is specifically organized around risk reduction, not the stated timeboxed adaptation rule. D incorrect The V-model is defined by paired development and test stages.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 195 · AM0031
records.text: AM0031 Question 195 SE25 SE-S02 Which design principle advocates for designing software components that have a single responsibility? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Encapsulation B Inheritance C Polymorphism D Single Responsibility Principle Single Responsibility Principle. SE25 identifies Single Responsibility among the core design principles. The question asks directly for one responsibility per component, so D is the exact named rule. Encapsulation protects internal decisions, inheritance creates subtype relations, and polymorphism supports varying implementations through a common interface. Those can help a design but do not themselves define a single responsibility. A incorrect Encapsulation hides implementation details rather than requiring one responsibility per component. B incorrect Inheritance establishes superclass/subclass reuse rather than the focused-responsibility rule. C incorrect Polymorphism supports compatible varying implementations rather than defining responsibility count. D correct Single Responsibility explicitly calls for one focused responsibility in a software component.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 196 · AM0032
records.text: AM0032 Question 196 SE27 Which design pattern is used to ensure that only one instance of a class is created throughout the system? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Singleton pattern B Factory pattern C Observer pattern D Decorator pattern Singleton. SE27 describes Singleton as controlling access to one instance. That is the pattern requested by the one-instance condition. Factory patterns address how concrete objects are created, Observer notifies subscribers and Decorator adds behavior by wrapping. None of those other pattern responsibilities guarantees a single shared instance by itself. A correct Singleton controls creation and access so that the intended class has one shared instance. B incorrect A factory selects or constructs products rather than inherently limiting a class to one instance. C incorrect Observer distributes notifications to subscribers rather than restricting object instance count. D incorrect Decorator adds behavior through wrapping rather than enforcing a single instance.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 197 · AM0033
records.text: AM0033 Question 197 SE36 Which test type checks that specified services produce the required outputs under normal operating conditions, without measuring speed/resources or user task ease? Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A Stress testing B Performance testing C Functional testing D Usability testing Functional testing Functional tests compare observable services and outputs with the SRS and acceptance criteria. That is the stated objective, so C applies. Performance testing measures speed, throughput or resources, and usability evaluates user task success or ease; neither is requested here. Stress testing exceeds normal limits. Normal operating conditions alone would not distinguish these types, but the explicit behavioral objective does. A incorrect Stress testing exceeds normal operating limits. B incorrect Performance testing measures speed, throughput or resources. C correct Functional testing checks specified services and outputs. D incorrect Usability testing evaluates user task ease or success.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 198 · AM0034
records.text: AM0034 Question 198 SE01 Which programming paradigm promotes the use of data and avoids side effects? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Functional programming B Procedural programming C Object-oriented programming D Event-driven programming Functional programming, for the side-effect emphasis. The phrase promotes the use of data is not distinctive because all these paradigms use data. The discriminating part is avoiding or controlling side effects. SE01 explicitly assigns function evaluation and controlled side effects to functional programming. Procedural, object-oriented and event-driven styles organize behavior differently and do not inherently impose that emphasis. A correct Functional programming emphasizes evaluating functions and controlling side effects. B incorrect Procedural decomposition organizes functions or procedures without inherently avoiding state-changing effects. C incorrect Object-oriented decomposition combines state and behavior and does not inherently exclude side effects. D incorrect Event-driven programs react to events; that does not itself require avoiding side effects.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 199 · AM0035
records.text: AM0035 Question 199 SE40 Which type of software maintenance involves making changes to a software system to adapt it to new environments or technologies? Classify the motive for the change before its implementation: repair, environment, useful capability or reduced future risk. A Corrective maintenance B Adaptive maintenance C Perfective maintenance D Preventive maintenance Adaptive maintenance. SE40 defines adaptive maintenance as responding to changes in the environment. New platforms or technologies therefore create an adaptive-maintenance need even when the original software is not faulty. Corrective maintenance fixes faults, perfective work improves useful capability or performance, and preventive work reduces future risk. The stated environmental motive makes B the appropriate category. A incorrect Corrective work fixes faults rather than primarily accommodating changed environments or technology. B correct Adaptive maintenance changes software so it continues working in a new environment or technology context. C incorrect Perfective work improves capability or performance rather than specifically responding to an environmental change. D incorrect Preventive work reduces future maintenance risk rather than defining adaptation to a new environment.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 200 · AM0036
records.text: AM0036 Question 200 SE36 What is the purpose of usability testing in software development? Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A To evaluate the performance of the software system under stress conditions B To assess the user-friendliness and ease of use of the software system C To verify the compliance of the software system with specified requirements D To identify and fix defects or issues in the software system To assess the user-friendliness and ease of use of the software system Usability testing examines ease of learning, task completion and user errors, with the goal of identifying and improving usability problems. A incorrect Stress performance is not the ease-of-use focus. See PDF p. 82. B correct Directly matches ease of use and learning. See PDF p. 82. C incorrect General requirements conformance is broader than this specific user-focused test. See PDF p. 82. D incorrect General fault fixing is broader; the test identifies user interaction difficulties rather than implementing all repairs. See PDF p. 82.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 201 · AM0037
records.text: AM0037 Question 201 SE05 Which software development methodology involves iterative development cycles called sprints? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Waterfall model B Agile methodology C Spiral model D V-model Agile methodology, specifically Scrum. SE05 places Sprints in Scrum, an Agile framework. B is therefore the available category that contains the specific process described. Agile as a whole does not require every method to call its iterations Sprints. Waterfall, spiral and the V-model have other organizing principles, so none is the named Sprint-based method. A incorrect Classical waterfall uses planned phases rather than Scrum Sprints. B correct Scrum is an Agile framework whose iterative delivery cycles are called Sprints. C incorrect Spiral uses risk-driven cycles rather than specifically the Scrum Sprint mechanism. D incorrect The V-model pairs development stages with tests rather than organizing work into Sprints.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 202 · AM0038
records.text: AM0038 Question 202 SE43 What is the primary purpose of code refactoring? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A To add new features to the software system B To optimize the performance of the software system C To improve the readability and maintainability of the code D To fix defects or issues in the software system To improve the readability and maintainability of the code Restructuring explicitly addresses maintainability, readability and understandability, while optimization separately addresses speed and memory. C matches refactoring’s purpose of improving internal structure and maintainability. A incorrect Adds behavior, whereas restructuring reorganizes existing design elements. See PDF p. 133. B incorrect Optimization is separately classified by performance goals. See PDF p. 133. C correct Direct match to the documented restructuring goals. See PDF p. 133. D incorrect Repairing a fault is correction; restructuring need not fix a behavioral defect. See PDF p. 133.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 203 · AM0039
records.text: AM0039 Question 203 SE05 SE03 SE06 Which approach treats customer participation in reviewing working results and reprioritizing future work as a foundational value, rather than merely a practice a project may choose? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Waterfall model B Agile methodology C Spiral model D V-model Agile methodology The project treats customer participation in reviewing results and reprioritizing future work as a foundational development value. This directly matches Agile’s customer collaboration and responsiveness to change. Waterfall and the V-model primarily define phase and test-stage organization. Spiral also includes stakeholder review, but risk assessment and reduction define its cycle. Participation alone is not exclusive; the explicit priority given to continual adaptive collaboration identifies the answer. A incorrect Classical waterfall’s defining organization is planned phase progression. B correct Agile explicitly prioritizes customer collaboration and adapting to feedback. C incorrect Spiral includes review but is defined by risk-driven cycles. D incorrect The V-model organizes linked development and test stages, rather than naming the stated collaboration values.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 204 · AM0040
records.text: AM0040 Question 204 SE35 SE36 Which type of testing involves running the entire software system in an environment that closely resembles the production environment? Separate testing scope, technique and purpose. Use the stated workload, observable result or coverage target rather than a universal ranking. A Unit testing B Integration testing C System testing D Regression testing System testing System testing evaluates the complete integrated software against its functional and nonfunctional requirements in a representative environment. Unit testing isolates a smaller element and integration testing concentrates on interfaces among combined parts. Regression testing instead checks for unintended consequences after change and is not restricted to any one level or environment. The question specifies the complete-product scope, making system testing the direct classification. A incorrect Unit testing isolates a function, class or small component. B incorrect Integration testing focuses on interfaces and interactions among combined parts. C correct System testing evaluates the complete integrated product in a representative environment. D incorrect Regression names an after-change checking purpose and can run at multiple levels.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 205 · AM0041
records.text: AM0041 Question 205 SE14 What is a use case in use case modeling? Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A A description of a specific user interface design B A step-by-step procedure for software installation C A sequence of activities performed by a user or system D A diagram that represents the relationships between software components A sequence of activities performed by a user or system A use case describes a system-provided function as a flow of events producing an actor-visible result. C is acceptable when understood as goal-related interactions, not any arbitrary sequence of activities. A incorrect UI layout is an implementation/interface design artifact. See PDF p. 47, 48. B incorrect Installation instructions are one possible documented procedure, not the general use-case definition. See PDF p. 47, 48. C correct Best matches the goal-oriented flow of events involving actors and the system. See PDF p. 47, 48. D incorrect Component relationships describe internal structure rather than actor-visible behavior. See PDF p. 47, 48.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 206 · AM0042
records.text: AM0042 Question 206 SE14 What is an actor in use-case modeling when the system boundary is fixed? Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A A component that performs specific actions in a software system B An external interacting role played by a person, device or another system. C A diagram that represents the flow of activities in a use case D A particular individual user account rather than a role. An external interacting role played by a person, device or another system. An actor is an external role that interacts across the chosen system boundary. A person, device or another system may play that role. It is not an internal component, a diagram, or merely one individual user account. Because actors model roles rather than particular people, one person can play multiple actors and multiple people can fulfill the same actor role. A incorrect An internal component is not an external actor merely because it acts. B correct The external interacting role is the actor. C incorrect An activity-flow diagram is a model artifact rather than an actor. D incorrect An individual account is not the role abstraction.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 207 · AM0043
records.text: AM0043 Question 207 SE16 What is the purpose of an include relationship between use cases? Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A To represent the reuse of common steps between use cases B To represent optional steps within a use case C To represent the extension of a use case with additional steps D To represent the relationship between actors and use cases To represent the reuse of common steps between use cases Factoring common functionality into one included use case eliminates redundant descriptions, as in shared HelpDispatcher behavior. A correct Direct reuse/commonality mechanism. See PDF p. 50, 50. B incorrect Optional exceptional behavior is more directly represented by extend. See PDF p. 50, 50. C incorrect Adds events under conditions through extend rather than reuse via include. See PDF p. 50, 50. D incorrect Actor/use-case communication uses associations, not include. See PDF p. 50, 50.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 208 · AM0044
records.text: AM0044 Question 208 SE16 Which statements describe extend between use cases? Select all that apply. Read optional as conditional behavior at an extension point. Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A To factor required reused steps into an included use case. B To represent optional steps within a use case C To represent the extension of a use case with additional steps D To represent the relationship between actors and use cases To represent optional steps within a use case; To represent the extension of a use case with additional steps Extend adds conditional behavior at extension points in an independently meaningful base use case. It therefore represents optional additional behavior and extends the base with added steps, making both B and C true. Factoring required reused behavior is the include relationship. Associations between actors and use cases are separate from the extend relationship linking use cases to one another. A incorrect Required reused behavior is factored with include. B correct Conditional additional behavior need not occur in every base execution. C correct Extend adds steps to an independently meaningful base. D incorrect Actor association is a different relationship.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 209 · AM0045
records.text: AM0045 Question 209 SE14 Which diagram is commonly used to visualize the relationships between actors and use cases in use case modeling? Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A Class diagram B Use case diagram C Activity diagram D Sequence diagram Use case diagram Use-case diagrams depict actors and use cases with communication associations; these are the requested external interaction relationships. A incorrect Describes class structure. See PDF p. 47, 48. B correct Direct actor/use-case representation. See PDF p. 47, 48. C incorrect Describes action/control flow. See PDF p. 47, 48. D incorrect Describes time-ordered object interactions, not the high-level actor/function map. See PDF p. 47, 48.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 210 · AM0046
records.text: AM0046 Question 210 SE16 What defines an abstract use case, rather than optionality, unfinished documentation or reuse alone? Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A To represent a use case that is not yet fully defined B To represent a use case that is optional in the system C It specifies behavior for specialization and is not directly instantiated as a complete use case. D To represent a use case that is reused by other use cases It specifies behavior for specialization and is not directly instantiated as a complete use case. An abstract use case specifies behavior for specialization and is not directly instantiated as a complete use case. That is different from being unfinished, optional or reused. Concrete behavior can be included for reuse, and extend can express conditional additions. Nor does the absence of a direct actor line by itself establish abstraction. Option C states the actual defining criterion. A incorrect An incomplete description is not the abstraction criterion. B incorrect Optional behavior is not the abstraction criterion. C correct Specialization without direct complete instantiation defines this abstraction. D incorrect Reuse alone can also involve concrete use cases.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 211 · AM0047
records.text: AM0047 Question 211 SE15 Which option states the most specific defining purpose of an exception flow, distinguishing it from a generic alternative flow? Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A To represent an error or exceptional situation in the use case B To represent an alternative path within the use case C To represent the termination of the use case D To represent the relationship between primary and secondary actors To represent an error or exceptional situation in the use case An exception flow handles an error or failure encountered in the use case. Such a path is also an alternative to the main success flow in a broad sense, but B alone does not distinguish exceptional handling from normal conditional variations. An exception may allow correction and recovery instead of terminating the use case. Actor relationships do not define its failure-handling purpose. A correct Error or exceptional handling is the specific defining purpose. B incorrect Alternative path is broader and does not identify the exceptional nature. C incorrect Exceptions need not terminate the entire use case. D incorrect Actor relationships do not describe failure handling.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 212 · AM0048
records.text: AM0048 Question 212 SE14 What is the primary goal of use case modeling? Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A To define the software architecture of the system B To identify and document user requirements C To design the user interface of the system D To implement the functionality of the system To identify and document user requirements Use cases capture externally visible functionality and let developers validate requirements with users, rather than defining internal architecture or implementation. A incorrect System design defines architecture after the external analysis model. See PDF p. 47, 62. B correct Directly captures actor-visible functional requirements. See PDF p. 47, 62. C incorrect UI layout can be explored alongside use cases but is not their primary purpose. See PDF p. 47, 62. D incorrect Implementation realizes the requirements instead of documenting them. See PDF p. 47, 62.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 213 · AM0049
records.text: AM0049 Question 213 SE15 What is an alternative flow in a use case? Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A A flowchart representation of the use case steps B A flow of activities that occurs in parallel with the main flow C A different sequence of steps based on specific conditions D A representation of the relationship between use cases A different sequence of steps based on specific conditions A flow of events describes interactions; exceptional conditions introduce alternative event sequences. This is a different path under a condition, rather than necessarily concurrency or inter-use-case structure. A incorrect A flowchart is a representation format, not the alternative sequence itself. See PDF p. 48, 50. B incorrect Parallel execution is not required by an alternative branch. See PDF p. 48, 50. C correct Directly describes a condition-dependent event sequence. See PDF p. 48, 50. D incorrect Include/extend/generalization describe relationships, not the definition of every alternative flow. See PDF p. 48, 50.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 214 · AM0050
records.text: AM0050 Question 214 SE14 What is the purpose of a use case diagram? Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A To describe the behavior of a use case in detail B To represent the internal structure of a use case C To visualize the relationships between actors and use cases D To represent the flow of activities within a use case To visualize the relationships between actors and use cases The diagram shows actors, functions and communication links; the separate textual template contains detailed event sequences and conditions. A incorrect Detailed flow belongs in the use-case description/template. See PDF p. 47, 48. B incorrect Internal structure is modeled with classes/components. See PDF p. 47, 48. C correct Direct high-level actor/function interaction view. See PDF p. 47, 48. D incorrect Activity diagrams or textual flows express detailed action sequences. See PDF p. 47, 48.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 215 · CS0007
records.text: CS0007 Question 215 SE21 Identifying and describing the fundamental software system abstractions and their relationships. Establishing the overall system architecture — in which phase are these activities done? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A System design B Requirement analysis and definition C System testing D Implementation System design System and software design establish the overall architecture and identify software abstractions and relationships. A correct Direct match to the described design tasks. See PDF p. 18, 116. B incorrect Establishes required services, constraints and goals. See PDF p. 18, 116. C incorrect Checks complete-system behavior. See PDF p. 18, 116. D incorrect Translates a design into code. See PDF p. 18, 116.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 216 · CS0008
records.text: CS0008 Question 216 SE04 SE06 Instead of delivering the system as a single delivery, development and delivery is broken down into phases with each phase delivering part of the required functionality. What type of development model is this? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Incremental B Waterfall C Spiral D Evolutionary Incremental Successive deliveries that each add part of the required usable functionality define incremental development. The product gains capability across these deliveries rather than waiting for a single completed-system handoff. Waterfall and a generic linear model organize phase sequence. Spiral is organized around risk assessment, and evolutionary development broadly describes refinement. Those can overlap with staged delivery, but incremental is the specific name for the delivery organization stated. A correct Incremental development adds usable required functionality in successive deliveries. B incorrect Waterfall names planned phase progression, not this particular staged-capability strategy. C incorrect Spiral names risk-driven cycles, even when increments are produced. D incorrect Evolutionary refinement is broader than the specific addition-of-functionality strategy described.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 217 · CS0009
records.text: CS0009 Question 217 SE03 We should NOT use the Waterfall software development process model in situations like: Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Plenty of resources with required expertise are available freely B There are no ambiguous requirements C The project is short D Software requirements change quickly Software requirements change quickly Waterfall should be used only when requirements are well understood and unlikely to change radically. Rapid requirement change violates this selection condition. A incorrect Available expertise is not the documented contraindication. See PDF p. 20. B incorrect Unambiguous stable requirements support, rather than undermine, the model. See PDF p. 20. C incorrect The module says waterfall works well for smaller projects with well-understood requirements. See PDF p. 20. D correct Directly violates the stability assumption and creates costly rework. See PDF p. 20.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 218 · CS0010
records.text: CS0010 Question 218 SE22 Which one of the following is false about divide and conquer or modularization process? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Separate people can work on each sub-divided part B Opportunities arise for making the component reusable C Each individual component is smaller, and therefore easier to understand D Replacing or changing a component is difficult because it affects other parts extremely Replacing or changing a component is difficult because it affects other parts extremely Subsystems can be assigned to separate teams, reused and changed with reduced impact when coupled loosely. D contradicts the change-isolation goal of good modularization. A incorrect Independent teams can realize different manageable subsystems. See PDF p. 118, 116, 32, 120. B incorrect Reusable self-contained modules are an explicit OO benefit. See PDF p. 118, 116, 32, 120. C incorrect Decomposition produces simpler manageable units. See PDF p. 118, 116, 32, 120. D correct Strong propagation of every change describes undesirable tight coupling, not good modularization. See PDF p. 118, 116, 32, 120.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 219 · CS0013
records.text: CS0013 Question 219 SE35 SE28 For this project, planned testing effort in hours is setup + (cases × hours per case). The estimates (setup,cases,hours/case) are Unit=(4,80,0.1), Acceptance=(3,10,1), System=(6,20,0.5), Integration=(4,20,0.5). Which level has the greatest planned effort? Use the effort formula given in the question separately for every level, then compare all computed totals. A Unit testing B Acceptance testing C System testing D Integration testing System testing The estimates give unit effort 4+80×0.1=12 hours, acceptance 3+10×1=13, system 6+20×0.5=16, and integration 4+20×0.5=14. System testing therefore has the greatest planned effort for this project. The note does not make any test level universally longest; the explicit workload and setup assumptions are what justify this particular ranking. A incorrect Unit totals twelve hours, below the maximum. B incorrect Acceptance totals thirteen hours, below the maximum. C correct System totals sixteen hours, the largest estimate. D incorrect Integration totals fourteen hours, below system testing.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 220 · NS0293
records.text: NS0293 Question 220 SE18 A filled composition diamond is at Car’s end of its Engine association. In this model Engine remains owned for its entire lifetime and cannot be detached or transferred. What does this imply? Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A Car uses Engine temporarily B Engine can exist independently of the Car C Engine is part of Car and cannot exist independently under the stated lifetime policy. D Car inherits from Engine Engine is part of Car and cannot exist independently under the stated lifetime policy. Composition makes Engine a strongly owned part of Car, with the filled diamond beside the whole. Parts still owned are destroyed when their composite is destroyed. Since this model does not permit Engine to detach or transfer, it cannot continue an independent lifetime without Car. Temporary use would be a dependency, and inheritance would be shown by a hollow triangle. A incorrect Temporary use is a dependency rather than composition. B incorrect The no-detachment policy excludes an independent Engine lifetime. C correct Engine is Car’s owned part and cannot outlive it under this policy. D incorrect Inheritance uses a hollow triangle.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 221 · NS0328
records.text: NS0328 Question 221 SE03 From the following statement which one is disadvantage of waterfall model? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A model is simple and easy to understand and use B It is easy manage due to the rigidity of the model C Not suitable for projects where requirements are at a moderate to high risk of changing D In this model phases are processed and completed one at a time Poor suitability when requirements have substantial change risk. SE03 says waterfall fits stable understood requirements and familiar technology. Late feedback can make changes costly, so moderate-to-high requirement-change risk is a direct disadvantage. Simplicity and milestone visibility are advantages. Sequential phase organization characterizes the classical model; it can contribute to rigidity, but C explicitly identifies the adverse scenario asked for. A incorrect Simplicity and ease of understanding are presented as advantages rather than the adverse scenario. B incorrect Manageable milestones can be an advantage of planned rigidity, despite its trade-offs. C correct Likely requirement changes make late feedback and rigid commitments costly. D incorrect Sequential phases describe the model; C more directly states the requested disadvantage.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 222 · NS0333
records.text: NS0333 Question 222 SE10 For a search service whose functions and database technology are already specified, which requirement adds a quantitative service-speed target? Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity. A The system allow user to generate PDF report. B The system respond to user’s request within 2 second under normal load C The system allow user to store data on relational database D The system allow user to submit emergency report The system respond to user’s request within 2 second under normal load The two-second response obligation bounds the speed of a service under the stated load, so it is a performance requirement. Generating a PDF and submitting an emergency report describe services the system provides. The database clause describes storage behavior together with an implementation choice; it does not impose a response-time threshold. The explicit performance scope removes the broader taxonomy overlap between nonfunctional requirements and technology constraints. A incorrect Report generation specifies a service, not its response-time limit. B correct A two-second response bound under normal load is a quantitative speed target. C incorrect This specifies storage behavior and a database technology, without a timing bound. D incorrect Submitting an emergency report specifies a function rather than its speed.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 223 · NS0347
records.text: NS0347 Question 223 SE17 SE-S03 Which one of the following UML building block that defines the static part of the model and represents physical and conceptual elements? Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. A Structural things B Behavioral things C An notational things D Grouping things Structural things. SE17 explicitly describes structural things as conceptual or physical structural elements. They make up the static model in contrast with behavior over time. Behavioral things cover dynamic aspects, grouping organizes elements and annotations add explanatory information rather than being the static elements themselves. Thus A directly matches both parts of the definition. A correct Structural things are the static conceptual or physical building blocks described. B incorrect Behavioral things concern dynamic behavior rather than the static structural elements. C incorrect Annotations add explanatory information rather than defining the static structural building blocks. D incorrect Grouping organizes model elements rather than being the stated conceptual/physical structural category.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 224 · NS0740
records.text: NS0740 Question 224 SE09 SE10 What is the difference between functional and non-functional requirements? Give an example of each. Distinguish observable services, measurable qualities and implementation constraints. Check scope, stakeholder meaning and the requested level of specificity. Functional requirements specify observable behavior; nonfunctional requirements specify qualities or constraints. Example: generate a PDF report versus respond within two seconds under a stated load. SE09 includes required and prohibited services, so generating a PDF report is functional. SE10 specifies qualities such as performance, usability and availability; a response-time threshold under defined load is nonfunctional. Security mechanisms can implement functional behavior as well as support quality goals, so a negative or security-related statement is not automatically nonfunctional.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 225 · NS0741
records.text: NS0741 Question 225 SE22 Why is low coupling considered good in software design? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. Low coupling limits dependencies, so changes remain local and modules are easier to understand, replace, test and maintain. SE22 measures coupling through dependencies between modules and recommends low coupling with high cohesion. Shared mutable data and knowledge of another module’s representation increase the chance that one change affects others. Stable interfaces and information hiding constrain that impact. More interfaces can add complexity, so minimizing harmful dependencies matters more than simply maximizing the number of modules.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 226 · NS0742
records.text: NS0742 Question 226 SE03 SE05 What is the difference between Waterfall and Agile methodologies? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. Waterfall uses planned, reviewed stages and suits stable requirements; Agile emphasizes collaboration, working results, feedback and adaptation. SE03 describes planned phases with costly late feedback, useful for stable requirements and familiar technology. SE05 values customer participation and adaptation with useful working increments. Agile still plans and documents; waterfall can revisit work under control. The practical difference is feedback and commitment organization, not a claim that one process forbids change or the other forbids documentation.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 227 · NS0743
records.text: NS0743 Question 227 SE16 What is the difference between <<include>> and <<extend>> in use case diagrams? Match the information to be represented with each model’s purpose. Read relationship direction, boundary and ownership conditions before classifying it. Include factors required reused behavior, with base→included; extend adds conditional behavior, with extension→base. SE16 uses include for reused required behavior incorporated when the inclusion point is reached. Extend adds behavior at extension points under a condition, and the base remains meaningful independently. The dashed arrows have different directions: including use case toward included, and extending use case toward base. Neither relation should be confused with actor association or specialization generalization.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 228 · NS0744
records.text: NS0744 Question 228 SE40 Why is maintenance often the most expensive phase of the SDLC? Classify the motive for the change before its implementation: repair, environment, useful capability or reduced future risk. Maintenance can dominate cost because it lasts years and repeatedly requires legacy understanding, changes, regression testing and release work. SE40 says maintenance often spans years and includes understanding existing code plus regression effort. Work is not limited to bug fixes: environments, useful capabilities and future risks also change. Repeated impact analysis, implementation and testing accumulate across the operational lifetime, so maintenance may dominate lifecycle cost. This is a common outcome, not a guarantee for every project.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 229 · NS0745
records.text: NS0745 Question 229 SE01 Which software development approach emphasizes breaking systems into functions or procedures that manipulate isolated data? Identify whether the scenario prioritizes delivery, learning, adaptation or risk reduction. Several processes can share individual practices, so compare their defining emphasis. A Object-Oriented Approach B Traditional Approach C Agile Approach D Iterative Approach Traditional/procedural decomposition. SE01 contrasts procedural decomposition organized around functions with object-oriented decomposition organized around objects combining state and behavior. B is the available traditional/procedural label for functions operating on data. Agile and iterative describe lifecycle organization rather than this decomposition paradigm, and either can be used with procedural or object-oriented programming. A incorrect Object orientation combines state and behavior in objects rather than organizing primarily around separate procedures. B correct Traditional/procedural decomposition organizes functions and procedures acting on data. C incorrect Agile concerns process adaptation rather than requiring function-based decomposition. D incorrect Iteration describes revisiting development work and does not determine procedural versus object decomposition.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 230 · NS0746
records.text: NS0746 Question 230 SE-S02 In the Object-Oriented Approach, which property allows classes to be used in different parts of the system or other projects without rewriting them? Separate responsibilities inside a component from dependencies across boundaries. Evaluate the stated structure, change and reuse goals without assuming guaranteed benefits. A Encapsulation B Polymorphism C Reusability D Abstraction Reusability. The stem explicitly asks about using existing classes elsewhere without rewriting them, which is reuse. SE01 lists reuse alongside encapsulation and consistent models as ways to reduce duplication and ease change. Encapsulation and abstraction can make reuse safer, while polymorphism supports compatible varying implementations, but those are enabling concepts rather than the name of the capability described. A incorrect Encapsulation hides implementation and can enable reuse, but it is not the capability's name. B incorrect Polymorphism supports differing implementations through compatible interfaces rather than directly naming reuse. C correct Reusability means using suitable existing classes or components in other contexts without rewriting them. D incorrect Abstraction exposes relevant contracts and can assist reuse, but the requested property is reusability.

records.title: Software Engineering — Question 231 · NS0747
records.text: NS0747 Question 231 SE40 Which of the four fundamental software process activities involves making updates to meet changing customer needs after deployment? Classify the motive for the change before its implementation: repair, environment, useful capability or reduced future risk. A Software Specification B Software Design and Implementation C Software Validation D Software Evolution Software evolution. SE40 describes maintenance and evolution through change requests, impact analysis, planning, implementation/testing and release. Updating a deployed product to meet changing customer needs belongs to evolution among the four broad process activities. Specification, implementation and validation still occur within that work, but D names the lifecycle-wide change activity asked for rather than one constituent task. A incorrect Specification captures needs but does not name the overall postdeployment change activity. B incorrect Design/implementation is part of making a change rather than the broad evolution activity.
