B incorrect Network interception is not the defining write mechanism. C correct This states the defining write beyond allocated buffer bounds. D incorrect Unauthorized file access is a possible harm rather than the definition.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 78 · AM0535
records.text: AM0535 Question 78 SEC26 Which statement defines SQL injection by its mechanism rather than merely describing a possible security consequence? Locate where untrusted data can become instructions and where they execute. A A vulnerability that allows attackers to intercept network traffic B A vulnerability that allows attackers to execute arbitrary code C A vulnerability that allows unauthorized access to a system's memory D Untrusted input changes SQL syntax through unsafe query construction Untrusted input changes SQL syntax through unsafe query construction SQL injection occurs when untrusted values become part of SQL syntax through unsafe query construction. That can change query behavior or expose protected records, but unauthorized database access alone does not define the flaw. Network interception and memory access are other broad harms, and arbitrary code execution can occur through multiple mechanisms. The choice identifies the query-syntax boundary that parameter binding is intended to protect. A incorrect Network interception does not define unsafe SQL construction. B incorrect Code execution is a broad possible consequence rather than the SQL-specific mechanism. C incorrect Unauthorized memory access does not identify the query-syntax boundary. D correct This states how untrusted input changes SQL command structure.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 79 · AM0536
records.text: AM0536 Question 79 SEC26 Which statement defines cross-site scripting by its execution context, rather than merely naming one possible effect? Locate where untrusted data can become instructions and where they execute. A A vulnerability that allows unauthorized access to a system's memory B Attacker-controlled script executes in a victim’s browser under the vulnerable site’s origin C A vulnerability that allows attackers to manipulate web page content D A vulnerability that allows unauthorized access to a database Attacker-controlled script executes in a victim’s browser under the vulnerable site’s origin XSS causes attacker-controlled script to run in a victim’s browser under the vulnerable site’s origin. Page-content manipulation can be an effect of that execution but is not a complete definition, since other flaws can also change content. Generic memory or database access likewise does not identify the browser-origin mechanism. The answer states the relevant execution context without treating all arbitrary code execution as XSS. A incorrect Unauthorized memory access does not define the browser-origin script mechanism. B correct This states the script execution and origin context that define XSS. C incorrect Page-content manipulation is a possible effect rather than the defining execution context. D incorrect Unauthorized database access is not the definition of XSS.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 80 · AM0537
records.text: AM0537 Question 80 SEC25 SEC07 SEC09 SEC21 What is the purpose of input validation in program security? Identify the unsafe operation or input boundary rather than only a possible consequence. A To ensure the confidentiality of data B To prevent unauthorized access to a system C To detect and block malicious input D To encrypt sensitive data during transmission Validate and reject unacceptable input Input validation checks whether data meets expected type, length, range and structure, allowing invalid or malicious inputs to be rejected. SEC25 requires server-side checks because clients are controllable. This supports C without claiming validation alone stops every attack: parameterized queries and context-specific output encoding remain separate protections. A incorrect Confidentiality is not the specific purpose of checking input type, range, length and structure. B incorrect Authentication/authorization enforce access; input validation instead checks whether supplied values are acceptable. C correct Validation detects values outside expected constraints so the program can reject unsafe or invalid input. D incorrect Encrypting transmission is channel protection rather than input validation.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 81 · AM0538
records.text: AM0538 Question 81 SEC27 SEC25 What is the role of secure coding practices in program security? Trace timing over shared state or distinguish finding a weakness from demonstrating consequences. A To prevent code duplication and improve program efficiency B To ensure compliance with industry standards and regulations C To minimize the number of bugs and vulnerabilities in code D To facilitate code collaboration among developers Reduce software defects and vulnerabilities Secure development aims to reduce exploitable defects through review, safe input/memory handling, least privilege and related practices described in SEC25–27. C states that direct aim. Efficiency, compliance and collaboration may be benefits of broader engineering practices, but none substitutes for minimizing flaws that can violate the program’s security requirements. A incorrect Avoiding duplication and improving efficiency are general engineering concerns rather than the specific security aim. B incorrect Compliance can be relevant but does not directly state the defect-reduction purpose of secure coding. C correct Secure coding reduces bugs and exploitable vulnerabilities through safer design and implementation. D incorrect Collaboration helps engineering but is not itself the security objective of minimizing exploitable code flaws.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 82 · AM0539
records.text: AM0539 Question 82 SEC09 SEC01 SEC12 What is the purpose of access control mechanisms in program security? Identify subject, object and permitted operation before comparing policy models. A To prevent unauthorized access to sensitive resources B To monitor and log system activities for auditing purposes C To encrypt data during storage and transmission D To protect against malware and viruses To prevent unauthorized access to sensitive resources Access enforcement authorizes subjects to perform operations on objects (PDF p.11), implementing limitation to authorized users (p.4). That protects sensitive resources from unauthorized access. A correct Restricting resource operations to authorized subjects is exactly access control. See PDF p.4, PDF p.11. B incorrect Logging is the separate accountability function. See PDF p.4, PDF p.11. C incorrect Encryption transforms data rather than assigning object permissions. See PDF p.4, PDF p.11. D incorrect Malware defense is broader and does not define access control. See PDF p.4, PDF p.11.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 83 · AM0540
records.text: AM0540 Question 83 SEC27 What is a race condition vulnerability? Trace timing over shared state or distinguish finding a weakness from demonstrating consequences. A A vulnerability that allows unauthorized access to a system's memory B A vulnerability that allows attackers to intercept network traffic C A vulnerability that allows attackers to execute arbitrary code D A vulnerability that occurs when the timing of program execution leads to unexpected behavior Timing/interleaving of shared state causes incorrect behavior SEC27 defines a race through timing-dependent correctness over shared state, such as check-then-use or lost updates. D states that mechanism. Unauthorized memory access, interception and arbitrary code execution may be possible harms from many vulnerabilities, but they do not define the interleaving dependency of a race condition. A incorrect Memory-access harm alone does not establish a shared-state timing or interleaving dependency. B incorrect Traffic interception is a different mechanism and does not define a race. C incorrect Code execution is a possible consequence of various flaws, not the timing-based race definition. D correct Timing-dependent unexpected behavior over shared state is the defining race-condition mechanism.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 84 · AM0541
records.text: AM0541 Question 84 SEC09 SEC25 SEC23 What is the principle of least privilege in program security? Identify subject, object and permitted operation before comparing policy models. A The principle of giving users the minimum necessary permissions to perform their tasks B The principle of encrypting all data stored in a system C The principle of regularly updating software to patch vulnerabilities D The principle of blocking all incoming network connections by default The principle of giving users the minimum necessary permissions to perform their tasks PDF p.5 says not to give more privileges than absolutely necessary for the required job. This directly selects the minimum-permissions option. A correct Minimum required permissions exactly matches least privilege. See PDF p.5. B incorrect Encrypting all data is a separate data-protection measure. See PDF p.5. C incorrect Patching repairs vulnerabilities rather than minimizing permissions. See PDF p.5. D incorrect Default blocking is not the definition of task-based minimum privilege. See PDF p.5.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 85 · AM0542
records.text: AM0542 Question 85 SEC24 What is the purpose of code obfuscation in program security? Separate observation from blocking and sensor placement from detection method. A To enhance program performance and execution speed B To make the code more difficult to understand and analyze C To encrypt sensitive data stored in the program D To detect and block malicious code during program execution Make code harder to understand and analyze SEC24 describes obfuscation as complicating understanding and analysis. It does not reliably hide embedded secrets or remove defects, so it is not equivalent to encryption or malware prevention. Nor does it imply better execution performance. B states the intended analysis-resistance purpose while preserving the note’s limits. A incorrect Obfuscation is not defined as a performance optimization and need not improve speed. B correct Making code more difficult to understand/analyze is the explicit obfuscation purpose. C incorrect Obfuscation is not encryption and does not reliably protect secrets embedded in a program. D incorrect Runtime malicious-code detection/blocking is a separate defensive function rather than obfuscation.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 86 · AM0543
records.text: AM0543 Question 86 SEC25 SEC33 What is a security patch in program security? Identify the unsafe operation or input boundary rather than only a possible consequence. A A technique used to prevent buffer overflow vulnerabilities B A software update released to fix known security vulnerabilities C A hardware device used to monitor network traffic for malicious activities D A set of security policies implemented by an organization A software update released to fix known security vulnerabilities The module warns that failing to update operating systems/applications leaves software vulnerable to bugs already identified and patched (PDF p.3). A security patch is the corrective software update described by B. A incorrect Buffer overflow is only one possible weakness; this is not the general update definition. See PDF p.3. B correct A corrective software update for known weaknesses follows the module’s patch/update account. See PDF p.3. C incorrect A patch is a software correction, not network-monitoring hardware. See PDF p.3. D incorrect Organizational policy is not the software bug correction discussed. See PDF p.3.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 87 · AM0544
records.text: AM0544 Question 87 SEC28 SEC01 What are the basic requirements for a trusted operating system? Separate security-policy enforcement and assurance from ordinary OS features. A Authentication, encryption, and firewall protection B User-friendly interface, multitasking, and device driver support C Confidentiality, integrity, availability, and accountability D User access control, software updates, and system backup Confidentiality, integrity, availability and accountability SEC28 connects trust to enforcement of a stated policy through identity, isolation, access enforcement, protected auditing and safe recovery. Those mechanisms support the broad confidentiality, integrity, availability and accountability requirements in C. The other options list selected mechanisms or ordinary usability features; they do not state the overall security requirements as completely. A incorrect Authentication/encryption/firewalls are selected controls and do not cover the overall trust requirements. B incorrect A GUI and multitasking do not establish security trust, as SEC28 explicitly warns. C correct These broad protection/accountability goals are supported by the trusted OS enforcement and auditing mechanisms. D incorrect Access controls, updates and backups contribute mechanisms but omit the complete high-level requirement set.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 88 · AM0545
records.text: AM0545 Question 88 SEC29 SEC33 What is the purpose of independent evaluation in computer security? Distinguish requirements, technical evaluation, evidence and certification decisions. A To certify that a system is immune to all security threats B To assess the effectiveness of security controls and mechanisms C To perform regular system backups and data recovery tests D To ensure compliance with industry standards and regulations Assess security controls against stated claims Independent evaluation examines evidence and tests controls against the product’s specified functional and assurance claims. B captures that assessment purpose. SEC29 explicitly rejects immunity to all attacks and universal regulatory conclusions. Backups are an operational recovery practice rather than the evaluation’s defining task. A incorrect A scoped evaluation cannot certify immunity to every present and future security threat. B correct Examining evidence and testing controls assesses whether their stated security claims are met. C incorrect Routine backups and restore tests are operational recovery tasks, not the defining independent-evaluation purpose. D incorrect Evaluation assesses specified security claims; it does not automatically establish every industry/regulatory obligation.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 89 · AM0546
records.text: AM0546 Question 89 SEC29 SEC27 What are the evaluation criteria used in the independent evaluation of operating systems? Distinguish requirements, technical evaluation, evidence and certification decisions. A User interface design and performance metrics B Compliance with international security standards C Vulnerability scanning and penetration testing results D Security functionality, assurance, and vulnerabilities Security functionality, assurance and vulnerability analysis SEC29 gives functional and assurance requirements in the Security Target, along with evaluator vulnerability analysis. D captures those evaluation dimensions. User-interface/performance measures are not the security criteria at issue; standards compliance is too broad, and scan/penetration results are evidence rather than the complete requirements framework. A incorrect Interface design and generic performance metrics do not state the security functional/assurance criteria. B incorrect Generic standards compliance omits the scoped Security Target’s concrete functionality and assurance requirements. C incorrect Testing results can be evidence but do not replace the requirements and assurance criteria themselves. D correct Functionality, assurance and vulnerability analysis match the evaluation dimensions described in SEC29.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 90 · AM0547
records.text: AM0547 Question 90 SEC29 What is the evaluation process for trusted operating systems? Distinguish requirements, technical evaluation, evidence and certification decisions. A Development, testing, and deployment B Risk assessment, vulnerability scanning, and patching C Security requirements analysis, design, and implementation D Independent evaluation, testing, and certification Independent evaluation, testing and certification SEC29 separates developer product/evidence work, evaluator examination/testing and the certification body’s review/decision. D names that evaluation-and-certification process. Development/deployment, patching and security design are related lifecycle activities but do not themselves constitute independent examination and the subsequent scoped certification decision. A incorrect Development/testing/deployment is a general software lifecycle and omits independent certification review. B incorrect Risk assessment and patching are administration/security operations rather than the full independent evaluation process. C incorrect Requirements/design/implementation are development activities that supply evidence, not the independent evaluation decision. D correct Independent examination/testing followed by certification review matches the process and roles in SEC29.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 91 · AM0548
records.text: AM0548 Question 91 SEC29 Under Common Criteria, which role oversees and reviews an independent product evaluation and issues the certification decision? Distinguish requirements, technical evaluation, evidence and certification decisions. A International Organization for Standardization (ISO) B National Security Agency (NSA) C National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) D The certification body of the applicable evaluation scheme The certification body of the applicable evaluation scheme Evaluators examine evidence, test the target and analyze vulnerabilities against its stated claims. The applicable scheme’s certification body oversees or reviews that evaluation and issues the certification decision. CCRA concerns mutual recognition rather than acting as a worldwide testing laboratory. The answer names the responsible scheme role instead of assigning a universal responsibility to one national organization without a jurisdiction or scheme being specified. A incorrect ISO’s name alone does not identify the applicable scheme certification body. B incorrect NSA’s name alone does not identify the applicable scheme certification body. C incorrect NIST’s name alone does not identify the applicable scheme certification body. D correct This is the oversight and certification-decision role specified here.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 92 · AM0549
records.text: AM0549 Question 92 SEC28 SEC29 What is the goal of security functionality evaluation in trusted operating systems? Separate security-policy enforcement and assurance from ordinary OS features. A To assess the system's resistance to external attacks B To evaluate the system's ability to protect sensitive information C To analyze the system's performance and resource utilization D To identify potential vulnerabilities and weaknesses in the system Evaluate claimed protection of sensitive information Functionality evaluation addresses whether claimed security behavior performs its intended protection, while assurance concerns confidence in that implementation. B most directly states that protection capability. External-attack resistance is narrower, performance is not security functionality, and weakness discovery is the vulnerability-analysis aspect rather than the complete functional goal. A incorrect Resistance to external attacks is only a subset and omits internal threats and broader claimed security behavior. B correct Assessing the ability to protect sensitive information matches evaluation of claimed security functionality. C incorrect Generic performance/resource use is not the security-functionality goal described. D incorrect Weakness identification is vulnerability analysis, a related evaluation activity rather than the overall functionality goal.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 93 · AM0550
records.text: AM0550 Question 93 SEC28 SEC29 What is the assurance level in the evaluation of trusted operating systems? Separate security-policy enforcement and assurance from ordinary OS features. A The level of protection provided by the system's security controls B The level of confidence in the system's security claims and implementation C The level of user satisfaction with the system's performance D The level of compliance with industry standards and regulations Confidence in security claims and implementation Assurance describes justified confidence that controls implement their claims; SEC28 states that distinction and SEC29 describes increasing evaluation rigor. B matches confidence in implementation. It must not be confused with the number or strength of functions, user satisfaction or generic compliance. Products with different scopes cannot be ranked automatically by assurance number alone. A incorrect Protection functionality is what controls do; assurance is confidence in the evidence and implementation. B correct Assurance is justified confidence in security claims and their implementation. C incorrect User satisfaction with performance is not security assurance. D incorrect Generic compliance is not the defined confidence measure or evaluation rigor represented by assurance.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 94 · AM0551
records.text: AM0551 Question 94 SEC27 SEC29 What is the role of vulnerability analysis in the independent evaluation of operating systems? Trace timing over shared state or distinguish finding a weakness from demonstrating consequences. A To identify potential weaknesses and vulnerabilities in the system B To analyze the system's performance and resource utilization C To assess the system's resistance to external attacks D To evaluate the system's ability to protect sensitive information To identify potential weaknesses and vulnerabilities in the system Vulnerability assessment explicitly locates and reports vulnerabilities and pen testing identifies weaknesses/strengths (PDF p.10). Thus identifying weaknesses is the directly supported purpose of vulnerability analysis, including when used within an evaluation. A correct Locating weaknesses directly matches the stated assessment task. See PDF p.10. B incorrect Performance/resource utilization is not the stated vulnerability-finding task. See PDF p.10. C incorrect Attack resistance is a broader test concern; locating weaknesses is the direct analysis function asked. See PDF p.10. D incorrect Protecting sensitive information is the broader security goal, not the immediate vulnerability-analysis output. See PDF p.10.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 95 · AM0552
records.text: AM0552 Question 95 SEC29 What is the purpose of certification in the evaluation of trusted operating systems? Distinguish requirements, technical evaluation, evidence and certification decisions. A To ensure compliance with industry standards and regulations B To guarantee absolute security and protection against all threats C To provide a warranty for the system's performance and reliability D To demonstrate that the system meets specific security requirements Demonstrate conformance to specified security requirements Certification records a reviewed decision about a scoped product/configuration meeting specified claims. D fits that purpose. The decision is not an unlimited guarantee against attacks, a performance warranty or proof of every industry/regulatory requirement. SEC29’s scope qualification is essential to interpreting what the certificate actually establishes. A incorrect Generic industry/regulatory compliance exceeds the specific scoped security claims established by certification. B incorrect Certification does not guarantee absolute security or protection against all threats. C incorrect A security certificate is not a warranty of general performance and reliability. D correct Certification demonstrates satisfaction of specified security requirements within the evaluated scope/configuration.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 96 · AM0553
records.text: AM0553 Question 96 SEC29 What is the significance of independent evaluation in trusted operating systems? Distinguish requirements, technical evaluation, evidence and certification decisions. A It guarantees absolute security and protection against all threats. B It ensures compliance with industry standards and regulations. C It provides assurance that the system is immune to all vulnerabilities. D It increases confidence in the system's security and reliability. Increase justified confidence in security and reliability Independent examination and testing add evidence supporting confidence in stated security behavior and reliability within scope. D gives that qualified benefit. SEC29 rejects the inference that certification makes a product immune to future attacks; it also does not establish every unrelated regulatory obligation. Confidence increases through evidence, rather than becoming an absolute guarantee. A incorrect Independent evaluation cannot guarantee absolute security against every threat. B incorrect It does not automatically establish compliance with all industry standards and regulations. C incorrect Tests and evidence cannot prove immunity to every possible vulnerability. D correct Independent scrutiny increases justified confidence in the product’s scoped security and dependable operation.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 97 · AM0554
records.text: AM0554 Question 97 SEC30 SEC01 Which listed properties are fundamental database-security goals, rather than operational growth or transaction-execution capabilities? Select all that apply. Match the control's scope to the disclosure or access path. A Availability B Concurrency C Scalability D Confidentiality Availability; Confidentiality Database security includes confidentiality, integrity, availability and accountability together. Availability and confidentiality are both present in the choices and must be selected. Concurrency concerns overlapping transactions and can require integrity-preserving control, while scalability concerns capacity growth. These capabilities matter to a database system but do not replace the named security goals. The revised selection wording preserves both valid goals instead of choosing confidentiality arbitrarily. A correct Availability is explicitly part of database security. B incorrect Concurrency is an execution capability, not a named security goal in this taxonomy. C incorrect Scalability describes growth capability rather than a named security goal. D correct Confidentiality is explicitly part of database security.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 98 · AM0555
records.text: AM0555 Question 98 SEC31 SEC30 SEC09 SEC24 Which technique ensures the reliability of a database system? Separate valid data states, permission to update and recovery. A Data encryption B Data replication C Role-based access control D Intrusion detection system Data replication can improve service availability Among these options replication supplies alternate service capacity, supporting database reliability/availability when failover and failure domains are properly handled. It does not guarantee correctness or replace backups; malicious changes can replicate too. Encryption, RBAC and IDS serve confidentiality, access restriction and detection rather than redundant database service capacity. A incorrect Encryption primarily protects confidentiality rather than providing alternate database service capacity. B correct Replication can supply alternate service capacity, with reliability dependent on failover and independent failure handling. C incorrect RBAC controls permitted operations; it does not itself provide redundant database capacity or crash recovery. D incorrect An IDS detects suspicious activity and does not itself maintain database availability after component failure.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 99 · AM0556
records.text: AM0556 Question 99 SEC31 SEC01 Which option gives the most direct definition of database integrity as a property of stored data, rather than a broader recovery activity, confidentiality control or monitoring activity? Separate valid data states, permission to update and recovery. A Ensuring data consistency and accuracy B Protecting data from unauthorized access C Preventing data loss or corruption D Monitoring and detecting security breaches Ensuring data consistency and accuracy Integrity concerns valid, accurate and consistent data and valid state transitions. A states that property directly. Preventing corruption can contribute to integrity, but the combined loss-or-corruption wording also includes availability and recovery concerns, so it is a broader activity rather than the most direct definition requested. Access protection can serve confidentiality, and monitoring detects events; neither describes the data-validity property as precisely as A. A correct Accuracy and consistency directly characterize the requested integrity property. B incorrect Generic access protection is broader and does not directly define data validity. C incorrect Preventing loss or corruption is a broader protection/recovery activity, though preventing corruption contributes to integrity. D incorrect Monitoring is a detection activity rather than the property of valid data.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 100 · AM0557
records.text: AM0557 Question 100 SEC30 SEC02 SEC09 Which controls directly restrict disclosure of database contents in their applicable scopes, rather than primarily reviewing evidence after activity? Select all that apply. Match the control's scope to the disclosure or access path. A Using strong access controls B Implementing encryption techniques C Enforcing secure data transmission protocols D Conducting regular security audits Using strong access controls; Implementing encryption techniques; Enforcing secure data transmission protocols Access controls restrict which subjects can read data. Encryption at rest protects stolen storage when keys remain separate, and protected transmission secures data on the connection. All three can directly contribute to secrecy in their respective scopes, though none prevents every disclosure. Audits principally inspect evidence and reveal problems rather than themselves concealing contents or enforcing every access. The stated direct-control distinction makes A, B and C the valid selection. A correct Access rules can directly restrict unauthorized readers. B correct Encryption protects content in its applicable scope when keys are properly separated. C correct Protected transport restricts disclosure on the communication channel. D incorrect Audits primarily review evidence rather than directly concealing content or enforcing each read.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 101 · AM0558
records.text: AM0558 Question 101 SEC32 What is inference control in database security? Consider what can be inferred from allowed outputs as well as direct access. A Controlling the flow of information within a database B Enforcing access controls based on user roles C Preventing unauthorized data leakage through inference D Detecting and mitigating security breaches in real-time Prevent protected facts being inferred from allowed outputs Inference control addresses indirect disclosure, such as subtracting a known salary from a two-person total to learn the protected value. SEC32 describes restricting/coarsening outputs and tracking queries to reduce that leakage. C names the specific purpose, while generic information flow, roles and real-time detection do not identify inference from combinations of permitted results. A incorrect Information-flow control is broader; this option omits inference from permitted outputs and auxiliary knowledge. B incorrect Role-based access alone does not prevent inference from otherwise permitted query results. C correct Inference control limits indirect disclosure of protected facts through combinations of outputs and outside knowledge. D incorrect Real-time breach detection is a separate incident-monitoring function rather than inference control.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 102 · AM0559
records.text: AM0559 Question 102 SEC32 SEC30 SEC24 How can multi-level databases ensure data confidentiality? Consider what can be inferred from allowed outputs as well as direct access. A By using data encryption techniques B By implementing mandatory access controls C By conducting regular security audits D By employing intrusion detection systems Mandatory label/clearance access controls SEC32 distinguishes multilevel databases by mandatory label/clearance restrictions, including controlled read/write flows. B names that mechanism. Encryption, audits and IDS can support security, but none alone enforces the multilevel policy. Even mandatory controls need consideration of inference and covert channels rather than a blanket confidentiality guarantee. A incorrect Encryption can protect stored/transmitted content but does not itself enforce multilevel classification/clearance rules. B correct Mandatory controls compare clearances/classifications and enforce the multilevel disclosure policy. C incorrect Audits review activity and controls; they do not themselves enforce every multilevel access decision. D incorrect IDS detects suspicious activity but does not implement the database’s mandatory label policy.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 103 · AM0560
records.text: AM0560 Question 103 SEC01 SEC30 Which security requirement is critical for protecting sensitive data in a database? Identify the property harmed: disclosure, improper change, unavailable service or lack of reliable attribution. A Availability B Scalability C Confidentiality D Concurrency Confidentiality Protecting sensitive data from disclosure requires confidentiality, which the module also calls privacy or secrecy (PDF p.3). Other system properties do not specifically express that disclosure restriction. A incorrect Availability protects timely authorized access rather than secrecy. See PDF p.3. B incorrect Scalability is not the disclosed-data protection goal. See PDF p.3. C correct Confidentiality is the stated secrecy/disclosure protection goal. See PDF p.3. D incorrect Concurrency is not the stated secrecy/disclosure protection goal. See PDF p.3.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 104 · AM0561
records.text: AM0561 Question 104 SEC30 SEC12 SEC01 What is the purpose of data encryption in database security? Match the control's scope to the disclosure or access path. A To ensure data availability B To protect data integrity C To achieve data secrecy D To control data access To achieve data secrecy The module equates confidentiality with secrecy (PDF p.3) and explains shared-key encryption so an adversary cannot understand the contents (p.7). Applying that transformation to database contents protects their secrecy. A incorrect Encryption alone does not ensure that data remains accessible on time. See PDF p.3, PDF p.7. B incorrect Plain encryption is not, by itself, the unauthorized-modification definition of integrity. See PDF p.3, PDF p.7. C correct Rendering data unintelligible without the key serves secrecy. See PDF p.3, PDF p.7. D incorrect Access-control permission decisions are a separate subject/object mechanism. See PDF p.3, PDF p.7.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 105 · AM0562
records.text: AM0562 Question 105 SEC09 SEC31 SEC24 Which permission mechanisms can prevent unauthorized database updates, while constraints and transaction logic separately enforce the validity of authorized changes? Select all that apply. Identify subject, object and permitted operation before comparing policy models. A Access control lists B Data replication C Intrusion detection systems D Role-based access control Access control lists; Role-based access control ACLs associate objects with allowed subjects or actions, while RBAC assigns update permissions through roles. Both can prevent updates by unauthorized subjects and therefore contribute to integrity. They do not by themselves establish that every authorized state change satisfies business rules; constraints and transaction logic address that separate requirement. Replication may copy bad updates, and intrusion detection reveals activity rather than serving as the requested permission mechanism. A correct ACLs can deny update permission to unauthorized subjects. B incorrect Replication copies state and is not an update-permission mechanism. C incorrect Intrusion detection observes or alerts rather than defining update permissions. D correct RBAC can restrict update permission through role assignments.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 106 · AM0563
records.text: AM0563 Question 106 SEC32 What is the primary purpose of inference control in database security? Consider what can be inferred from allowed outputs as well as direct access. A To prevent unauthorized data modification B To enforce secure data transmission C To detect and prevent unauthorized data leakage D To control data access based on user roles Prevent unauthorized information leakage through inference Inference control concerns disclosure derived from combinations of permitted outputs and outside knowledge rather than direct unauthorized writes or merely role membership. SEC32’s salary example shows why direct column restrictions are insufficient. C states this leakage-prevention goal; secure transmission and role-based decisions address different channels or controls. A incorrect Unauthorized modification concerns integrity, whereas inference control targets indirect disclosure. B incorrect Secure transport protects a connection but does not prevent inference from authorized query results. C correct Detecting/reducing unauthorized information leakage from combined results is the inference-control goal. D incorrect Role permissions alone do not stop users inferring protected facts from outputs they may access.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 107 · CS0174
records.text: CS0174 Question 107 SEC06 SEC03 SEC04 XYZ Company is attacked by intruders causing system crashes, slowing down of services and denying services to targeted users. The company is attacked by? Match the resource bottleneck or wireless mechanism to the relevant protection layer. A Access attack B Viruses C Information gathering D Denial of Services (DoS) Denial of Services (DoS) The decisive symptom is denial of service to intended users; that is the module’s DoS definition (PDF pp.3,5). Crashes and slowing can implement that outcome without uniquely identifying malware. A incorrect Access attacks concern gaining control, not the specific denial outcome. See PDF p.3, PDF p.5. B incorrect A virus could be a cause, but no virus evidence is stated. See PDF p.3, PDF p.5. C incorrect Information gathering does not by itself deny users service. See PDF p.3, PDF p.5. D correct Denial of Services directly names the reported blocked access. See PDF p.3, PDF p.5.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 108 · CS0175
records.text: CS0175 Question 108 SEC03 Which one of the following is wrongly coupled about passive (offline) and active (online) attacks? Classify the action actually described and distinguish observation, alteration, disruption and identity claims. A Active attack -> add or delete messages B Active attack -> traffic analysis C Passive attack -> monitoring traffic D Passive attack -> obtain message contents Active attack -> traffic analysis PDF p.4 defines passive attacks as learning information without affecting resources and active attacks as alteration/effect on operation. Merely analyzing observed traffic fits passive learning, so B is the wrong pairing. A incorrect Adding/deleting messages changes resources and is active. See PDF p.4. B correct Traffic analysis, when only observing, is passive rather than active. See PDF p.4. C incorrect Monitoring without interference is passive. See PDF p.4. D incorrect Obtaining contents without changing resources is passive. See PDF p.4.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 109 · CS0176
records.text: CS0176 Question 109 SEC16 Which one of the following is NOT correct about symmetric key? Distinguish shared-key architecture, key distribution and bulk-data use. A It requires sender and receiver to share a common secret key B Previous key cannot be used for a new key C Trusted third party can generate and deliver keys D Repetitive key change is encouraged to limit data being compromised Previous key cannot be used for a new key PDF p.8 explicitly permits use of a previous key to encrypt a new key, so B contradicts a stated symmetric key-distribution alternative. A and C are explicit, while session-key disposal supports limiting reuse. A incorrect Sharing a common secret is explicitly required. See PDF p.7, PDF p.8. B correct B denies prior-key use that p.8 explicitly allows for distributing a new key. See PDF p.7, PDF p.8. C incorrect A third party can select and deliver keys to both participants. See PDF p.7, PDF p.8. D incorrect Discarding session keys after one session supports limiting key reuse and exposure. See PDF p.7, PDF p.8.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 110 · CS0177
records.text: CS0177 Question 110 SEC05 SEC06 Which one of the following is NOT a wireless attack? Identify the trust claim or communication mapping being abused. A Bluesnarfing B Phishing C Rogue access point D Bluejacking Phishing is not specifically a wireless attack SEC06 defines Bluetooth information theft as bluesnarfing, unsolicited Bluetooth messages as bluejacking and rogue access points as wireless service impersonation/bypass. Phishing is social deception across many media, not a wireless-specific mechanism. It can be delivered over a wireless connection, but that transport does not make its defining attack category wireless. A incorrect Bluesnarfing steals information over Bluetooth and is specifically a wireless attack mechanism. B correct Phishing is medium-independent trusted-source deception rather than a wireless-specific mechanism. C incorrect A rogue access point imitates or bypasses approved wireless service. D incorrect Bluejacking sends unsolicited Bluetooth messages, making it a wireless-specific attack category.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 111 · CS0178
records.text: CS0178 Question 111 SEC11 Considering a vulnerability shared by identically configured components, which statement is NOT correct? Interpret diversity’s benefits as possible reductions in common-mode compromise, not guarantees of minimum loss. Start with the stated attacker path or physical hazard and the limits of each control. A Non-uniform configurations may reduce loss from a vulnerability shared by one configuration B Uniform configurations can increase predictability C A vulnerability in the identical shared configuration cannot affect the other identically configured components D Diverse configurations may avoid exposing every resource to the same configuration-specific vulnerability A vulnerability in the identical shared configuration cannot affect the other identically configured components Uniform configurations simplify prediction and administration, but a vulnerability in the shared configuration can create correlated failures across components. Diversity may reduce that common-mode exposure, although it increases administrative cost and does not guarantee minimum loss. Option C wrongly denies the possibility of the same configuration vulnerability affecting peers. The other statements now describe qualified benefits rather than absolute guarantees. A incorrect Diversity can reduce exposure to a vulnerability limited to one configuration. B incorrect Uniformity can simplify prediction and administration. C correct Identical shared vulnerabilities can affect peer components, so this denial is false. D incorrect Diversity can reduce common-mode exposure without guaranteeing immunity.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 112 · CS0184
records.text: CS0184 Question 112 SEC24 SEC23 SEC04 SEC-S03 ______ is a system that monitors traffic into and out of a network and automatically alerts personnel when suspicious traffic patterns occur. Separate observation from blocking and sensor placement from detection method. A Anti-virus Software B IDS C Firewall D Router Intrusion detection system Traffic observation followed by alerts about suspicious patterns is the IDS function in SEC24. The stem does not require inline blocking. Antivirus, firewalls and routers have different primary functions, though products can combine capabilities. B identifies the functional system described without assuming a firewall always detects every intrusion. A incorrect Antivirus targets malicious software and is not the generic traffic-pattern alerting system named in the note. B correct An IDS observes traffic/activity and alerts personnel to suspected intrusion patterns. C incorrect A firewall primarily enforces traffic policy; observation-and-alerting specifically identifies intrusion detection. D incorrect Routing selects packet next hops rather than defining suspicious-pattern detection and alerts.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 113 · NS0327
records.text: NS0327 Question 113 SEC05 SEC03 SEC06 Suppose Mr. Negesa might act as Mr. Dereje and send message to Registrar X, the registrar might be lead to believe that message indeed come from Mr. Dereje. What types of attack Mr. Negesa has committed? Identify the trust claim or communication mapping being abused. A Denial of service B Modification of message C Masquerade D Replay Masquerade Negesa presents the message as coming from Dereje, so the registrar attributes it to the wrong person. SEC05 defines that false identity claim as masquerade. No service exhaustion, alteration of a prior message or reuse of an old valid message is stated; those attack mechanisms must not be inferred from impersonation alone. A incorrect The scenario does not deny service or exhaust resources. B incorrect No prior message is modified; the central behavior is a false sender identity. C correct Claiming Dereje’s identity to fool the registrar is masquerade. D incorrect Replay requires reusing a valid old message, which the scenario does not describe.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 114 · NS0343
records.text: NS0343 Question 114 SEC23 SEC24 SEC22 Which one of following monitors incoming and outgoing network traffic and decides whether to allow or block specific traffic based on a defined set of security rules? Identify which traffic is mediated and what information drives the device's decisions. A Intrusion detection system (IDS) B Proxy server C Virtual Private network D Firewall Firewall The described allow/block decisions follow a defined traffic policy, the firewall function in SEC23. IDS observes/alerts, a proxy mediates application requests and a VPN supplies logical private connectivity. A proxy may implement policy in some deployments, but the generic boundary traffic-policy device directly named by the definition is a firewall. A incorrect An IDS observes and alerts rather than being defined by enforcing allow/block rules. B incorrect A proxy mediates application exchanges; the general traffic-policy enforcement definition specifically names a firewall. C incorrect A VPN extends private connectivity and is not inherently a generic rule-based traffic filter. D correct A firewall enforces allow/block traffic policy based on configured rules.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 115 · NS0361
records.text: NS0361 Question 115 SEC01 What is the difference between confidentiality, integrity, and availability? Give an example of a breach of each. Identify the property harmed: disclosure, improper change, unavailable service or lack of reliable attribution. Confidentiality limits disclosure: copying a private credit-card database breaches it. Integrity preserves correctness: changing an account balance improperly breaches it. Availability provides timely usable service: crashing a server or starving resources breaches it. SEC01 defines the three goals by the property harmed, not by one fixed attack label. Copying can breach secrecy without changing the original; alteration harms correctness; denied service harms availability. One incident can violate several goals, so these examples illustrate the primary property rather than mutually exclusive incident classes.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 116 · NS0362
records.text: NS0362 Question 116 SEC07 SEC08 Why is multi-factor authentication more secure than passwords alone? Separate identity claims from proof, and factor type from factor count. MFA requires independent factor classes, such as a password plus a possessed card or biometric. Stealing the password alone then does not satisfy the other proof. Password plus PIN is still knowledge-only, not two independent factors. SEC07 distinguishes knowledge, possession and inherence. Combining classes adds a separate proof rather than merely another secret from the same class. That reduces dependence on a password alone, although implementation, recovery channels and compromise of the additional factor still matter; MFA is not a guarantee against every attack.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 117 · NS0363
records.text: NS0363 Question 117 SEC18 SEC16 What is the difference between symmetric and asymmetric encryption? Why do we use both? Identify the intended recipient or signer and separate confidentiality from verification. Symmetric encryption shares a secret key and efficiently protects bulk data. Asymmetric encryption uses a recipient public/private pair: encrypt to the authenticated public key and decrypt with the private key. Hybrid systems use public-key mechanisms to establish a symmetric secret, then symmetric protection for content. SEC16 supplies the efficient shared-secret model; SEC18 supplies recipient key direction and hybrid composition. Public keys ease distribution only with authentic identity bindings. Combining them addresses distribution/authentication and bulk-data efficiency without claiming either family is inherently more secure or assigning fixed speed ratios.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 118 · NS0364
records.text: NS0364 Question 118 SEC06 SEC03 What is a DDoS attack and how does it differ from a DoS attack? Match the resource bottleneck or wireless mechanism to the relevant protection layer. DoS exhausts or disables a resource so authorized users lose usable service. DDoS is DoS launched through multiple distributed sources, often bots or reflected/amplified responses. The distinction is source distribution, not a different security goal: both primarily harm availability. SEC06 defines the resource-exhaustion/disabling mechanism and distributed sources. Multiple sources can stress different bottlenecks, so appropriate responses include rate limits, filtering and upstream capacity controls. The number of sources does not imply the attacker obtained control of the victim; the demonstrated harm is unavailable service.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 119 · NS0365
records.text: NS0365 Question 119 SEC26 Why is SQL injection dangerous? How is it prevented? Locate where untrusted data can become instructions and where they execute. SQL injection lets untrusted input alter SQL syntax through unsafe string construction, changing query behavior or affected rows. Use prepared statements with bound data values, allow-list nonparameterizable identifiers, and give the application account minimal privileges. Stored procedures/ORMs must also avoid unsafe dynamic SQL. The danger is crossing the data-versus-query-syntax boundary, not merely accepting an unusual string. Parameter binding keeps supplied values as data, while identifier allow-lists handle structure that cannot be bound. Restricting database rights limits impact. SEC26 warns that a procedure or ORM name alone does not make dynamically concatenated SQL safe.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 120 · NS0366
records.text: NS0366 Question 120 SEC24 What is the difference between IDS and IPS? Separate observation from blocking and sensor placement from detection method. An IDS observes activity and alerts about suspected attacks. An IPS can actively block traffic, usually inline. Detection can use signatures or anomaly baselines; neither system guarantees every attack is detected or every alert represents a real attack. The key distinction in SEC24 is observation/alerting versus enforcement. Host sensors examine host events and network sensors inspect traffic, independently of that IDS/IPS action distinction. Inline prevention adds a blocking decision; false positives can then deny legitimate activity, so detection context and policy remain important.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 121 · NS0417
records.text: NS0417 Question 121 SEC01 What are the three primary security goals known as the CIA triad? Identify the property harmed: disclosure, improper change, unavailable service or lack of reliable attribution. The CIA triad is confidentiality, integrity and availability: restrict unauthorized disclosure, prevent improper changes, and provide timely usable service to authorized users. SEC01 defines each goal by a separate property. Secrecy concerns who learns information, integrity concerns correct information/changes, and availability concerns usable service. These goals can be harmed together; satisfying one does not establish the others. Authentication and authorization support protection but are not replacements for the three CIA goals.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 122 · NS0418
records.text: NS0418 Question 122 SEC02 What is a 'vulnerability' in the context of computer security? Distinguish weaknesses, potential harmful events, actual attempts and the effect of a control. A vulnerability is an exploitable weakness in a system or its protection. It differs from a threat, which is a potentially harmful circumstance, and an attack, which is an actual attempt to cause harm. SEC02 separates weakness, potential harm and attempted exploitation. A software flaw can exist without an attack taking place; controls reduce likelihood or impact. Calling every flaw an active attack would erase that distinction and misstate what a vulnerability finding actually proves.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 123 · NS0419
records.text: NS0419 Question 123 SEC02 What is the difference between 'prevention' and 'detection' in computer security? Distinguish weaknesses, potential harmful events, actual attempts and the effect of a control. Prevention attempts to block a harmful event; detection reveals that an event or suspicious activity has occurred. Encryption can prevent disclosure, while audit logs supply detective/accountability evidence. Recovery is a further function that restores safe operation after damage. SEC02 classifies controls by effect rather than by whether they are physical or technical. A preventive control can fail, and a detective control may then expose the event. Detection does not itself imply blocking; combining these stages supports a fuller protection and response process.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 124 · NS0420
records.text: NS0420 Question 124 SEC01 SEC20 Which security property ensures that a message was not altered by unauthorized individuals? Identify the property harmed: disclosure, improper change, unavailable service or lack of reliable attribution. Integrity is the property that protects a message against unauthorized or improper alteration. A suitable keyed MAC or digital signature can provide integrity evidence under the relevant key/trust assumptions. SEC01 defines integrity by correctness of content and changes. SEC20 explains that an unkeyed hash alone requires a trusted reference because an attacker can recompute it after modification. Therefore the property is integrity, while the mechanism used to establish it must be selected with an appropriate trust model.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 125 · NS0421
records.text: NS0421 Question 125 SEC01 What is Data Security focused on protecting? Identify the property harmed: disclosure, improper change, unavailable service or lack of reliable attribution. Data security protects information at rest, in use and in transit against unauthorized disclosure, improper changes and loss of usable access. It includes accidental corruption as well as deliberate attacks. SEC01 explicitly covers the information lifecycle and accidental as well as intentional harm. Protection is broader than encrypting network traffic: storage, processing and access/recovery controls also matter. The CIA goals describe complementary properties, so secrecy alone is not the whole of data security.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 126 · NS0422
records.text: NS0422 Question 126 SEC03 What are the '4D's' of security threats? Classify the action actually described and distinguish observation, alteration, disruption and identity claims. The four are disclosure, deception, disruption and usurpation. Disclosure exposes information; deception supplies false material or beliefs; disruption harms service; usurpation means unauthorized control. SEC03 explicitly names this classification and distinguishes disruption from control. A denial-of-service event demonstrates disruption and availability loss, but does not by itself prove the attacker usurped the victim. The categories describe kinds of harm rather than requiring every attack to produce all four.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 127 · NS0423
records.text: NS0423 Question 127 SEC03 What is the key difference between passive and active attacks? Classify the action actually described and distinguish observation, alteration, disruption and identity claims. Passive attacks observe without changing the exchange, such as sniffing or traffic analysis. Active attacks inject, modify, replay or disrupt communications or service. Passive/active does not mean offline/online. The distinction is intervention in the target exchange, as SEC03 explains. Traffic analysis can infer relationships from timing and sizes even with encrypted content, so passive observation still creates risk. Neither category is universally easy to detect or prevent; those claims depend on the mechanism and deployed controls.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 128 · NS0424
records.text: NS0424 Question 128 SEC06 SEC01 What is a Denial of Service (DoS) attack? Match the resource bottleneck or wireless mechanism to the relevant protection layer. A denial-of-service attack exhausts or disables a resource so authorized users cannot obtain timely usable service. Examples include incomplete-handshake state exhaustion or resolver query flooding. Distributed DoS uses multiple sources. SEC06 identifies the mechanism as service exhaustion/disabling. SEC01 connects unavailable or unusable service to availability loss. The attacker need not alter stored data or gain control of the target; the resource bottleneck and service effect distinguish this attack from other harms.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 129 · NS0425
records.text: NS0425 Question 129 SEC03 What does 'snooping' refer to in network security? Classify the action actually described and distinguish observation, alteration, disruption and identity claims. Snooping is unauthorized observation or interception of information, such as reading captured network traffic. When it only observes the exchange without modifying it, it is a passive attack against confidentiality. SEC03 groups interception with observing/copying data and lists sniffing among passive attacks. This differs from modification or fabrication, which change or inject material. Encryption can hide content while traffic timing/size still supports traffic analysis, so observing communication metadata can remain informative.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 130 · NS0426
records.text: NS0426 Question 130 SEC01 SEC20 What is 'repudiation' in computer security? Identify the property harmed: disclosure, improper change, unavailable service or lack of reliable attribution. Repudiation is denying involvement, such as denying having sent or received a message. Non-repudiation supplies evidence supporting origin or receipt under identity/key-custody assumptions; it does not make a person physically unable to deny an action. SEC01 frames non-repudiation as evidentiary support rather than an absolute ban on denial. SEC20 explains why signatures can support origin/integrity while shared-key MACs limit third-party attribution because both holders can create them. The strength of the evidence depends on trustworthy identities, keys and records.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 131 · NS0427
records.text: NS0427 Question 131 SEC04 What distinguishes a worm from a computer virus? Separate propagation, disguise and payload when classifying malicious software. A virus attaches to a host program/document and spreads when the infected host executes. A worm replicates independently, commonly across networks. The distinction is host dependency, not a universal ranking of speed or required user action. SEC04 defines propagation mechanisms separately from payloads and disguise. A malware package may contain several components, so a worm can also carry another malicious function. That does not change the independent-replication distinction or justify assuming every worm always spreads faster than every virus.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 132 · NS0428
records.text: NS0428 Question 132 SEC04 What is a Trojan Horse in cybersecurity? Separate propagation, disguise and payload when classifying malicious software. A Trojan horse presents apparently useful or legitimate behavior while hiding malicious activity. Unlike virus/worm labels, the definition concerns disguise and does not require self-replication. SEC04 distinguishes propagation, disguise and payload properties. A Trojan may contain other malware components, but merely looking useful while concealing harmful behavior is the identifying clue. It should not be defined as a worm simply because its payload might later spread.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 133 · NS0429
records.text: NS0429 Question 133 SEC04 What is a Logic Bomb? Separate propagation, disguise and payload when classifying malicious software. A logic bomb is malicious code that waits for a specified trigger before activating its payload. The defining feature is conditional activation, rather than a particular replication method or inevitable immediate execution. SEC04 identifies the trigger dependency. Other malware terms describe independent replication, host attachment, disguise or hidden access; those properties can coexist with a triggered payload. Thus the answer identifies when the harmful behavior activates without inventing a particular date, event or payload not supplied by the question.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 134 · NS0430
records.text: NS0430 Question 134 SEC03 SEC27 What is the difference between a White Hat and Black Hat hacker? Classify the action actually described and distinguish observation, alteration, disruption and identity claims. White-hat security testing is authorized and stays within agreed scope. Black-hat activity is malicious or unauthorized. Technical skill or the word hacker alone does not establish legality. SEC03 makes authorization and scope the decisive distinction. Good claimed intentions do not create permission to test another system, and insider/outsider status describes a different dimension. An authorized tester must remain within the approved activity; the label alone cannot excuse actions outside that scope.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 135 · NS0431
records.text: NS0431 Question 135 SEC05 What is phishing? Identify the trust claim or communication mapping being abused. Phishing impersonates a trusted source to trick someone into revealing secrets or performing an unsafe action. Spear phishing targets a particular person. Verify suspicious requests using an independently known channel. SEC05 defines the deception mechanism and the targeted variant. It is a human-trust attack, not necessarily a wireless mechanism or direct password-guessing algorithm. Independent verification matters because replying through the attacker-supplied contact path can preserve the impersonation rather than test it.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 136 · NS0432
records.text: NS0432 Question 136 SEC12 SEC20 SEC16 What is the primary goal of cryptography? Trace message transformations and separate data, keys, algorithms and codebreaking. Cryptography protects information using key-based mathematical mechanisms. Encryption primarily conceals meaning; suitable MACs/signatures or authenticated encryption additionally support integrity and authenticity. There is no single confidentiality-only description that captures every cryptographic service. SEC12 defines encryption/decryption, while SEC20 distinguishes hashes, MACs and signatures. These mechanisms address different goals and assumptions: a signature does not conceal content, and an unkeyed hash alone does not establish authentic origin. The goal must be matched to the mechanism rather than treating all cryptography as encryption.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 137 · NS0433
records.text: NS0433 Question 137 SEC18 SEC16 SEC12 What is the difference between symmetric and asymmetric key cryptography? Identify the intended recipient or signer and separate confidentiality from verification. Symmetric cryptography uses a shared secret between parties. Asymmetric confidentiality uses an authenticated public encryption key and corresponding private decryption key; signatures instead use a private signing key and public verification key. Not every public-key algorithm supports encryption. SEC16 gives the shared-secret model and SEC18 the asymmetric key directions. Symmetric keys require secure distribution and can efficiently protect bulk data. Public keys simplify distribution only when their identity bindings are authentic; hybrid protocols combine these advantages instead of assuming one family is inherently stronger.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 138 · NS0434
records.text: NS0434 Question 138 SEC13 In Caesar's cipher with a shift of 3, what does the letter 'A' become? Separate symbol replacement from position changes and apply the alphabet and modular direction. A becomes D. With A=0 and shift k=3, C=(0+3) mod26=3, which is D. SEC13 specifies the A=0 through Z=25 convention and forward addition for Caesar encryption. Applying that convention avoids confusing encryption with the reverse decryption shift or using a different numeric alphabet. No wraparound is needed for A, but the modulo rule handles letters near the alphabet end.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 139 · NS0435
records.text: NS0435 Question 139 SEC13 What formula is used for encryption in the Caesar cipher? Separate symbol replacement from position changes and apply the alphabet and modular direction. Using A=0 through Z=25, Caesar encryption is C=(P+k) mod26. Here P is the plaintext letter number, k the shift and C the ciphertext letter number. Decryption subtracts the same shift modulo 26. SEC13 fixes both the numeric alphabet and the direction. Modulo 26 wraps results into the letter range, including negative intermediate values in decryption. A stated shift of 3 therefore maps A to D; reversing the sign would describe decryption instead of the requested encryption formula.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 140 · NS0436
records.text: NS0436 Question 140 SEC15 Why is the One-Time Pad considered the most secure cipher? Check the precise ordering or key-use assumptions rather than relying on a cipher's name. A genuine one-time pad has perfect secrecy when its key is independent, uniformly random, secret, at least as long as the message and never reused. Without every condition, a Vernam/XOR construction is not automatically a one-time pad. SEC15 makes the guarantee conditional, not a blanket ranking of every cipher implementation. Pad reuse exposes C1 XOR C2=P1 XOR P2 and leaks relationships between plaintexts. Key delivery and storage are substantial practical costs even though the ideal construction supplies perfect secrecy under its assumptions.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 141 · NS0437
records.text: NS0437 Question 141 SEC13 What is the main weakness of a monoalphabetic substitution cipher? Separate symbol replacement from position changes and apply the alphabet and modular direction. One fixed substitution throughout a message preserves letter-frequency patterns, enabling statistical analysis despite a large nominal key space. This is the main weakness of monoalphabetic substitution. SEC13 distinguishes symbol replacement from transposition and stresses that fixed mappings leak patterns. Increasing the nominal number of possible substitution alphabets does not erase language statistics. Classical substitution therefore serves teaching purposes rather than providing modern data protection, even if exhaustive enumeration of every alphabet is impractical.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 142 · NS0438
records.text: NS0438 Question 142 SEC14 How does the Vigenere cipher improve on monoalphabetic ciphers? Identify the cipher's unit, key structure and assumptions before judging its strength. Vigenère applies position-dependent shifts from a key, so the same plaintext letter can encrypt differently at different positions. That reduces the single fixed-substitution frequency pattern, but repeating a short key still leaks periodic structure. SEC14 gives C_i=(P_i+K_i) mod26 and explains the position dependence. The improvement is multiple mappings rather than a guarantee of modern security. A periodic key allows related positions to share the same shift, preserving exploitable regularities instead of eliminating statistical structure altogether.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 143 · NS0439
records.text: NS0439 Question 143 SEC12 SEC20 What is steganography and how does it differ from cryptography? Trace message transformations and separate data, keys, algorithms and codebreaking. Steganography conceals the existence of a message by hiding it within other data. Encryption conceals its meaning by transforming plaintext into ciphertext. Cryptography also includes integrity/authenticity mechanisms; it is broader than just encryption. SEC12 states the existence-versus-meaning distinction. Discovering a hidden carrier can defeat concealment of existence without necessarily revealing separately encrypted content. SEC20’s MAC/signature roles further explain why cryptography cannot be reduced to steganography or to secrecy of the communication’s existence.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 144 · NS0440
records.text: NS0440 Question 144 SEC12 What are the five ingredients of cryptography? Trace message transformations and separate data, keys, algorithms and codebreaking. For the conventional symmetric-encryption model, the five ingredients are plaintext, encryption algorithm, secret key, ciphertext and decryption algorithm. This is not a universal inventory of every cryptographic construction. SEC12 supplies this five-part teaching model. Plaintext enters encryption with a secret key, producing ciphertext; decryption recovers the plaintext with the appropriate secret. The qualifier symmetric matters because signature, hash and public-key constructions have different interfaces and cannot all be reduced to this particular five-item list.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 145 · NS0441
records.text: NS0441 Question 145 SEC17 In DES, what is the block size and key size? Track block width, effective key bits and the transformations within a round. DES uses 64-bit data blocks and 56 effective key bits. A commonly stored 64-bit key representation includes eight parity bits, which do not increase the effective key space. DES has 16 Feistel rounds and is a legacy algorithm. SEC17 distinguishes block width from effective key entropy and parity representation. Calling DES a 64-bit-key security level would count nonsecret parity bits as independent choices. The note also warns that DES/triple DES are legacy mechanisms rather than recommendations for new protection.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 146 · NS0442
records.text: NS0442 Question 146 SEC17 Why does DES divide the plaintext into left and right halves? Track block width, effective key bits and the transformations within a round. DES splits its 64-bit block into two 32-bit halves for Feistel rounds: L_i=R_(i-1) and R_i=L_(i-1) XOR f(R_(i-1),K_i). This permits inversion using the same overall structure with reversed round keys, without requiring f to be invertible. SEC17 gives the round equations and inversion property. The old right half becomes the new left half; the old left is mixed with a keyed transformation of the old right. Keeping those relationships allows recovery by reversing the key order rather than independently inverting every S-box/transformation.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 147 · NS0443
records.text: NS0443 Question 147 SEC17 What is the purpose of the S-box in DES? Track block width, effective key bits and the transformations within a round. DES S-boxes provide nonlinear substitution: each of eight boxes maps six input bits to four output bits. The outer two bits select the row and the inner four select the column, giving 32 output bits altogether. SEC17 identifies the S-boxes as the nonlinear component that resists simple linear descriptions. Their six-to-four mapping follows expansion and key mixing, then a permutation rearranges the outputs. They are not merely a reversible bit permutation; Feistel structure supplies overall invertibility without requiring each S-box itself to be invertible.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 148 · NS0444
records.text: NS0444 Question 148 SEC19 In RSA, what are the formulas for encryption and decryption? Check key-generation conditions as well as modular arithmetic. Textbook RSA encrypts c=m^e mod n and decrypts m=c^d mod n, for 0≤m<n. Here n=pq, e is coprime to φ=(p−1)(q−1), and d=e^−1 mod φ. Real RSA additionally requires appropriate standardized padding. SEC19 supplies the formulas and their key-generation preconditions. The modular-inverse condition is necessary for a valid key pair, so arbitrary e values are not acceptable. These arithmetic expressions teach RSA operations; raw unpadded modular exponentiation is not a complete secure deployment recipe.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 149 · NS0445
records.text: NS0445 Question 149 SEC19 In textbook RSA key generation with p=7, q=19 and φ=108, choose the smallest integer e greater than 1 satisfying 1<e<φ and gcd(e,φ)=1. What is e? Check key-generation conditions as well as modular arithmetic. e = 5 The exponent must be greater than one, below 108 and coprime to 108. Testing candidates in increasing order, 2 shares factor 2, 3 shares factor 3 and 4 shares factor 2 with 108. Five shares neither prime factor of 108, so gcd(5,108)=1. It is therefore the smallest admissible exponent. Other values can also be admissible, but the explicit smallest-value rule makes this open-ended answer unique.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 150 · NS0446
records.text: NS0446 Question 150 SEC14 What is the Playfair cipher and what unique element does its grid contain? Identify the cipher's unit, key structure and assumptions before judging its strength. Playfair is a digraph substitution cipher using a keyed 5×5 letter grid, commonly combining I and J into one cell. It encrypts pairs by same-row, same-column or rectangle rules; fillers and padding must be specified. SEC14 explains the 25-cell grid and letter-pair operations. Combining I/J is the conventional element that fits the alphabet into the grid, not a claim about numeric cells. Repeated-letter fillers and final padding affect actual ciphertext, so computations require those conventions rather than guessing them.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 151 · NS0447
records.text: NS0447 Question 151 SEC05 What is ARP Spoofing and which OSI layer does it target? Identify the trust claim or communication mapping being abused. ARP spoofing supplies false local IPv4-to-MAC associations, directing traffic toward an unintended link endpoint. It targets local link-address resolution at the network/data-link boundary and is commonly treated as a data-link-layer attack. SEC05 identifies the poisoned association rather than DNS names or transport state. Its scope is local IPv4-to-MAC resolution, so describing it simply as arbitrary IP routing would miss the mechanism. The layer answer refers to manipulating the local link mapping, while ARP connects network and link addressing.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 152 · NS0448
records.text: NS0448 Question 152 SEC22 What three primary services does IPSec provide? Match the communication task to the protocol and trace key handling separately from signing. The principal IPsec services are confidentiality, integrity and origin authentication for IP traffic. They depend on the chosen protocol/association: AH supplies integrity/authentication without encryption, while ESP can supply confidentiality and integrity; IKE negotiates associations and keys. IPsec operates at the network layer, with distinct AH, ESP and IKE roles. Listing the service set must not imply every IPsec packet is encrypted or that IKE itself carries protected application content. Transport/tunnel mode describes coverage/encapsulation rather than replacing the service-selection and key assumptions.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 153 · NS0449
records.text: NS0449 Question 153 SEC06 SEC03 How does a TCP SYN flood attack work? Match the resource bottleneck or wireless mechanism to the relevant protection layer. A TCP SYN flood creates many incomplete connection handshakes, occupying server state and exhausting resources needed for legitimate connections. Rate limits, SYN cookies, filtering or upstream controls address different parts of that resource bottleneck. SEC06 defines the attack by incomplete-handshake state consumption. The goal is denial of usable service, not necessarily gaining control of the target. Defenses must match the constrained resource and traffic path; no single listed measure guarantees resistance to every distributed load or bandwidth bottleneck.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 154 · NS0450
records.text: NS0450 Question 154 SEC21 What is the difference between SSL and TLS? Distinguish peer identity, channel protection and risks outside that channel. TLS is the successor to obsolete SSL and provides an authenticated protected channel. Handshakes negotiate parameters, authenticate peers as required and establish keys; symmetric authenticated record protection carries data. Exact handshake messages depend on TLS version. SEC21 warns against treating an old SSL/ChangeCipherSpec narrative as the universal TLS1.3 sequence.
