The useful distinction is protocol succession and version-specific behavior, not a claim that the names are interchangeable or that every deployment of either is automatically secure.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 155 · NS0451
records.text: NS0451 Question 155 SEC21 What does HTTPS stand for and what security does it add over HTTP? Distinguish peer identity, channel protection and risks outside that channel. HTTPS is secure HTTP: HTTP over TLS. It adds authenticated channel protection for HTTP paths, headers and content. It does not conceal all metadata, such as endpoint IPs/timing, or protect plaintext after a compromised endpoint decrypts it. SEC21 identifies the composition and coverage. Protection depends on authentication and certificate validation rather than the mere appearance of the URL scheme. It concerns the communication channel; endpoint compromise and visible traffic metadata remain outside that confidentiality boundary.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 156 · NS0452
records.text: NS0452 Question 156 SEC05 SEC06 What is DNS Spoofing? Identify the trust claim or communication mapping being abused. DNS spoofing provides false name-resolution data, potentially redirecting a requested domain to an attacker-chosen destination. Cache poisoning is a form that places false answers in a resolver cache. DNSSEC authenticates DNS data when appropriately deployed and validated. SEC05 distinguishes false DNS mapping from ARP/IP spoofing. SEC06 separates DNS flooding, which consumes query capacity, from answer authenticity. A successful-looking name lookup can still be maliciously wrong; checking that a response exists is different from establishing its trusted origin and integrity.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 157 · NS0453
records.text: NS0453 Question 157 SEC22 SEC-S03 What is the purpose of SSH (Secure Shell)? Match the communication task to the protocol and trace key handling separately from signing. SSH (Secure Shell) protects remote login, command execution and file transfer such as SFTP. It uses host keys and supports several client-authentication methods. Correct host-key validation and restricted management access remain important. SEC22 states the protected remote-administration functions. SSH is not merely encryption of a password; it protects the session and requires authentic peer identity. File transfer through SFTP is related to SSH rather than being ordinary FTP with a new name.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 158 · NS0454
records.text: NS0454 Question 158 SEC05 SEC18 What is a Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) attack? Identify the trust claim or communication mapping being abused. A man-in-the-middle attack places an attacker between communicating parties to intercept and potentially alter their exchange. Authentication of the intended peer and a protected channel are needed; encryption without authentic key binding can still allow intermediary substitution. SEC05 gives the interception/alteration mechanism, while SEC18’s unauthenticated Diffie–Hellman example explains why secrecy mechanisms alone are insufficient. The attacker may relay messages so both victims believe they communicate directly, making peer authentication and correct certificate/key checks essential.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 159 · NS0455
records.text: NS0455 Question 159 SEC22 SEC21 What is the SET (Secure Electronic Transaction) protocol and who developed it? Match the communication task to the protocol and trace key handling separately from signing. SET means Secure Electronic Transaction. It was a Visa/Mastercard-led specification for protecting payment-card transactions with certificates and signatures. It is distinct from an ordinary HTTPS connection or a general payment-processing system. SEC22 supplies the expansion, origin and protection role. Certificates/signatures support authenticated transaction relationships rather than defining the entire financial settlement infrastructure. Calling every TLS-protected checkout SET would conflate separate protocols with different scope and structure.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 160 · NS0456
records.text: NS0456 Question 160 SEC05 What is Session Hijacking? Identify the trust claim or communication mapping being abused. Session hijacking is taking over an existing authenticated session by stealing or predicting a valid session token. Defenses include protected transport, regenerating IDs after login, restrictive cookie handling and server-side authorization on sensitive requests. SEC05 identifies token possession/prediction as the takeover path. Establishing a secure initial login does not alone protect the later bearer token, and checking authorization on every sensitive action remains necessary. The mechanism differs from replaying an old message, although stolen session material can enable reused requests.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 161 · NS0457
records.text: NS0457 Question 161 SEC28 SEC23 What is a firewall and what are its three characteristics as a 'reference monitor'? Separate security-policy enforcement and assurance from ordinary OS features. A firewall enforces traffic policy on flows it mediates. As a reference-monitor design, enforcement must cover every relevant access, resist tampering and be small/simple enough to analyze. For a firewall this is its traffic boundary, not every host-memory operation. SEC28 defines the three reference-monitor requirements and explicitly limits a firewall to traversing traffic. SEC23 describes policy enforcement and bypass limits. Thus complete mediation requires preventing alternate paths within the claimed boundary; deploying a firewall does not make it a universal host security kernel.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 162 · NS0458
records.text: NS0458 Question 162 SEC23 What is the key difference between a Packet-Filtering firewall and a Stateful Inspection firewall? Identify which traffic is mediated and what information drives the device's decisions. A stateless packet-filtering firewall matches each packet’s header fields such as addresses, protocol and ports. Stateful inspection also tracks permitted connection context, allowing decisions based on whether traffic belongs to an allowed exchange. SEC23 distinguishes header matching from connection-aware inspection. Both can filter ports, so the difference is not port-filtering capability alone. State tracking does not imply unlimited application-content understanding or automatic encryption; those are additional, separate functions.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 163 · NS0459
records.text: NS0459 Question 163 SEC23 What is an Application-Level Gateway (proxy firewall)? Identify which traffic is mediated and what information drives the device's decisions. An application-level gateway/proxy terminates and relays application exchanges on behalf of clients/services and can inspect application content. It differs from a simple header packet filter or circuit relay that lacks full application-content interpretation. SEC23 defines the proxy by its application mediation boundary. It can enforce application-specific policy because it participates in the exchanges rather than merely routing packets. That role does not inherently mean encryption or protection against traffic that bypasses the proxy.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 164 · NS0460
records.text: NS0460 Question 164 SEC24 What is the difference between an IDS and an IPS? Separate observation from blocking and sensor placement from detection method. An IDS detects suspicious activity and alerts. An IPS can enforce prevention/blocking, usually on the traffic path. Both need contextual analysis because false positives and missed attacks remain possible. SEC24 makes action the distinction, independently of host/network sensor location or signature/anomaly detection method. Observing a suspected attack does not itself prevent it. Inline blocking can affect legitimate service when an alert is false, so evidence and policy determine the appropriate response.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 165 · NS0461
records.text: NS0461 Question 165 SEC24 What are the two main types of IDS detection methods? Separate observation from blocking and sensor placement from detection method. The two main detection methods are signature-based and anomaly-based. Signatures recognize known patterns; anomaly methods compare behavior with a baseline and may find novel deviations. Both can miss attacks or produce false positives. SEC24 explicitly gives these methods and their limitations. A deviation is not automatically malicious, and a matching signature does not prove every attack variant is captured. Host-based versus network-based describes sensor placement, a different classification from how the detection decision is made.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 166 · NS0462
records.text: NS0462 Question 166 SEC23 What limitation does a firewall have regarding data outside its perimeter? Identify which traffic is mediated and what information drives the device's decisions. A firewall cannot enforce policy on data or attack paths that bypass it. Insiders, removable media and uninspected encrypted content can evade its protection, so outside/perimeter-bypassing data needs endpoint, access and other controls. SEC23 confines firewall protection to traffic actually mediated and inspectable under its design. A boundary rule does not sanitize every file after it arrives through another path. This is a scope limitation rather than proof that firewalls are useless or that all encrypted traffic is malicious.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 167 · NS0463
records.text: NS0463 Question 167 SEC22 SEC20 SEC-S03 What is PGP (Pretty Good Privacy) and what security services does it provide? Match the communication task to the protocol and trace key handling separately from signing. PGP (Pretty Good Privacy)/OpenPGP combines symmetric encryption for content, public-key handling of content keys and digital signatures. It can provide confidentiality and integrity/origin-authentication evidence according to which operations are used and how keys are validated. SEC22 gives the hybrid composition and SEC20 explains signature scope. A signature alone does not conceal content; encryption alone is not the same as a validated signature. Recipient/signer key authenticity and custody therefore matter to the protection actually obtained.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 168 · NS0464
records.text: NS0464 Question 168 SEC22 SEC20 SEC21 What is S/MIME and how does 'Signed and Enveloped Data' work? Match the communication task to the protocol and trace key handling separately from signing. S/MIME protects MIME messages using certificates for signatures and/or enveloped encryption. In sign-then-encrypt, sign the MIME entity, package its content/signature, encrypt it with a fresh symmetric content key and protect that key for each recipient. The recipient recovers the key, decrypts, then verifies with the validated signer certificate. SEC22 specifies this construction while allowing other nesting orders with different coverage. Signed data supplies origin/integrity evidence without inherently concealing content; enveloped data encrypts content and wraps keys. Signing is not generic private-key encryption of the whole message, and certificate/key validation is essential to interpreting verification.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 169 · NS0465
records.text: NS0465 Question 169 SEC23 What is a Circuit-Level Gateway and what OSI layer does it operate at? Identify which traffic is mediated and what information drives the device's decisions. A circuit-level gateway relays connections, commonly using SOCKS, without full application-content interpretation. Textbook OSI mappings associate it with session/transport functions rather than a universally fixed physical OSI device layer. It need not encrypt traffic or constitute a VPN. A circuit gateway relays connections, while application proxies inspect content and packet filters match headers. The session/transport layer label is a teaching mapping; the relay function is the stable distinction. Unspecified circuit gateways must not be assumed to supply authenticated encrypted tunnels.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 170 · NS0466
records.text: NS0466 Question 170 SEC19 In the RSA example where p=3, q=13, and public key e=3, what is the ciphertext for plaintext m=5? Check key-generation conditions as well as modular arithmetic. The modular exponentiation gives c=5^3 mod(3×13)=125 mod39=8. However φ=(3−1)(13−1)=24 and gcd(3,24)=3, so e=3 has no modular inverse. This is an arithmetic result, not a valid RSA encryption/decryption key pair. SEC19 explicitly identifies the defective source example. Showing ciphertext 8 must not endorse the key setup: RSA requires e coprime to φ so a private exponent can invert it. The calculation and the validity check answer different parts of the example, and both must be preserved.

records.title: Computer Security — Question 171 · NS0467
records.text: NS0467 Question 171 SEC14 What is the Hill Cipher and why is it considered strong? Identify the cipher's unit, key structure and assumptions before judging its strength. Hill is a polygraphic matrix substitution cipher, C=KP mod26. Its key must be invertible modulo 26, with determinant coprime to 26. It is not strong by modern standards: enough independent known plaintext/ciphertext blocks reveal the key through its linear structure. SEC14 rejects the supplied claim of known-plaintext resistance. Combining letters into vectors does not remove linear algebraic relationships, and a large-looking matrix key is not proof of modern security. The correct answer explains the construction while correcting the question’s implied blanket strength claim.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Study notes
records.text: Network and System Administration Administration keeps services useful, available and controlled through configuration, monitoring, troubleshooting and repeatable automation. Diagnose from evidence: a failed connection, expired lease or large organization alone does not identify one cause or one best storage design. Practice service provisioning as a chain: link, address, route, DNS, transport connection, authentication and application. Match each tool to the evidence it can actually provide. Compare account/permission models, RAID layouts, backup types and security controls using stated requirements rather than unconditional best choices. Read and trace small Python 3 or shell scripts. Identify inputs, branching, repeated work, failures and outputs; then construct a reusable check or backup task.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Roles, principles and change discipline
records.text: System administrators maintain hosts, accounts, storage, software and availability; network administrators maintain connectivity, addressing, routes, network devices and performance. Security administrators coordinate controls and policy. These duties overlap, so account management, testing patches and training users are not exclusive to one job title. Patience, communication, ethics, technical understanding and organization matter alongside command knowledge. Use documentation, standardization, least privilege, automation and measured change. Record the current state, intended change, rollback and validation. Schedule maintenance according to service impact and urgency, not merely because a calendar date arrived. Fault management restores failures; performance management measures service behavior; configuration management tracks settings; security management controls access; accounting tracks usage. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module

records.title: Network and System Administration — Network foundations for administrators
records.text: Clients request services; servers provide them. Peer-to-peer systems can do both. A server can also be a client of DNS or backups, so dedicated role does not mean it never makes requests. A network OS is not universally installed only on a dedicated server: clients also require networking support. Specify centralized service software versus the OS on all participants. Switching normally forwards frames using MAC addresses within a LAN; routing forwards IP packets between networks. TCP supplies an ordered reliable byte stream, while UDP preserves datagrams without that guarantee. Ports distinguish application endpoints, not physical connectors. Draw switches, links, subnets, gateways, service hosts and dependencies in a network diagram. A topology’s shape alone does not guarantee security. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module

records.title: Network and System Administration — Address, prefix, gateway and loopback
records.text: An IPv4 address is 32 bits; a CIDR prefix determines its network. Compute network=address AND mask; devices use a route/gateway for remote subnets. Private ranges are 10/8,172.16/12 and 192.168/16; private addresses are not directly Internet-routable. Neither IP alone nor a class label determines today’s subnet. 127.0.0.1 conventionally names the local IPv4 loopback interface; 127/8 is reserved for loopback. Loopback tests local protocol processing, not cable, switch or remote reachability. Programs can use it for local services. Several loopback descriptions or several 127/8 addresses may be valid; compare each with the stated role. Example Worked microexample 192.168.2.70/26 has 64-address blocks: network .64, broadcast .127, ordinary host range .65–.126. A gateway must be reachable through an appropriate route; NAT does not repair a missing route. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module RFC 1122 host requirements

records.title: Network and System Administration — DHCP exchange and lease lifecycle
records.text: DHCP supplies addresses and configuration options. Typical initial IPv4 allocation is Discover→Offer→Request→ACK. The server manages its scope/pool, allocated leases, exclusions and reservations; options may include mask, gateway and DNS servers. A dynamic lease lasts for a specified interval, not forever. A client renews before expiry; it later tries rebinding if renewal fails. A disconnected host does not automatically renew forever. On lease expiry the address becomes eligible for reuse, subject to server policy. Reconnection normally triggers validation/renewal/new allocation, so an expired lease alone does not prove persistent failure. A reservation gives a predictable address to a known client while retaining DHCP configuration. Example Worked microexample If a disconnected client’s lease expires while other clients obtain addresses, its old address may be reassigned. It must not simply resume using it without validating its configuration. RFC 2131 DHCP

records.title: Network and System Administration — DHCP deployment, fallback and diagnosis
records.text: Use a scope matching the subnet, exclude manually assigned server/router addresses, set correct options and provide a relay when client broadcasts must cross a router. Static assignments and DHCP can coexist; avoid address conflicts. DHCP lowers repetitive administration but availability/security depend on deployment and protection from rogue replies. It does not guarantee connectivity whenever a device changes location. For a returning client, inspect current lease/address, reachable server/relay, free pool capacity and logs. New devices can exhaust a pool, but absent observations this is only a hypothesis. Some clients self-configure IPv4 link-local addresses such as 169.254.2.33 after DHCP failure; these support same-link communication, not ordinary routed Internet access. 0.0.0.0 is unspecified and 255.255.255.255 is limited broadcast. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module RFC 3927 IPv4 Link Local RFC 2131 DHCP

records.title: Network and System Administration — DNS forward/reverse resolution and evidence
records.text: Forward resolution obtains an address from a name, using A for IPv4 and AAAA for IPv6. Reverse lookup uses a PTR record in the reverse namespace to obtain a name from an address. CNAME aliases a name, MX identifies mail exchangers and NS identifies authoritative name servers. Forward and reverse records need not both exist or be perfect inverses. Resolvers cache answers for their TTL. Query nslookup name or specify the DNS server explicitly; compare the configured resolver with the authoritative answer when appropriate. A successful ping by address but failed name lookup suggests naming/configuration trouble. Ping by name may display a resolved address, but nslookup is the direct DNS diagnostic. “Resolving” is a general term that includes forward resolution. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module RFC 1035 DNS Microsoft nslookup

records.title: Network and System Administration — Choose the command that exposes the required state
records.text: Windows ipconfig shows addresses, mask and gateway; ipconfig /all adds complete adapter configuration including physical/MAC address, DHCP and DNS information. /renew requests renewal, /release releases a dynamic address and /flushdns clears the client DNS cache. Linux ip addr and ip route show interface addresses and routes; exact persistent configuration varies by distribution. netstat displays connections/endpoints/protocols and TCP states; netstat -ano displays numeric addresses/ports and PIDs. Use the exact command name netstat rather than netstart. ping probes IP reachability; traceroute/tracert reveals responding hops using TTL/hop-limit expiry. ICMP filtering can prevent replies without proving the service is down. nslookup inspects DNS. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module Microsoft ipconfig Microsoft netstat Microsoft nslookup

records.title: Network and System Administration — A repeatable troubleshooting procedure
records.text: Define the symptom, scope, time and recent changes; gather the configuration, baseline and logs. Form a testable hypothesis, test the least disruptive explanation, isolate the failing component, apply a targeted fix, verify the user service and document the result. Change one relevant factor at a time when possible. A reboot can hide evidence and is not a diagnosis by itself. Use bottom-up checks from physical link, top-down checks from application errors, or divide-and-conquer by testing a middle layer. Divide-and-conquer narrows the working/failing boundary; it is not random trial-and-error. Rebooting, updates, resetting settings and scanning can all be troubleshooting actions in suitable circumstances; use fault evidence to choose among them. Example Worked microexample One client fails while others work: inspect that client’s link, address and policy first. All clients fail name lookup but reach server IPs: inspect shared DNS/its configuration before replacing every cable. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module

records.title: Network and System Administration — Connectivity diagnosis by layers
records.text: Check power, cable/connector and link state, then NIC/driver state, VLAN membership, address/prefix, local gateway, route, DNS and finally application port/authentication. A recognized NIC makes a missing driver less likely, not proof of a working physical link. Ethernet commonly uses RJ45 connectors; an RJ11 telephone jack is not the expected Ethernet connection. If same-subnet traffic works but remote traffic fails, compare gateway/routes and filtering. If ping fails but the application connection works, ICMP filtering is plausible. If an application port is refused, the destination is reachable enough to reject it; inspect service/listener policy. A timeout can result from loss, filtering or a down host and needs more evidence. Example Worked microexample After NIC replacement, recognized/enabled adapter but no link light: try a known-good Ethernet cable and switch port. Merely knowing that the OS recognizes the NIC cannot prove one particular cable is defective. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module

records.title: Network and System Administration — Service catalog and remote access
records.text: DNS resolves names; DHCP supplies host configuration. SMTP sends/relays mail, while IMAP/POP retrieve it. FTP is a named file-transfer protocol; HTTP also transfers files, so “transfers files” is not an exclusive FTP description. HTTP/HTTPS serve web resources. SSH provides encrypted remote login; SFTP transfers files over SSH and differs from FTP or FTPS. A VPN extends private connectivity over another network; secure tunneling commonly encrypts/authenticates traffic but depends on protocol/configuration. RTP carries real-time media timing/sequence information, often over UDP; it does not guarantee timely delivery. Network printers expose services shared by clients. Provide accounts, permissions, configuration, monitoring and recovery for each service, not just its protocol name. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module

records.title: Network and System Administration — Routing, NAT and port translation
records.text: Routing selects a next hop using a destination prefix; NAT rewrites addresses. Many-to-one address-and-port translation (PAT/NAPT) maps internal flows to one public address using distinct port bindings. For example, two private client sockets can appear as public-address ports 40001 and 40002, with replies translated back to the correct clients. NAT is often used when private IPv4 clients access public networks; it does not itself replace a gateway, route, firewall or authentication. One-to-one NAT and destination translation are other forms, so NAT does not always mean many hosts share one address. Public addressing inside a LAN does not automatically require NAT. Unsolicited inbound service access may require explicit mapping and filtering. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module

records.title: Network and System Administration — Proxies, gateways and quality of service
records.text: A proxy acts on behalf of a client or backend service and can cache, filter or mediate application requests. A default IP gateway is a next-hop router; an application gateway may translate protocols. It need not be a modem/router combination. These terms describe functions that can coexist on one machine. QoS classifies, queues and prioritizes traffic to meet performance objectives such as low delay or limited loss. It can operate across layers and support applications, so it is not exclusively an application-layer service. Installing a new service is an administrative action; email configuration is another action and proxies/agents are components. Distinguish service-management actions from components using a stated taxonomy. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module

records.title: Network and System Administration — Workgroups, domains and directory services
records.text: A workgroup has locally managed accounts on individual machines; sharing may require local credentials and per-host configuration. A domain centralizes identities and policies through directory infrastructure. These are administrative arrangements, not physical topologies. Avoid treating an old recommended workgroup size as a hard protocol limit. HomeGroup is a historical Windows sharing feature, not another name for an AD domain. A domain controller runs AD DS, authenticates domain accounts and participates in directory replication. Redundant controllers improve service continuity only if dependencies and failure domains are considered; two virtual controllers on one failed physical host are not independent availability. Provisioning requires correct addressing, DNS, time and supported OS/hardware; version-specific minimum sizes are not universal architecture rules. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module

records.title: Network and System Administration — LDAP operations and secure directory access
records.text: LDAP accesses directory entries/attributes identified by distinguished names. Bind authenticates a session; search retrieves matching entries; compare tests an attribute value; add/delete/modify change entries; modify-DN renames or moves; unbind ends the session. StartTLS upgrades a connection to TLS where supported; LDAPS uses TLS from connection setup. Protect credentials and verify server identity. LDAP commonly uses TCP 389 and LDAPS TCP 636; an acronym/port alone does not make authentication secure. AD also uses DNS and Kerberos; LDAP is not identical to the entire directory product. Do not equate modern TLS-protected LDAP or LDAPS with retired LDAPv2. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module Microsoft, Enable LDAP over SSL

records.title: Network and System Administration — AD logical structure and delegation
records.text: A directory object represents a user, computer, group or resource and has schema-defined attributes. Security principals have SIDs; display names are not the sole security identity. A domain groups directory objects and a replicated domain database. A tree groups domains in a contiguous DNS namespace; a forest groups trees with a shared schema/configuration and global-catalog framework. OUs organize objects and provide convenient scopes for delegated administration and Group Policy; they are not separate forests/security boundaries. Use groups to assign access and OUs to structure policy/delegation. Schema changes require care because they propagate broadly; ordinary directory objects can be deleted, unlike the special restrictions on schema definitions. Apply schema restrictions to the specific directory object type being discussed. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module

records.title: Network and System Administration — AD sites, replication and trusts
records.text: Sites group IP subnets to model network locality, influence controller selection and manage replication traffic. They are distinct from domains/OUs. AD replicates directory changes among controllers; notification can trigger pulls within a site while schedules/link costs influence traffic between sites. Replication is not an independent backup of previous good states. If domain A trusts B, B’s identities can be authenticated for resources in A, subject to permissions. Trust alone grants no automatic file access. Direction (one/two way) and transitivity (extends/does not extend) are independent. An explicit trust is not necessarily one-way or nontransitive; the trust type/configuration determines that. State the direction in words before drawing arrows. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module Microsoft AD trust concepts

records.title: Network and System Administration — Accounts, rights and password diagnosis
records.text: Create named accounts, assign only needed groups/rights, disable departed users and audit privileged activity. Authentication verifies the account; authorization permits operations. A user right such as remote logon differs from a permission on one file. Group-based administration is easier to review than many hidden individual grants. If only one domain user cannot change a password, inspect that account’s cannot-change-password setting and relevant policy/permission before blaming all directory infrastructure. Other possibilities include minimum password age, password rules or account state; the setting is a plausible exam cause, not a conclusion from failure alone. Membership in Administrators does not inherently prohibit changing one’s password. Privileged reset and user-initiated password change are different operations. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module

records.title: Network and System Administration — Windows permissions and effective access
records.text: Windows file/folder permissions include read, write, read/execute, modify and full control, plus more granular rights such as delete. Inherited and explicit entries, group membership, deny entries and object scope affect effective access; use the effective-access view for a real account rather than adding labels informally. Network access can be constrained by both share and filesystem permissions. Deleting can be an explicit permission in Windows; specify the operating system before comparing permission names. Modify and full control are not identical: full control includes changing permission/ownership capabilities. Separate data access from logon rights. A user allowed to read a file is not necessarily allowed to write it or administer its parent folder. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module

records.title: Network and System Administration — Unix rwx and octal permissions
records.text: The nine ordinary permission bits are owner, group and other triplets. In each triplet read=4,write=2,execute=1; sum enabled bits to get an octal digit. A leading ls -l character denotes file type, not another permission bit. For directories, read lists names, execute permits traversal/search, and write changes entries subject to other checks. File deletion usually depends on parent directory permissions, with sticky-bit/ACL rules also possible. Example Worked microexample -rwxr--r-- means ordinary file, owner7/group4/other4, hence 744. 755 means rwxr-xr-x. A permission string must include all nine ordinary permission bits; missing hyphens cannot be inferred. Confirm the complete nine-bit permission string before converting it to octal. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module Linux man-pages chmod(2)

records.title: Network and System Administration — Linux paths, filesystems and checks
records.text: / is the filesystem root; /root is the administrative user’s home. /etc stores configuration, /home ordinary user homes, /var variable data/logs, /dev device nodes, /proc kernel/process information, /boot boot material and /tmp temporary files. Cleanup/mount layouts vary; do not assume every partition has lost+found or every reboot erases every temporary directory. ext2 is a Linux filesystem; ext4 is a later filesystem; HPFS is historically associated with OS/2, while swap is backing space rather than an ordinary user-file filesystem. fsck checks and optionally repairs filesystems through filesystem-specific tools; it is not init, halt or an inittab file. Repairs require the filesystem’s supported offline/safe procedure. Mount attaches a filesystem to a directory; partitioning, mounting, quotas and capacity belong to storage administration. Linux can access some foreign-origin filesystems, including HPFS when its driver is available. Filesystem origin and Linux driver support are different questions. Swap is a paging area rather than an ordinary user-file filesystem. ext2 is a native Linux-filesystem example; broader Linux filesystem support can also include HPFS, so distinguish origin from driver support. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module util-linux fsck(8) Linux kernel Read/Write HPFS documentation

records.title: Network and System Administration — Profiles, registry and persistent configuration
records.text: A local profile keeps settings on one client; a roaming profile synchronizes supported user settings/data through a server at logon/logoff. Large profiles can slow these operations; redirected folders avoid repeatedly copying selected folders. A central profile is backed up only if the server’s backup policy actually includes it. A cached profile is not a newly created independent local security account. The Windows registry is a hierarchical configuration database with keys, subkeys and typed values. HKLM describes machine settings and HKCU the current user view. ACLs protect registry access. Not all historical root handles apply to current versions. Record/export the relevant configuration before an authorized change, and verify the intended service behavior afterward. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module

records.title: Network and System Administration — Performance monitoring and bottleneck decisions
records.text: Measure a baseline, sample over an interval, compare with workload and correlate symptoms before changing hardware. CPU utilization/run queues identify processing pressure; low free memory alone is weak evidence because cache may be reclaimable. Persistent paging with high latency indicates memory pressure. Storage capacity and I/O latency are separate: a disk can be nearly empty but saturated, or nearly full while lightly loaded. Measure interface bytes/second, errors, drops, packet delay/loss and utilization against link rate. Distinguish capacity (maximum available rate) from observed throughput. Logs can reveal both security incidents and performance faults. Performance counters expose measured events; system calls/APIs and log parsers are ways scripts can collect them. Example Worked microexample Transferring 80 MB in 10 s gives 8 MB/s≈64 Mb/s before overhead. A 95%-busy CPU with a growing runnable queue suggests CPU pressure; a 95%-full disk requires capacity action even if its latency is low. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module

records.title: Network and System Administration — Monitoring, capture and assessment tools
records.text: Task Manager shows running processes/resource use; Resource Monitor/Performance Monitor give more detailed counters. Wireshark captures and dissects packets. Nmap discovers hosts/ports/services. Nessus assesses vulnerabilities/configuration. Snort can detect suspicious traffic and alert, and can prevent traffic in suitable inline deployments; it also has sniffing/logging roles. Thus packet-capture capability is not exclusive to one product, although Wireshark is the conventional analyzer choice. An IDS detects/alerts; an IPS can block inline. Scanning identifies potential weaknesses rather than proving successful exploitation. A captured packet, open port or alert needs context. Monitoring network usage is not the same as configuring access control or encrypting communications. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module Wireshark User Guide, Introduction Nmap Reference Guide Snort project Tenable Nessus User Guide

records.title: Network and System Administration — Backups, restore and continuity
records.text: Backups recover previous data after deletion, compromise, corruption, failed upgrades/migrations or hardware loss. Authorization controls current access, a different function. A mirror/replica also copies deletions or corruption and does not replace versioned independent backups. Keep protected copies in separate failure domains, define retention and test restores. A full backup copies the chosen dataset; incremental copies changes since the last backup; differential copies changes since the last full backup. Restoring incrementals generally needs the full plus each subsequent incremental, whereas differential needs the full plus latest differential. RPO is tolerable lost-data time and RTO tolerable restoration time. Compression reduces storage, scheduling runs the operation and restore testing establishes whether recovery actually works. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module

records.title: Network and System Administration — RAID layouts, capacity and selection
records.text: RAID0 stripes for capacity/throughput with no disk-failure tolerance. RAID1 mirrors; a two-disk mirror has one disk’s usable capacity and survives one disk failure. RAID2 uses bit striping/Hamming-code redundancy, RAID3 byte striping with dedicated parity, RAID4 block striping with dedicated parity and RAID5 block striping with distributed parity. RAID6 distributes dual parity and tolerates two disk failures. RAID10 stripes mirrored pairs; survival depends on which disks fail. With N equal disks of capacity D, RAID0 usable=ND, paired RAID1/10≈ND/2, RAID5=(N−1)D and RAID6=(N−2)D. Hardware RAID may offload work to controller resources/cache but does not universally outperform software RAID. Rebuilds consume bandwidth; parity writes have overhead. A large university/bank alone does not select a level. Striping plus parity is not uniquely RAID5 unless distributed block parity is specified. Example Worked microexample Four 2 TB disks give 8 TB RAID0, 4 TB RAID10, 6 TB RAID5 or4 TB RAID6, ignoring metadata. Choose using failure tolerance, workload, capacity and recovery requirements; none of these layouts replaces backups. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module Intel server storage options

records.title: Network and System Administration — Security policy development and purpose
records.text: A security policy states required behavior, scope, accountable roles and enforcement. Begin with assets/service objectives, assess threats and weaknesses, choose controls, define exceptions/incident procedures, approve/communicate, monitor and periodically review. CIA means confidentiality, integrity and availability; neither sensitive-data protection nor availability alone is the universal primary goal. A policy can require password controls, approved encryption, restricted administrative access, backups and patch deadlines; firewall rules implement part of it. Open unrestricted wireless access conflicts with controlled internal access unless intentionally isolated as a guest service. “Use the system passively” is not a purpose of security policy. Policies coordinate action and reduce risk; they do not guarantee every attack will fail. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module

records.title: Network and System Administration — Hardening, controls and vulnerabilities
records.text: Hardening reduces exposure through unnecessary-service removal, supported patches, restricted accounts/permissions and appropriate port filtering. Blocking an unused known port can be hardening; blocking every useful port merely destroys availability. Weak passwords and unpatched exploitable software are vulnerabilities; attacks exploit weaknesses, and risk combines likelihood with impact. Preventive controls restrict harmful actions, detective controls expose them and recovery controls restore service. Account lifecycle, backup procedures, device configuration and traffic analysis can all be security controls under a stated objective. A vulnerability scan checks known weakness patterns, not bandwidth. Test/stage patches, prepare rollback, deploy and verify; testing and installation are both legitimate administrator duties. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module

records.title: Network and System Administration — Encryption, hashes and script secrets
records.text: Encryption provides confidentiality with correct key/nonce use; authenticated encryption adds integrity/authenticity. Unspecified encryption alone does not guarantee both properties. A password hash supports verification without recovering the original password; it is not a reversible credential store. Encryption can protect a recoverable credential only if its key is separately protected. Keep reusable secrets out of source code and routine logs; obtain them from an appropriately protected credential service or restricted runtime source. Environment variables and configuration files are transport/storage choices, not automatic encryption. A script that must authenticate to another service often needs the actual credential/token, so replacing it with a one-way hash will not work. State whether the question is about password verification or recoverable service credentials. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module RFC 5116 Authenticated Encryption

records.title: Network and System Administration — Incidents, evidence and reports
records.text: Incident response prepares, detects/analyzes, contains, removes the cause, restores service and learns from the event. Investigation is reactive response; routine patching and backup are normally preventive/preparatory operations. Document timestamps, affected systems, evidence, impact, actions, responsible people and recovery results. An incident report may record policy violations, but its scope is broader than that alone. DoS harms service availability; DDoS uses distributed sources. Phishing deceives users, brute force tries credentials and an interception attack reads/alters communications. Correlate logs using time and identity/context. Preserve relevant evidence before resetting systems. A suspicious event is not automatically confirmed compromise; record facts and uncertainty. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module

records.title: Network and System Administration — Segmentation, NAC and remote administration
records.text: Segmentation separates groups of systems and enforces allowed flows with routing/filtering policies; VLAN membership alone does not establish complete security. NAC assesses device/user admission and can reject or quarantine unauthorized/noncompliant devices. Authentication proves an identity, while access rules decide which resources it may use. Use authenticated protected remote administration such as SSH or properly secured management services, with restricted source access and auditing. VPNs provide protected connectivity under their defined security model; they are not packet analyzers. Firewall filtering permits/blocks traffic according to policy; it is not inherently encryption. Losing remote connectivity while changing a management route/firewall is an operational risk to plan for. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module Cisco, Network Access Control

records.title: Network and System Administration — Scripting: inputs, control flow and reusable work
records.text: Scripts automate repeatable administration; they are not inherently faster than compiled programs or automatically secure. Python, shells and PowerShell are common choices; HTML is markup. Define inputs and outputs, use variables for state, if/elif/else for decisions, loops for repeated work and functions for reusable operations. Python indentation defines blocks; == compares while = assigns. Make reruns predictable: compute the desired state, compare with current state and change only what differs. Validate a small dry run before mutation. Avoid requiring privilege for read-only reporting. A good script reports failures and has a meaningful exit status rather than printing success unconditionally. Example Worked microexample def warn_percent(values, limit): for name, percent in values: if percent >= limit: print(name, "high", percent) warn_percent([("root", 92), ("data", 40)], 90) # Output: root high 92 (with spaces from print). Only the first pair meets the threshold. Python tutorial, control flow

records.title: Network and System Administration — Launching commands with Python subprocess
records.text: Python subprocess is a module, not a universal shell command. run launches a child program and returns its result; capture_output collects stdout/stderr, text=True decodes text, timeout bounds waiting and check=True raises for nonzero exit. Pass an argument list to avoid accidental shell interpretation; quote handling differs from composing a shell string. Echo prints, grep searches text and ipconfig/ifconfig reports/configures networking; none is the general Python child-process abstraction. Specify the scripting language before selecting subprocess for process execution. Example Worked microexample import subprocess result = subprocess.run(["ip", "addr", "show"], text=True, capture_output=True, check=True, timeout=5) print(result.stdout) # Linux with iproute2 installed. Missing program raises OSError; # nonzero status raises CalledProcessError; timeout raises TimeoutExpired. Python subprocess documentation

records.title: Network and System Administration — File input, configuration parsing and updates
records.text: File I/O obtains/persists configuration; string operations parse values; regex can recognize patterns. File I/O, string operations and regex can all help manipulate configuration; choose according to the task. Use the format’s parser for structured JSON/INI rather than blindly replacing every matching substring. Open text with an explicit encoding and use with so files close even when processing fails. For changes, validate the desired output, preserve a known-good copy, write to a temporary file in the same filesystem, then atomically replace the target where supported. Check permissions and configuration syntax, reload the affected service, verify and retain a rollback. Merely appending the same setting on every run is not idempotent. Example Worked microexample import json with open("settings.json", encoding="utf-8") as handle: config = json.load(handle) port = config["port"] if not isinstance(port, int) or not 1 <= port <= 65535: raise ValueError("port must be 1..65535") print("validated port", port) # This example validates/reports and does not alter a system file. Python tutorial, input/output

records.title: Network and System Administration — Arguments and targeted error handling
records.text: Command-line parsing converts user inputs into named, typed values and displays usage. In Python argparse, positional arguments supply required inputs and flags enable options. Validate ranges and paths before work; do not let unchecked input become executable shell text. Example Worked microexample import argparse from pathlib import Path p = argparse.ArgumentParser() p.add_argument("logfile", type=Path) p.add_argument("--limit", type=int, default=10) a = p.parse_args() if a.limit <1: p.error("limit must be positive") try: print(a.logfile.read_text(encoding="utf-8")[:a.limit]) except (OSError, UnicodeError) as exc: p.exit(1, f"read failed: {exc}\n") # Input limit controls characters here. Exceptions skip the rest of try; # catching specific failures makes unexpected programming errors visible. Python argparse documentation Python errors and exceptions tutorial

records.title: Network and System Administration — Regex log analysis and rotation
records.text: Regex recognizes textual patterns; it does not encrypt, compress or rotate logs. search finds a match anywhere, while fullmatch requires the entire string to fit. Use raw Python strings for backslash-heavy patterns, capture only the needed fields and treat unmatched/malformed lines explicitly. Log rotation bounds file size and preserves historical segments; it is complementary to parsing. Count the event actually requested, use timestamps/hosts to correlate, and separate absence of matches from failure to read the log. Logs support security and performance analysis, so neither purpose is universally exclusive. Example Worked microexample import re pattern = re.compile(r"status=(\d{3})\b") counts = {} for line in ["status=200 ok", "status=503 unavailable", "noise"]: match = pattern.search(line) if match: code = match.group(1) counts[code] = counts.get(code,0)+1 print(counts) # {"200":1,"503":1}; noise is deliberately ignored. Python re documentation

records.title: Network and System Administration — Collecting CPU and memory measurements
records.text: A cumulative CPU counter must be sampled twice to calculate interval use; a single lifetime total is not current utilization. On Linux /proc/stat exposes cumulative CPU categories; define which categories count as idle and avoid double-counting guest fields. A simple convention is busy fraction=1−Δidle/Δtotal using idle+iowait as the chosen nonbusy categories. Iowait interpretation has limitations. /proc/meminfo exposes MemAvailable, an estimate of memory available without swapping; MemFree alone excludes reclaimable memory. Windows Performance Counters and OS APIs expose analogous measurements through different interfaces. System calls, counters and log parsing can all contribute; selecting one as the only monitoring technique is unjustified without a platform/API. Example Worked microexample If total CPU counters grow by 1000 ticks and chosen idle counters by 250, measured busy≈75%. If MemTotal=8192 MiB and MemAvailable=2048 MiB, approximate unavailable/used fraction is75%, not a prediction that an allocation of exactly 2048 MiB must succeed. records.title: Network and System Administration — Scheduling a backup and checking restoration
records.text: Schedule recurring work using cron/systemd timers on suitable Unix systems or Task Scheduler on Windows. A user crontab uses minute,hour,day-of-month,month,day-of-week then command. Use absolute paths, known environment, protected inputs, logs, bounded runtime and a lock when overlap is unsafe. Do not assume an interactive PATH, current directory or stored credentials exist in a scheduled job. Compression packages data; scheduling chooses when the operation runs. Test exit status and the archive contents, then restore a sample into an isolated destination. A successful command alone does not prove a usable backup. Version control of scripts helps review but does not replace data backup. Example Worked microexample One user-crontab entry (keep the command on one line): 0 2 * * * /usr/bin/python3 /opt/backup.py /srv /bak >>/var/log/bak.log 2>&1 This runs daily at 02:00 in the scheduler’s timezone as the crontab owner. The script takes its configured source and destination arguments. Paths, permissions, logging and the backup program must already be configured. Standard user crontabs omit a username field; system crontabs may include one. Data Communication and Computer Networking module Network and System Administration module crontab(5) manual

records.title: Network and System Administration — Construct a bounded backup script
records.text: Separate argument parsing, preconditions, copying/archive creation and result reporting. Require a source directory, avoid putting the backup inside that source, create unique output names and ensure a failed partial file is not mistaken for a completed backup. Real backup policies also need application consistency, capacity checks, retention and independent protected copies. The following teaching script packages a directory; it does not silently install a scheduled job. Example Worked microexample import argparse, shutil from pathlib import Path from datetime import datetime, timezone p = argparse.ArgumentParser() p.add_argument("source", type=Path) p.add_argument("destination", type=Path) a = p.parse_args() src, dst = a.source.resolve(), a.destination.resolve() if not src.is_dir() or not dst.is_dir(): p.error("source and destination must be existing directories") if dst == src or src in dst.parents: p.error("destination must be outside source") name = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("copy-%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ") base = dst /name try: archive = shutil.make_archive(str(base), "gztar", root_dir=src) except OSError as exc: base.with_suffix(".tar.gz").unlink(missing_ok=True) p.exit(1, f"backup failed: {exc}\n") print(archive) # Run against a teaching directory, verify archive members, then restore # into a different empty directory and compare selected files. Python tutorial, control flow Python tutorial, input/output Python errors and exceptions tutorial Python shutil documentation

records.title: Network and System Administration — Operations principles versus development and delivery models
records.text: Least privilege limits an account or process to the rights its task needs. Agile development instead organizes frequent delivery and adaptation of software. Object-oriented programming organizes software around objects with state and behavior. Cloud computing supplies on-demand access to a shared pool of configurable computing resources. A development approach or hosting model does not itself define an access-rights principle. Network and System Administration module · page 43 Agile Manifesto — Principles Oracle — Object-oriented programming concepts: objects NIST SP 800-145 — The NIST Definition of Cloud Computing

records.title: Network and System Administration — Disaster recovery as a planning objective
records.text: Disaster recovery planning prepares for restoring systems and data after disruptive loss. Regular protected backups and tested restoration are part of that plan. Continuing operation despite a component failure is a fault-tolerance objective; possessing extra components alone does not establish that older valid data can be recovered. Network and System Administration module · page 30 NIST SP 800-34 Revision 1 — Contingency planning

records.title: Network and System Administration — Initialization, shutdown and filesystem-check tools
records.text: In a traditional SysV-style system, init starts and supervises configured processes; /etc/inittab is its configuration file. The halt command stops the system through the supported shutdown procedure. Neither initialization, shutdown nor their configuration file is a filesystem-consistency check; fsck supplies that separate checking and optional repair role. Debian sysvinit manual — init Debian sysvinit manual — halt

records.title: Network and System Administration — What an ICMP reachability probe actually tests
records.text: Ping uses ICMP echo messages to test IP reachability. A reply shows that the addressed host and path support that exchange; no reply alone does not prove the host is disconnected, because filtering or loss can suppress responses. Traceroute instead discovers responding intermediate hops through packet-lifetime expiry; it is a path-discovery diagnostic, not the same question as an end-to-end echo test. Network and System Administration module · page 27

records.title: Network and System Administration — Distinguish scripting features by their responsibility
records.text: Exception handling transfers control from a failing operation to a matching handler. A try block contains the attempted work; an except clause handles specified raised exceptions. A loop repeats operations, a conditional chooses an ordinary branch, and a function packages reusable work; these constructs do not by themselves intercept exceptions. A module groups definitions and statements that can be imported. A class bundles data with functionality for its objects. These organize a program, while command-line parsing interprets the arguments and flags supplied at invocation. Their implementation can use functions or classes, but organization alone does not parse arguments. A signal handler responds when a process receives a specified asynchronous event notification. Handling such a notification is distinct from reading CPU or memory measurements through an OS interface, a performance counter or a log that actually records the metric. Python tutorial — Errors and exceptions Python tutorial — Modules Python tutorial — Classes Python library — Signal handlers for asynchronous events

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 1 · Q00011
records.text: Q00011 Question 1 NSA07 You administer a network and need to display active connections with their protocol, local address and port, foreign address and port, and connection state. Which command provides this connection table? Match the requested observation to the tool’s actual output; distinguish configuration, name lookup, reachability and hop discovery. A traceroute B ipconfig C netstat D nslookup netstat. NSA07 identifies netstat as the tool that displays connections, protocol names, local and foreign endpoints, and TCP connection states. That is the complete set of information requested, so option C is right. Numeric-output flags can keep addresses and ports numeric; the Windows form netstat -ano also includes process IDs. A incorrect Traceroute reports responding hops on a network path, not a connection table with local/foreign ports and TCP states. B incorrect Ipconfig reports adapter addressing and configuration, not active transport connections and their remote endpoints. C correct Netstat displays the requested protocol, endpoint and connection-state information. D incorrect Nslookup queries DNS records rather than listing active connections or TCP states.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 2 · Q00077
records.text: Q00077 Question 2 NSA04 NSA05 Which statements about ordinary dynamic DHCP allocation are incorrect? Select all that apply. Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A An IP leased by the DHCP for a host is permanent B DHCP assures connectivity ever users move from location to location C The IP address are chosen from a predetermined range of address D DHCP allows a host to acquire an IP address automatically An IP leased by the DHCP for a host is permanent; DHCP assures connectivity ever users move from location to location A dynamic DHCP lease lasts for a specified interval and must be renewed; it is not a permanent assignment. DHCP can automate address configuration after moving, but connectivity also depends on a reachable server or relay, a suitable scope and a working network. The server selects addresses from its configured pool. Thus the permanence and guaranteed-connectivity claims are false, while pool selection and automatic acquisition are true. A correct A leased dynamic address is time-limited and can become reusable after expiration; it is not permanent. B correct DHCP alone cannot assure connectivity after every location change; server, relay and network conditions matter. C incorrect A DHCP server manages an address scope/pool, supporting selection from a predetermined range. D incorrect Automatic acquisition of an address and options is a supported DHCP function.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 3 · Q00091
records.text: Q00091 Question 3 NSA04 NSA06 Which listed operation is not a DHCP server function? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A It grants an IP address when receives a request from a client. B It maintains the information about client configuration parameters. C It maintains a database of available IP addresses. D Resolve hostnames to IP addresses using DNS records. Resolve hostnames to IP addresses using DNS records. A DHCP server manages address pools, lease allocations and configuration parameters supplied to clients. It may allocate an address in response to a client exchange and retain information about availability and options. Hostname-to-address resolution is a DNS function instead. Repairing the duplicated malformed option supplies a distinct nonfunction while preserving the original distinction between automatic configuration and other network services. A incorrect Allocating an address in response to client requests is a DHCP server function. B incorrect The server manages lease and configuration parameters, so this is not a nonfunction. C incorrect Maintaining scope/pool availability is explicitly part of DHCP server management. D correct Hostname-to-address resolution belongs to DNS rather than DHCP allocation.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 4 · Q00185
records.text: Q00185 Question 4 NSA01 NSA26 Based on the predefined policy of Network management, controlling access to the network is the task of Distinguish the security objective from the control that prevents, detects or recovers from the stated problem. A Fault Management B Performance Management C Security Management D Configuration Management E None Security Management PDF p.30 places restricting access to authorized users under security procedures. The requested access-control responsibility therefore matches Security Management. A incorrect Fault management concerns failures rather than the access authorization described on p.30. B incorrect Capacity/performance is a different responsibility (p.29), not authorization. C correct Security procedures explicitly ensure only authorized users have network access (p.30). D incorrect Configuration management is not the named access-security responsibility. E incorrect The security alternative directly matches the stated responsibility.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 5 · Q00186
records.text: Q00186 Question 5 NSA20 NSA-S03 A Unix utility which used for checking and repairing file system inconsistencies. Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A init B halt C inittab D fsck fsck NSA20 directly defines fsck as the filesystem-checking and optional repair utility. Repairs must follow the filesystem’s supported safe or offline procedure. The alternatives refer to initialization/shutdown or an initialization configuration file, not the checking-and-repair role stated in the question. A incorrect Init concerns system initialization/service management rather than the filesystem-checking utility defined in NSA20. B incorrect Halt stops a system; it is not the utility for checking and repairing filesystem inconsistencies. C incorrect Inittab is an initialization configuration file, not the filesystem-checking command. D correct Fsck checks filesystems and can invoke filesystem-specific repair tools under supported safe conditions.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 6 · Q00188
records.text: Q00188 Question 6 NSA04 A PC obtains its IP address from a DHCP server. If the PC is taken off the network for repair, what happens to the IP address configuration? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A The address is returned to the pool for reuse when the lease expires B The address lease is automatically renewed until the PC is returned C The configuration is held by the server to be reissued when the PC is returned D The configuration is permanent and nothing changes The address becomes reusable when its lease expires Taking the PC offline does not make the dynamic assignment permanent or cause endless automatic renewal. NSA04 says a disconnected client’s lease can expire and the address then becomes eligible for reuse. On return, the client must validate, renew or obtain new configuration rather than assume it still owns its former address. A correct After expiry the address becomes eligible for return to the available pool, subject to server policy. B incorrect A disconnected client does not automatically renew indefinitely while it remains off the network. C incorrect The server need not hold the old address for that client after lease expiry without a reservation. D incorrect A dynamic lease has a finite interval and is not an unchanging permanent assignment.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 7 · Q00189
records.text: Q00189 Question 7 NSA07 Which command in Microsoft Windows allows you to verify your IP address, subnet mask, default gateway, and MAC address? Match the requested observation to the tool’s actual output; distinguish configuration, name lookup, reachability and hop discovery. A C:\>ipconfig/all B C:\>ping C C:\>ipconfig D C:\>ipstatus ipconfig /all The distinguishing requirement is the MAC address as well as IP, mask and gateway. NSA07 assigns this complete adapter detail to ipconfig /all; basic ipconfig covers the ordinary addressing summary. A displays the command with its /all switch. Ping tests reachability and ipstatus is not the defined Windows diagnostic. A correct The /all switch supplies the detailed adapter information, including the physical/MAC address requested. B incorrect Ping probes reachability rather than reporting the adapter’s complete IP and MAC configuration. C incorrect Basic ipconfig reports IP, mask and gateway but omits the requested detailed physical/MAC information. D incorrect Ipstatus is not the Windows adapter-configuration command established by the complete note.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 8 · Q00191
records.text: Q00191 Question 8 NSA17 You are the administrator of an active directory domain. A user complains to you that he is unable to change his password. No other users have this issue. What is the most likely cause of the problem? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Insufficient login credentials B He is a member of the Administrators group C He is not a member of the domain D The property "User cannot change password" has been enabled when it was created The account’s User cannot change password property A failure isolated to one domain user favors inspecting that user’s permissions and cannot-change-password setting. D is the specific account control matching the symptom, and NSA17 explicitly identifies it as a plausible exam cause. It remains a most-likely option among these choices, not proof of its actual state: password age/rules and other account conditions would require real diagnosis. A incorrect Generic insufficient credentials gives no specific cause for this domain user’s isolated password-change restriction. B incorrect Administrators membership does not inherently prohibit users from changing their own passwords. C incorrect The scenario concerns a domain user; lacking domain membership is not the specific account restriction supported here. D correct The cannot-change-password setting directly blocks the operation and matches the isolated account symptom.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 9 · Q00353
records.text: Q00353 Question 9 NSA06 NSA14 Which is the most specific DNS term for obtaining an IP address from a hostname? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Forward resolution B Backward resolution C Binding D Resolving Forward resolution Forward resolution names the specific direction from a hostname to an address record. Resolving is a broader term that also includes this operation, so it is less specific than the requested answer. Reverse lookup goes from an address to a name, and binding is not the DNS operation defined here. Asking for the most specific term makes the overlapping general description a meaningful distractor. A correct Forward resolution is the precise name-to-address operation defined by NSA06. B incorrect Reverse lookup runs in the opposite direction, obtaining a name from an address. C incorrect Binding is not the note’s term for the DNS name-to-address operation; LDAP bind authenticates a session. D incorrect Resolving includes forward lookup but is broader than the most specific term requested.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 10 · Q00354
records.text: Q00354 Question 10 NSA06 NSA07 You know a server hostname and want to query its DNS address records directly, optionally choosing the DNS server. Which listed diagnostic tool is designed for that task? Match the requested observation to the tool’s actual output; distinguish configuration, name lookup, reachability and hop discovery. A Nslookup B Ping command C Traceroute D Netstat Nslookup Nslookup directly queries DNS for the address records associated with a name and can use a specified DNS server. Ping may display a resolved address, but its principal task is testing IP reachability. Traceroute examines responding path hops, while netstat exposes endpoints and connection state. The direct-DNS-query requirement identifies the intended diagnostic without relying on incidental address displays from other commands. A correct Nslookup directly queries DNS records for the known name and is the conventional diagnostic here. B incorrect Ping primarily tests reachability; displaying a resolved address is not the direct DNS-record query requested. C incorrect Traceroute inspects responding hops rather than directly querying DNS address records. D incorrect Netstat reports existing endpoints/connections and is not a direct lookup for an arbitrary server name.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 11 · Q00355
records.text: Q00355 Question 11 NSA03 NSA11 LAN clients must reach public IPv4 destinations through a gateway with working routes. Which listed address situation commonly calls for source NAT at that gateway? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Default gateway of LAN isn't configured B Global IP address is used in the LAN C He/she don't know type of IP address used in the LAN D Private IP address is used in the LAN Private IP address is used in the LAN Private IPv4 addresses are not directly routed as public Internet destinations. A gateway can translate those source addresses, often using port bindings so several clients share a public address. This works together with valid routing and the external connection. A missing default gateway must be repaired separately, and public addressing or uncertainty about the current configuration is not by itself a reason to enable NAT. A incorrect A missing gateway requires routing configuration; address translation is not a replacement for it. B incorrect Public addressing in a LAN does not automatically require address translation. C incorrect Not knowing the address type calls for inspecting configuration, not blindly enabling NAT. D correct Private IPv4 clients commonly need source translation when reaching public destinations through this gateway.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 12 · Q00356
records.text: Q00356 Question 12 NSA04 NSA05 Which single option gives the complete set of scenarios where DHCP can meet the stated address-management goal, assuming a correctly deployed service? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A A small network needing automatic host address configuration. B Fixed-purpose devices needing predictable addresses through DHCP reservations. C A large device population needing centrally managed address configuration. D All are correct All are correct DHCP can reduce repetitive configuration in small as well as large networks. Reservations allow a known device to receive a predictable address while retaining centrally supplied options. A complex population of clients may also benefit from centrally managed scopes and configuration. The scenarios state these goals rather than treating size or complexity alone as a mandate. Each individual option is valid but incomplete as the requested complete set. A incorrect DHCP can automate this small network, but A alone omits the other qualifying scenarios. B incorrect Reservations meet the predictable-address goal, but B alone is incomplete. C incorrect Centralized DHCP management can meet this goal, but C alone is incomplete. D correct All three stated goals can be met by an appropriately configured DHCP service.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 13 · Q00550
records.text: Q00550 Question 13 NSA04 NSA05 A disconnected client returns after its old DHCP lease expired. The correct scope has 20 assignable addresses, all now leased to other active clients; the server and relay are reachable. What best explains why the returning client cannot obtain an address? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A the IP address lease has expired on the DHCP server. B the DHCP scope needs to be redefined. C the DHCP pool limit has been reached. D the DHCP server needs to be restarted. the DHCP pool limit has been reached. A reachable DHCP service still needs an available address in the correct pool. Here all twenty assignable addresses are already leased to other active clients, so the returning client cannot receive a free dynamic allocation. Its expired lease permits reuse but does not alone explain persistent failure after reconnection. The pool-capacity observation supplies the diagnosis; it does not establish a need to redefine the scope or restart the server. A incorrect The old lease expired, but normal reacquisition would succeed if pool capacity remained; expiry alone is insufficient. B incorrect The scope is correct; the evidence identifies exhausted capacity rather than an incorrect subnet definition. C correct All assignable pool addresses are leased, so the pool limit prevents a new allocation. D incorrect The server is reachable and processing requests; a restart does not create free pool capacity.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 14 · Q00563
records.text: Q00563 Question 14 NSA09 NSA08 After a NIC replacement, the adapter is recognized and enabled in firmware and Device Manager, but there is no link light. On the same switch port, replacing only the CAT5 cable with a known-good cable restores connectivity. Which listed fault is isolated? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A the CAT5 cable is defective B the NIC is disabled in BIOS C The NIC is disabled in Device Manager D The RJ11 jack is defective the CAT5 cable is defective The test changes one relevant factor while keeping the adapter and switch port unchanged. Connectivity returns with a known-good cable, which isolates the original cable or its terminations as the failing component. The explicit enabled-state checks exclude the two disabling explanations. RJ11 is a telephone connector rather than the Ethernet connection being tested, so it does not describe the observed fault. A correct Replacing only the cable restores the link, isolating the original CAT5 cable or its terminations. B incorrect The adapter is explicitly enabled in firmware. C incorrect The adapter is explicitly enabled in Device Manager. D incorrect RJ11 is a telephone connector, not the expected Ethernet RJ45 connection in this NIC scenario.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 15 · Q00586
records.text: Q00586 Question 15 NSA19 Permissions of a file are represented by which of the following characters? Identify the platform and permission model; for an rwx string, separate owner/group/other triplets and use the stated bit weights. A r,w,x B w,x C x,w,e D x,w r, w and x NSA19 groups ordinary Unix permission bits into owner/group/other triplets, each containing read, write and execute. Their conventional letters are r, w and x, with numeric weights 4, 2 and 1 respectively. Only A contains the complete set; the alternatives omit read or substitute a nonpermission letter.
