A correct r, w and x denote the complete read, write and execute permission set. B incorrect This omits r, the read bit, and therefore is not the full ordinary permission-letter set. C incorrect The letter e is not an ordinary Unix rwx permission bit and read is missing. D incorrect This lists execute and write but omits the read permission represented by r.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 16 · Q00633
records.text: Q00633 Question 16 NSA02 In a centralized client-server deployment, where must centralized file/directory service software be installed at minimum? Client networking support is a separate component. Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Server B every system in the network C both server and every system in the network D None Server The question distinguishes server-side service software from the networking support required on every participant. A centralized service runs on a server that provides it; clients need their own networking support but do not all need the server component installed. Options requiring deployment on every system therefore exceed the minimum location asked for. This does not imply that client operating systems lack networking capabilities. A correct The server hosts the centralized server-side component. B incorrect Installing the server component on every system is not the minimum required deployment. C incorrect Requiring every client as well as the server exceeds the minimum server-side placement. D incorrect A centralized service does require a host, so none is false.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 17 · Q00635
records.text: Q00635 Question 17 NSA20 Which listed item is a native Linux filesystem for ordinary user files, rather than a foreign-origin filesystem or paging area? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A ext2 B hpfs C swap D All ext2 Ext2 is a Linux filesystem used for ordinary files. HPFS has its historical origin in OS/2, although Linux can access it when the appropriate driver is available. Swap supplies paging backing space rather than an ordinary user-file filesystem. The native-origin scope therefore identifies ext2 without incorrectly denying Linux support for foreign filesystems or treating swap as a conventional file-storage format. A correct Ext2 is the native Linux filesystem listed. B incorrect HPFS is historically associated with OS/2, so it is not the native Linux example requested. C incorrect Swap is paging backing space, not an ordinary filesystem for storing user files. D incorrect The all option includes swap as a filesystem, contrary to the note’s explicit distinction.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 18 · Q00650
records.text: Q00650 Question 18 NSA20 The top-level directory on a Linux system is represented as _____ Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A / B $ C * D # / PDF p.63 states that the tree begins at a forward slash and calls that directory root. Thus the top-level directory is /. A correct The forward slash is explicitly the root directory (p.63). B incorrect The cited root symbol is /, not $. C incorrect The cited root symbol is /, not *. D incorrect The cited root symbol is /, not #.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 19 · Q00900
records.text: Q00900 Question 19 NSA12 Which listed item is a traffic-prioritization mechanism that can operate across layers, rather than an application mediator or service installation/configuration activity? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Proxies and agents B Installing a new service C . E-mail configuration D Quality of service Quality of service Quality of service classifies, queues and prioritizes traffic to meet performance objectives such as low delay or limited loss. It can span layers while supporting applications. Proxies and agents are mediating components, and installing a service or configuring email are administrative activities. The revised question uses those explicit functional categories, so it does not require an unsupported taxonomy that labels every item an application-layer service. A incorrect Proxies and agents mediate requests as components rather than naming the traffic-prioritization mechanism. B incorrect Installing a service is an administrative activity, not a traffic-prioritization mechanism. C incorrect Email configuration is an administrative activity rather than cross-layer traffic prioritization. D correct QoS classifies and prioritizes traffic and can operate across layers.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 20 · Q00924
records.text: Q00924 Question 20 NSA25 A data-center volume has exactly two equal disks and must retain service after either disk fails. One disk’s usable capacity is sufficient. Which listed RAID level meets these requirements? Compare striping granularity, redundancy placement, usable capacity and required disk-failure tolerance. A RAID level 3 B RAID level 1 C . RAID level 2 D RAID level 0 RAID level 1 With exactly two equal disks, RAID1 mirrors the data and leaves one disk’s usable capacity while tolerating either disk failing. RAID0 provides no disk-failure tolerance. RAID2 and RAID3 rely on different striping and redundancy layouts rather than the two-disk mirrored arrangement that meets these requirements. The choice follows the stated disk count, capacity and failure goal rather than the institution’s size or industry. A incorrect RAID3 uses byte striping with dedicated parity, not the required two-disk fault-tolerant layout. B correct A two-disk RAID1 mirror has one disk’s capacity and survives either disk failing. C incorrect RAID2 uses bit striping with Hamming redundancy, rather than the two-disk solution meeting this requirement. D incorrect RAID0 has no disk-failure tolerance.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 21 · Q00937
records.text: Q00937 Question 21 NSA25 Which listed RAID layout uses block-level striping with distributed parity and tolerates one disk failure? Compare striping granularity, redundancy placement, usable capacity and required disk-failure tolerance. A RAID 2 B RAID 1 C RAID 5 D RAID 0 RAID 5 RAID5 distributes parity across disks while striping data at block level. That distinguishes it from RAID2’s bit striping and Hamming-code redundancy. RAID1 mirrors copies instead of organizing the array as distributed-parity striping, while RAID0 adds no redundancy. The explicit granularity and parity placement identify the intended layout rather than treating every form of redundant striping as equivalent. A incorrect RAID2 uses bit striping with Hamming redundancy, not distributed block parity. B incorrect RAID1 mirrors data rather than using the specified striping-with-parity organization. C correct RAID5 uses block striping with distributed parity and one-disk failure tolerance. D incorrect RAID0 stripes without redundant parity and provides no disk-failure tolerance.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 22 · Q00954
records.text: Q00954 Question 22 NSA07 NSA-S04 Which tool directly sends ICMP echo probes to test IP reachability? Match the requested observation to the tool’s actual output; distinguish configuration, name lookup, reachability and hop discovery. A Ipconfig B Ping C Encryption D Firewall Ping Ping sends ICMP echo requests and observes replies to test IP reachability. A reply confirms that the path and target support that exchange. A missing reply may reflect filtering or loss, so it does not alone prove disconnection. Interface configuration inspection, confidentiality protection and traffic-policy enforcement serve different purposes from sending this diagnostic probe. A incorrect Ipconfig displays local adapter configuration; it does not send the requested echo probes. B correct Ping sends ICMP echo requests and checks for replies. C incorrect Encryption protects confidentiality rather than generating an echo reachability test. D incorrect A firewall permits or blocks traffic according to policy rather than being the echo-probe utility.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 23 · Q01003
records.text: Q01003 Question 23 NSA07 NSA06 Suppose you are network administrator, you want to determine the path between two connections, often a connection to another device will have to go through multiple routers. Which command would you use? Match the requested observation to the tool’s actual output; distinguish configuration, name lookup, reachability and hop discovery. A ping B nslookup C traceroute D All of the above traceroute Traceroute discovers responding intermediate hops by using packet-lifetime expiry. That provides evidence about the multi-router path toward a destination. Ping instead tests an end-to-end echo exchange, and nslookup asks DNS questions. Neither produces the requested hop sequence, so combining all the tools is not the correct description of the specific path-discovery command. Some routers may suppress responses, leaving gaps in the trace. A incorrect Ping probes end-to-end reachability, not the intermediate-hop sequence. B incorrect Nslookup inspects DNS name-resolution information, not router hops. C correct Traceroute discovers responding intermediate hops toward the destination. D incorrect Not all listed commands perform hop discovery.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 24 · Q01191
records.text: Q01191 Question 24 NSA05 NSA04 In a deployment with one unprotected DHCP server, which statements are not actual disadvantages of DHCP? Select all that apply. Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Fault on the DHCP server can affect the whole network B It is not a secured way of assigning IP addresses C Static IP address assignment can't be used. D It minimizes the load of network admin Static IP address assignment can't be used.; It minimizes the load of network admin A single DHCP service can become an availability dependency for clients needing configuration, and rogue replies are a risk in an unprotected deployment. However, DHCP does not prohibit static assignments: administrators can exclude manually used addresses to avoid conflicts. Reducing repetitive administration is also an advantage. Therefore the false limitation about static addressing and the genuine administrative benefit are the requested exceptions. A incorrect Depending on deployment, DHCP-server failure can impair clients needing leases, so this can be a disadvantage. B incorrect Rogue replies and insecure deployment are genuine risks, although DHCP security depends on protections. C correct This alleged disadvantage is false: static assignments and DHCP can coexist safely with exclusions. D correct Reducing repetitive administrator work is an advantage rather than a disadvantage.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 25 · Q01210
records.text: Q01210 Question 25 NSA03 Which listed address is the conventional IPv4 loopback address normally chosen to test the local IP stack? Select one. Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A 127.0.0.1 B 1.0.0.127 C 127.0.0.0 D 127.0.0.255 127.0.0.1 The whole 127/8 range is reserved for loopback, but 127.0.0.1 is the conventional address normally used for this test. The other 127-prefixed choices belong to the broader reserved block without being the conventional address requested. The reversed-looking 1.0.0.127 is outside loopback space. A successful loopback probe tests local protocol processing and does not establish that cables or remote devices work. A correct 127.0.0.1 is the conventional IPv4 loopback address explicitly named in the note. B incorrect 1.0.0.127 is outside the reserved 127/8 loopback block. C incorrect This belongs to loopback-reserved 127/8, but is not the conventional address requested. D incorrect This also lies in 127/8, but is not the conventional loopback address requested.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 26 · Q01216
records.text: Q01216 Question 26 NSA25 Most of the time, it is recommended to apply a Hardware RAID into your system in terms of system performance. Why? Because Hardware RAID: Compare striping granularity, redundancy placement, usable capacity and required disk-failure tolerance. A A physical storage device that is built into a system B Can appear as a single hard disk in the system C There is no difference between regular hardware and the RAID devices D Can use its own resources Hardware RAID can use its own controller resources NSA25 supports controller resources/cache as a reason hardware RAID may offload work from the host. D directly states that relevant mechanism. Appearing as one disk is a presentation property rather than the performance explanation, and neither simply being physical nor denying differences explains offload. The note also rejects any universal claim that hardware RAID always performs better. A incorrect Being a physical device alone does not explain any RAID performance advantage or computation offload. B incorrect A single logical-disk presentation does not establish that host processing work is offloaded. C incorrect Denying differences provides no performance mechanism and ignores dedicated controller resources. D correct Dedicated controller resources/cache can perform RAID work rather than relying entirely on the host CPU.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 27 · Q01271
records.text: Q01271 Question 27 NSA20 NSA17 All of the following are the roles of a system admin related to the file system and disk space management EXCEPT? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Assigning user ID and User name for system users B Determining desk usage and quota C Creating a Mounting point D Partition disk space Assigning user ID and User name for system users PDF p.42 assigns account permissions and capabilities to user administration, p.53 monitors free disk space, and p.64 identifies a mount point. Assigning a username/ID is the account task, while the other options concern storage organization or capacity. A correct This belongs to account administration (p.42), making it the requested exception. B incorrect Disk usage and quota concern the storage capacity being monitored on p.53. C incorrect A mounting point belongs to the filesystem organization illustrated by /mnt (p.64). D incorrect Partitioning concerns organizing disk space, within the storage subject rather than naming users.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 28 · Q01307
records.text: Q01307 Question 28 NSA19 NSA18 In the ordinary Unix owner/group/other rwx permission-bit model, which operation has no separate file permission bit? Identify the platform and permission model; for an rwx string, separate owner/group/other triplets and use the stated bit weights. A Read B Write C Execute D Delete Delete Each ordinary Unix permission triplet contains read, write and execute bits. There is no fourth delete bit in that model. Deletion generally depends on permissions on the parent directory, with other mechanisms such as sticky bits or ACLs able to add restrictions. Windows can have an explicit delete permission, so naming the Unix rwx model is essential to make the exception accurate. A incorrect Read is a recognized permission in both Windows and ordinary Unix permission models. B incorrect Write is a recognized access permission, not the requested generic exception. C incorrect Execute/read-execute permissions exist in the models described in the note. D correct Unix rwx has no separate delete bit; deletion usually depends on the parent directory.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 29 · Q01495
records.text: Q01495 Question 29 NSA05 NSA03 After DHCP fails at startup, a client self-configures an IPv4 link-local interface address for same-link communication. Which address could it assign? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A 255.255.255.255 B 127.0.0.1 C 169.254.2.33 D 0.0.0.0 169.254.2.33 as an IPv4 link-local fallback An IPv4 link-local fallback uses the 169.254 range; 169.254.2.33 is a usable example. This can permit communication with peers on the same link, but does not provide ordinary routed Internet connectivity. The other values serve special broadcast, loopback or unspecified-address roles. In particular, 0.0.0.0 may appear before configuration but is not the assigned link-local address requested here. A incorrect This is the limited-broadcast destination, not an assigned host address. B incorrect Loopback addresses the local host, not its link-local interface. C correct 169.254.2.33 is an IPv4 link-local fallback address. D incorrect The unspecified address is not a configured link-local host address.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 30 · Q01592
records.text: Q01592 Question 30 NSA27 NSA01 Which action is not sound OS hardening when required services must remain available? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Remove unnecessary applications and services B Install patches C Configure users and permissions D Block every port, including ports required by legitimate services. Block every port, including ports required by legitimate services. Hardening reduces unnecessary exposure while preserving the services the system must provide. Removing unused software, deploying supported patches and restricting accounts or permissions all support that goal. Filtering unused ports can help too, but indiscriminately blocking ports required by legitimate services destroys availability. The port option states that harmful action explicitly rather than treating every form of port filtering as inappropriate. A incorrect Removing unnecessary applications/services reduces attack surface and is an explicit hardening action. B incorrect Supported patches repair known weaknesses and are part of hardening. C incorrect Restricting users and permissions is an explicit hardening measure. D correct Blocking ports required by legitimate services defeats availability rather than sound hardening.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 31 · SM0028
records.text: SM0028 Question 31 NSA-S04 NSA07 You know the upstairs computer’s IP address and want a basic end-to-end ICMP echo reachability test, rather than a router-hop trace. Which command should you use? Match the requested observation to the tool’s actual output; distinguish configuration, name lookup, reachability and hop discovery. A nslookup B ping C DHCP discover D traceroute ping Ping directly tests whether the addressed computer and path support an ICMP echo exchange. A reply is useful reachability evidence; absence of a reply may result from filtering or loss. Nslookup tests DNS, DHCP discovery seeks configuration service, and traceroute identifies responding intermediate hops. These answer different operational questions from the basic echo test requested. A incorrect Nslookup queries DNS, which is unnecessary for the specified known-IP echo test. B correct Ping performs the requested end-to-end ICMP echo test. C incorrect DHCP discovery locates configuration service rather than testing this remote host. D incorrect Traceroute probes the hop path rather than performing the requested basic echo test.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 32 · SM0084
records.text: SM0084 Question 32 NSA01 Which one of the following is correct about human role in system administration? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Ethics is not a requirement to manage computers B It requires patience, understanding and knowledge C It doesn't need organizational skills D System administrator is not expected to have skills and confidence Patience, understanding and knowledge NSA01 includes human abilities and responsible conduct in administration: patience, communication, ethics, technical understanding and organization. B agrees with that account. The other statements deny ethics, organization or expected competence, directly contradicting the note’s description of the role rather than identifying a valid human requirement. A incorrect NSA01 explicitly includes ethics among the qualities required for responsible administration. B correct Patience and technical understanding/knowledge agree directly with the human qualities listed in NSA01. C incorrect Organization is explicitly important, so denying organizational skills contradicts the note. D incorrect The role requires technical understanding and competent administration rather than an absence of skills.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 33 · SM0270
records.text: SM0270 Question 33 NSA01 NSA08 A planned hardware upgrade requires the system to be powered off, and an acceptable maintenance window and rollback are arranged. Which listed circumstance justifies the planned shutdown? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Using regular schedules B For maintenance and upgrade C To check for security alerts D When there is a failure For maintenance and upgrade A shutdown is justified when the required procedure needs it and its service impact has been planned. Here the hardware upgrade explicitly requires power-off and an acceptable window has been arranged. A calendar schedule alone is insufficient, checking alerts ordinarily requires no shutdown, and no failure is described. The decision therefore follows the actual maintenance requirement rather than a universal rule that systems should stop periodically. A incorrect A regular calendar schedule alone does not justify shutting down a service without considering impact and necessity. B correct The stated maintenance/upgrade procedure requires a planned power-off. C incorrect Checking alerts does not ordinarily require stopping the system and supplies no shutdown justification here. D incorrect No failure is described; the shutdown is required for the planned upgrade.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 34 · SM0287
records.text: SM0287 Question 34 NSA24 NSA17 Which one of the following is NOT a reason for the need of backups? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Security incidents B Upgrades and migrations C Hardware failures D Authorization Authorization Backups preserve recoverable earlier data after hardware loss, compromise, corruption or failed upgrades and migrations. These events can destroy or damage the live copy, so independent protected copies and tested restores address their consequences. Authorization instead decides who may access current resources. It is essential security policy, but is a separate function from preserving copies for recovery. A incorrect Compromise can damage or delete data, creating a restoration need. B incorrect Failed upgrades or migrations can require restoring the previous valid data. C incorrect Hardware failure can destroy the live copy and require recovery. D correct Authorization governs current access rights; it is not a data-loss recovery reason.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 35 · SS099
records.text: SS099 Question 35 NSA19 The ordinary file permission string -rwxr--r-- is represented by which octal mode? Identify the platform and permission model; for an rwx string, separate owner/group/other triplets and use the stated bit weights. A 744 B 700 C 755 D 766 744. The leading hyphen identifies an ordinary file and is not a permission bit. Split the remaining characters as rwx | r-- | r--. The owner has 4+2+1=7, the group has read only (4), and others have read only (4). Writing those three octal digits in order gives 744, so A is correct. A correct 744 exactly represents owner rwx, group r-- and others r--. B incorrect 700 would deny both group and others all permissions, unlike the two read permissions shown. C incorrect 755 would give group and others execute permission as well as read permission; those execute bits are absent. D incorrect 766 would give group and others write permission; neither triplet contains w.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 36 · AM0564
records.text: AM0564 Question 36 NSA01 What is the primary role of a system administrator? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Designing computer networks B Developing software applications C Managing and maintaining computer systems D Providing technical support to end-users Managing and maintaining computer systems PDF p.28 describes getting computer systems running and keeping them running; p.29 calls system administration the management of computers. C captures that broad primary role rather than one subtask. A incorrect Network design is one challenge (p.30), narrower than maintaining computer systems. B incorrect The definition is operational management, not developing applications (p.28). C correct Managing and maintaining systems directly matches pp.28–29. D incorrect User support is included (p.29), but is only part of the broader role.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 37 · AM0565
records.text: AM0565 Question 37 NSA01 NSA22 Under the note’s primary division of administrative responsibilities, which listed task directly concerns ongoing network connectivity, performance and protection? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Installing and configuring operating systems B Monitoring network performance and security C Developing software applications D Providing end-user training Monitoring network performance and security Network administrators primarily maintain connectivity, addressing, routes, devices and performance. Monitoring network performance and security directly matches that operational scope. Operating-system installation and user training may be shared administrative duties, but they do not directly describe the ongoing network-monitoring task asked for. Developing software applications has a different primary purpose. The scope selects the core network responsibility without claiming exclusive job boundaries. A incorrect OS installation can overlap with administrative work, but is not the ongoing network-monitoring task requested. B correct Monitoring network performance and security directly matches network-administration responsibilities. C incorrect Developing application software is not a network-administration responsibility established by this note. D incorrect User training may be shared, but does not directly name monitoring network operation.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 38 · AM0566
records.text: AM0566 Question 38 NSA01 What is the purpose of system administration? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Managing software development projects B Ensuring the availability and reliability of computer systems C Managing user accounts and permissions D Designing computer networks Ensuring the availability and reliability of computer systems Keeping systems running (PDF p.28) and seeking predictability as the basis of reliability (p.31) support availability and reliability as the purpose. User permissions are a means of administration (p.42), not its full goal. A incorrect Software-project management is not the system-operation goal defined on p.28. B correct Availability follows from keeping systems running; reliability is explicitly tied to predictability (pp.28,31). C incorrect Account and permission management is a narrower activity (p.42). D incorrect Design is one planning task, narrower than the operational goal (pp.28,30).

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 39 · AM0567
records.text: AM0567 Question 39 NSA17 NSA-S01 What is a key principle of system administration? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Least privilege B Agile development C Object-oriented programming D Cloud computing Least privilege NSA01 explicitly identifies least privilege among administration principles: give accounts and processes only the access required for their work. Agile development and object-oriented programming are development approaches; cloud computing is a computing/deployment model. They may occur in administered systems but are not the administration access principle asked for. A correct Least privilege is explicitly named as a system-administration principle in NSA01. B incorrect Agile development organizes software work rather than specifying the administration access principle in the note. C incorrect Object-oriented programming structures software; it is not the stated system-administration principle. D incorrect Cloud computing is a delivery/deployment model, not the access-control principle listed in NSA01.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 40 · AM0568
records.text: AM0568 Question 40 NSA01 NSA17 Using the note’s primary role division, which role is responsible for host-local accounts together with host storage, software and availability? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Network administrator B Database administrator C Security administrator D System administrator System administrator System administrators maintain hosts, accounts, storage, software and availability. Network administrators focus on connectivity and routes, while security administrators coordinate controls and policy. Database administration concerns a different resource scope. Responsibilities can overlap, but the stated question asks for the primary host-level role associated with the complete stated set of duties rather than implying that no other administrator ever manages accounts. A incorrect The primary network role concerns connectivity, addressing and routing rather than this host-level bundle. B incorrect Database-account administration is a narrower resource scope than the host-level duties listed. C incorrect Security administration coordinates controls and policy rather than the complete host-maintenance bundle. D correct System administration is assigned hosts, accounts, storage, software and availability.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 41 · AM0569
records.text: AM0569 Question 41 NSA01 NSA02 What is the purpose of network administration? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Managing computer hardware B Managing computer software C Managing network infrastructure D Managing user accounts Managing network infrastructure PDF p.29 distinguishes the management of computers from management of network infrastructure devices, explicitly adopting the latter meaning for network administration. C is the direct match. A incorrect General hardware management is broader than the infrastructure-device definition on p.29. B incorrect General software management is not the adopted network-administration definition. C correct The module defines network administration as managing routers, switches and network infrastructure (p.29). D incorrect Account management is an administration subtask but not the adopted infrastructure-focused definition.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 42 · AM0570
records.text: AM0570 Question 42 NSA26 NSA01 What is the role of a security administrator in system administration? Distinguish the security objective from the control that prevents, detects or recovers from the stated problem. A Monitoring network performance B Managing user accounts and permissions C Enforcing security policies and procedures D Configuring network devices Enforcing security policies and procedures PDF p.30 requires putting security procedures in place and ensuring they are followed; p.34 says domain controllers enforce security policy. Enforcing policies and procedures is therefore the best statement of the security role, without assuming exclusive staffing boundaries. A incorrect Performance monitoring is separately discussed as capacity management (p.29). B incorrect Account permissions contribute to access security but are narrower than enforcing security procedures. C correct The duty to ensure security procedures are followed is explicit on p.30. D incorrect Configuring devices is not by itself the policy-enforcement purpose described on p.30.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 43 · AM0571
records.text: AM0571 Question 43 NSA-S02 NSA24 Which concept in system administration emphasizes the importance of regularly backing up data? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Redundancy B Fault tolerance C Disaster recovery D Load balancing Disaster recovery PDF p.30 explicitly pairs “Backup and disaster recovery planning.” Its backup duty protects against network/component failure. Disaster recovery is therefore the choice directly connected to regular data backup in the module. A incorrect Redundancy can protect operation but is not the theme explicitly paired with backups on p.30. B incorrect Fault tolerance is not the module’s named backup-planning concept here. C correct Backup and disaster recovery planning are explicitly paired (p.30). D incorrect Load balancing is not connected to backup planning in this passage.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 44 · AM0572
records.text: AM0572 Question 44 NSA08 NSA09 Which skill describes the general process of diagnosing faults and selecting fixes across system-administration tasks, rather than a specialized design, database or cabling task? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Graphic design B Database query optimization C Troubleshooting and problem-solving D Network cable installation Troubleshooting and problem-solving Troubleshooting and problem-solving cover defining symptoms, gathering evidence, forming testable hypotheses, isolating causes, applying targeted fixes and verifying service. This process applies across many administration duties. Graphic design, query optimization and cable installation may be useful specialized activities, but none names the broad diagnostic process requested. The scope does not imply that administrators never perform those other tasks. A incorrect Graphic design concerns visual communication rather than the general diagnostic process. B incorrect Query optimization improves database query behavior, a specialized task. C correct Troubleshooting and problem-solving name the requested cross-task diagnostic skill. D incorrect Cable installation is a physical infrastructure task rather than the general reasoning process.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 45 · AM0573
records.text: AM0573 Question 45 NSA27 Which tasks belong to administrator-side software update and patch management, rather than authoring the software patch? Select all that apply. Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Developing software patches B Testing software updates C Installing and deploying software updates D Analyzing software vulnerabilities Testing software updates; Installing and deploying software updates; Analyzing software vulnerabilities Patch administration includes assessing relevant weaknesses, testing or staging an update, preparing rollback, deploying it and verifying the result. These steps help choose and safely apply the appropriate repair. Writing the vendor’s software patch is a development activity rather than the operational workflow being classified. The multiple-selection instruction retains the complementary assessment, testing and deployment responsibilities instead of forcing an installation-only answer. A incorrect Writing the software patch is a development responsibility, not the patch-administration workflow stated here. B correct Testing/staging updates before deployment is an explicit administrator duty. C correct Deploying and verifying software updates is also an explicit administrator duty. D correct Assessing known weaknesses helps prioritize relevant patches and is part of the stated vulnerability-management workflow.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 46 · AM0574
records.text: AM0574 Question 46 NSA10 Which listed protocol sends or relays email messages between mail systems? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A FTP B HTTP C SMTP D DHCP SMTP SMTP is the mail sending and relay protocol. HTTP serves web resources, so a webmail interface can use HTTP without making it the mail-transfer protocol requested here. FTP transfers files as its named service, and DHCP supplies host configuration. Distinguishing the mail transport role from a user-facing web interface removes the broad interpretation of providing email services. A incorrect FTP is a file-transfer protocol, not the listed mail relay protocol. B incorrect HTTP serves web resources; webmail access is distinct from mail-system relay. C correct SMTP sends and relays email messages. D incorrect DHCP supplies host configuration rather than transferring email.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 47 · AM0575
records.text: AM0575 Question 47 NSA06 NSA10 Which service translates domain names into IP addresses? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A DNS B DHCP C FTP D HTTP DNS Name-to-address translation is forward DNS resolution. NSA06 specifies A records for IPv4 and AAAA for IPv6. DHCP instead provides host configuration, while FTP and HTTP provide application data-transfer services. Those functions are distinct from resolving a domain name into its address records. A correct DNS forward resolution maps names to address records, using A or AAAA as appropriate. B incorrect DHCP supplies client addresses and options rather than translating arbitrary domain names. C incorrect FTP transfers files and does not provide the domain-name resolution service. D incorrect HTTP exchanges web resources rather than serving as the name-to-address directory service.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 48 · AM0576
records.text: AM0576 Question 48 NSA10 NSA06 Which listed protocols transfer file content from a server to a client as part of their ordinary service? Select all that apply. Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A SMTP B DNS C FTP D HTTP FTP; HTTP FTP is specifically a file-transfer protocol, while HTTP also transfers file resources through web request and response exchanges. Their service semantics differ, but the broad content-transfer capability applies to both. SMTP is classified here as mail submission and relay, and DNS as name resolution. The revised selection instruction recognizes the two qualifying services without pretending that file transfer is exclusive to one protocol. A incorrect SMTP is identified with mail submission/relay rather than the file-transfer service in this comparison. B incorrect DNS resolves names and is not the offered file-content transfer service. C correct FTP is explicitly a named protocol for client/server file transfer. D correct HTTP also transfers file resources, so the general function is not exclusive to FTP.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 49 · AM0577
records.text: AM0577 Question 49 NSA04 NSA10 Which service is responsible for assigning IP addresses to devices on a network? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A DNS B DHCP C FTP D HTTP DHCP NSA04 assigns host-address configuration to DHCP, including a server-managed scope and time-limited leases. DNS resolves names, while FTP and HTTP transfer application content. Therefore DHCP is the network service responsible for automatically supplying a device’s IP configuration among these options. A incorrect DNS resolves names into records; it does not lease the device’s own network address. B correct DHCP supplies addresses and configuration options to clients from a managed scope. C incorrect FTP transfers files rather than assigning network addresses to devices. D incorrect HTTP provides web request/response services and not host-address allocation.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 50 · AM0578
records.text: AM0578 Question 50 NSA10 NSA30 Which protocol is used for secure remote login and file transfer? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A SSH B DNS C FTP D HTTP SSH, with SFTP for file transfer over SSH NSA10 assigns protected remote login to SSH and file transfer over that protected connection to SFTP. Thus SSH is the underlying secure protocol family among these options. DNS provides naming; ordinary FTP and HTTP do not by themselves provide the protected remote-login capability in the stem. A correct SSH protects remote login and supports the SFTP file-transfer service over SSH. B incorrect DNS resolves names and supplies neither remote terminal login nor a secure file-transfer session. C incorrect Ordinary FTP transfers files but is distinct from SFTP and does not supply encrypted remote login. D incorrect Ordinary HTTP supplies web exchange semantics, not the SSH remote-login and SFTP functions.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 51 · AM0579
records.text: AM0579 Question 51 NSA11 NSA06 Which service is used for translating private IP addresses to public IP addresses? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A NAT B DNS C FTP D HTTP NAT NAT rewrites network addresses, commonly translating private internal IPv4 addresses for access to a public network. Routing still selects the path and NAT does not replace firewall or authentication policy. DNS resolves names, FTP transfers files, and HTTP serves web resources. Those application services may run through a translating router, but they do not perform the address-rewriting function themselves. A correct NAT performs the requested address translation. B incorrect DNS maps names and related records rather than rewriting packet addresses. C incorrect FTP transfers files rather than translating network addresses. D incorrect HTTP serves web resources rather than rewriting IP addresses.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 52 · AM0580
records.text: AM0580 Question 52 NSA10 Which protocol is used for web browsing? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A SMTP B DNS C FTP D HTTP HTTP Web browsing obtains resources through web request/response exchanges. NSA10 identifies HTTP/HTTPS for these resources, making HTTP the offered protocol. SMTP handles mail submission/relay, DNS handles name resolution and FTP handles its own file-transfer service; they may assist applications but do not define the web exchange asked for. A incorrect SMTP submits and relays email rather than serving browser web resources. B incorrect DNS resolves server names and is a supporting service rather than the web resource-transfer protocol. C incorrect FTP is a separate file-transfer protocol, not the normal web-browsing exchange named in the note. D correct HTTP supplies web-resource request/response exchanges and is explicitly named for web services.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 53 · AM0581
records.text: AM0581 Question 53 NSA10 NSA30 Which service provides remote access to a network from a different location? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A VPN B DNS C FTP D HTTP VPN A remote user can extend private-network connectivity through a VPN over another network, matching the service in the stem. DNS performs lookup, FTP transfers files and HTTP serves web resources. Those can be reachable remotely but do not by themselves extend private network access as the VPN service does. A correct A VPN extends private connectivity across another network to support remote access. B incorrect DNS supplies name resolution rather than a remote private-network connection. C incorrect FTP supplies access to a file-transfer service rather than general remote network connectivity. D incorrect HTTP supplies web-resource access rather than the private-network extension described.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 54 · AM0582
records.text: AM0582 Question 54 NSA10 Which protocol is used for real-time communication, such as video conferencing? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A SMTP B DNS C FTP D RTP RTP NSA10 identifies RTP as carrying real-time media timing and sequence information, commonly over UDP. That is the relevant protocol for conference media among the options. The answer does not imply guaranteed deadlines: actual delivery depends on the network and application. SMTP, DNS and FTP have unrelated mail, naming and file-transfer roles. A incorrect SMTP handles mail submission/relay, not real-time conference media timing and sequencing. B incorrect DNS resolves names and is not the media transport protocol described. C incorrect FTP transfers files rather than carrying the real-time media timing/sequence service. D correct RTP carries real-time media timing and sequence information, including uses such as video conferencing.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 55 · AM0583
records.text: AM0583 Question 55 NSA11 Which service, using its many-to-one address-and-port translation form, lets several private IPv4 devices share one public IPv4 address? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A NAT B DNS C FTP D HTTP NAT Many-to-one NAT with port translation maintains separate bindings for internal flows. Multiple clients can therefore appear under one public address while distinct translated ports allow replies to return to the right client. This is a particular form of NAT, not a property of every NAT configuration. DNS, FTP and HTTP supply naming, file-transfer and web services rather than the address-sharing mechanism. A correct NAT in its PAT/NAPT form maps multiple internal flows to one public address. B incorrect DNS resolves names rather than maintaining address-and-port translation bindings. C incorrect FTP transfers files; it is not the address-sharing mechanism. D incorrect HTTP serves web resources; it does not provide the translation bindings.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 56 · AM0584
records.text: AM0584 Question 56 NSA26 Which policy conflicts with restricting access to a protected internal network to authorized users, assuming the wireless service directly admits users to that network? Distinguish the security objective from the control that prevents, detects or recovers from the stated problem. A Password complexity requirements B Firewall configuration C Regular data backups D Open wireless network access Open wireless network access A protected internal network requires controlled admission. Password requirements, appropriately configured firewall rules and protected regular backups can implement security and recovery policy. Unrestricted open wireless admission to the same protected network bypasses that admission requirement. An intentionally isolated guest service would be a different case; it is excluded by the stated direct-access condition. A incorrect Password requirements support authentication and controlled access. B incorrect Firewall policy can restrict access to authorized systems. C incorrect Regular backups support recovery and availability. D correct Unrestricted open wireless admission bypasses authorization for the protected network.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 57 · AM0585
records.text: AM0585 Question 57 NSA30 NSA28 NSA12 Which purpose is directly served when a firewall applies permit/deny rules to incoming network traffic? Distinguish the security objective from the control that prevents, detects or recovers from the stated problem. A To prevent unauthorized access to the network B To encrypt network traffic C To manage network bandwidth D To monitor network performance To prevent unauthorized access to the network A firewall applies policy to allow permitted traffic and reject disallowed access. This directly supports preventing unauthorized network access. Encryption protects confidentiality, bandwidth management allocates or shapes traffic capacity, and performance monitoring measures service behavior. A device may combine these features, but the stated permit/deny operation is access enforcement rather than those separate functions. A correct Permit/deny filtering directly prevents disallowed network access. B incorrect Encryption protects confidentiality and is not inherent in traffic filtering. C incorrect Bandwidth management controls traffic capacity rather than authorization. D incorrect Performance monitoring measures behavior rather than enforcing permit/deny policy.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 58 · AM0586
records.text: AM0586 Question 58 NSA27 NSA28 NSA30 Which of the following is an example of a network security vulnerability? Distinguish the security objective from the control that prevents, detects or recovers from the stated problem. A Weak password policies B Regular software updates C Use of strong encryption algorithms D Implementing access control lists Weak password policies NSA27 identifies weak passwords as exploitable weaknesses. A policy permitting them creates the corresponding vulnerability. Regular updates, appropriate encryption and access-control lists are protective measures when correctly deployed, rather than examples of the weakness requested. They are not guarantees of security, but their stated role here is defensive. A correct Weak password policy permits easily compromised credentials and creates an exploitable access weakness. B incorrect Regular updates address known software weaknesses rather than constituting the vulnerability example requested. C incorrect Strong appropriately used encryption is a protective measure rather than an example of weak authentication policy. D incorrect Access-control lists restrict permitted actions/traffic and are a defensive control when properly configured.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 59 · AM0587
records.text: AM0587 Question 59 NSA23 NSA28 What is the purpose of intrusion detection systems (IDS)? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A To prevent network attacks B To monitor network traffic for suspicious activities C To encrypt network communications D To block malicious software Monitor for suspicious activity and alert NSA23 distinguishes detection from prevention. An IDS monitors for suspicious activity and generates detection/alerts; blocking inline is an IPS capability. Encryption is a separate data-protection mechanism. Although IDS findings can support a broader prevention program, direct prevention or malware blocking is not the defining IDS role stated here. A incorrect Direct blocking/prevention is the IPS distinction; an IDS primarily detects and alerts. B correct Monitoring traffic for suspicious behavior matches the IDS detection/alert role. C incorrect Encrypting communications is a confidentiality mechanism, not intrusion detection. D incorrect Blocking malicious software is a preventive action, not the defining monitoring/alert purpose of an IDS.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 60 · AM0588
records.text: AM0588 Question 60 NSA08 NSA-S04 During troubleshooting, which action tests IP reachability with ICMP echo messages without changing the system or network configuration? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Configuring a firewall rule B Conducting a security audit C Installing antivirus software D Ping testing network connectivity Ping testing network connectivity A ping test gathers reachability evidence by exchanging ICMP echo messages. It is a diagnostic observation rather than a configuration change. Firewall rule changes can be legitimate fixes for a diagnosed filtering fault, while audits and antivirus installation serve other security purposes. None of those alternatives performs the specific echo test requested. A failed test must still be interpreted alongside filtering and loss. A incorrect Changing a firewall rule changes policy rather than performing the specified observation. B incorrect A security audit assesses controls; it is not an ICMP echo test. C incorrect Installing antivirus changes host protection rather than sending echo probes. D correct Ping performs the specified reachability test without changing network policy.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 61 · AM0589
records.text: AM0589 Question 61 NSA23 Under the note’s primary tool-role classification, which is the conventional general-purpose packet capture and dissection analyzer? Match the requested observation to the tool’s actual output; distinguish configuration, name lookup, reachability and hop discovery. A Wireshark B Nmap C Snort D Nessus Wireshark Wireshark is identified as the conventional analyzer for capturing and dissecting packets. Snort also has sniffing and logging capabilities, but its primary role in this comparison is suspicious-traffic detection and alerting. Nmap discovers hosts, ports and services, while Nessus assesses vulnerabilities and configuration. The primary-role scope distinguishes the intended analyzer without incorrectly denying overlapping packet capabilities in other tools. A correct Wireshark captures and dissects packets and is a conventional general packet analyzer. B incorrect Nmap performs host, port and service discovery rather than general packet capture/dissection. C incorrect Snort can sniff and log, but is classified primarily here by suspicious-traffic detection rather than as the conventional general analyzer. D incorrect Nessus is identified with vulnerability/configuration assessment rather than the packet-analyzer role.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 62 · AM0590
records.text: AM0590 Question 62 NSA29 Which of the following is an example of a denial-of-service (DoS) attack? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Man-in-the-middle attack B Phishing attack C Distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack D Brute-force attack Distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) DDoS is denial of service performed from distributed sources, so it is directly a type of DoS. Interception, phishing and brute force describe different attack mechanisms; each might have secondary effects, but those names alone do not identify the service-availability attack requested. NSA29 supplies the explicit DoS/DDoS relationship. A incorrect An interception attack reads or alters communications; its name does not identify denial of service. B incorrect Phishing deceives users rather than specifically exhausting or denying a service. C correct DDoS is a denial-of-service attack using distributed sources. D incorrect Brute force tries credentials; that mechanism is distinct from the denial-of-service category asked about.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 63 · AM0591
records.text: AM0591 Question 63 NSA10 NSA28 NSA12 For a secure VPN tunnel already providing private connectivity, which option identifies the mechanism that keeps intercepted tunnel payloads confidential? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A To encrypt network traffic B To block unauthorized access C To manage network bandwidth D To analyze network performance To encrypt network traffic A secure VPN commonly encrypts and authenticates its tunnel traffic. Encryption protects the content against disclosure to an observer who intercepts packets, assuming appropriate configuration and keys. Admission rules can restrict who connects, but that is a different question from protecting intercepted payloads. Bandwidth management and performance analysis also serve different purposes. The secure-tunnel scope avoids claiming that every unqualified VPN automatically encrypts. A correct Encryption hides tunnel payload contents from an interceptor without the required keys. B incorrect Blocking unauthorized admission is distinct from protecting the content of already intercepted packets. C incorrect Bandwidth management is QoS/traffic management, not the defining private-connectivity purpose of a VPN. D incorrect Performance analysis is monitoring; VPN connectivity does not make it a packet or performance analyzer.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 64 · AM0592
records.text: AM0592 Question 64 NSA29 NSA27 Which of the following is an example of a security incident response action? Distinguish the security objective from the control that prevents, detects or recovers from the stated problem. A Regular software updates B Password policy enforcement C Incident investigation and analysis D Network configuration backup Incident investigation and analysis PDF p.30 requires personnel to respond quickly and effectively to security failures and to diagnose and troubleshoot problems. Investigation and analysis is the option that reacts to an incident rather than routine prevention or preservation. A incorrect Regular updating is a routine patching activity (p.30), rather than investigating an incident. B incorrect Password-policy enforcement is an ongoing access-security measure, not the incident investigation requested. C correct Investigation/analysis implements diagnosis and effective response after security failure (p.30). D incorrect Configuration backup preserves data and is not the investigative response action.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 65 · AM0593
records.text: AM0593 Question 65 NSA23 Which tool is commonly used for network scanning and host discovery? Match the requested observation to the tool’s actual output; distinguish configuration, name lookup, reachability and hop discovery. A Wireshark B Nmap C Snort D Nessus Nmap The requested scanning and discovery role directly matches Nmap in NSA23. Wireshark captures/dissects packets, Snort detects suspicious traffic and Nessus assesses vulnerabilities/configurations. These capabilities can complement discovery, but Nmap is the tool explicitly named for the requested host/port/service scan rather than those other primary purposes. A incorrect Wireshark’s identified role is packet capture/dissection rather than active host and port discovery. B correct Nmap is explicitly described as discovering hosts, ports and services. C incorrect Snort’s identified role is traffic inspection/detection, not the host-discovery scanning tool requested. D incorrect Nessus assesses vulnerabilities/configuration; Nmap is the note’s explicit general host/port discovery tool.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 66 · AM0594
records.text: AM0594 Question 66 NSA26 NSA28 A policy is being developed specifically to prevent disclosure of confidential records to unauthorized people. Which listed goal directly matches that objective? Distinguish the security objective from the control that prevents, detects or recovers from the stated problem. A Ensuring system availability B Protecting sensitive data C Increasing network speed D Enhancing user experience Protecting sensitive data Security policies can support confidentiality, integrity and availability, with priorities set by organizational objectives. This scenario explicitly prioritizes preventing unauthorized disclosure of confidential records, which is sensitive-data protection. Availability remains a legitimate security goal but addresses continued service rather than disclosure. Network speed and user experience have different primary objectives. The explicit policy objective determines the selection without imposing one universal priority on all policies. A incorrect Availability concerns continued service rather than the specified disclosure objective. B correct Protecting sensitive data directly addresses the stated confidentiality goal. C incorrect Network speed is a performance objective, not the security-policy priority defined in the note. D incorrect User experience can affect usability but is not the stated universal security-policy goal.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 67 · AM0595
records.text: AM0595 Question 67 NSA26 Which of the following is an example of a security policy? Distinguish the security objective from the control that prevents, detects or recovers from the stated problem. A Setting strong password requirements B Monitoring network bandwidth C Updating software patches D Configuring firewall rules Strong password requirements A states a required behavior: passwords must satisfy specified strength requirements. That matches policy rather than an observation or operational change. Patching and firewall configuration implement controls and can be required by policy, but the options describe those actions without stating the governing requirement. Monitoring bandwidth is measurement rather than a policy statement. A correct Requiring strong passwords states mandatory behavior and is an explicit security-policy example. B incorrect Monitoring bandwidth is an operational measurement, not a stated security requirement. C incorrect Applying patches implements protection; a policy would state the required deadline/scope rather than merely the action. D incorrect Configuring rules implements policy, whereas the option does not itself state required behavior or governance.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 68 · AM0596
records.text: AM0596 Question 68 NSA17 NSA18 NSA30 Which option states the most general purpose of access control, covering user permissions on logical resources as well as physical restrictions? Distinguish the security objective from the control that prevents, detects or recovers from the stated problem. A Limiting physical access to servers B Controlling user access to resources C Monitoring network traffic D Performing system backups Controlling user access to resources Access control decides which users or other subjects may use protected resources and which actions they may perform. Limiting physical entry to a server is one particular control, but does not express the broader account-and-resource permission function. Traffic monitoring observes activity, and backups preserve recoverable data. The general resource-access description therefore best covers the stated scope. A incorrect Physical server access restriction is a valid but narrower example. B correct Controlling user access to resources expresses the general purpose. C incorrect Monitoring observes activity rather than deciding resource permissions. D incorrect Backups preserve copies for recovery rather than granting access rights.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 69 · AM0597
records.text: AM0597 Question 69 NSA30 NSA23 Which option describes a firewall’s direct traffic-enforcement role, rather than observation, auditing or confidentiality protection? Distinguish the security objective from the control that prevents, detects or recovers from the stated problem. A Monitoring network traffic for security threats B Encrypting network communications C Blocking unauthorized access to the network D Auditing network activity Blocking unauthorized access to the network A firewall enforces traffic policy by permitting authorized flows and blocking disallowed ones. Monitoring and audit records can accompany this enforcement, but observing or recording activity does not itself express the requested permit-or-block action. Encryption protects communication confidentiality and is a separate function, even when a product combines it with firewall features. A incorrect Monitoring may accompany filtering, but observation is not the requested enforcement action. B incorrect Encryption protects confidentiality rather than deciding whether a flow is permitted. C correct Blocking unauthorized access directly enforces the traffic policy. D incorrect Auditing records or reviews activity rather than directly enforcing a traffic decision.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 70 · AM0598
records.text: AM0598 Question 70 NSA23 NSA27 What is the purpose of vulnerability scanning in network and system administration? Distinguish the security objective from the control that prevents, detects or recovers from the stated problem. A Identifying security weaknesses and vulnerabilities B Encrypting sensitive data during transmission C Monitoring network bandwidth usage D Managing system logs Identify potential security weaknesses Vulnerability scanning assesses potential weaknesses and configuration problems, as NSA23 explains. It does not itself prove successful exploitation. Encryption, bandwidth measurement and log management are separate administration functions. Therefore A identifies the scan’s purpose while retaining the note’s caution that scan findings require contextual verification. A correct Finding potential security weaknesses and configuration vulnerabilities is the purpose assigned to vulnerability assessment. B incorrect Encryption protects data confidentiality and is not the act of checking for weaknesses. C incorrect Bandwidth monitoring measures traffic use rather than testing known vulnerability patterns. D incorrect Log management stores/organizes records and is distinct from scanning systems for weaknesses.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 71 · AM0599
records.text: AM0599 Question 71 NSA27 NSA30 Which of the following is a common vulnerability in computer systems? Distinguish the security objective from the control that prevents, detects or recovers from the stated problem. A Strong password policies B Regular software updates C Unpatched software vulnerabilities D Secure network segmentation Unpatched exploitable software NSA27 explicitly gives unpatched exploitable software as a vulnerability. Strong password policy, software updates and secure segmentation are defensive practices intended to reduce exposure. They can be imperfectly implemented, but as stated they are not the example of an exploitable weakness requested by the question. A incorrect Strong password policy is intended to reduce credential weaknesses rather than exemplify one. B incorrect Regular updates address known flaws and are a hardening practice. C correct Unpatched exploitable software contains a known weakness that an attack can exploit. D incorrect Secure segmentation restricts exposure and permitted flows rather than constituting the vulnerability example.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 72 · AM0600
records.text: AM0600 Question 72 NSA29 What is the purpose of security incident response in network and system administration? Distinguish the security objective from the control that prevents, detects or recovers from the stated problem. A Preventing security incidents from occurring B Recovering data after a security breach C Analyzing network performance D Detecting and responding to security incidents Detecting and responding to security incidents PDF p.30 requires responding quickly and effectively to security failure, while p.54 includes intrusion detection and security monitoring. Detection and response therefore cover the requested process more fully than prevention alone or post-breach data recovery alone. A incorrect Prevention alone omits the explicit response to failures that occur (p.30). B incorrect Recovery is a narrower possible consequence; the response duty is broader (p.30). C incorrect Performance analysis addresses operational resources rather than the security-failure response. D correct Security detection/monitoring (p.54) plus responding to failures (p.30) jointly supports this.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 73 · AM0601
records.text: AM0601 Question 73 NSA28 NSA30 NSA24 What protection does correctly implemented authenticated encryption provide for network data? Distinguish the security objective from the control that prevents, detects or recovers from the stated problem. A Preventing unauthorized access to the network B Monitoring network traffic for anomalies C Protecting data confidentiality and integrity D Performing system backups Protecting data confidentiality and integrity Encryption supplies confidentiality when keys and nonces are used correctly. Authenticated encryption also detects unauthorized alteration through integrity and authenticity protection. This explicit construction therefore supports both properties named together in the selected option. Network admission, traffic-anomaly monitoring and backup recovery are separate controls; none is performed merely by encrypting and authenticating a data payload. A incorrect Network admission/access control is distinct from encrypting content for confidentiality. B incorrect Anomaly detection is a monitoring function and does not describe the role of encryption. C correct Authenticated encryption combines confidentiality with integrity/authenticity protection. D incorrect Backups recover previous data and are not performed by encryption itself.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 74 · AM0602
records.text: AM0602 Question 74 NSA27 Which listed activities can be security controls when implemented for the stated purpose: A recovery, B least-privilege account provisioning, C secure device configuration, D suspicious-traffic detection? Select all that apply. Distinguish the security objective from the control that prevents, detects or recovers from the stated problem. A Data backup and recovery procedures B User account creation C Network device configuration D Network traffic analysis Data backup and recovery procedures; User account creation; Network device configuration; Network traffic analysis Security controls include prevention, detection and recovery rather than only one technical mechanism. Backups support recovery, controlled account creation restricts access, secure device configuration reduces exposure, and traffic analysis can detect suspicious behavior. Each listed activity therefore qualifies under its explicit purpose. Simply performing an activity without an objective would not prove effectiveness, but the question supplies the security objective needed to classify it. A correct Backups and recovery procedures restore service/data after harmful events. B correct Controlled account creation implements identity lifecycle and access restriction. C correct Secure device configuration can reduce exposure and enforce permitted network behavior. D correct Traffic analysis is a detective control when used to identify suspicious behavior.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 75 · AM0603
records.text: AM0603 Question 75 NSA29 What is the purpose of a security incident report in network and system administration? Distinguish the security objective from the control that prevents, detects or recovers from the stated problem. A Documenting security policy violations B Sharing threat intelligence with other organizations C Investigating network performance issues D Identifying system vulnerabilities Document security incidents, including policy violations NSA29 assigns reports the documentation of affected systems, evidence, impact, actions and recovery results, and explicitly includes policy violations within that scope. A therefore states a legitimate report purpose among the choices, although it is not exhaustive. Threat sharing, performance investigation and weakness identification are separate activities that incident findings may later support. A correct Documenting policy violations is a valid part of incident reporting, although reports also cover impact and response. B incorrect External threat-intelligence sharing is a separate activity, not the documentation purpose established for this report. C incorrect Performance investigation is broader troubleshooting and does not specifically define a security incident report. D incorrect Finding vulnerabilities is assessment; incident reporting documents observed events, evidence and response.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 76 · AM0604
records.text: AM0604 Question 76 NSA08 Which actions can be valid troubleshooting steps when supported by a tested fault hypothesis and an appropriate recovery plan? Select all that apply. Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Rebooting the system B Performing a software update C Resetting network configurations D Conducting a network scan Rebooting the system; Performing a software update; Resetting network configurations; Conducting a network scan Rebooting, updating software, resetting configuration and scanning can each help with an appropriate diagnosed problem. Their value depends on the hypothesis and operational context: an update may address a known bug, a reset may correct damaged settings, and a scan may gather service evidence. None should be performed blindly. The question asks which actions can belong to troubleshooting, not which one should always be tried first. A correct Rebooting can be a justified troubleshooting action, although it can hide evidence and is not itself diagnosis. B correct An update can address a diagnosed software defect affecting network behavior. C correct Resetting incorrect network settings can resolve a configuration fault after preserving needed evidence. D correct A targeted network scan can gather reachability/service evidence for diagnosis.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 77 · AM0605
records.text: AM0605 Question 77 NSA35 NSA22 Which purposes can analysis of existing system and network logs serve? Select all that apply. Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Identifying potential security breaches B Monitoring network performance C Configuring firewall rules D Encrypting network communications Identifying potential security breaches; Monitoring network performance Logs can reveal suspicious activity that suggests a security breach and can also expose timing, error or workload patterns related to performance. These are complementary uses of recorded observations. Changing firewall rules may follow the analysis, but it is a separate configuration action. Encryption protects communications in transit or storage rather than emerging from analysis of past records. Both analytical purposes therefore qualify. A correct Security events in logs can reveal potential breaches and support incident investigation. B correct Log timing/errors can reveal performance faults and complement measured counters. C incorrect Rule configuration may follow findings, but is not the act or direct purpose of log analysis. D incorrect Encryption protects communications; parsing historical records does not itself encrypt traffic.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 78 · AM0606
records.text: AM0606 Question 78 NSA-S04 NSA10 A client has valid IP configuration. Which listed utility can send ICMP echo requests to a gateway as the next reachability diagnostic? Match the requested observation to the tool’s actual output; distinguish configuration, name lookup, reachability and hop discovery. A Ping B VPN C FTP D DNS Ping Ping sends ICMP echo requests and checks the returned replies. Testing the gateway can help isolate whether the client can exchange IP traffic with that next-hop device. A VPN provides extended protected connectivity, FTP transfers files and DNS resolves names; none is the requested echo-probe utility. Missing replies need further investigation because filtering or loss can suppress otherwise reachable devices. A correct Ping generates the requested ICMP echo probes. B incorrect A VPN provides protected connectivity rather than being an echo-test utility. C incorrect FTP transfers files rather than issuing the specified reachability probe. D incorrect DNS resolves names rather than sending ICMP echo requests.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 79 · AM0607
records.text: AM0607 Question 79 NSA22 NSA23 An administrator is monitoring network capacity and utilization, rather than conducting a vulnerability assessment. Which activity directly measures that objective? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Identifying security vulnerabilities B Tracking network bandwidth usage C Configuring user access controls D Performing system backups Tracking network bandwidth usage Capacity monitoring compares observed traffic with the available link rate and follows usage over time. Tracking bandwidth usage therefore measures the specified performance objective. Vulnerability assessment searches for weaknesses, access-control configuration changes permissions, and backups preserve data for recovery. All can be administration activities, but they do not measure the traffic utilization asked for here. A incorrect Vulnerability identification assesses weaknesses rather than measuring capacity utilization. B correct Bandwidth-usage tracking measures traffic utilization against available capacity. C incorrect Configuring access controls changes authorization rather than measuring traffic load. D incorrect Backups preserve recovery copies rather than observing utilization.
