records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 80 · AM0608
records.text: AM0608 Question 80 NSA08 Which troubleshooting approach tests a middle layer, then narrows the working/failing boundary upward or downward? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Divide and conquer B Trial and error C Random testing D Full system restore Divide and conquer Divide-and-conquer starts with a test at a middle layer and uses the result to decide which side of the boundary needs further investigation. It therefore narrows the scope systematically. Trial-and-error is a broader description of making attempts and does not specifically name this layer-boundary method. Random testing lacks the defined decision process, and a full restore is a recovery action rather than the approach described. A correct Divide-and-conquer is explicitly supported and isolates a working/failing boundary by testing a middle layer. B incorrect Trial-and-error does not specifically identify the middle-layer boundary-isolation approach described. C incorrect Random testing lacks the testable hypothesis and controlled isolation recommended by NSA08. D incorrect A full restore is a potentially disruptive recovery action, not the routine diagnostic approach identified in NSA08.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 81 · AM0609
records.text: AM0609 Question 81 NSA02 NSA01 A static network diagram records devices, links and their arrangement for later troubleshooting. What direct purpose does creating this diagram serve? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Documenting network configurations B Identifying security vulnerabilities C Monitoring network performance D Configuring network devices Documenting network configurations A network diagram documents the arrangement of devices and links and may record configuration relationships. That record helps a troubleshooter reason about expected connectivity. An analyst might subsequently infer weaknesses from it, but creating a static diagram does not itself establish vulnerabilities, sample live performance or apply device settings. The question asks for the direct documentation purpose. A correct Documenting the network arrangement and configuration is the direct purpose. B incorrect A diagram can inform security analysis, but creating it does not itself establish vulnerabilities. C incorrect A static diagram does not measure live performance counters or traffic. D incorrect Drawing the topology does not apply settings to devices.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 82 · AM0610
records.text: AM0610 Question 82 NSA23 NSA28 NSA30 Which measures can provide a network security control under their ordinary stated purposes? Select all that apply. Distinguish the security objective from the control that prevents, detects or recovers from the stated problem. A Intrusion Detection System (IDS) B User authentication C Data encryption D Network traffic analysis Intrusion Detection System (IDS); User authentication; Data encryption; Network traffic analysis An IDS detects suspicious activity and alerts, while traffic analysis can provide additional detective evidence. User authentication establishes identity for subsequent access decisions. Correctly implemented encryption protects data against unauthorized disclosure. These mechanisms address different security needs, so all are examples of controls under the broad question. Their inclusion does not imply that any single mechanism provides complete security by itself. A correct An IDS supplies detective monitoring and alerts about suspicious activity. B correct Authentication establishes an identity before access decisions and supports controlled admission. C correct Appropriate encryption protects transmitted content against unauthorized disclosure. D correct Traffic analysis can detect suspicious behavior and is explicitly included among security controls.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 83 · AM0611
records.text: AM0611 Question 83 NSA30 What is the direct network-structural purpose of segmentation with enforced intersegment policies? Select the most specific description. Identify whether the task requires input/output, control flow, code organization, process execution or collection of a specific measurement. A Controlling user access to resources B Encrypting network communications C Isolating network segments for security purposes D Monitoring network traffic Isolating network segments for security purposes Segmentation separates groups of systems and enforces permitted flows between them. This structural isolation can support access restrictions, but controlling user access is a broader result also achieved through other mechanisms. The most specific description is therefore isolating network segments for security. Encryption and monitoring are distinct controls and do not automatically follow from dividing the network into segments. A incorrect Access control may be an outcome, but this broad description does not name segmentation’s direct structural purpose. B incorrect Segmentation restricts connectivity but does not inherently encrypt the communications it permits. C correct Segmentation isolates system groups into network segments and enforces intersegment flows. D incorrect Traffic monitoring observes activity; it is distinct from establishing and enforcing segment boundaries.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 84 · AM0612
records.text: AM0612 Question 84 NSA30 NSA22 What is the role of a Network Access Control (NAC) system in network security? Distinguish the security objective from the control that prevents, detects or recovers from the stated problem. A Managing user account credentials B Monitoring network bandwidth C Detecting and blocking unauthorized devices D Auditing network activity Assess admission and reject unauthorized devices NSA30 defines Network Access Control as assessing device/user admission and rejecting or quarantining unauthorized or noncompliant devices. C matches that admission function. Credential management, bandwidth monitoring and general activity auditing can support network operations, but they do not state the specific NAC enforcement role. A incorrect Managing account credentials is identity administration, not the complete device-admission role defined for NAC. B incorrect Bandwidth monitoring measures network use rather than deciding whether a device may join. C correct NAC can detect unauthorized/noncompliant devices during admission and reject or quarantine them. D incorrect Auditing records activity; NAC’s distinguishing role is admission assessment and enforcement.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 85 · AM0613
records.text: AM0613 Question 85 NSA09 NSA08 In the note’s bottom-up connectivity procedure, which listed action belongs to the initial physical-link check? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Checking physical cable connections B Updating antivirus software C Configuring firewall rules D Performing system backups Checking physical cable connections A bottom-up procedure begins with power, cable or connector condition and link state before examining interfaces, addressing, routes or application policy. Checking physical cable connections directly fits that initial stage. Firewall configuration may become relevant later when evidence identifies filtering. Antivirus updates and backups serve maintenance or recovery purposes rather than the first physical-link inspection specified in this question. A correct Cable/connector and link-state checks directly diagnose physical connectivity problems. B incorrect Updating antivirus is maintenance rather than a direct connectivity-isolation technique supported by this stem. C incorrect Firewall rules may require later inspection, but are not the initial physical-link check. D incorrect Backups support recovery but do not directly test or correct the network-connectivity path.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 86 · AM0614
records.text: AM0614 Question 86 NSA31 NSA-S01 Which of the following scripting languages is commonly used for system administration tasks? Identify whether the task requires input/output, control flow, code organization, process execution or collection of a specific measurement. A Java B C++ C Python D HTML Python NSA31 explicitly names Python among common system-administration scripting choices, along with shells and PowerShell. HTML is markup. Java and C++ are programming languages but are not the common scripting choice identified among these options. The answer concerns ordinary administration automation, not whether those languages could ever perform administrative work. A incorrect Java can implement programs, but it is not the common administration scripting choice identified in NSA31. B incorrect C++ is a compiled programming language rather than the listed common administration scripting choice. C correct Python is explicitly identified as a common language for administrative scripts. D incorrect HTML is markup and does not provide the administrative scripting control flow requested.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 87 · AM0615
records.text: AM0615 Question 87 NSA31 What is the primary advantage of using scripts for system administration tasks? Identify whether the task requires input/output, control flow, code organization, process execution or collection of a specific measurement. A Faster execution compared to compiled programs B Ability to automate repetitive tasks C Greater control over system resources D Enhanced security and encryption features Automate repetitive work NSA31 identifies repeatable automation as the reason to use administration scripts. Their value is consistent execution of recurring tasks, not guaranteed speed relative to compiled code, stronger encryption or inherently greater resource control. Those properties depend on implementation and environment rather than following from the use of a script. A incorrect Scripts are not inherently faster than compiled programs; the note explicitly rejects that universal claim. B correct Automation of repetitive administrative work is the primary script benefit given in NSA31. C incorrect Greater resource control is not an inherent consequence of scripting rather than another implementation method. D incorrect Scripts are not automatically secure and do not inherently add encryption features.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 88 · AM0616
records.text: AM0616 Question 88 NSA32 In Python, which listed module provides an API for launching child programs and collecting their results? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A echo B ifconfig C grep D subprocess subprocess Python’s subprocess module launches child programs and provides interfaces for collecting output, checking status and limiting runtime. It is a language module rather than a universal shell command. Echo prints values, ifconfig handles interface configuration, and grep searches text. Naming the language and asking for the module makes the intended process-execution abstraction precise without confusing it with one particular program a script might launch. A incorrect Echo prints values and is not a general child-process execution abstraction. B incorrect Ifconfig reports/configures network interfaces rather than generally launching arbitrary programs. C incorrect Grep searches text and is not the general program-execution mechanism requested. D correct The Python subprocess module launches child programs and returns their results.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 89 · AM0617
records.text: AM0617 Question 89 NSA-S05 NSA31 Which scripting feature is useful for handling errors and exceptions in system administration scripts? Identify whether the task requires input/output, control flow, code organization, process execution or collection of a specific measurement. A Looping constructs B Conditional statements C Exception handling D Function definitions Exception handling The NSA34 example uses try with specific exception handlers to report expected read failures while exposing unexpected programming errors. Exception handling is therefore the language feature directly intended for handling errors and exceptions. Loops repeat work, conditions choose branches and functions package reusable operations; none alone supplies exception interception. A incorrect Loops repeat operations and do not themselves intercept raised exceptions. B incorrect Conditionals choose branches from ordinary conditions but do not replace exception handlers. C correct Exception handling catches specified failures and controls reporting or recovery when exceptions occur. D incorrect Functions organize reusable work; they still require appropriate error/exception handling inside or around calls.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 90 · AM0618
records.text: AM0618 Question 90 NSA33 NSA31 Which concept directly reads configuration bytes from a file or writes updated content back to it, rather than interpreting or holding values? Identify whether the task requires input/output, control flow, code organization, process execution or collection of a specific measurement. A File input/output B Regular expressions C String manipulation D Variable assignment File input/output File input/output obtains configuration content from storage and persists revised content. Regular expressions and string operations can interpret or construct that content after it has been read, while variables hold values during processing. All can assist a configuration script, but only file I/O directly crosses the file-storage boundary asked about. Structured formats should still be parsed with their appropriate parsers. A correct File I/O obtains and persists the configuration content being manipulated. B incorrect Regex interprets patterns in content rather than directly reading or writing file storage. C incorrect String manipulation processes text rather than directly transferring it to or from a file. D incorrect Variable assignment holds values in program state rather than performing file I/O.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 91 · AM0619
records.text: AM0619 Question 91 NSA35 Which scripting technique recognizes textual patterns and extracts matching fields or events from individual system-log lines? Identify whether the task requires input/output, control flow, code organization, process execution or collection of a specific measurement. A Database integration B File compression C Log rotation D Regular expression matching Regular expression matching Regular expressions describe text patterns and can capture fields from matching log lines. A script can then count events, correlate entries or report anomalies. Database integration supplies storage or query infrastructure, compression reduces data size, and rotation manages log segments and retention. Those may support an overall monitoring system, but they do not themselves perform the specific textual matching operation requested. A incorrect Database integration stores or queries information rather than specifying the requested text pattern. B incorrect Compression reduces data size rather than extracting matching fields. C incorrect Rotation manages file size and historical segments, not textual matching. D correct Regular expressions match patterns and capture requested fields or events.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 92 · AM0620
records.text: AM0620 Question 92 NSA34 NSA-S05 Which scripting language feature allows passing command-line arguments to a script? Match the requested observation to the tool’s actual output; distinguish configuration, name lookup, reachability and hop discovery. A Functions B Modules C Classes D Command-line parsing Command-line parsing NSA34 identifies command-line parsing as the mechanism for interpreting invocation arguments as named, typed inputs and options. The example uses argparse. Functions, modules and classes can organize a parser’s implementation, but they do not by themselves define argument interpretation or validation; D states the requested feature directly. A incorrect Functions organize callable work but do not inherently parse invocation arguments. B incorrect Modules organize code; a parser module still needs command-line parsing behavior to interpret inputs. C incorrect Classes organize state/behavior and do not themselves define command-line argument processing. D correct Command-line parsing interprets the arguments and options supplied when invoking a script.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 93 · AM0621
records.text: AM0621 Question 93 NSA37 Which scripting technique is commonly used for automating system backup and restore tasks? Identify whether the task requires input/output, control flow, code organization, process execution or collection of a specific measurement. A File compression B Version control C Scheduling D Event logging Scheduling Automating recurring backup/restore work requires choosing when the operation runs. NSA37 assigns this to schedulers such as cron/systemd timers or Windows Task Scheduler. Compression packages data, version control tracks script changes and logging records outcomes. Those can support a backup process but do not themselves trigger the scheduled task. A incorrect Compression packages data but does not determine when a backup or restore operation executes. B incorrect Version control tracks changes in scripts and does not replace scheduling or data backups. C correct Scheduling triggers recurring work at configured times through the platform’s scheduler. D incorrect Event logging records execution/results rather than initiating the recurring operation.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 94 · AM0622
records.text: AM0622 Question 94 NSA28 A script must recover a stored service credential to authenticate later. With the decryption key protected separately, which listed mechanism cryptographically protects that recoverable credential at rest? Identify whether the task requires input/output, control flow, code organization, process execution or collection of a specific measurement. A Environment variables B Encryption algorithms C Hashing functions D Configuration files Encryption algorithms The script needs the actual credential for later authentication, so a one-way password hash cannot meet the recoverability requirement. Encryption can protect the stored credential while allowing authorized decryption, provided the key is separately protected. Environment variables and configuration files describe storage or delivery choices and are not automatically encrypted. The explicit use case therefore identifies encryption without treating it as sufficient when its key is exposed. A incorrect Environment variables deliver or hold values but do not by themselves encrypt stored credentials. B correct Encryption protects a recoverable credential when its key is separately protected. C incorrect A one-way hash supports verification but cannot recover the service credential. D incorrect A configuration file is a storage choice and is not automatically cryptographically protected.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 95 · AM0623
records.text: AM0623 Question 95 NSA36 NSA-S05 Which techniques can collect CPU or memory measurements when the relevant logs or OS interfaces expose those metrics? Select all that apply. Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Log parsing B System calls C Signal handling D Performance counters Log parsing; System calls; Performance counters Resource measurements can be recorded in logs, exposed through operating-system APIs or published as performance counters. Scripts may use any of those interfaces when the requested metrics are available. Signal handling instead reacts to process notifications and is not itself a CPU or memory measurement interface. The multiple-selection instruction preserves the complementary collection techniques without claiming one universal platform-independent API. A correct Parsing logs can collect recorded resource metrics when suitable measurements are present. B correct OS system calls/APIs can expose resource measurements used by monitoring scripts. C incorrect Signal handling manages process notifications; it is not the measurement interface for CPU/memory utilization. D correct Performance counters directly expose measured resource events and utilization-related values.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 96 · CS0188
records.text: CS0188 Question 96 NSA-S04 NSA07 Suppose you are a network administrator and want to determine the path between two connections, which often goes through multiple routers. Which command would you use? Match the requested observation to the tool’s actual output; distinguish configuration, name lookup, reachability and hop discovery. A ping B nslookup C traceroute D All of the above traceroute Traceroute discovers responding hops toward a destination by causing packet-lifetime expiry at successive distances. It is therefore the appropriate command for investigating a multi-router path. Ping checks an end-to-end echo exchange and nslookup inspects DNS resolution, which do not supply the requested hop sequence. Some intermediate devices may not reply, so the displayed trace is evidence from responding hops rather than a guarantee that every router is visible. A incorrect Ping checks end-to-end reachability, not the requested hop sequence. B incorrect Nslookup queries DNS information, not intermediate router hops. C correct Traceroute discovers responding intermediate hops along the path. D incorrect The other commands do not all perform route-hop discovery.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 97 · CS0189
records.text: CS0189 Question 97 NSA03 Which statements correctly describe IPv4 loopback? In D, 127.0.0.1 means the conventional example rather than the entire reserved range. Select all that apply. Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A It helps to refer to the host itself B It allows programs to access network protocols for local services C It is an external pseudo address D It is denoted by the IP address: 127.0.0.1 It helps to refer to the host itself; It allows programs to access network protocols for local services; It is denoted by the IP address: 127.0.0.1 Loopback lets a host address its own protocol stack and reach local services without an external link. The conventional IPv4 address is 127.0.0.1, within the broader reserved 127/8 block. It is therefore local self-reference rather than an external address. The example wording permits all three true descriptions without incorrectly restricting the entire loopback range to a single address. A correct Loopback refers to the host itself rather than a remote device. B correct Programs can reach local services through network protocols using loopback. C incorrect Loopback is local and does not require an external network link. D correct 127.0.0.1 is the conventional IPv4 loopback address, although the reserved block is broader.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 98 · NS0296
records.text: NS0296 Question 98 NSA12 Which listed item is a traffic-prioritization mechanism that can operate across layers, rather than an application mediator or service installation/configuration activity? Identify the required operational function, then compare its scope, inputs and constraints with the cited note definitions. A Proxies and agents B Installing a new service C E-mail configuration D Quality of service Quality of service Quality of service classifies, queues and prioritizes traffic to meet performance objectives such as low delay or limited loss. It can span layers while supporting applications. Proxies and agents are mediating components, and installing a service or configuring email are administrative activities. The revised question uses those explicit functional categories, so it does not require an unsupported taxonomy that labels every item an application-layer service. A incorrect Proxies and agents mediate requests rather than naming the traffic-prioritization mechanism. B incorrect Installing a service is an administrative activity. C incorrect Email configuration is an administrative activity. D correct QoS classifies and prioritizes traffic and can operate across layers.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 99 · NS0313
records.text: NS0313 Question 99 NSA25 A data-center volume has exactly two equal disks and must retain service after either disk fails. One disk’s usable capacity is sufficient. Which listed RAID level meets these requirements? Compare striping granularity, redundancy placement, usable capacity and required disk-failure tolerance. A RAID level 3 B RAID level1 C RAID level 2 D RAID level 0 RAID level1 With exactly two equal disks, RAID1 mirrors the data and leaves one disk’s usable capacity while tolerating either disk failing. RAID0 provides no disk-failure tolerance. RAID2 and RAID3 rely on different striping and redundancy layouts rather than the two-disk mirrored arrangement that meets these requirements. The choice follows the stated disk count, capacity and failure goal rather than the institution’s size or industry. A incorrect RAID3 uses byte striping with dedicated parity, not the required two-disk fault-tolerant layout. B correct A two-disk RAID1 mirror provides one disk’s capacity and survives either disk failing. C incorrect RAID2 uses bit striping and Hamming redundancy rather than the required two-disk solution. D incorrect RAID0 cannot tolerate a disk failure.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 100 · NS0324
records.text: NS0324 Question 100 NSA25 A storage administrator configures four equal 2 TB disks. Each stripe stores data blocks on three disks and a parity block on the fourth; the disk holding parity changes between stripes. Ignoring metadata, which listed RAID layout provides 6 TB of usable capacity and tolerates one disk failure? Compare striping granularity, redundancy placement, usable capacity and required disk-failure tolerance. A RAID 2 B RAID 1 C RAID 5 D RAID 0 RAID 5 The changing parity disk means parity is distributed across the array while data are striped in blocks, identifying RAID5. Its usable capacity is (N−1)D, so four 2 TB disks provide 6 TB and retain one disk’s worth of redundancy. RAID2 uses bit striping with Hamming-code redundancy, RAID1 mirrors data, and RAID0 provides no disk-failure tolerance. A incorrect RAID2 uses bit striping with Hamming-code redundancy, not the described block stripes with rotating parity. B incorrect RAID1 mirrors data; it does not place one rotating parity block in each stripe. C correct RAID5 distributes parity across block stripes and gives (4−1)×2 = 6 TB usable capacity. D incorrect RAID0 would provide 8 TB without parity, so it fails the one-disk-failure requirement.

records.title: Network and System Administration — Question 101 · NS0350
records.text: NS0350 Question 101 NSA26 Which one of the following is WRONGLY stated about an importance of security policy? Distinguish the security objective from the control that prevents, detects or recovers from the stated problem. A To help minimize risk. B To ensure the confidentiality, integrity and availability of data. C To coordinate and enforce a security program across an organization. D To use the system in a passive way Passive system use is not a security-policy purpose NSA26 assigns policies risk reduction, coordinated required behavior and CIA goals. D’s passive-use statement does not describe those governance/protection purposes and is explicitly rejected here. B expresses the desired CIA objective, not a guarantee that policy alone prevents every incident. The remaining statements fit legitimate policy aims. A incorrect Reducing risk is a stated security-policy aim, so this is not wrongly stated. B incorrect CIA protection is a legitimate policy objective, with actual success depending on implemented controls. C incorrect Coordinating required behavior and enforcement across the organization is a legitimate policy purpose. D correct Passive use is not the defined purpose of security policy and does not express its governance/protection objectives.

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Study notes
records.text: Automata and Complexity Theory Connect a language to a grammar and recognizer, prove limits of weaker models, and distinguish computability from resource complexity. State alphabets, epsilon conventions, decision formulations and reduction directions explicitly when solving automata and complexity problems. Design a DFA/grammar/PDA and justify its invariant, soundness and completeness, not merely examples. For pumping, choose a witness after the pumping length and defeat every allowed split. For reductions, write the map, the time/computability bound and both yes/no implications; known-hard source reduces to new target. Treat language hierarchy, decidability and complexity as separate questions. Recalculate symbols and evaluate each choice using language and machine definitions.

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Symbols, alphabets, words and length
records.text: An alphabet Σ is a finite set of symbols. A word/string is a finite ordered sequence of symbols from Σ; a language is a set of words, L⊆Σ*. An empty word ε, also written λ, has length zero. The empty language ∅ contains no words; {ε} contains one. Neither ε nor ∅ is the numeric symbol 0. Length counts occurrences, not distinct symbols: |caddba|=6, so |caddba|²=36. By contrast |(caddba)²|=12 because the word is concatenated twice. Distinguish |Z|², the square of a word’s length, from |Z²|, the length of its repeated concatenation; keep the exponent in its stated position. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Concatenation, powers and reversal
records.text: Concatenation xy writes x followed by y: cddc·ababb=cddcababb; order generally matters. εx=xε=x. Define x⁰=ε and xⁿ as n copies for n≥1. Reverse xᴿ reads symbols backward: caddba reverses to abddac; (xy)ᴿ=yᴿxᴿ and (xᴿ)ᴿ=x. For languages, LM={xy:x∈L,y∈M}, L⁰={ε}, and Lⁿ⁺¹=LⁿL. Thus {e,fgh}{c,d}={ec,ed,fghc,fghd}; fghe is absent. A language power is a set, so L⁰=ε is a type error unless braces are understood. Symbols are case-sensitive; uppercase symbols do not equal lowercase symbols unless a conversion is explicitly specified. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Language operations and empty-word edge cases
records.text: Σⁿ contains words of exactly n symbols; for |Σ|=k, |Σⁿ|=kⁿ, including Σ⁰={ε}. Σ*=⋃n≥0Σⁿ and Σ⁺=⋃n≥1Σⁿ. Over a nonempty alphabet, Σ⁺ excludes ε and Σ*=Σ⁺∪{ε}. Σ² over {a,b} is {aa,ab,ba,bb}. For an arbitrary language L, L*=⋃n≥0Lⁿ and L⁺=LL*. Unlike alphabet positive closure, L⁺ can contain ε when ε∈L. ∅*={ε}, ∅⁺=∅, and {ε}*={ε}. Union means membership in either set; intersection requires the same word in both, not concatenation. Complement is Σ*−L and needs a fixed alphabet. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Grammars generate; automata recognize
records.text: Write G=(V,Σ,P,S): finite variables V, terminals Σ disjoint from V, productions P and start variable S∈V. A production replaces its left side by its right side. The language is L(G)={w∈Σ*:S⇒*w}. A recognizer processes a word and accepts exactly the language members. Grammars generate languages; automata recognize languages, not grammars. Two grammars are equivalent when their generated languages are equal, regardless of rule counts or variable names. One common word, equal alphabets or one-way inclusion is insufficient. A regular expression denotes a language but is not itself the set of matched words. Natural languages such as English are not the intended formal-language examples; give a precisely specified set instead. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Chomsky hierarchy and the epsilon convention
records.text: Type 3 regular grammars correspond to finite automata; type 2 CFGs to nondeterministic PDAs; type 1 context-sensitive/noncontracting grammars to nondeterministic LBAs; type 0 unrestricted grammars to Turing recognizers. In an unrestricted production α→β, α contains at least one variable; unrestricted does not mean any meaningless rewrite is allowed. Use REG ⊊ CFL ⊊ CSL ⊊ DECIDABLE ⊊ RE, under the usual convention allowing S→ε with S absent from right sides when needed. Strict noncontracting grammars otherwise cannot generate ε. Stronger families can describe lower-family languages: asking which grammar is capable is often nonunique. Ask for the least sufficient family or the exact family equivalent to a machine model. This is an expressiveness hierarchy, not a runtime ranking. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — DFA definition and acceptance
records.text: A deterministic finite automaton (DFA) is M=(Q,Σ,δ,q₀,F), with finite nonempty Q, start q₀∈Q, accepting set F⊆Q and total δ:Q×Σ→Q. Exactly one next state is specified per state/symbol pair; this does not mean the whole machine has one transition. F may be empty, recognizing ∅. State names q₀,q₁,… do not determine accepting status. Start at q₀ and consume the entire input. Accept iff the ending state is in F; visiting an accepting state earlier is insufficient. ε is accepted exactly when q₀∈F. A nonaccepting sink loops on every symbol and cannot reach acceptance; it still finishes after finite input. Finite automata have finite memory encoded by states, not no state or no ability to remember any history. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Design and trace a finite-state recognizer
records.text: Choose states with invariant meanings: the information about the consumed prefix needed to decide future acceptance. For binary words ending 01 use q₀=no useful suffix, q₁=last suffix 0, q₂=last suffix 01; only q₂ accepts. Transitions on (0,1) are q₀→(q₁,q₀), q₁→(q₁,q₂), q₂→(q₁,q₀). Input 10101 follows q₀,q₀,q₁,q₂,q₁,q₂ and accepts. For length at least two use meanings 0 symbols, 1 symbol, at least 2 symbols. Every input advances toward the third state, which loops and accepts. Calling it q₂ is a naming choice: without a diagram or state definitions no numbered-state answer follows. To verify a design, test ε, shortest accepted/rejected words and overlaps; sample agreement alone is not a proof. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Minimum states: prefix, suffix and valid alphabets
records.text: For a fixed valid word w of length n, a DFA for strings ending in w needs n+1 states representing the longest consumed suffix that is a prefix of w. Overlapping prefixes determine fallback transitions. Distinct prefixes are distinguishable by suitable continuations, proving the lower bound; do not add an unnecessary rejecting sink. For strings starting with w, a complete DFA ordinarily has n matched-prefix stages, an accepting continuation state and a rejecting sink: n+2 when n≥1 and the alphabet allows mismatches. Over a unary alphabet the sink may be unreachable. If w contains a symbol outside Σ, the language is empty, whose minimal complete DFA has one rejecting state. Thus starting abc over {a,b} needs one state, not five; five requires an alphabet containing a,b,c. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — NFA and epsilon transitions
records.text: A nondeterministic finite automaton (NFA) permits zero, one or many successors: δ:Q×Σ→𝒫(Q). An ε-NFA additionally permits moves without consuming input, using domain Q×(Σ∪{ε}). Some books include ε moves in the term NFA; state the convention. An NFA accepts iff at least one finite path consumes the complete word and finishes in F, including permitted ε moves before/after symbols. Other paths may get stuck. An NFA is not more expressive than a DFA: both recognize exactly REG. Nondeterminism can make a description smaller. A DFA is a special NFA after interpreting its unique successor as a singleton set. ε is a zero-input move, not an ordinary input character or permission to accept with unread input. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Subset construction with epsilon closure
records.text: ε-closure(T) contains T and every state reachable through ε moves. Start the DFA at ε-closure({q₀}); for each current subset T and symbol a compute ε-closure(⋃q∈Tδ(q,a)). A subset accepts iff it intersects F. Explore only reachable subsets; the empty subset is the rejecting sink when reached. An n-state NFA yields at most 2ⁿ DFA states, not necessarily exactly 2ⁿ. Example over Σ={a}: states p,r, start p, final r; δ(p,a)={p,r}, δ(r,a)=∅. The subset machine starts {p}, reaches {p,r} on a, and stays there on further a's. It accepts a⁺. With an ε edge p→r, the starting subset would already contain r and ε would also be accepted. Automata and Complexity Theory module Sipser MIT Lecture 2: nondeterminism and closure

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Equivalence, minimization and diagram checks
records.text: First discard unreachable DFA states. Partition remaining states into accepting/nonaccepting blocks; repeatedly split a block when two states transition on some symbol into different blocks. Stable blocks are equivalence classes and can be merged. Equivalent states have identical acceptance for every continuation; current acceptance alone is insufficient. For DFA equivalence build pairs of states and search from the start pair. Any reachable pair with exactly one accepting component supplies a distinguishing word; if none exists, the languages agree. A partial diagram must first be completed consistently with a sink. To reject a proposed RE quickly, compare ε and the shortest cycles: an accepting start plus an ab return cycle forces ε and ab into the language. Every equivalent expression must contain both. Automata and Complexity Theory module Cornell CS412/413: DFA minimization

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Regular-expression notation and precedence
records.text: Classical expressions use ∅, ε, symbols, union, concatenation and star. A union B is written A|B or A+B; postfix r⁺ means one-or-more r repetitions and is a different use of +. Parenthesize when conventions might clash. Star binds tightest, concatenation next, union last. r? means r|ε; r⁺=rr*. (a|b)*a denotes words ending a; 0*10* denotes exactly one 1; a*(b|c) gives zero-or-more a's then exactly one b or c, so aab belongs but aaa and aaabc do not. (0|ε)(0|1)* is simply all binary words because ε permits any suffix. Programming regex features such as backreferences may exceed classical regular-language power; wildcard dot is an extra notation, not a basic alphabet-independent theorem. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Build expressions and convert representations
records.text: To require at least one a anywhere over {a,b}, use (a|b)*a(a|b)*. b*ab* requires exactly one a. At least two zeros uses (0|1)*0(0|1)*0(0|1)*; the zeros need not be adjacent. Testing 010 distinguishes it from a requirement for substring 00. For S→aS|ε, any number of a's is generated, giving a*. RE→automaton uses ε-NFA fragments: parallel alternatives for union, connect accepting ends to the next fragment for concatenation, and add bypass/repetition ε moves for star. Then apply subset construction. For automaton→RE, eliminate a state k while updating edge i→j as rᵢⱼ | rᵢₖ(rₖₖ)*rₖⱼ; include new start/final nodes where required. These operations preserve the whole language, not just tested examples. Automata and Complexity Theory module Sipser MIT Lecture 3: FA/RE and pumping

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Regular grammars and closure constructions
records.text: Right-linear rules have form A→aB, A→a or permitted ε rules; left-linear rules put the single variable at the opposite end, A→Ba. Both consistent orientations generate REG; arbitrarily mixing them can generate nonregular languages, for example S→aA|ε, A→Sb generates aⁿbⁿ. A CFG rule A→aBA is legal but not regular-grammar form. For right-linear grammar→NFA, variables become states, A→aB becomes an a edge, A→a leads to a fresh final state, and A→ε makes A accepting. Regular languages are closed under union, concatenation, star, reversal, intersection, difference and complement. Reverse edges and exchange start/final roles using an ε-NFA to obtain reversal. Complement requires a complete DFA; then swap accepting/nonaccepting states. Product-state constructions implement intersection/difference. Automata and Complexity Theory module Sipser MIT Lecture 2: closure constructions

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Regular pumping lemma: use the quantifiers
records.text: If L is regular, some p≥1 satisfies: every s∈L with |s|≥p has a split s=xyz, |xy|≤p, |y|≥1, and xyⁱz∈L for every i≥0. To disprove regularity, assume an arbitrary pumping length p, choose s, then show every allowed split can be broken by some i. Finding one bad split proves nothing; satisfying this necessary condition alone does not prove regularity. For L={aⁿbⁿ:n≥0}, choose aᵖbᵖ. Every allowed y=aᵏ with k≥1; pumping i=0 leaves fewer a's than b's. The contradiction excludes every DFA. For an n-state DFA, an accepted word of length at least n repeats a state along its path, giving an accepted cycle that can be repeated indefinitely. Thus a fixed DFA's language is infinite iff it has an accepted word of length at least its state count. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — CFG derivations, sentences and parse trees
records.text: In a context-free grammar (CFG) each production has one variable on the left, A→α with α∈(V∪Σ)*. The left side therefore also belongs to V∪Σ and its string closure; alternatives stating these weaker memberships can all be true. A sentential form is any string derived from S, including terminal-only sentences and S itself. A leftmost derivation always replaces the leftmost variable; a rightmost one replaces the rightmost variable. This is not scanning the completed input in opposite directions. A complete parse tree has root S, internal variable nodes expanded by productions and terminal leaves, with ε leaves when that convention is used. Read the leaves left-to-right for the yielded word. The whole tree represents derivation structure; a path in a derivation graph is a different object. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Design and validate context-free grammars
records.text: Use a recursive rule to enforce matched structure and a base rule to stop. S→aSb|ε generates exactly aⁿbⁿ for n≥0: n recursive steps add n a's on the left and n b's on the right. Derive aabb by S⇒aSb⇒aaSbb⇒aabb. For n≥1 replace ε by base ab. For aⁿbᵐ with n>m≥0, use S→aSb|A and A→aA|a: each S recursion adds a matched pair, then A adds at least one extra a. For balanced parentheses use S→(S)S|ε. Validate soundness—each rule preserves the intended property—and completeness—decompose any desired nonempty word into pieces matching a production. Merely producing several examples does not establish exact language equality. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Ambiguity and precedence
records.text: A CFG is ambiguous when some word has two distinct parse trees, equivalently two different leftmost derivations. Different expansion orders that give the same tree do not prove ambiguity. E→E+E|E*E|id allows id+id*id to group as (id+id)*id or id+(id*id). Separate precedence levels: E→E+T|T, T→T*F|F, F→id|(E). Multiplication binds inside T before addition at E, and left recursion encodes left association. Uniqueness follows by the top-level last operator split and induction. S→SS|ε is already ambiguous for ε. S→A|B is ambiguous if A→ab and B→abB|ε both produce ab. Ambiguous grammar and inherently ambiguous language differ: another grammar may remove ambiguity. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Simplification, CNF and membership
records.text: A null production is A→ε; a unit production is A→B with one variable. Mark nullable variables and add alternatives omitting nullable occurrences, preserving ε through a fresh start when needed. Remove unit rules by copying nonunit productions reachable through unit chains. Remove nongenerating variables, then unreachable symbols. Do not delete a nullable variable's every use and lose valid nonempty words. Chomsky normal form uses A→BC or A→a, with an optional isolated S₀→ε. Replace terminals in long right sides by variables and split long variable sequences into binary steps: A→aBC becomes A→XC₁, X→a, C₁→BC. For CNF membership, CYK fills variables generating each substring, combining splits with A→BC. For a fixed grammar its time is O(n³); n>0 derivations contain n terminal rules and n−1 binary rules. Automata and Complexity Theory module Virginia Tech OpenDSA: transforming grammars

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Greibach form and left recursion
records.text: Greibach normal form requires A→aA₁…Aₖ, k≥0: one leading terminal followed only by variables. Handle ε separately through a fresh start that never appears on a right side. A nonempty word of length n takes exactly n leftmost rule applications because each contributes one terminal to the prefix. A constructive route removes ε/unit/useless rules, orders variables, substitutes rules beginning with earlier variables, removes left recursion, and substitutes until every rule begins with a terminal. Some algorithms first convert to CNF; this is a method choice, not a universally mandatory first step. Direct A→Aα|β can become A→βR, R→αR|ε, then further normalization handles ε. GNF cannot retain direct or indirect left recursion. A question demanding the first step must name its chosen algorithm. Automata and Complexity Theory module Duke CPS140: CNF and Greibach conversion

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — PDA configuration and acceptance
records.text: A nondeterministic pushdown automaton (PDA) adds a stack to finite control: (Q,Σ,Γ,δ,q₀,Z₀,F). Its transition relation maps (state,input symbol or ε,stack top) to possible (new state,replacement stack string) pairs. Fix which end denotes the top before tracing. Replacing X by X leaves the stack unchanged; ε input means consume no symbol, while replacing X by ε pops it. These are different uses of ε. A configuration records state, unread input and stack. Final-state acceptance requires all input consumed and a final state; empty-stack acceptance requires all input consumed and an empty stack. For NPDAs the modes characterize the same language family, through a construction, not necessarily the same unmodified machine. Deterministic-PDA acceptance conventions need extra care and are not automatically interchangeable. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Construct PDA recognizers and compare determinism
records.text: For aⁿbⁿ, push one X per a, switch to a b-reading phase, pop one X per b, and accept when input ends at the bottom marker. Reject a after entering the b phase and b when no X remains. Handle ε explicitly if n=0 is permitted. A stack counts without storing the full input as random-access memory. For even palindromes wwᴿ over {a,b}, push the first half, nondeterministically guess its midpoint, then pop matching symbols. No center marker makes that language context-free but not deterministic context-free. With a marker wcwᴿ the switch point is visible and a DPDA suffices. Unary even palindromes are merely even-length words and regular. A PDA cannot compare two arbitrary halves in the same forward order: {ww:w∈{a,b}*} is the copy language, not the palindrome language. Automata and Complexity Theory module Jeannette Wing, CMU: Formal methods for computer systems

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — CFL closure and counterexamples
records.text: CFLs are closed under union, concatenation, star, reversal and intersection with a regular language. For CFL∩REG combine PDA control with DFA control, using the original stack; each consumed symbol updates both states, while an ε move leaves the DFA state unchanged. The result is guaranteed context-free, not necessarily regular: intersect aⁿbⁿ with a*b* to get aⁿbⁿ. CFLs are not closed under arbitrary intersection. Both {aⁿbⁿcᵐ} and {aᵐbⁿcⁿ} are context-free; their intersection aⁿbⁿcⁿ is not. Nor are CFLs closed under complement or arbitrary difference. CFL minus a regular language remains CFL by intersecting with the regular complement. A failed construction of one proposed PDA proves only that construction fails, not that every PDA fails. Automata and Complexity Theory module Old Dominion University CS390: CFL properties

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — CFL pumping proof and copy versus mirror
records.text: If L is context-free, some p ensures each sufficiently long s∈L has s=uvxyz with |vxy|≤p, |vy|≥1 and uvⁱxyⁱz∈L for every i≥0. The two pieces v and y are pumped together; either may be empty, not both. A non-CFL proof must defeat every allowed decomposition. For s=aᵖbᵖcᵖ, the window vxy cannot contain both an a and a c. Pumping affects at most two blocks and at least one count. Use i=0 or 2: the unaffected third block retains p while another count changes, or symbol order breaks. Hence aⁿbⁿcⁿ is not CFL. The copy language ww is also non-CFL over two symbols, whereas wwᴿ has the explicit grammar S→aSa|bSb|ε. An expression that writes ww and calls it a palindrome is contradictory. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Context-sensitive rules and linear bounded automata
records.text: A context-sensitive rule αAβ→αγβ replaces A in context, with γ nonempty. Equivalently, noncontracting grammar presentations preserve/increase total length, with the isolated ε exception. The condition is on the complete sides, not an unrelated comparison |β|≥|α|. A linear bounded automaton (LBA) is a TM with O(n) tape cells on length-n input; the standard CSL characterization uses nondeterministic LBAs. For aⁿbⁿcⁿ first verify a*b*c* order, repeatedly mark one unmarked a, b and c, and reject missing/excess symbols. All marks stay within the input region. A fixed input has finitely many configurations, at most |Q|m|Γ|ᵐ for m cells. Reachability search in that finite graph decides acceptance, even if some machine branches loop. Thus every CSL is decidable. Automata and Complexity Theory module Illinois CS373: unrestricted grammars and LBAs

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Classify languages with justified boundaries
records.text: a*b* and {aⁿb:n≥0} are regular. aⁿbⁿ is CFL but not regular. Over a two-symbol alphabet, wwᴿ is CFL, ww is not CFL; both are decidable. aⁿbⁿcⁿ is CSL but not CFL, and therefore decidable. Every finite language is regular. A stronger grammar or TM can still recognize any of these lower-family languages. Unary prime length {aᵖ:p prime} is nonregular: choose prime q above pumping length p; if pump piece has length k≥1, using exponent q+1 gives length q(k+1), composite. Every unary CFL is regular, so this language is not CFL either. It is nevertheless context-sensitive: count the input in bounded workspace and test divisors. The balanced-three-count, prime-length, palindrome and aⁿb examples above are all recursive languages. Automata and Complexity Theory module UMass, David Barrington: unary context-free languages

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — TM components, transitions and configurations
records.text: For a Turing machine (TM), use M=(Q,Σ,Γ,δ,q₀,qaccept,qreject), with finite state/tape alphabets, Σ⊆Γ and blank □∈Γ−Σ. The blank symbol belongs to the tape alphabet Γ, not the input alphabet Σ. The standard machine has finite control, a read/write head and an unbounded tape. Input is initial tape content, not a separate hardware organ; no separate stack is required. δ(q,a)=(p,b,L) means read a in q, write b, move one cell left and enter p. Accept/reject halting states have no further moves under this convention. In ID u q av the head scans a; the left-move successor, when u=u'c, is u' p cbv. For a right move it is ub p v, showing a blank if the head enters unused tape. State and transition names must follow the diagram's declared convention. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — TM design, variants and computation limits
records.text: To decide aⁿbⁿcⁿ, repeatedly mark matching triples, resetting the head between scans, then verify no unmatched symbol remains. Each round marks additional input cells, so finitely many rounds suffice. To decide ww, reject odd length, locate the midpoint using marks/counters, and compare corresponding symbols of the two halves; writable tape permits access a single stack lacks. State both the acceptance test and why every input halts. An off-line TM has a read-only input tape and separate read/write work tape. Multitape, multihead, two-way-infinite-tape and nondeterministic TMs have the same language-recognition power as standard TMs, though simulation costs differ. Two unbounded stacks can simulate a tape. Turing completeness means ability to simulate general TM computation, not polynomial speed or literally using infinitely many cells in a finite run. The Church–Turing thesis connects effective procedures to this formal model; it is not a proved runtime theorem. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Deciders, recognizers and complements
records.text: A decider halts on every input and accepts exactly its language; these languages are recursive/decidable. A recognizer must halt and accept every member, but on a nonmember may halt-reject or loop. Its languages are recursively enumerable (RE), Turing-recognizable or semidecidable. Looping is nonacceptance, not a rejecting halt. An undecidable language may still have a recognizer. Every decidable language is RE, and the containment is strict. If L and its complement are both RE, simulate their recognizers in dovetailed steps until one accepts, obtaining a decider. Conversely complementing a decider works because it always halts. Flipping final states in an arbitrary recognizer fails to handle nonmembers that loop. Recursive function theory's total computable functions are not merely programs written with recursive self-calls; partial computable functions may be undefined where computation does not halt. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Halting, diagonalization and Rice’s theorem
records.text: HALT={⟨M,w⟩:M halts on w} is recognizable: simulate and accept upon any halt. Suppose a decider H determines halting. Construct D(x) that loops if H(x,x) says halt, otherwise halts. Running D on its own description contradicts H in both cases. Thus HALT is undecidable and witnesses RE beyond DECIDABLE. Its complement is not RE, or both recognizers would yield a decider. Rice's theorem makes every nontrivial semantic property of a TM's recognized language undecidable. Nontrivial means some recognized languages have it and some do not. Empty language, contains ε and at least three accepted words qualify. Number of states and whether a particular symbol is written are machine-behavior/syntactic properties, not automatically language properties; prove such claims separately. Undecidable means no general decider exists, not merely no algorithm is currently known. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Which decision questions are solvable?
records.text: DFA/NFA word membership is decidable by simulation or reachable state sets. FA emptiness is reachable-accepting-state search; DFA equivalence searches the product for an acceptance disagreement. CFG membership is decidable by parsing/CYK and emptiness by marking variables that can generate terminal strings. These procedures halt and are not the same as deciding arbitrary TM membership. TM acceptance on input is RE-complete and undecidable; HALT is undecidable. General CFG ambiguity and CFG equivalence are undecidable even though membership for a given CFG and word is decidable. A concrete grammar's two parse trees can establish that particular grammar is ambiguous; this does not give an algorithm deciding ambiguity for every grammar. FORTRAN/programming-language questions must distinguish CFG-style syntax, semantic restrictions and Turing-complete computation; a language's name alone does not choose one formal classification. Automata and Complexity Theory module Sipser MIT Lecture 7: decision problems

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Computable reductions for undecidability
records.text: A many-one reduction A≤mB is a total computable transformation f satisfying x∈A iff f(x)∈B. If B had a decider, compute f and invoke it to decide A. Therefore known-undecidable A reduced to B proves B undecidable. Showing B≤mA alone does not establish B's hardness. Example HALT≤mA_TM: given ⟨M,w⟩, construct N that ignores its input, simulates M(w), and accepts if M ever halts, including rejecting halts. Then ⟨N,ε⟩ is accepted iff M(w) halts. Construction of N's finite description terminates; the simulation inside N may not. Reductions require both yes and no directions and a computable mapping, not just a resemblance between two problems. Automata and Complexity Theory module Sipser MIT Lecture 9: reducibility

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Measure resources with the right input size
records.text: Time counts computation steps; space counts cells/memory used, specifying whether read-only input is excluded. For a deterministic decider use the maximum over all length-n inputs; for a time-bounded nondeterministic decider every branch meets the bound. Big-O is an asymptotic upper bound, not inherently a worst-case label: it can describe a worst-, average- or best-case function. Θ adds a matching lower bound. Growth typically orders 1,log n,n,n log n,n²,2ⁿ,n!. A fixed polynomial nᵏ differs from exponent 2ⁿ. Encoding matters: the number N in binary has Θ(log N) bits, so O(N) work is not polynomial in its binary input length. Pseudopolynomial algorithms depend on numeric magnitude rather than encoding length. A polynomial of enormous degree need not be practical. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — P, NP and polynomial verification
records.text: Complexity classes here contain decision languages. P consists of deterministic polynomial-time decidable languages; NP consists of nondeterministic polynomial-time decidable languages, equivalently polynomially verifiable yes-instances with polynomial-size certificates. A verifier must accept some certificate exactly for yes-inputs; no certificate may falsely establish a no-instance. NP means nondeterministic polynomial, not non-polynomial. For CLIQUE, the certificate lists k vertices; verify they are distinct and every pair is an edge. This is polynomial in the graph encoding. P⊆NP because a verifier can ignore its certificate and run the P algorithm. P=NP remains open; NP does not mean definitely hard or definitely outside P. Finding versus verifying is an intuition for witnesses, not a rule that all NP instances need exponential search. Automata and Complexity Theory module Sipser MIT Lecture 14: P, NP, certificates Clay Mathematics Institute: P versus NP

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Polynomial reductions: direction and consequences
records.text: A≤pB means f is computable in polynomial time and x∈A iff f(x)∈B. Solving B then solves A, so B is at least as hard under this reduction. If B∈P then A∈P; if A is NP-hard then B is NP-hard. A∈P does not force B∈P, and the reduction alone does not place both problems in the same class. Polynomial reductions compose. To prove a new target X hard, reduce a known hard problem Y to X, not X to Y. The mapping and target instance must have polynomial size. For undecidability, general computable reductions suffice; for NP-completeness, an arbitrarily slow computable transformation is insufficient. Always state which reduction and resource bound are being used. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — NP-hard versus NP-complete; decision versus optimization
records.text: X is NP-hard if every A∈NP satisfies A≤pX. It need not belong to NP and can even be undecidable. X is NP-complete if X∈NP and X is NP-hard. NP-complete languages lie inside NP and can be decided by finite exhaustive certificate search in exponential time. They are not known to require exponential time. SAT asks whether a Boolean formula has a satisfying assignment; Cook–Levin establishes SAT NP-complete. CNF-SAT and 3-SAT are NP-complete versions. TSP decision asks whether a tour of cost at most B exists; it is NP-complete for standard finite encoded inputs. Finding the shortest tour is optimization and NP-hard; call it NP-complete only after specifying a decision formulation. Fixed 2-colorability is in P, while fixed k-colorability for k≥3 is NP-complete. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Work a hardness proof: 3-SAT to CLIQUE
records.text: First CLIQUE belongs to NP by the pairwise-edge certificate check. For a 3-CNF formula with m clauses, make one vertex for each literal occurrence. Connect two vertices iff they come from different clauses and are not complementary literals. Ask whether the graph has a clique of size m. Construction takes polynomial time and space. A satisfying assignment supplies one true literal per clause; they are mutually consistent and form a clique. Conversely an m-clique selects one occurrence per clause, with no variable chosen both positively and negatively, so assign those literals true and extend remaining variables arbitrarily. Both implications prove equivalence. For (x₁∨¬x₂)∧(¬x₁∨x₂∨x₃)∧¬x₃, the assignment (true,true,false) satisfies all clauses because ¬false is true. Automata and Complexity Theory module Sipser MIT Lecture 15: NP-completeness

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — PSPACE, quantifiers and space reuse
records.text: PSPACE is ⋃kSPACE(nᵏ), using deterministic polynomial workspace. NP⊆PSPACE because candidate polynomial witnesses can be enumerated and checked one at a time, reusing memory; exponentially many candidates do not require retaining them all. Savitch's theorem gives NSPACE(s)⊆DSPACE(s²) for appropriate s≥log n, hence NPSPACE=PSPACE. It does not prove P=NP. TQBF asks whether a fully quantified Boolean formula is true and is PSPACE-complete. Evaluate ∃x by trying one branch or the other; evaluate ∀x by requiring both. Depth-first evaluation stores assignments and recursion state using polynomial space despite potentially exponential time. For example ∀x∃y(x↔y) is true, but ∃y∀x(x↔y) is false. PSPACE-complete means membership plus hardness for every PSPACE language under the stated reduction. Automata and Complexity Theory module Sipser MIT Lecture 17: PSPACE and Savitch

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Known hierarchy and open separations
records.text: Use L⊆NL⊆P⊆NP⊆PSPACE⊆EXPTIME⊆EXPSPACE. Here L/NL use logarithmic workspace; EXPTIME is ⋃kTIME(2^(nᵏ)), an upper-bound class that also contains P, not a statement that every member requires exponential time. Suitable hierarchy theorems prove P⊊EXPTIME and PSPACE⊊EXPSPACE. They do not establish every adjacent containment strictly. P versus NP, NP versus PSPACE and PSPACE versus EXPTIME remain unresolved. coNP contains complements of NP languages; P⊆NP∩coNP, and NP=coNP is open. If any NP-complete language is in P, all NP collapses to P. This does not make every decidable language polynomial or make undecidable problems decidable. Avoid blanket claims about all cryptography or all problems becoming easy; the class and encoding matter. Automata and Complexity Theory module Sipser MIT Lecture 21: hierarchy theorems

records.text: For S→11S|0A|1A and A→0|1|0S, every reachable form has at most one variable, at the right end. A complete terminal word is still a sentential form. For example S⇒11S⇒1111S⇒111111S⇒1111110A⇒11111101. Returning to S appends a pair 11,00 or 10; use that invariant to rule out impossible prefixes rather than guessing from string length. For A→aB|bA|bBa and B→bB|cA|b, specify a start variable first. With A assumed, a terminating membership test recursively removes the required a/b prefix or b…a wrapper; B either matches b or removes b before B/c before A. Every recursive residual is shorter. Apply the membership test to every candidate word; none qualifies in this four-word example under the assumed start A. Use the membership test to justify whether a candidate word belongs to the language. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Specify languages, states and start symbols
records.text: Use the exact readable language formula and alphabet when testing membership. State labels are arbitrary: use the transition diagram, initial state and accepting markings, or a definition assigning meanings to states. Language theory alone cannot identify an arbitrary state label. An accepting start state and an ab return cycle require a corresponding regular expression to include both ε and ab. Declare the start variable before testing grammar membership; with A assumed in the grammar above, none of the four candidate words qualifies. Distinguish the non-CFL copy language ww from the even-palindrome language wwᴿ. Generic capable, contains and most difficult questions need a least-family, exact-class or reduction qualifier. For GNF first-step questions identify the conversion algorithm. Evaluate each description against the stated language and machine conventions. Automata and Complexity Theory module

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Computability, complexity and abstract machines
records.text: Computability theory asks whether an effective algorithm can solve a problem at all. For a decision problem, a decision procedure must terminate with the correct yes-or-no result on every input. Computational complexity theory studies the time and memory resources required to solve problems as functions of encoded input size. Automata theory studies abstract machine models and the languages they recognize; these subjects overlap but ask different questions. records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — The stack discipline and its queue contrast
records.text: A stack is last-in, first-out: push adds an item at the top and pop removes the top item, so the most recently pushed item is removed first. A PDA accesses this top rather than an arbitrary interior position. A queue is first-in, first-out: insertion at the rear and removal at the front returns the oldest waiting item. A linked list can implement a storage discipline, but the implementation container is different from the abstract push/pop or enqueue/dequeue access rule. records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Why satisfiability was the first NP-complete problem
records.text: Boolean satisfiability was the first problem proved NP-complete, through the Cook–Levin theorem. Its hardness proof starts directly from an arbitrary nondeterministic polynomial-time computation and constructs a Boolean formula that is satisfiable exactly when an accepting computation exists. This starting point matters: once one NP-complete problem is available, later hardness proofs can reduce that known problem to a new target. Membership in NP remains a separate obligation. Checking a satisfying assignment is efficient; whether finding one is always polynomial-time remains unresolved. University of Toronto CSC373: Complexity, slide 28

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Finite procedures are different from undecidable tasks
records.text: Sorting a finite numeric list is a terminating computation. Quicksort, for example, chooses a pivot, partitions the other entries and recursively sorts the smaller sublists. Each recursive subproblem has fewer entries. A large running time does not make the task undecidable. A finite linear system with exactly represented rational coefficients can be processed by Gaussian elimination and back substitution. Row exchanges handle unsuitable pivots; row reduction detects inconsistency or leaves free variables describing multiple solutions. These finite algebraic procedures differ from a general halting decider, which does not exist. records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Question 1 · Q00015
records.text: Q00015 Question 1 AUT01 Which of the following term refers to the number of symbols composing a string? Distinguish symbols, finite strings, their lengths and sets of strings. Apply the operation to its stated operands, including empty cases. A Length B Symbols C Alphabet D Word Length Count symbols rather than distinct symbols: that count is the string’s length, |w|. Alphabet is the set from which symbols are drawn, not the count in a particular string. A correct This is precisely the defined count |w|. B incorrect Symbols are the individual objects being counted. C incorrect An alphabet is a finite set of symbols. D incorrect A word/string is the sequence whose length is measured.

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Question 2 · Q00024
records.text: Q00024 Question 2 AUT02 Let L₁={c,d} and L₂={e,fgh}. Which lowercase word is NOT an element of L₂L₁? Distinguish symbols, finite strings, their lengths and sets of strings. Apply the operation to its stated operands, including empty cases. A fghc B ed C fghe D ec fghe Language concatenation preserves order: each word of L₂ is followed by a word of L₁. The four products are ec, ed, fghc and fghd. Thus fghe is the unique nonmember: its ending e is not one of the words available from L₁. The lowercase transcription repair makes the symbols consistent with the declared languages. A incorrect fghc is fgh followed by c, so it belongs to the product. B incorrect ed is e followed by d, so it belongs to the product. C correct fghe cannot be formed because e is not in L₁. D incorrect ec is e followed by c, so it belongs to the product.

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Question 3 · Q00032
records.text: Q00032 Question 3 AUT-S01 Which theory provides mechanisms for classifying combinatorial problems and measuring the computational resources necessary to solve them? Check whether the required procedure must halt on every input, and distinguish solving a task from recognizing its yes-instances. A Computability theory B Set theory C Complexity theory D Automata theory Complexity theory The requested quantity is the resources needed to solve a problem. Computational complexity estimates time and space requirements. Computability instead asks whether a membership algorithm exists at all. A incorrect Computability concerns existence of algorithms, rather than their resource costs. B incorrect Set theory does not name the study of time and space requirements. C correct Matches the resource-estimation definition directly. D incorrect Automata studies abstract machines; the specific resource classification asked here is complexity.

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Question 4 · Q00192
records.text: Q00192 Question 4 AUT13 Which language over {0,1} is denoted by (0+1)*0(0+1)*0(0+1)*? Here + means union. Track mandatory symbols and factors that may repeat or disappear. Use short test words to check both directions of each proposed language description. A Strings with substring 00 B Strings with at least two 0's C Strings with at most two 0's D Strings with postfix 1. Strings with at least two 0's Each starred factor denotes any binary string, including the empty string. The two unstarred zeros therefore require at least two zero occurrences, while permitting arbitrary symbols before, between and after them. Conversely, any word with at least two zeros can be split at two selected zero positions to fit the expression. For example, 010 fits without containing adjacent zeros, and 000 fits although it has more than two zeros. No final 1 is required. A incorrect 010 is generated but does not contain the adjacent substring 00. B correct Two explicit zeros are required; the starred factors allow additional zeros and ones. C incorrect 000 is generated, so there is no upper bound of two zeros. D incorrect 00 is generated and ends in 0.

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Question 5 · Q00193
records.text: Q00193 Question 5 AUT06 The transition function in a finite-state automaton maps which pair? Read the transition domain and acceptance condition carefully. Track which inputs are consumed and evaluate the whole word under the stated model. A Q and Σ to Σ B Q and Q to Σ C Σ and Σ to Q D Q and Σ to Q Q and Σ to Q For a deterministic finite automaton, finite control receives the current state and input symbol and chooses the next state. Thus δ:Q×Σ→Q. A general NFA instead has a set of possible next states, so the stem tacitly uses the deterministic convention. A incorrect Outputs an input symbol, not a state. B incorrect The second input must be a symbol, not another state. C incorrect Omits the current state and uses two input symbols. D correct Correct deterministic domain and codomain.

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Question 6 · Q00194
records.text: Q00194 Question 6 AUT40 AUT16 With start variable A and productions A→aB|bA|bBa and B→bB|cA|b, which offered string is generated? Apply the stated transition, closure or equivalence rule step by step; distinguish a guaranteed bound from a value for one particular machine. A abbcabbcbbbcbbaca B bcbbbcabbcbaa C acbcbbbbcabaa D bbbbcbbbbcab acbcbbbbcabaa With A as the start variable, the candidate follows the production sequence A⇒aB⇒acA⇒acbBa⇒acbcAa⇒acbcbAa⇒acbcbbAa⇒acbcbbbAa⇒acbcbbbbBaa⇒acbcbbbbcAaa⇒acbcbbbbcaBaa⇒acbcbbbbcabaa. Each rewrite uses one of the displayed rules, including a final B→b that removes the remaining variable. The other three offered words fail the complete shrinking-residual membership test. A incorrect Every permitted prefix or wrapper decomposition eventually leaves a residual that neither required variable generates. B incorrect The required A/B prefix and wrapper decompositions do not reach the terminating B→b production. C correct The displayed derivation produces acbcbbbbcabaa from start A. D incorrect Following the required variable after each prefix does not produce this word.

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Question 7 · Q00195
records.text: Q00195 Question 7 AUT04 When can we say two grammars are equivalent? Distinguish symbols, finite strings, their lengths and sets of strings. Apply the operation to its stated operands, including empty cases. A When the language derived from one grammar is a subset of the other B When the alphabets of the two grammars are the same C When the languages represented by both grammars are the same D When a single string is a member of both languages When the languages represented by both grammars are the same A grammar specifies its generated sentences. Equality of the generated sets, not equality of alphabets or overlap, is the criterion for semantic equivalence. For example {a} and {a,aa} have the same alphabet and a common string but different languages. A incorrect One-way inclusion allows extra strings in the other language. B incorrect Same terminal alphabet permits different sets of sentences. C correct Equality of the full generated languages establishes equivalence. D incorrect A single shared string establishes overlap only.

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Question 8 · Q00196
records.text: Q00196 Question 8 AUT14 If L1 and L2 are two regular languages, which one of the following is true Track mandatory symbols and factors that may repeat or disappear. Use short test words to check both directions of each proposed language description. A LiU L2 is a regular language only if empty string is not a member B Li* is the same with L2* and are both regular languages C LiL is also a regular language D L:* is a regular language and is equivalent to L; The concatenation L1L2 is regular. Regular languages are closed under concatenation, so any two regular languages have a regular concatenation. Reversal preserves regularity but need not preserve the original language. Union needs no exclusion of the empty word, and arbitrary closures need not coincide. A incorrect Union is regular even if it contains the empty word; the only-if restriction is false. B incorrect Both stars are regular, but arbitrary regular languages need not have equal Kleene closures. C correct The image reads L1L2; regular languages are closed under this concatenation operation. D incorrect The image reads reversal: it remains regular but need not equal L1, for example {ab} reverses to {ba}.

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Question 9 · Q00197
records.text: Q00197 Question 9 AUT40 AUT16 Let G = {N, T, P, S} be a grammar where: N={S, A}, T={ 0, 1}, S={S} and P= {S—11S|0A]|1A,A>0]|1] 0S}. Which one of the following is a sentential form? Apply the stated transition, closure or equivalence rule step by step; distinguish a guaranteed bound from a value for one particular machine. A 111011110S B 11111101 C 0000111001AS D OOO011L1I0A 11111101 The grammar is S→11S|0A|1A, A→0|1|0S, and option D is 00001110A. Terminal sentences are also sentential forms. B has the derivation S⇒11S⇒1111S⇒111111S⇒1111110A⇒11111101. Every reachable form contains at most one nonterminal, at the right end. Before final termination, a return to S appends either 11, 00, or 10. A cannot be segmented into these pairs (its last prefix pair is 01); C has two variables; D has prefix ending at A which cannot be obtained by those pairs followed by 0 or 1. A incorrect Before S the terminal prefix must be a sequence of pairs 11,00,10; 111011110 contains a forbidden pair 01 and has odd length. B correct The explicit derivation ends at this terminal sentence, which is also a sentential form. C incorrect Two variables AS cannot arise from rules that never introduce two variables. D incorrect The form 00001110A would require an odd-length prefix before A (pairs followed by one symbol); its eight-symbol prefix has even length.

records.title: Automata and Complexity Theory — Question 10 · Q00198
